### CF-D14. Connection plate fit: the diaphragm bolt row on the connection plate (CFD) and on the bearing stiffener (CFE); auto-design respects it   [§4: new check items] [cross-frame projects: checks identical]
Engineer's decision (2026-10-13): add a check that the bolt row fits the connection plate (it was shown only in the drawings, CF-D11 open item 1).
- **Where (anchors):**
  - `cfDiaChecks(R, out, end)`, after the bolt-line item (anchor `// connection plate fit (CF-D14, 2026-10-13)`): two new items in CFD (plate = `cfCP(p)`, the Transverse stiffeners connection plate, CF-D13) and in CFE (plate = `cfCP(p, true)`, the bearing stiffener, else the same connection plate), from the same geometry the drawings use (`cfDiaFit`, CF-D11; flange thicknesses `SB ? SB.tt : 1`, `SB ? SB.tc : 0.75` as the drawings):
    ```js
    const cp = cfCP(p, end), G = cfDiaFit(R, q, cp, SB ? SB.tt : 1, SB ? SB.tc : 0.75), de = G.ecc - G.gap, mA = Math.min(G.edge, de), okA = mA >= em - 1e-9 && G.gap >= cp.tw / 2 + 1e-9;
    it(`Connection plate fit: bolt line ${f2(G.ecc)} in from the web centerline, edge distances to the plate's free edge and to the diaphragm end (6.13.2.6.6)`, …, okA ? 'pass' : 'fail', mA > 0 ? em / mA : 99.99);
    it(`Connection plate fit: end bolts to the plate ends (flange faces less the ${frac(cp.c)} in corner clip; 6.13.2.6.6)`, `${f2(G.vEdge)} in`, `≥ ${frac(em)} in`, G.vEdge >= em - 1e-9 ? 'pass' : 'fail', G.vEdge > 0 ? em / G.vEdge : 99.99);
    ```
    with (from `cfDiaFit`) edge = t<sub>w</sub>/2 + b<sub>s</sub> − e; gap = `cfDiaGap` = max(0.5, e − 1.5); diaphragm end distance = e − gap; lap = t<sub>w</sub>/2 + b<sub>s</sub> − gap (= edge + diaphragm end distance, so "lap ≥ both edge distances" is these two items); vEdge = min(d/2 − (n−1)s/2 − t<sub>f,bot</sub> − c, d − t<sub>f,top</sub> − c − (d/2 + (n−1)s/2)). The CFD/CFE note gets one sentence with the values. Status **fail** when any distance is below e<sub>min</sub> or the diaphragm end reaches the web (code minimum).
  - Auto-design: new `adCfPlate(C0, q, end, em, s)` before `adCfDiaInt` (anchor `const adCfPlate =`): the most bolts that fit the plate height, n<sub>pl</sub> = ⌊(d − 2 max(t<sub>f</sub>) − 2c − 2e<sub>min</sub>)/s⌋ + 1, and whether the bolt line e itself misfits (edge or diaphragm end < e<sub>min</sub>). `adCfDiaInt` and `adCfDiaEnd`: `nMax` = min(web limit (unchanged), n<sub>pl</sub>) (before: web limit only); when e misfits, the "Connection plate fit: bolt line" item is left out of the pass test (no section or bolt count can fix it; e is an input and is kept) and the message says so: "Diaphragm connection: the bolt line e = 6.00 in … does not fit the 6 × 1/2 in connection plate (0.25 in to its free edge, 1.50 in to the diaphragm end; e_min = 1 1/8 in, 6.13.2.6.6). No bolt count can fix this: with this plate e must not exceed t_w/2 + b_s − e_min = 5.13 in (e is an input and was not changed). The plate-fit item fails"; when nothing passes, the message adds "(at most n bolts fit the height of the … plate …)" if the plate limited the count.
  - Detailing tab (`renderGeometry`, anchor `/^(Depth|Bolt line|Connection plate fit)/`): the two items are listed with the depth and bolt-line items.
  - Inputs: the read-only plate line's note reads "β<sub>sec</sub>, drawings, plate fit"; drawing caption "the values β<sub>sec</sub> and the plate-fit check use"; Manual "Diaphragms (Cross-frames module)": one "Plate fit (CFD, CFE)" paragraph.
- **Cross-frame (angles):** no plate-fit item. The module's connection model (CF5, CF6) has the angle bolts in one line through the connected leg and a **gusset plate** (`cf.conn.tg`), not through the connection plate; the gusset-to-connection-plate connection is not modeled ("Gusset plate and connection plate design" is listed under "Not checked here"). A plate-fit item for the angles would need that gusset geometry.
- **§4 callout (new check):**
  - **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.13.2.6.6, Table 6.13.2.6.6-1 (minimum edge distance; the module's value for rolled/gas-cut edges, `BOLT[d].emin.cut`: 7/8 in bolt 1 1/8 in, 1 in bolt 1 1/4 in, as the existing CFD bolt-line item and CF6).
  - **Formula:** t<sub>w</sub>/2 + b<sub>s</sub> − e ≥ e<sub>min</sub>; e − gap ≥ e<sub>min</sub> and gap ≥ t<sub>w</sub>/2; end bolts to the plate ends (flange face less clip c) ≥ e<sub>min</sub>. **Before:** none (shown in the drawing only). **After:** fail if violated.
  - **Check case, repro (headless Chromium; W30x99, 5 - 7/8 in bolts at 3 in, e = 3.5 in, d = 38.88 in, t<sub>w</sub> = 1/2, t<sub>f</sub> = 1 1/8 bottom / 3/4 top, c = 1 in, e<sub>min</sub> = 1 1/8 in):**
    - CFD, TS Type B 6 × 1/2 (CF-D13): edge 0.25 + 6 − 3.5 = **2.75 ≥ 1.125**; gap = 3.5 − 1.5 = 2.00, diaphragm end 3.5 − 2.0 = **1.50 ≥ 1.125**; lap 6.25 − 2.00 = 4.25 = 2.75 + 1.50; ratio 1.125/1.50 = 0.75, pass. End bolts at 19.44 ± 6: bottom 13.44 − 1.125 − 1 = **11.32**, top 38.88 − 0.75 − 1 − 25.44 = 11.69 → 11.32 ≥ 1.125 (0.10), pass.
    - With the 5 × 1/2 plate (no Transverse stiffeners connection-plate type, the `cf.sb` inputs): edge 0.25 + 5 − 3.5 = **1.75 ≥ 1 1/8, pass** (0.75, the diaphragm end governs).
    - CFE, bearing stiffener Type A 7 × 7/8 (narrowest used): edge 0.25 + 7 − 3.5 = 3.75; diaphragm end 1.50; end bolts 11.32; pass.
    - **e = 6 in (misfit):** CFD edge 0.25 + 6 − 6 = **0.25 < 1.125, fail (ratio 4.50)**; gap 4.50, diaphragm end 1.50, lap 1.75; end bolts 11.32 pass. CFD fails (status, module badge, Design all). CFE (7 in stiffener): 0.25 + 7 − 6 = 1.25 ≥ 1.125, pass (0.90). Auto-design keeps W30x99 with 5 bolts and e = 6 and reports the misfit (message above; e ≤ 0.25 + 6 − 1.125 = 5.13 in). With the 5 in plate: 0.25 + 5 − 6 = −0.75 (outside the plate), fail.
    - **Plate height limits the bolt count:** clip 7.5 in on both plates, jacking R<sub>j</sub> = 175 kip at 12 in: n<sub>pl</sub> = ⌊(38.88 − 2(1.125) − 2(7.5) − 2(1.125))/3⌋ + 1 = ⌊19.38/3⌋ + 1 = 7 (web limit 9 for W30x99); the end diaphragm tried W30x99, W33x118, W36x135 with up to 7 bolts, none passes the bolt force, so CFE fails and the message names the plate limit; with 7 bolts the end bolts are 1.82 ≥ 1.125 in from the plate ends.
  - **Default example (cross-frame):** no CFD/CFE, no new item; every check identical.
- **Saved data:** no key or format change.
- **How verified (CF-D13 and CF-D14):** `node --check` on the inline scripts; headless Chromium (Playwright), main vs branch, after merging origin/main (PR #180). Default example (cross-frame): every module's checks (ids, statuses, items), Summary, Member forces, cross-frame auto-design result, Design all (statuses, quantities, costs, conflicts), autosave and every localStorage key identical (timestamps masked); differences only in the cross-frame report's input list (the read-only plate line in place of the b<sub>s</sub>, t<sub>s</sub> inputs), the elevation (plate 6 in) and the DXF plate outline/note. Repro (diaphragm): CFD/CFE identical to main plus the two items each; auto-design W30x99 / 5 bolts both ends; e = 6 misfit; plate-height limit; bearing-stiffener and Transverse-stiffeners fallbacks; cross-frame with h = 40 in (β<sub>sec</sub> change above). Saved data both directions (the same saved diaphragm project in main and branch gives the same `P.cf` after auto-design). Screenshots: inputs (read-only plate line, fallback), Checks (CFD items), both elevations, misfit. No console errors.
- **Other copies:** none.
- **Open items (raised, not changed):**
  1. The end-bolt distance subtracts the corner clip even when the bolt line is outside the clip (as the CF-D11 caption does): conservative.
  2. The plate's free edge uses `cf.sb.tw` for the web; the bearing stiffener rows have their own t<sub>w</sub>.
  3. e<sub>min</sub> uses the rolled/gas-cut column; a sheared plate edge needs the larger value (1 1/2 in for 7/8 in bolts).

A cross-frame on a girder below the minimum gives a warning, not a failure. Auto-design selects the type: below the minimum it switches to the diaphragm and picks the lightest channel, then W, at least 0.75 d deep that passes every CFD item, with the fewest bolts (one row, pitch 3 in or 3d); at or above the minimum it designs the cross-frame and switches a diaphragm back. Double-click the <b>Intermediate bracing used</b> label to lock the choice (and the shape, bolt count, or pitch labels to lock those). Preliminary sizing sends its own minimum (Framing tab) with the cross-frame geometry, and its Suggest tab states the recommendation. Design all counts the diaphragm steel (S less the end gaps, times the weight per foot from the nominal area) and its bolts in place of the angles.</p>

## 2026-10-13 — PR: claude/girderdetail-xs1 (cross-section and dead loads, PR1 of 4: display only; engineer's decisions 2026-10-13; PR link added after merge)

LLDF and DLs module (`GM.df`), main page only. The PL_B64 line and the Cross-frames module are not touched. Ported by copying and adapting from `lldf.html` (unchanged; CLAUDE.md §3): `MD.footprints` / `MD.headroom` / `MD.draw` (drawing) and `renderDLCalcs` (worked calculations). **No result changes:** `dfDead`, `dfEdges`, `GM.df.compute`, `dfPayload`, and every input, key, and saved format are unchanged; the new code only reads `R.dead` (the `dfDead` result), `R.b`, `R.base`, and `R.p.dl`.

### XS1. Drawings tab: new card "Cross-section and dead loads" (`dw-xs`)   [display only] [results bit-identical]
- **Where (anchors):** new `const DF_LCOL`, `const DF_DIST`, `function dfXsSVG(R)` (before `function dfSensSVG`); `GM.df.drawings` (anchor `return card('dw-xs', 'Cross-section and dead loads'`) puts the card before the existing "Cross-section and lever rule" card (unchanged). New CSS `.dwg.dfxs { min-width: 520px; max-width: 900px; }` after `.dwg.sec2`.
- **What it draws:** deck slab, haunches, girders (I symbols), SIP forms (dashed, clear bays), barriers per side (barrier mode: schematic profile, width `b.barrier`), or curb (width `cw`, height `ch`) and railing post at `rp` (on the curb when `rp ≤ cw`, else on the deck or sidewalk) in curb mode (`b.edge`), sidewalks (deck edge to `swL`/`swR`, thickness), median (centered, joint shown dashed red when "Yes"), wearing surface strip (r<sub>L</sub> to W − r<sub>R</sub>), pedestrian load arrows over the walkable width (f to sw, as `dfDead`), added line loads as arrows at their x. Each load from `R.dead.per` is labeled "`desc`: w klf `class`" in its class colour (DC1 #1f4e8c, DC2 #3f7fc4, DW #12806e, PL #8a6d1d, the Structural analysis diagram colours), in label rows above the section with leaders (rows assigned greedily so labels do not overlap). Below each girder: DC1, DC2, DW (and PL when any) in klf from `R.dead`. Girder-spacing dimension chain, deck width, centroid x̄ (MassDOT method), legend. Widths and positions to scale; heights schematic (as lldf).
- **Check case:** built-in example: labels "Left barrier: 0.400 klf DC2", "Right barrier: 0.400 klf DC2", "Future wearing surface: 1.038 klf DW" (25 psf × 41.5 ft); G1 DC1 0.895 / DC2 0.341 / DW 0.208 — the same as the "Dead load distribution per girder" table.
- **Other copies:** `lldf.html` `MD.draw` (source, unchanged).

### XS2. Derivations tab, card "Dead load distribution" (`cap-dl`): full worked calculation   [display only] [results bit-identical]
- **Where (anchors):** `GM.df.capacity` — before: the `Edl` array built inline (anchor `Edl.push(eq('Deck by tributary width'`), four kinds of `eq()` blocks (deck, haunch + SIP, pile-cap rule, one per load). After: `h += card('cap-dl', 'Dead load distribution', …, dfDLCalcs(R));` with new `function dfDLCalcs(R)` (before `function dfSensSVG`).
- **Content (`eq()` blocks with tables):** (1) tributary width b<sub>trib,i</sub>, table with Σ = W<sub>deck</sub>; (2) DC1 = deck + haunch + SIP (+ added DC1 rows) as `dfDead` computes them, with a G1 example and the check Σw<sub>deck</sub> = W<sub>deck</sub>(t<sub>s</sub>/12)γ<sub>c</sub>; (3) pile-cap group properties x̄, c<sub>i</sub>, c<sub>i</sub><sup>2</sup>, Σc<sup>2</sup>; (4) the distribution rules as GD implements them today: equal P/N<sub>b</sub>; pile-cap P/N<sub>b</sub> + max(0, Pec<sub>i</sub>/Σc<sup>2</sup>) (no uplift relief); two adjacent P(1 − t), Pt, and a load at or outside an exterior girder all to that girder (the lldf F6 overhang lever is **not** ported here; PR2); FWS always equal; (5) worked example on the largest pile-cap load (governing girder; table P/N<sub>b</sub>, Pec<sub>i</sub>/Σc<sup>2</sup>, R<sub>i</sub>, Σ); (6) every load (pile-cap: e; two adjacent: t; equal: P/N<sub>b</sub>; ΣR); (7) per-girder summary DC1, DC2, DW, DC1 + DC2 + DW, PL.
- **Governing provision:** MassDOT Bridge Manual Part I 3.5.3 (pile-cap analogy, no uplift relief; wearing surface equally); AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 4.6.2.2.1 (equal). No formula changed; the displayed formulas are those already in `dfDead`.
- **Check case (built-in example, girders at 3.25, 12.75, 22.25, 31.75, 41.25 ft, W = 44.50 ft):** x̄ = 111.25/5 = 22.25 ft; Σc<sup>2</sup> = 2(19.00²) + 2(9.50²) = 902.50 ft²; left barrier P = 0.400 klf at x = 0.75, e = −21.50: R<sub>1</sub> = 0.400/5 + 0.400(−21.50)(−19.00)/902.50 = 0.080 + 0.181 = 0.261 klf; R<sub>4</sub>, R<sub>5</sub> = 0.080 (clipped); ΣR = 0.672 klf (P + 0.272). Sidewalk case (swL = 6 ft × 8 in): P = 6(8/12)(0.150) = 0.600 klf at x = 3.00, e = −19.25: R<sub>1</sub> = 0.120 + 0.600(−19.25)(−19.00)/902.50 = 0.120 + 0.243 = 0.363 klf (screen: 0.363). Deck: Σ = 44.50(0.667)(0.150) = 4.450 klf (table Σ 4.450).

### XS3. Factors and loads tab: card "Loads on the bridge" (`cb-xl`)   [display only] [results bit-identical]
- **Where (anchors):** `GM.df.combos` — before: the sub-table `<h4 class="sub-h">Superimposed loads</h4>` inside card `cb-dl` (load, category, x, w, distribution, G1…GN). After: removed from `cb-dl` and replaced by `h += card('cb-xl', 'Loads on the bridge', …, dfLoadsTbl(R));` right after `cb-dl`; new `function dfLoadsTbl(R)` (before `function dfSensSVG`).
- **Content:** every superimposed load: name, class, x, P, distribution, R per girder, ΣR, and the check "ΣR = P" or "ΣR = P + d" (pile-cap, no uplift relief); a total row per class (ΣP, per-girder sums, ΣR); the per-girder class sums are compared with `R.dead.dc2`, `dw`, `pl` (and `dc1` less deck, haunch, SIP), and the note states the result (an inconsistency would be named).
- **Check case:** example: DW total P = 1.038, each girder 0.208, ΣR = P; DC2 total P = 0.800, ΣR = 1.343 (P + 0.543, the two barriers' clipped shares).

### Verification (XS1–XS3)
- `node --check` on every inline script.
- Headless Chromium (Playwright), `origin/main` (e8a50c9) vs this branch (after merging e8a50c9), five projects: built-in example (barrier mode); sidewalks 6 ft × 8 in / 5 ft × 9 in, median 4 ft × 9 in with joint, ped 75 psf, added rows (DW pile-cap, DC2 two-adjacent on the overhang, DC1 two-adjacent between girders, DC2 equal, the 0-plf example row); curb mode (curb 12 × 10 in and 10 × 8 in, railings at 0.5 and 1.25 ft); curb mode with a left sidewalk and the added rows; AASHTO (equal) method with the sidewalk loads. Identical: `JSON.stringify(GM.df.compute(P.df))` (bridge ts zeroed), `GM.sa.compute` for every girder, the `gd-dfx` payload (`dfPayload`, ts zeroed), Checks and Summary tab text, Design all (built-in example and sidewalk project: status, cost, conflicts), saved data `P` and all localStorage keys (only timestamps and `ui.otab`, the tab the script last opened, differ). Only the Factors and loads, Derivations, Drawings tab content (and so the report) differ, as intended. No console errors.
- Screenshots at 1400 px and 1000 px viewport widths: the cross-section fits the card at 1000 px (scrolls below 520 px), labels do not overlap.
- **Other copies:** none (the ported code is adapted, not shared; `lldf.html` is unchanged).
- **Open items (for PR2–PR4):** see the PR description.

## 2026-10-13 — PR: claude/girderdetail-xs2 (cross-section and dead loads, PR2 of 4: inputs, overrides, mountable rule, F6; engineer's decisions 2026-10-13; PR link added after merge)

LLDF and DLs module (`GM.df`), main page only. The PL_B64 line is not touched (the deck edges stay owned by Preliminary sizing until PR3). `lldf.html` is reference only and unchanged (CLAUDE.md §3). Every new input is optional and stored only when entered (no new default keys, so `deepMerge` of an older project adds nothing). XS4 and XS5 change no result for a project without the new inputs; XS6 and XS7 are §4 changes for the cases they state.

### XS4. Input tab "Cross-section and dead loads": element inputs in sections; railings or fences on sidewalks, overlays, wearing surface by thickness, appurtenance γ<sub>c</sub>, utilities as DW   [new optional inputs] [results unchanged without them] [default example row: DW, "Follows the method"]
- **Where (anchors):** `GM.df.itabs` (`['df_dl', 'Dead loads']` → `['df_dl', 'Cross-section and dead loads']`); `GM.df.panes` `df_dl:` (rewritten in sections: Deck edges, Sidewalks, Median, Wearing surface and overlays, Utilities and other line loads, Distribution method); new `function dfEdgeSummary(b)`, `const dfOpt`, `function dfXsIn(p, errors)` (before `GM.df = {`); `GM.df.rowSpec2` / `rowPath2: 'ovl'` / `rowNew` (overlay rows); `GM.df.def.extra[0]`; `GM.df.rowSpec` dist option `['auto', 'Follows the method']`; `GM.df.compute` (anchor `const xs = dfXsIn(p, errors)` and the `dfDead(...)` call); `dfEdges(b, wcA)`; `dfDead` (anchors `ua = a.uwcA > 0`, `id: 'fenceL'`, `id: 'ovl' + k`, `L.dist !== 'auto'`, `byMethod`); `gmRowEdit` (anchors `rows = P[id][path] || (P[id][path] = [])`, `GM[id].rowNew[path]`); display: `dfXsSVG` (overlay strips, fence posts, legend), `dfLoadsTbl` ("(method)"), `dfDLCalcs` (new step "Superimposed line loads from the cross-section", rules note, per-load reference), drawings caption.
- **New optional saved fields (absent = today's behaviour):** `P.df.dl.wcA` (kcf; curbs, sidewalks, median; blank = deck w<sub>c</sub>), `P.df.dl.fenceL`, `fenceXL`, `fenceR`, `fenceXR` (railing or fence on a sidewalk: klf, ft from its deck edge; must lie on the sidewalk), `P.df.dl.wsMode` (`''` = psf from Preliminary sizing as today, `'thk'` = thickness × γ), `P.df.dl.wsThk` (in), `P.df.dl.wsGam` (kcf), `P.df.ovl` (rows `{name, mode: 'psf'|'thk', psf, thk, gam}`), and the row distribution value `'auto'` ("Follows the method"). No key renamed or removed; older builds ignore the new fields.
- **What the loads are:** fence: DC2 line load at x (right side: W<sub>deck</sub> − x). Overlay: DW, q/1000 × (wearing-surface width), equal to all girders (as the wearing surface). Wearing surface by thickness: q = t/12 × γ × 1000 psf replaces the Preliminary sizing psf. γ<sub>c</sub>: curb (cw/12)(ch/12)γ<sub>c</sub>, sidewalk w(t/12)γ<sub>c</sub>, median w(t/12)γ<sub>c</sub>; deck, haunch, SIP keep the deck w<sub>c</sub>. "Follows the method" (engineer: DW = utilities + wearing surface, MassDOT pile-cap for DC2 and equal for DW): MassDOT → DW equally, DC1/DC2/PL pile-cap; AASHTO → equally. A row with an explicit rule keeps it (as before).
- **Defaults:** the built-in example's 0-plf utility row becomes `cat: 'DW', dist: 'auto'` (was DC2, pile-cap). It is 0 klf (skipped by `dfDead`), so no result changes. Saved rows keep their stored category and rule (arrays are not merged).
- **Governing provision:** MassDOT Bridge Manual Part I 3.5.3 (engineer's decisions 2026-10-13); AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 4.6.2.2.1 (equal option). No formula, factor, or existing input changed.
- **Check case (built-in bridge, sidewalks 6 ft × 8 in / 5 ft × 9 in, γ<sub>c</sub> = 0.145, wearing surface 2.5 in × 0.144 kcf, overlays 5 psf and 1.25 in × 0.145 kcf, fences 0.050 klf at 5.5 ft (left) and 0.030 klf at 4.5 ft (right), gas main DW 0.080 klf at 25 ft "follows the method", signal conduit DC2 0.020 klf at 40 ft "follows the method"):** left sidewalk 6(8/12)(0.145) = 0.580 klf; wearing surface q = 2.5/12 × 0.144 × 1000 = 30.0 psf × (44.50 − 6 − 5 = 33.50 ft) = 1.005 klf, 0.201 per girder; latex overlay q = 15.10 psf → 0.506 klf; gas main equal 0.016 per girder; signal conduit pile-cap R<sub>5</sub> = 0.004 + 0.020(17.75)(19.00)/902.5 = 0.011 klf; right fence at x = 40.00 ft. Screen values identical.
- **Other copies:** none (`lldf.html` `footprints`/`autoLoads` were the reference; not shared code).

### XS5. Per-load overrides of the automatic loads (distribution rule, line load, x) and beam-class labels   [new optional inputs] [results unchanged without them]
- **Where (anchors):** `dfDead` (anchors `// per-load overrides of the automatic loads (XS5`, `const clsAuto = cls.slice()`, `...(a.bcls ? { clsAuto } : {})`); `GM.df.compute` (anchor `const g0 = regions[0].geo, lo = p.loadOverrides`; validation; `ovr: lo, bcls:` in the `dfDead` call); `GM.df.panes` `df_dl` (Distribution method: "Beam classification (labels only)" `#df-bcls`; new section "Load overrides" `#df-ovr`); `GM.df.after` (`dfOvrSync(R)`); new `function dfOvrSync(R)` and its `change`/`click` listeners (`data-dfov`, `data-dfcls`, `data-dfovr`), `const DF_DIST_S`; CSS `.df-ov`, `.df-ovt`; display: `cb-dl` classification cell ("set"), `dfXsSVG` labels "(override)" and barrier/curb labels at the load's x, `dfLoadsTbl` outlined overridden cells, `dfDLCalcs` per-load title "override of …".
- **New optional saved fields:** `P.df.loadOverrides` = `{ <load id>: { x?, plf?, dist? } }` (as lldf `state.loadOverrides`; ids `barL`, `barR`, `curbL`, `curbR`, `railL`, `railR`, `swL`, `swR`, `fenceL`, `fenceR`, `med`, `ws`), and `P.df.beamClass` = `{ <girder index from 0>: <class key of DF_CLS> }`. Created only when a value is entered, removed when the last one is cleared. Ids that no longer exist (or girder indices ≥ N<sub>b</sub>) are kept but ignored, so nothing saved is discarded.
- **Behaviour:** a blank cell uses the automatic value (shown under the load's name); an entered value replaces it before distribution and is outlined in the input table (as GD's import overrides) and in the "Loads on the bridge" table, with the automatic value on hover; ↺ resets the load. x is from the left deck edge (0 to W<sub>deck</sub>), line load ≥ 0. Added line loads, overlays, and the pedestrian load are not overridden here (they have their own inputs; the pedestrian load is left as is per the engineer). The beam-class override changes only the label (tables, CSV), not any load.
- **AASHTO method and added rows:** a row set to "Follows the method" (XS4) becomes equal under AASHTO; a row with an explicit rule keeps it (stated on the input tab, with the example "a pile-cap row stays pile-cap under AASHTO").
- **Governing provision:** MassDOT Bridge Manual Part I 3.5.3 and Fig. 3.5.3-1 (classes). No formula changed.
- **Check case (built-in bridge with the XS4 sidewalks, fence 0.050 klf at 5.5 ft, overrides: left barrier x = 0.90 ft and 0.450 klf; right barrier x = 43.00 ft and "two adjacent"; right sidewalk "two adjacent"; median 0.500 klf; wearing surface pile-cap; G1 class "exterior safety curb", G3 "median beam (continuous)"):** left barrier R<sub>1</sub> = 0.450/5 + 0.450(0.90 − 22.25)(−19.00)/902.5 = 0.090 + 0.202 = 0.292 klf (screen 0.292); right barrier at 43.00 > 41.25: all to G5 = 0.400 (before F6, XS7); wearing surface pile-cap R<sub>5</sub> = 0.838/5 + 0.838(0.50)(19.00)/902.5 = 0.176 (screen 0.176); classes G1 "Exterior safety curb beam (set)", G3 "Median beam (continuous slab, interior) (set)"; loads unchanged by the class labels.
- **Other copies:** none (`lldf.html` `loadOverrides` / `beamClass` were the reference).

### XS6. Mountable sidewalks (< 12 in) are ignored when positioning the live load; the traffic face is the next non-mountable element   [§4: live load position, roadway, N<sub>L</sub>, d<sub>e</sub>] [changes projects with a sidewalk thinner than 12 in]
- **Where (anchors):** new `function dfLLFace(b, dl, xs, fL, fR)` and `const dfLLTxt` (before `function dfOvrSync`); `GM.df.compute` — before: `rL: Math.max(fL, swL), rR: Math.max(fR, swR)` in `const base = {`; after: `const ll = dfLLFace(b, p.dl, xs, fL, fR);` and `rL: ll.L.r, rR: ll.R.r`; `R.ll` returned (`return { errors: [], b, MR, regions, dead, base, p, ll }`). `dfDead` — before: `const wx0 = p.rL, wx1 = Wd - p.rR;` after: `const wx0 = Math.max(p.fL, swL), wx1 = Wd - Math.max(p.fR, swR);` (the wearing surface keeps its width between the curb faces: identical to before in every case). Display: `dfOvrSync` (`#df-llface` note on the Sidewalks section), Derivations "Roadway and design lanes" (r<sub>L</sub>, r<sub>R</sub> rows with the governing element), `dfXsSVG` (red dashed "LL face" lines, caption), Sidewalks note, DF3 note.
- **Rule (engineer's decision 2026-10-13):** a curb or sidewalk less than 12 in high is mountable and ignored when positioning the live load; 12 in or more limits it. Each side: r = the largest (innermost) of: the deck-edge traffic face f (barrier width, or in curb mode the "edge to traffic face" entered in Preliminary sizing), the sidewalk width when its thickness t ≥ 12 in, and the x of a railing or fence on the sidewalk (XS4) when entered.
  - **Before:** r<sub>L</sub> = max(f<sub>L</sub>, w<sub>sw,L</sub>) for any sidewalk thickness.
  - **After:** r<sub>L</sub> = max(f<sub>L</sub>, [w<sub>sw,L</sub> if t<sub>sw,L</sub> ≥ 12 in], [x<sub>fence,L</sub> if entered]); the same on the right.
  - r feeds `dfGeometry` (roadway w = W<sub>deck</sub> − r<sub>L</sub> − r<sub>R</sub>, N<sub>L</sub>, lane width, d<sub>e</sub> = overhang − r), `dfLever` (trucks 2 ft from r), and `dfRigid` (curb position), so every live load distribution factor that uses them.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.6.1.1.1 (number of design lanes INT(w/12), w = clear roadway between curbs and/or barriers; the tool cites 3.6.1.1.1 for the roadway), 3.6.1.3.1 (design lane / wheel 2.0 ft from the face of the curb or railing; the tool's lever rule), 4.6.2.2.1 (d<sub>e</sub> to the interior edge of the curb or traffic barrier; DF1 and the e-factor), Tables 4.6.2.2.2d-1 and 4.6.2.2.3b-1 (e-factor), Eq. C4.6.2.2.2d-1 (rigid cross-section); the 12 in mountable-curb limit is the engineer's rule (owner practice), not an AASHTO number.
- **In curb mode** the deck-edge face is the "edge to traffic face" f entered in Preliminary sizing, taken as given (a curb under 12 in at the deck edge is not re-evaluated until GirderDetail owns the deck edges in PR3).
- **Check case (built-in example: 5 girders at 9.50 ft, overhangs 3.25 ft, barrier 1.50 ft, W<sub>deck</sub> = 44.50 ft, span 1 L = 110 ft; sidewalks 6.00 ft each side, no median or pedestrian load):**
  - 10 in sidewalks, before: r = max(1.50, 6.00) = 6.00 ft; w = 44.50 − 12.00 = 32.50 ft, N<sub>L</sub> = 2; d<sub>e</sub> = 3.25 − 6.00 = −2.75 ft; exterior: rigid 2 lanes, curb at X<sub>ext</sub> + d<sub>e</sub> = 19.00 − 2.75 = 16.25 ft, Σe = 11.25 + (−0.75) = 10.50, R = 2/5 + 19.00(10.50)/902.50 = 0.621; e-factor with d<sub>e</sub> limited to −1.0: e<sub>M</sub> = 0.77 − 1.0/9.1 = 0.660, g = 0.660(0.708) = 0.467; lever 1 lane 0.300. g<sub>M,ext</sub> = **0.621**, g<sub>V,ext</sub> = **0.651**, fatigue M **0.250**, g<sub>Δ</sub> = 2(1.00)/5 = **0.400**.
  - 10 in sidewalks, after (mountable: r = 1.50 ft, the barrier face): w = 44.50 − 3.00 = 41.50 ft, N<sub>L</sub> = 3; d<sub>e</sub> = 3.25 − 1.50 = 1.75 ft; rigid 2 lanes: curb 19.00 + 1.75 = 20.75 ft, Σe = 15.75 + 3.75 = 19.50, R = 0.400 + 19.00(19.50)/902.50 = 0.811 (3 lanes: 0.85(0.600 + 19.00(11.25)/902.50) = 0.711); e<sub>M</sub> = 0.77 + 1.75/9.1 = 0.962, g = 0.681; lever 1 lane 0.789. g<sub>M,ext</sub> = **0.811**, g<sub>V,ext</sub> = **0.850**, fatigue M **0.658**, g<sub>Δ</sub> = 3(0.85)/5 = **0.510**. Interior girders unchanged (0.708 / 0.963). Dead loads unchanged (DC2 G1 1.003, DW 0.186 to 0.206; the wearing surface stays 32.50 ft wide).
  - 12 in sidewalks: r = 6.00 ft (sidewalk curb face) before and after; every result identical.
- **Outputs that change (only where a sidewalk is thinner than 12 in and wider than the deck-edge face, or a railing/fence is entered):** roadway, N<sub>L</sub>, lane width, d<sub>e</sub> (DF1 items), every lever-rule, e-factor and rigid result and so the exterior (and, with N<sub>b</sub> = 3 or S > 16 ft, interior) moment, shear and fatigue factors, the deflection factor g<sub>Δ</sub>, the Factors and loads / Derivations / Drawings tabs, the `gd-dfx` payload to Preliminary sizing (span and pier factors; when "Use these factors" is Yes the sizing demands and everything fed from sizing), and the Structural analysis live load. Dead loads, the pedestrian load and its walkable width, and saved data do not change. **Note:** the sidewalk thickness default is 8 in, so every saved project with a sidewalk wider than its traffic face and a thickness left below 12 in changes.
- **Preliminary sizing (PlateLine) is not changed:** its own roadway and d<sub>e</sub> (`brGeom`, its built-in approximate factors when "Use these factors" is No) still use its faces; it has no sidewalk input. That is left to PR3, when GirderDetail owns the deck edges.
- **Other copies:** none (`lldf.html` `faceOffset` still uses max(railing/curb, sidewalk); unchanged per CLAUDE.md §3 and the plan).

### XS7. "Two adjacent" rule: a load on an overhang is levered about the first interior girder (port of lldf F6)   [§4: dead-load distribution] [more conservative for the exterior girder; less conservative (relief) for the first interior girder]
- **Where (anchors):** `dfDead`, arrow `two` (anchor `// two adjacent (lldf F6, XS7)`); display: `dfDLCalcs` "Distribution rules" equation and note, and the per-load equation for a two-adjacent load outside the exterior girder (anchor `overhang } a =`).
- **Before:**
  ```js
  const two = (P, xL) => { const r = ub.map(() => 0); if (xL <= ub[0]) r[0] = P; else if (xL >= ub[N - 1]) r[N - 1] = P; else { let k = 0; while (k < N - 2 && ub[k + 1] < xL) k++; const t = (xL - ub[k]) / (ub[k + 1] - ub[k]); r[k] = P * (1 - t); r[k + 1] = P * t; } return r; };
  ```
- **After:**
  ```js
  // two adjacent (lldf F6, XS7): a load outside an exterior girder is levered about the first interior girder, R_ext = P(1 + a/S), R_next = -P a/S (sums to P)
  const two = (P, xL) => { const r = ub.map(() => 0);
    if (xL <= ub[0]) { const S1 = N > 1 ? ub[1] - ub[0] : 0, a = ub[0] - xL; if (S1 > 0 && a > 0) { r[0] = P * (1 + a / S1); r[1] = -P * a / S1; } else r[0] = P; }
    else if (xL >= ub[N - 1]) { const S1 = N > 1 ? ub[N - 1] - ub[N - 2] : 0, a = xL - ub[N - 1]; if (S1 > 0 && a > 0) { r[N - 1] = P * (1 + a / S1); r[N - 2] = -P * a / S1; } else r[N - 1] = P; } else { let k = 0; while (k < N - 2 && ub[k + 1] < xL) k++; const t = (xL - ub[k]) / (ub[k + 1] - ub[k]); r[k] = P * (1 - t); r[k + 1] = P * t; } return r; };
  ```
  (lldf F6 code adapted: `a > 0` added so a load exactly on the exterior girder still gives P to it and 0, not −0, to the next.)
- **Problem:** a load outside the exterior girder set to "Two adjacent beams" went entirely (P) to the exterior girder. Simple-span lever action about the first interior girder gives P(1 + a/S) to the exterior girder and −Pa/S to the next one. lldf.html made this change as F6; GD's copy was not updated.
- **Governing provision:** statics (simple-span lever distribution between the exterior and first interior girders), the "two adjacent beams" option of MassDOT Bridge Manual Part I 3.5.3 as implemented in lldf.html (fixlog/lldf.md F6). **Open:** lldf O6 / LLDF-O6 (MassDOT to confirm whether the negative share on the first interior girder should be kept, as statics gives, or dropped like the pile-cap rule's no-uplift relief) is still open; this port keeps the statics, as lldf does meanwhile.
- **Check case (built-in example, girders at 3.25, 12.75, 22.25, 31.75, 41.25 ft, S = 9.50 ft):**
  - P = 0.500 klf at x = 1.00 ft (a = 2.25 ft): before G1 0.500, G2 0; after G1 = 0.500(1 + 2.25/9.50) = **0.618**, G2 = −0.500(2.25/9.50) = **−0.118** (Σ = 0.500).
  - P = 0.200 klf at x = 43.50 ft (a = 2.25 ft): before G5 0.200, G4 0; after G5 **0.247**, G4 **−0.047**.
  - P = 0.050 klf at x = 2.00 ft (a = 1.25 ft): G1 0.050 → **0.057**, G2 0 → **−0.007**.
  - Loads between girders and loads exactly on a girder: unchanged.
  - With all three in the sidewalk test project: DC2 G1 1.465 → 1.590, G2 0.703 → 0.578, G4 0.698 → 0.651, G5 1.105 → 1.153 klf; the gd-dfx dead loads to Preliminary sizing (ext DC2 1.465 → 1.590, int 0.703 → 0.651) and the Structural analysis DC2 moments change accordingly.
- **Affected projects:** only those with a load whose rule is "Two adjacent beams" and whose x is outside an exterior girder: an added line load row with that rule, or (XS5) an automatic load overridden to it. The defaults never use "Two adjacent". Changes: the per-girder DC1/DC2/DW/PL of the two girders, the gd-dfx dead loads (when "Use these factors" is Yes, the sizing DC2/DW demands), Structural analysis dead-load effects.
- **Other copies:** `lldf.html` `distribute` arrow `two` (F6; the source, unchanged).

## 2026-10-13 — PR: claude/girderdetail-xs3 (cross-section and dead loads, PR3 of 4: the LLDF and DLs module owns the deck edges; engineer's decisions 2026-10-13; PR link added after merge)

Main page (LLDF and DLs module `GM.df`) and the embedded Preliminary sizing (PlateLine, `PL_B64`, decoded, edited, re-encoded on its one line). Engineer's decision: "this should replace the current barrier input" — the deck edges are now entered in LLDF and DLs → Cross-section and dead loads; Preliminary sizing's Bridge-tab deck-edge fields and its Suggest-tab barrier weight are read-only and written from GirderDetail. `lldf.html` is unchanged. No `bridgeSuite.v1.*` key or payload, no storage key, and no existing saved field is renamed or removed. **Migrated projects give bit-identical results** (checked below); XS9 changes Preliminary sizing's own roadway and d<sub>e</sub> only where GirderDetail's live-load traffic face differs from the deck-edge face (§4 callout in XS9).

New optional saved fields (absent in older projects; an older build ignores and keeps them):
- `P.df.edges` = `{ L: {...}, R: {...} }` (GirderDetail project data and autosave), per side: `type` (`'barrier'` | `'curb'`), `bw` (barrier width at the deck, ft), `bwt` (barrier weight, klf), `cw`, `ch` (curb width and height, in), `rw` (railing weight, klf), `rp` (railing load point from the edge, ft), `rf` (railing traffic face from the edge, ft; blank = `rp`), `face` (optional edge to traffic face, ft; governs when entered).
- `P.bridge.xs` (Preliminary sizing saved data): the record GirderDetail sends (per side the fields above plus `f`, the traffic face at the deck edge, and `r`, the live-load traffic face after the sidewalk rule; and `wcA`). It is echoed as an optional `xs` key in the `gd-bridge` message (so `P.df.bridge` carries it).

  - curb and railing, curb height h < 12 in (mountable, engineer's rule 2026-10-13): f = railing traffic face (blank: the railing load point);
  - curb h ≥ 12 in: f = max(curb width/12, railing traffic face) (the curb face unless the railing stands farther in).
  Then XS6 applies unchanged: r = max(f, sidewalk width if t ≥ 12 in, railing or fence on the sidewalk). r feeds the roadway, N<sub>L</sub>, d<sub>e</sub>, the lever rule and the rigid method as before.
- **Loads:** barrier: DC2 `bwt` at `bw`/2 from its edge (each side its own width and weight; before: one width and one weight from Preliminary sizing for both sides). Curb and railing: as before (curb (cw/12)(ch/12)γ<sub>c</sub> at cw/24, railing `rw` at `rp`).
- **Migration (CLAUDE.md §5):** `P.df.edges` is absent in every project saved before this PR. On the first complete bridge received from Preliminary sizing (`gd-bridge`, `ok`), and only when `P.df.edges` is absent, `dfEdgesInit` fills it once from what Preliminary sizing holds: a GirderDetail record it already carries (`bridge.xs`) if any; else curb mode: per side `cw`, `ch`, `rw`, `rp` from `bridge.edge`, and its traffic faces `faceL`/`faceR` (= `bridge.edge.fL`/`fR`) as the entered "edge to traffic face"; else barrier mode: `bw` = `bridge.barrier`, `bwt` = `suggest.bar` on both sides (face left blank: the derived face is the barrier width, the face Preliminary sizing used). It is never re-run once `P.df.edges` exists, so the user's edges are never overwritten. While `P.df.edges` is absent (a project opened before Preliminary sizing has loaded), every result is computed from the bridge Preliminary sizing sent, exactly as before. The migrated values reproduce Preliminary sizing's loads and faces, so every result is unchanged (checked, below).
- **§4 callout (curb and railing with no entered face):** before, the curb-mode traffic face was always the value entered in Preliminary sizing; now, when "edge to traffic face" is blank, it is derived by the 12 in rule. Migrated curb projects keep their entered faces, so nothing changes for them until the user clears the field.
  - **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.6.1.1.1 (roadway between curbs and/or barriers), 3.6.1.3.1 (wheel 2.0 ft from the face of the curb or railing), 4.6.2.2.1 (d<sub>e</sub> to the inside face of the curb or barrier); the 12 in mountable limit is the engineer's rule (owner practice), not an AASHTO number.
  - **Check case (curb test project: built-in bridge, 5 girders at 9.50 ft, overhangs 3.25 ft, W<sub>deck</sub> = 44.50 ft; left curb 12 × 10 in, railing 0.050 klf at 0.50 ft; right curb 10 × 8 in, railing 0.030 klf at 1.25 ft; faces entered in Preliminary sizing 1.00 / 1.50 ft):**
    - Migrated (faces entered 1.00 / 1.50): identical to before: roadway 44.50 − 2.50 = 42.00 ft, N<sub>L</sub> 3, d<sub>e</sub> 2.25 / 1.75 ft, g<sub>M,ext</sub> G1 0.853 (lever), G5 0.811 (rigid).
    - Faces cleared (both curbs < 12 in, mountable → railing face = load point): f = 0.50 / 1.25 ft; roadway 44.50 − 1.75 = 42.75 ft, N<sub>L</sub> 3; d<sub>e</sub> 2.75 / 2.00 ft; G1 lever 1.2 × ½ × [(9.50 + 2.75 − 2) + (9.50 + 2.75 − 8)]/9.50 = 0.6 × 14.50/9.50 = **0.916** (was 0.853); G5 lever 0.6 × (9.50 + 2.00 − 2 + 9.50 + 2.00 − 8)/9.50 = 0.6 × 13.00/9.50 = **0.821** (was 0.811 rigid); g<sub>V,ext</sub> 0.894 → 0.960 and 0.850 → 0.861. Screen values identical.
    - Left curb raised to 12 in (not mountable): f<sub>L</sub> = 12/12 = 1.00 ft (curb face); G1 back to 0.853. Right railing traffic face entered 0.90 ft: f<sub>R</sub> = 0.90, d<sub>e,R</sub> = 2.35 ft, G5 0.853. Dead loads change only with the curb size (left curb 12 × 12 in: 1.00 × 1.00 × 0.150 = 0.150 klf, was 0.125).
- **Other copies:** none (`lldf.html` `edgeInputs`/`faceOffset` were the reference; unchanged).

### XS9. GirderDetail sends the deck edges to Preliminary sizing (`gd-xs`); its deck-edge fields are read-only; its roadway, d<sub>e</sub> and barrier DC2 use GirderDetail's traffic faces and per-side weights   [§4: Preliminary sizing roadway, d<sub>e</sub>, built-in approximate factors, deflection factor, where GirderDetail's live-load face differs from the deck-edge face] [migrated projects identical]
- **Where (anchors), main page:** new `function dfXsMsg(p)` and `function dfXsPost()` (before `function dfFeed(R)`); `dfFeed` (first line `dfXsPost();`); the `gd-bridge` listener (anchors `const ae = document.activeElement, keep = !init`, `dfXsPost(); autosave();`, `const nx = o => JSON.stringify({ ...o, ts: 0, xs: 0 })`); new `pl-goto` listener (anchor `e.data.type !== 'pl-goto'`); `gdScheduleRefresh` (anchor `ae.closest('#ipane-df_dl')`); Manual part "Scope and the bridge definition"; Sidewalks note.
- **Where (anchors), decoded PlateLine:** `brGeom` (anchor `X = b.xs && b.xs.L && b.xs.R ? b.xs : null`); `bridgeDef` (anchor `...(B.xs ? { xs: B.xs } : {})`); message listener (anchor `e.data.type === 'gd-xs'`); new `function xsLegacy(B, SG, X)`, `const XS_RO`, `function syncEdgeRO()` and the `[data-goxs]` click listener; `fillInputs` (`syncSpacingVis(); syncEdgeRO();`); Bridge tab `<p ... id="br-edge-ro">`; Suggest tab `<p ... id="sg-bar-ro">`; CSS `input[data-k]:disabled, select[data-k]:disabled`, `.hint .link-btn`; Manual "Variable spacing and deck edges".
- **Messages (no `bridgeSuite.v1.*` change):** GirderDetail posts `{ type: 'gd-xs', xs }` to the embedded Preliminary sizing whenever its record (`dfXsMsg`) differs from the echo `P.df.bridge.xs` (as `gd-an` does with `analysis`). Preliminary sizing ignores an identical record; otherwise it stores `P.bridge.xs`, rewrites its own fields (`xsLegacy`), recomputes and posts `gd-bridge` with the `xs` echo. The record depends only on GirderDetail's inputs (not on the bridge), so the exchange ends after one round (checked: no further `gd-bridge`/`gd-xs` in 10 s after each edit). A change of the echo alone does not trigger the "Bridge changed: updating every module" refresh; a change of the faces or the legacy fields does (as an edit in Preliminary sizing did before). While the user types in a cross-section input, the returning `gd-bridge` does not rebuild that pane (focus and typed text kept) and the refresh waits until the field is left. The "Set in LLDF and DLs → Cross-section and dead loads" button in Preliminary sizing posts `pl-goto`; GirderDetail opens LLDF and DLs on the Cross-section and dead loads tab at Deck edges.
- **Preliminary sizing fields written (`xsLegacy`; an equal stored value is kept, so a migrated project's fields and `sgGeoSig` are unchanged):** both sides barriers: `edge.mode` 'barrier', `bridge.barrier` = (f<sub>L</sub> + f<sub>R</sub>)/2, `suggest.bar` = (w<sub>L</sub> + w<sub>R</sub>)/2; any curb side: `edge.mode` 'curb' and per side `cw`, `ch`, `rp`, `rw`, and `f` = the deck-edge face; a barrier side next to a curb side is stored as a zero-size curb with a railing of the barrier weight at its centroid (bw/2). An older build reading the project therefore finds valid values with the same loads and deck-edge faces (checked below). These fields are disabled (read-only) while `bridge.xs` is present, with a note naming each side and a link back.
- **Before (`brGeom`):**
  ```js
  const E = b.edge || { mode: 'barrier' }, curb = E.mode === 'curb', wc = num(b.wc) || 0.150;
  let faceL = num(b.barrier), faceR = num(b.barrier), barW = barW0;
  if (curb) { ...
    faceL = num(E.fL); faceR = num(E.fR);
    const wL = num(E.cwL) / 12 * num(E.chL) / 12 * wc + num(E.rwL), wR = num(E.cwR) / 12 * num(E.chR) / 12 * wc + num(E.rwR); barW = (wL + wR) / 2; }
  ```
- **After:**
  ```js
  const E = b.edge || { mode: 'barrier' }, X = b.xs && b.xs.L && b.xs.R ? b.xs : null, wc = num(b.wc) || 0.150;
  let curb = E.mode === 'curb', faceL = num(b.barrier), faceR = num(b.barrier), barW = barW0;
  if (X) {   // deck edges set in GirderDetail's LLDF and DLs module (XS9)
    const wcx = X.wcA > 0 ? X.wcA : wc, w = q => q.type === 'curb' ? q.cw / 12 * q.ch / 12 * wcx + q.rw : q.bwt, ok = ...;
    if (![X.L.r, X.R.r, w(X.L), w(X.R)].every(ok)) errs.push('The deck edges from the LLDF and DLs module are incomplete: ...');
    curb = X.L.type === 'curb' || X.R.type === 'curb'; faceL = X.L.r; faceR = X.R.r; barW = (w(X.L) + w(X.R)) / 2; }
  else if (curb) { ... unchanged ... }
  ```
  Sizing DC2 per girder stays `2 * BG.barW / nb` = (w<sub>L</sub> + w<sub>R</sub>)/N<sub>b</sub> (identical to 2·w/N<sub>b</sub> when the sides are equal: (w + w)/2 = w exactly in floating point). Sizing still uses the average face (`bar = (faceL + faceR)/2`, roadway = W − 2·bar, d<sub>e</sub> = max overhang − bar), as before.
- **§4 callout — what changes in Preliminary sizing:** its traffic faces were the deck-edge faces (barrier width, or the entered curb traffic faces); they are now GirderDetail's live-load faces r, so they also include a sidewalk 12 in or thicker, a railing or fence on a sidewalk (XS4/XS6), and, when no face is entered, the curb 12 in rule (XS8); and the barrier weight is per side. Outputs that change: roadway, d<sub>e</sub> (its G7 range item), its built-in approximate factors (used when "Use these factors" is No, and for Suggest/Full design trial layouts whose geometry differs from the current one), the live-load deflection factor N<sub>L</sub>m/N<sub>b</sub> (A1), the Spacing study d<sub>e</sub> filter, and the suggested sections. Migrated projects (barrier mode, curb mode with entered faces, sidewalks under 12 in) are unchanged.
  - **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.6.1.1.1 (number of lanes INT(w/12), w between curbs and/or barriers), 4.6.2.2.1 (d<sub>e</sub>), Table 4.6.2.2.2d-1 (lever rule, e = 0.77 + d<sub>e</sub>/9.1), 3.6.1.1.2 (multiple presence), 2.5.2.6.2 (deflection distribution); engineer's 12 in mountable rule; MassDOT 3.5.3 for the per-side barrier loads.
  - **Check case 1 (built-in bridge with 6 ft sidewalks, 12 in thick, both sides; 5 girders at 9.50 ft, overhangs 3.25 ft, W = 44.50 ft; span 1 L = 110 ft, K<sub>g</sub> = 936,395 in⁴, t<sub>s</sub> = 8 in):** before: faces 1.50 / 1.50, bar = 1.50, roadway 44.50 − 3.00 = 41.50 ft (N<sub>L</sub> 3), d<sub>e</sub> = 3.25 − 1.50 = 1.75 ft; after: faces 6.00 / 6.00 (sidewalk curb face), roadway 32.50 ft (N<sub>L</sub> 2), d<sub>e</sub> = −2.75 ft (G7 "d<sub>e</sub>" item pass → warn, outside −1.0 to 5.5). Built-in exterior factor, span 1: lever a<sub>1</sub> = S + d<sub>e</sub> − 2: before 9.25, a<sub>2</sub> = 3.25, g = 1.2 × ½ × 12.50/9.50 = **0.789**; after a<sub>1</sub> = 4.75, a<sub>2</sub> < 0, g = 0.6 × 4.75/9.50 = **0.300**; e-factor before 0.962 × 0.708 = 0.681, after (0.77 − 2.75/9.1) × 0.708 = 0.468 × 0.708 = **0.331**; g<sub>M,ext</sub> 0.789 → **0.331**, g<sub>V,ext</sub> 0.789 → **0.300**; interior unchanged (0.708 / 0.918). Deflection factor 3(0.85)/5 = 0.510 → 2(1.00)/5 = **0.400** (A1 ratios 0.31 → 0.24). Fast suggestion web depth 63 → 61 in. With "Use these factors" Yes the analysis live load still uses GirderDetail's factors (unchanged: GirderDetail already used r = 6.00 ft since XS6).
  - **Check case 2 (sidewalks 6 ft × 8 in / 5 ft × 9 in with fences 0.050 klf at 5.50 ft and 0.030 klf at 4.50 ft, XS4 test project xsA):** faces 1.50 / 1.50 → 5.50 / 4.50 (fences); bar 1.50 → 5.00; roadway 41.50 → 34.50 ft (N<sub>L</sub> 3 → 2); d<sub>e</sub> 1.75 → −1.75 ft; fast suggestion web depth 63 → 60 in.
  - **Check case 3 (per-side weights, built-in bridge):** left barrier 0.500 klf, right 0.300 klf: DC2 = (0.500 + 0.300)/5 = 0.160 klf per girder (the same as 2 × 0.400/5); `suggest.bar` written 0.400. Right barrier 2.00 ft wide: faces 1.50 / 2.00, bar 1.75 (written to `bridge.barrier`), roadway 41.00 ft, d<sub>e</sub> 1.50 ft. Right side changed to curb 12 × 10 in with railing 0.050 klf at 0.50 ft (mountable: face 0.50 ft): w<sub>R</sub> = (12/12)(10/12)(0.150) + 0.050 = 0.175 klf; DC2 = (0.500 + 0.175)/5 = **0.135** klf; faces 1.50 / 0.50, roadway 42.50 ft; legacy fields: mode curb, left cw = ch = 0, rp = 0.75, rw = 0.500, f = 1.50.
- **Found here, fixed in XS10:** Preliminary sizing's built-in exterior factor (`sgDF`) had no rigid cross-section check and did not limit d<sub>e</sub> to −1.0 ft in the e-factor (GirderDetail does both); with the larger live-load face of check case 1 its exterior factor dropped to 0.331 while GirderDetail gives 0.621. The values in check case 1 are those of this commit (XS9); XS10 raises the built-in exterior factor to 0.621.
- **Other copies:** none.

-<h3>Scope and the bridge definition</h3><p>Live load distribution factors for every girder of a steel I-girder bridge with a composite concrete deck (AASHTO LRFD 4.6.2.2, cross-section type (a)), and the distribution of the deck and superimposed dead loads to the girders (MassDOT Bridge Manual 3.5.3). The module works only from a <b>complete bridge</b>: it takes the spans, continuity, skews, girder count and spacing, overhangs, barrier width, deck, concrete, barrier weight, future wearing surface, and the girder plates in every region from the Preliminary sizing module, which publishes them each time it recalculates without input errors. Until then, or whenever the sizing has errors or an incomplete bridge, the module is locked and says why. It updates automatically when the sizing changes; the bridge is edited only in Preliminary sizing. The engine is a port of the standalone LL &amp; DL Distribution calculator (validated there against the FHWA steel girder example) and reproduces its factors exactly.</p>

The <b>deck edges</b> (barrier, or curb and railing, each side) are set in this module (Cross-section and dead loads tab); the first bridge received fills them from the values Preliminary sizing held, and from then on its deck-edge fields are read-only and follow this module. Until then, or whenever the sizing has errors or an incomplete bridge, the module is locked and says why. It updates automatically when the sizing changes; the rest of the bridge is edited only in Preliminary sizing. The engine is a port of the standalone LL &amp; DL Distribution calculator (validated there against the FHWA steel girder example) and reproduces its factors exactly.</p>
 <h3>Design regions (Table C4.6.2.2.1-2)</h3><p>Every span is a region for positive moment and shear, with L equal to the span; every interior support of a continuous girder is a region for negative moment and the interior reaction, with L the average of the adjacent spans. Each region uses K<sub>g</sub> = n(I + Ae<sub>g</sub>²) from the girder section at that location (the maximum positive moment section of the span, or the section at the support), with e<sub>g</sub> = (d − ȳ) + t<sub>h</sub> + t<sub>s</sub>/2 and n = E<sub>s</sub>/E<sub>c</sub>.</p>
 <h3>Interior girders</h3><div class="eq-math">\\[g_{M1} = 0.06 + \\left(\\tfrac{S}{14}\\right)^{0.4}\\left(\\tfrac{S}{L}\\right)^{0.3}\\left(\\tfrac{K_g}{12Lt_s^3}\\right)^{0.1},\\ g_{M2} = 0.075 + \\left(\\tfrac{S}{9.5}\\right)^{0.6}\\left(\\tfrac{S}{L}\\right)^{0.2}\\left(\\tfrac{K_g}{12Lt_s^3}\\right)^{0.1},\\ g_{V1} = 0.36 + \\tfrac{S}{25},\\ g_{V2} = 0.2 + \\tfrac{S}{12} - \\left(\\tfrac{S}{35}\\right)^2\\]</div><p>With N<sub>b</sub> = 3 the moment is the lesser of the equation and the lever rule and the shear is by the lever rule; with S &gt; 16 ft the lever rule is used.</p>
 <h3>Exterior girders</h3><p>One lane: the lever rule (multiple presence 1.2). Two or more lanes: the larger of the e-factor (e<sub>M</sub> = 0.77 + d<sub>e</sub>/9.1, e<sub>V</sub> = 0.60 + d<sub>e</sub>/10, d<sub>e</sub> ≥ −1.0 ft) times the interior factor, and the rigid cross-section method R = N<sub>L</sub>/N<sub>b</sub> + X<sub>ext</sub>Σe/Σx² with multiple presence. The lever rule slides a train of trucks (6 ft wheel lines, adjacent trucks at the input gap, at least 4 ft) across the roadway with the wheels at least 2 ft from the barrier faces, for every truck count whose design lanes fit. A roadway 20 to 24 ft wide has two lanes of half the width (3.6.1.1.1).</p>

 <p><b>Quick suggestion and full design.</b> Suggest has two modes. The <b>quick suggestion</b> updates as you edit. It picks the web depth and web type with the lowest estimated cost from a fast sizing (one constant-stiffness beam model, flange areas from lever-arm estimates, this tool's layout checks), then checks that girder with the same staged analysis and AASHTO checks as Full design (listed below) for the interior and exterior girders, including the Table 2.5.2.6.3-1 minimum depths when span-to-depth applies to Suggest. Where a ratio exceeds 1.0 it increases the flange plates there (required area = current area &times; ratio/0.97 &times; 1.01, at most 1.35 times per round, never less than the plate already there) and thickens the web by one increment if the web ratio exceeds 1.0, then checks again, up to 8 rounds. Plates are only increased, never trimmed, so the quick suggestion passes the strength and service checks (the card says so, or names the ratio that still exceeds 1.0) but is not necessarily the lightest girder. The check runs in the background after the fast result appears (the card shows &ldquo;checking&rdquo; with a progress bar; typically a second or less after the fast result); a new edit restarts it, and Apply pressed during the check applies the checked result, after confirmation, when it is ready. The girder-count study and the Alternatives study use the fast sizing only, without this check, to rank layouts. <b>Run full design</b> optimizes for the least steel: it takes the best fast candidates and, for each, repeats: the staged, cracked analysis of the current layout (the Structural analysis settings); the AASHTO checks at every node for the interior and exterior girders, on both sides of every plate boundary (Strength I positive flexure with the plastic moment, compactness, D<sub>p</sub>/D<sub>t</sub>, and 1.3M<sub>y</sub>; Strength I negative flexure by 6.10.8 with flange local buckling, lateral-torsional buckling at the cross-frame spacing with C<sub>b</sub> from the quarter-point moments of each unbraced segment (10th Edition 6.10.8.2.3b: C<sub>b</sub> = 12.5M<sub>max</sub>/(2.5M<sub>max</sub> + 3M<sub>A</sub> + 4M<sub>B</sub> + 3M<sub>C</sub>), with M<sub>max</sub> the largest moment compressing the flange and M<sub>A</sub>, M<sub>B</sub>, M<sub>C</sub> the absolute envelope values at the quarter points (largest compression, or smallest tension where the flange is never in compression), as defined in Appendix D6.6; brace points at the supports and at the cross-frame spacing), and R<sub>b</sub>; where the compression flange changes within the unbraced length, lateral-torsional buckling uses the smallest compression flange in it (conservative; the γ<sub>e</sub> methods of Appendix D6.6 are not implemented); deck-placement lateral-torsional buckling also uses C<sub>b</sub> from the deck-placement moments; Service II flange stresses and web bend-buckling; deck-placement constructibility; flange fatigue, Fatigue I, Category B at the flange-to-web welds (extreme fiber) and Category C′ at the connection plates welded to the flanges at every cross-frame (inner flange face, 6.6.1.3.1), unless turned off or limited to Category B; and optionally L/800 deflection); and resizing, with each flange's required area set from the check ratio so plates are thickened where a check exceeds 1.0 and trimmed where there is spare capacity. When the layout stops changing it is verified against its own recomputed demands, and the cheapest passing candidate is selected. The result lists the governing check and ratio for every plate. Applying it replaces the girder layout (and the stiffener setting); Revert restores the previous design.</p>
 <p><b>Current girder compared with the suggestion.</b> Below the quick suggestion (or full design) card, the Suggest tab compares the current girder (the Girder tab plates and splices, with the Framing tab stiffeners and cross-frame spacing) with the suggestion, so you can see what the suggestion changes. The overall rows give the web depth and thickness, transverse stiffeners and d<sub>o</sub>/D, cross-frame spacing, field splices, shop transitions, steel per girder and per deck area, cost (Unit costs), the largest strength and service ratio, and the code proportion check counts, with each changed row highlighted. The top flange, web, and bottom flange are then compared plate by plate: the two plate lists are merged by station, so each row is a station range with the current and the suggested plate and what changes (for example &ldquo;t 1 1/8 &rarr; 1 1/4&rdquo;, &ldquo;b 16 &rarr; 15&rdquo;, &ldquo;new transition at 28 ft&rdquo;). A plot shows the flange thickness and width along the girder for both. The current girder is checked in the background with the same staged analysis and strength and service checks as the quick suggestion, at its own cross-frame spacing (an edit restarts the check); the card says whether a change is needed (the current girder exceeds 1.0, is shallower than the Table 2.5.2.6.3-1 minimum depth where that applies, or fails a code proportion check) or would only save steel and cost, and &ldquo;No change suggested&rdquo; when the suggestion is the same as the current girder. If the current girder has input errors, the card lists them instead. The comparison changes nothing until you press Apply.</p>
 <h3>Analysis model</h3><p>The analysis of the current design uses a variable-stiffness, staged line-girder model: DC1 on the steel section, DC2 and DW on the long-term composite section, and live load on the short-term composite section, with the composite stages cracked near interior supports. Its settings (staged or constant EI, cracked zones, deck reinforcement) are made in GirderDetail's Structural analysis module. Suggest mode searches trial layouts with the faster constant-EI model and then designs the chosen layout with the staged model.</p>

The framing plan, cross-section, deck width, and GirderDetail's LLDF and DLs module use each bay; the sizing checks and the built-in approximate distribution factors use the average spacing, and the spacing and overhang checks are made bay by bay. <b>Deck edges</b> can be a barrier (width and the Suggest barrier weight) or a <i>curb and railing</i> on each side: curb width and height, railing load point and weight, and the distance from the deck edge to the traffic face, which sets the roadway. When GirderDetail's LLDF and DLs module is in use, its factors and MassDOT dead loads replace the built-in ones (see the Analysis tab).</p>

The copy survives a reload and is replaced the next time you apply a suggestion or alternative. <b>Keep and dismiss</b> discards it.</p>

### XS10. Preliminary sizing's built-in exterior-girder factors follow the LLDF and DLs rules: d<sub>e</sub> limited to −1.0 ft in the e-factor, lever rule, rigid cross-section method, S > 16 ft and N<sub>b</sub> = 3 rules   [§4: built-in approximate live load distribution factors, exterior girders] [more conservative; changes Suggest, Full design and the width study]
- **Decision:** coordinator, 2026-10-13 (engineer offline): "don't ship an unconservative built-in factor"; make `sgDF`'s exterior factors follow GirderDetail's LLDF module (copied, not shared: CLAUDE.md §3). This resolves the XS9 open item.
- **Where (anchors), decoded PlateLine:** new `const SG_MPF`, `function sgLeverC`, `function sgLever(G, N)`, `function sgRigid(G)` (copies of GirderDetail `DF_MPF`, `dfLeverC`, `dfLever` for the exterior girder j = 0, `dfRigid`, adapted to equal spacing S, N<sub>b</sub> girders, d<sub>e</sub> the same on both sides, and the roadway w); `sgDF(S, L, Kg, ts, de, nb, ext, rdwy)` (new 8th argument, the roadway); callers `demand` (anchor `sgDF(S, Ls, KgS[i].Kg, ts, de, nb, ext, rdwy)`) and `wsCase` (anchor `setup.W - 2 * setup.bar`); the exterior-girder derivation block on the Suggest tab (anchor `4.6.2.2.2d rigid cross-section`). Main page: the `pl-goto` listener scrolls Deck edges below the sticky section header (`scrollMarginTop`), display only.
- **Before:**
  ```js
  const a1 = S + de - 2, a2 = a1 - 6, lev = 1.2 * 0.5 * (Math.max(a1, 0) + Math.max(Math.min(a2, S), 0)) / S;   // lever rule, one lane, m = 1.2
  if (!ext) return { mM: Math.max(m1, m2), mV: Math.max(v1, v2), m1, m2, v1, v2, kr };
  const eM = 0.77 + de / 9.1, eV = 0.6 + de / 10;
  return { mM: Math.max(lev, eM * m2), mV: Math.max(lev, eV * v2), m1, m2, v1, v2, kr, lev, eM, eV };
  ```
  g<sub>ext</sub> = max(lever 1 lane, e·g<sub>int,2+</sub>), e = 0.77 + d<sub>e</sub>/9.1 (moment), 0.60 + d<sub>e</sub>/10 (shear), d<sub>e</sub> not limited.
- **After:** (interior factors unchanged)
  ```js
  const w = rdwy != null && isFinite(rdwy) ? rdwy : (nb - 1) * S + 2 * de, twoHalf = w >= 20.0 - 1e-9 && w <= 24.0 + 1e-9, NL = twoHalf ? 2 : Math.max(1, Math.floor(w / 12)), laneW = twoHalf ? w / 2 : 12;
  ... G = { pos, nb, de, rw0: -de, rw1: -de + w, NL, laneW, xc, sumX2 };
  const l1 = sgLever(G, 1), lev = l1 ? l1.df : 0, deE = Math.max(de, -1.0), eM = 0.77 + deE / 9.1, eV = 0.6 + deE / 10;
  let mE = eM * m2, vE = eV * v2;
  if (S > 16.0) { const l2 = sgLever(G, 2); mE = vE = l2 ? l2.df : 0; }
  else if (nb === 3) { const l2 = sgLever(G, 2); mE = Math.min(mE, l2 ? l2.df : mE); vE = l2 ? l2.df : vE; }
  const rig = sgRigid(G);
  return { mM: Math.max(lev, mE, rig.g), mV: Math.max(lev, vE, rig.g), ..., lev, eM, eV, deE, mE, vE, rig: rig.g, rigN: rig.n, NL, w, rule };
  ```
  g<sub>ext,M</sub> = max(g<sub>lever,1</sub>, e<sub>M</sub>·g<sub>int,M,2+</sub>, g<sub>rigid</sub>), g<sub>ext,V</sub> = max(g<sub>lever,1</sub>, e<sub>V</sub>·g<sub>int,V,2+</sub>, g<sub>rigid</sub>), with d<sub>e</sub> ≥ −1.0 ft in e; g<sub>rigid</sub> = max over n = 1…N<sub>L</sub> of m<sub>n</sub>(n/N<sub>b</sub> + X<sub>ext</sub>Σe/Σx²), e<sub>i</sub> = X<sub>ext</sub> + d<sub>e</sub> − (5 + 12(i − 1)) ft; N<sub>L</sub> = INT(w/12) (two lanes of w/2 for 20 ≤ w ≤ 24 ft); S > 16 ft: two or more lanes by the lever rule; N<sub>b</sub> = 3: moment the lesser of the e-factor and the two-lane lever rule, shear the two-lane lever rule. These are exactly GirderDetail's `dfMember` rules for an exterior girder (without its skew factors: Preliminary sizing applies its own skew correction for shear as before, and takes no moment reduction). The one-lane lever rule (truck 2 ft from the traffic face, m = 1.2) gives the same value as before in every normal case (it no longer caps the second wheel at one spacing, which only matters for d<sub>e</sub> > 8 ft). The fatigue factors (lever/1.2 for the exterior girder) are unchanged; the deflection factor (N<sub>L</sub>m/N<sub>b</sub>) is computed elsewhere and was already on the same roadway (XS9). Interior girders keep the equations (GirderDetail's S > 16 ft / N<sub>b</sub> = 3 rules for interior girders are not ported: not requested).
- **Problem:** the built-in exterior factor had no rigid cross-section check and no d<sub>e</sub> limit, so it was below GirderDetail's factor for the same bridge (built-in example 0.789 vs 0.811), and far below it with a live-load face inside a 12 in sidewalk (0.331 vs 0.621). Less conservative; fixed.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 4.6.2.2.2d-1 (exterior girder moment: lever rule one lane, e = 0.77 + d<sub>e</sub>/9.1, range −1.0 ≤ d<sub>e</sub> ≤ 5.5 ft), Table 4.6.2.2.3b-1 (shear: e = 0.60 + d<sub>e</sub>/10), 4.6.2.2.2d and Eq. C4.6.2.2.2d-1 (rigid cross-section, steel beam-slab bridges with diaphragms or cross-frames: the exterior factor is not less than this), 3.6.1.1.1 and 3.6.1.1.2 (lanes, multiple presence), Table 4.6.2.2.2b-1 note (N<sub>b</sub> = 3) and the S > 16 ft lever rule (Tables 4.6.2.2.2b-1, 4.6.2.2.3a-1).
- **Check cases (span 1, L = 110 ft, K<sub>g</sub> = 936,395 in⁴, t<sub>s</sub> = 8 in, S = 9.50 ft, N<sub>b</sub> = 5: X<sub>ext</sub> = 19.00 ft, Σx² = 902.50 ft², g<sub>int,M,2+</sub> = 0.708, g<sub>int,V,2+</sub> = 0.918):**
  - **Built-in example** (d<sub>e</sub> = 1.75 ft, w = 41.50 ft, N<sub>L</sub> = 3): lever 0.789; e-factor M 0.962 × 0.708 = 0.681, V 0.775 × 0.918 = 0.711; rigid: curb = 19.00 + 1.75 = 20.75, e = 15.75, 3.75, −8.25; 1 lane 1.2(0.200 + 19.00 × 15.75/902.50) = 0.638; 2 lanes 1.0(0.400 + 19.00 × 19.50/902.50) = **0.811**; 3 lanes 0.85(0.600 + 19.00 × 11.25/902.50) = 0.711. g<sub>M,ext</sub> 0.789 → **0.811**, g<sub>V,ext</sub> 0.789 → **0.811** (= GirderDetail 0.811 / 0.850 before its skew correction for shear; GirderDetail's shear includes its skew factor).
  - **6 ft × 12 in sidewalks** (d<sub>e</sub> = −2.75 ft, w = 32.50 ft, N<sub>L</sub> = 2): lever 0.300; e-factor with d<sub>e</sub> limited to −1.0: e<sub>M</sub> = 0.77 − 1.0/9.1 = 0.660, 0.660 × 0.708 = 0.467; e<sub>V</sub> = 0.500, 0.459; rigid: curb = 16.25, e = 11.25, −0.75; 2 lanes 1.0(0.400 + 19.00 × 10.50/902.50) = **0.621**. g<sub>M,ext</sub> 0.331 → **0.621**, g<sub>V,ext</sub> 0.300 → **0.621** (GirderDetail: 0.621).
  - **xsA** (fences; d<sub>e</sub> = −1.75 ft, w = 34.50 ft, N<sub>L</sub> = 2): lever 0.363; e-factor (d<sub>e</sub> → −1.0) 0.467 / 0.459; rigid 2 lanes 0.400 + 19.00(12.25 + 0.25)/902.50 = **0.663**; g<sub>M,ext</sub> 0.409 → **0.663**, g<sub>V,ext</sub> 0.390 → **0.663**.
  - **Curb project, faces cleared** (d<sub>e</sub> = 2.375 ft, w = 42.75 ft): lever 0.868 governs (rigid 0.837): unchanged 0.868.
- **Effect on the built-in example (saved with main, migrated):** with "Use these factors" Yes (default) the analysis of the current layout still uses GirderDetail's factors: its checks and demands are unchanged. The built-in factors are used for trial layouts, so these change:
  - Fast suggestion: web depth 63 → **69 in**; flanges: top 1.500 → 1.375 in and 0.875 → 0.750 in in four pieces, bottom widths 16/20 → 15/19 in; estimated cost $1,696,419 → $1,714,870.
  - Full design: top flange 1.125 → 1.250 in (two pieces), bottom 1.125 → 1.250 in (one piece); governing ratio 0.965 → 0.957; cost $1,597,506 → $1,616,264 (+1.2%).
  - Width study (W = 44.50 ft, N = 4 to 12): the exterior factor now rises with the overhang (rigid method), so the "balanced" overhang (exterior g closest to interior g) moves to the minimum overhang, 1.50 ft (d<sub>e</sub> = 0) for every girder count (was 2.75 ft for N = 4, 2.25 ft for N = 5–7, 2.00 ft for N = 8, 1.75 ft for N = 9–10, 1.50 ft for N = 11–12); for N = 5: S 10.00 → 10.38 ft, g<sub>E</sub> 0.690 → 0.776, web 65 → 68 in, 27.37 → 27.91 psf. Every row still passes.
  - Design all (built-in example and the sidewalk project): unchanged (it uses the current layout).
  - With "Use these factors" No, the current layout's exterior factors also rise (0.789 → 0.811 for the built-in example).
- **Other copies:** GirderDetail `DF_MPF`, `dfLeverC`, `dfLever`, `dfRigid`, `dfMember` (main page; the source, unchanged).

## 2026-10-13 — PR: claude/girderdetail-xs4 (cross-section and dead loads, PR4 of 4: downstream consumers of the cross-section; engineer's decisions 2026-10-13; PR link added after merge)

Main page only. The PL_B64 line (Preliminary sizing) is not touched, and `lldf.html` is unchanged. **No calculation change:** no formula, factor, load, or default changed, and every module computes the same results (checked below). The Deck overhang inputs change only when the user presses the new button. No storage key, saved field, or `bridgeSuite.v1.*` payload is added, renamed, or removed. The fill undo is kept in memory and is not saved. The 3D layer state is saved in the existing `P.ui.v3b.lay` object, with one new optional key (`app`, default on). It is written when the 3D view is first opened in a project without a stored 3D state, or when the box is changed; a stored state without it reads as on, and an older build ignores it.

### XS11. Deck overhang: "Fill from cross-section" button (manual, with a confirmation; undo; locks respected)   [new button] [results unchanged until it is pressed]
- **Where (anchors):** `GM.oh.panes`, section "Loads on the brackets" (anchor `id="oh_fill"`): a new button "Fill from cross-section", a hidden "Undo fill from cross-section" button, and a note `#oh-fill-note`. `GM.oh` has a new `after() { ohFillNote(); }`. These are new and come after `GM.oh`: `let OH_FILL_UNDO`, `const OH_FILL_K`, `function ohFillVals()`, `function ohFillNote()`, `function ohFill()`, `function ohFillUndo()`, and a click listener (`oh_fill`, `oh_fill_undo`).
- **Before:** the bracket deck geometry (`oh.wOH` "Deck width carried by brackets", `oh.tOH` "Overhang deck thickness", `oh.wc`) could be entered by hand or imported from Preliminary sizing (`mods.oh.gen` in its export: `wOH = max(ohL, ohR)·12 − topB/2` with topB taken 1 ft from the first support, `tOH = t_s`, `wc`).
- **After:** the button reads the LLDF and DLs cross-section (`GM.df.compute(P.df)`, the bridge from Preliminary sizing with this module's deck edges) and fills:
  - `wOH` = overhang × 12 − b<sub>f,top</sub>/2. The overhang is measured from the exterior girder centerline to the deck edge. The side with the larger overhang is used, or the left side when they are equal. b<sub>f,top</sub> is the narrowest top flange of the girder (`bridge.plates.top`), which gives the widest deck strip outside the flange. This matches the module's own definition, as Preliminary sizing uses it when it sends this module's inputs. Rounded to 0.01 in, as there.
  - `tOH` = deck t<sub>s</sub> (`tsDeck`). The bridge data has no overhang thickening, and the haunch lies over the flange, not over the brackets.
  - `wc` = the deck concrete unit weight.
  - It asks for a confirmation that lists each value, before → after, with its source.
  - A locked input (double-click its label) is kept and listed in the confirmation.
  - It records the fill in the module's Source line, which shows in the input pane and in the report: "Deck geometry filled from the cross-section (left overhang) date: …".
  - "Undo fill from cross-section" restores the previous values and the Source line. It works until the page is reloaded or another project is loaded; nothing is saved for it.
- **Permanent deck-edge loads are not filled.** Engineer's decision: the permanent barrier is not a deck-placement (bracket) load unless it is cast before the forms are stripped. This module also has no input for permanent loads; its "Railing" and "Walkway" are construction items on the bracket. The barrier, or the curb and railing, on the chosen side is therefore only listed, with its weight and position, in the note and in the confirmation.
- **Note (display only):** the pane shows what the cross-section gives and whether the current inputs differ, for example: "Cross-section (LLDF and DLs): Deck width carried by brackets 31.00 in (left overhang 3.25 ft × 12 − 16.00/2 in, the narrowest top flange); … The inputs match. Permanent deck-edge loads on that side, not bracket loads and not filled (no input here): Left barrier 0.400 klf at 0.75 ft from the deck edge."
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.10.3.4 and C6.10.3.4 (deck overhang loads on the brackets during deck placement). The module's formulas are unchanged: the deck load = w<sub>c</sub>(t<sub>OH</sub>/12)(w<sub>OH</sub>/12).
- **Check case:** built-in example with the right overhang changed to 4.50 ft in Preliminary sizing, top flanges 16 in, t<sub>s</sub> = 8 in, w<sub>c</sub> = 0.150 kcf, and the inputs first set by hand to w<sub>OH</sub> = 30 in, t<sub>OH</sub> = 9 in.
  - The button fills w<sub>OH</sub> = 4.50 × 12 − 16/2 = **46.00 in** (right side, the larger overhang), t<sub>OH</sub> = **8.00 in** and w<sub>c</sub> = 0.150.
  - Overhang deck load: before 0.150(9/12)(30/12) = 0.281 kip/ft; after 0.150(8/12)(46/12) = **0.383** kip/ft.
  - w<sub>u</sub>: 0.817 → **0.964** kip/ft. OH1 at the first location: f<sub>ℓ</sub> 18.06 → 20.51 ksi, ratio 0.66 → 0.71 (screen).
  - Undo returns 30 / 9 in and w<sub>u</sub> 0.817.
  - With t<sub>OH</sub> locked, only w<sub>OH</sub> and w<sub>c</sub> are filled, and w<sub>u</sub> = 1.024.
  - Built-in example with equal 3.25 ft overhangs (inputs as imported from Preliminary sizing): 3.25 × 12 − 8 = 31.00 in and 8.00 in, the same as the imported values ("The inputs match").
- **Other copies:** none. (Preliminary sizing's export, `oh.gen` in the PL_B64 line, uses the same definition with the flange 1 ft from the first support; it is unchanged.)

### XS12. DXF typical section and 3D view: barriers, curbs with railings, sidewalks with railings or fences, median, wearing surface and overlays   [drawing only] [results bit-identical]
- **Where (anchors):**
  - New `function dfFoot(R)` (before `dfXsSVG`) holds the element footprints that the Drawings-tab cross-section already used. `dfXsSVG` now reads its sidewalk, median, and barrier or curb footprints from it. This is a pure refactor: the SVG string is identical on all eight test projects (checked).
  - New `const DF_APP_H`, `function dfApp(R)`: the element list for the DXF and the 3D view.
  - New `function dxfApp(D, xL, xR, yTop)` (before `function dxfSplice`).
  - `dxfSection`: anchors `const yA = dxfApp(D, xL, xR, yT + hh + ts), yDk = …`, `D.chainH(ly.d, pts, yDk + 4 * h, …`, `D.text(ly.t, xL, yDk + 11 * h, …`.
  - 3D view: `V3B_LAY` (new `app: true`); the checkbox list (anchor `['app', 'Barriers, curbs, sidewalks']`); `v3bBuild`, block `// barriers, curbs with railings, sidewalks with railings or fences, median (XS12)`; the note text (anchor `nApp ?`).
- **Source:** `GM.df.compute(P.df)`, the same footprints as the Drawings-tab cross-section (XS1).
  - Barriers: the per-side width at the deck, at the deck edge (on the sidewalk when there is one). Curbs: width × height.
  - Railings: at their load point, on the curb when the load point is on it, else on the deck or sidewalk surface. Railings or fences on a sidewalk: at their x.
  - Sidewalks: width × thickness. Median: width × thickness, centered, with the longitudinal joint.
  - Wearing surface and overlays: between the curb faces.
  - Overridden x or line loads are used as in the drawing.
  - The barrier profile and the barrier and railing heights are not inputs. They are drawn schematically (34 in barrier, 42 in railing, as the Drawings-tab cross-section does) and labeled "SHAPE AND HEIGHT SCHEMATIC" or "HEIGHT SCHEMATIC". No dimension is given to a schematic height.
- **DXF (both formats: R12 model space and the AutoCAD 2018 layouts):**
  - New layers following the existing major-minor names, with the user's prefix: `DECK-BARR`, `DECK-CURB`, `DECK-RAIL`, `DECK-SDWK`, `DECK-MEDN`, `DECK-WSRF`. Labels and leaders go on `ANNO-TEXT`; the dimension chain goes on `DIMS`.
  - Wearing surface and overlays: a strip of their thickness when it is known (thickness × unit weight); otherwise a HIDDEN line 1/2 in above the deck, labeled "THICKNESS NOT SET (LINE ONLY)". No hatch entity: the DXF writer has none.
  - One dimension chain gives the element widths and positions across the deck.
  - Labels name each element with its size and its line load and class, for example "LEFT SIDEWALK 6'-0" x 8" (0.580 KLF DC2)" or "FUTURE WEARING SURFACE 2 1/2" x 144 PCF = 30 PSF (1.005 KLF DW)". Overrides are marked ", OVERRIDE".
  - Labels are stacked in rows with leaders: left half leftmost highest, right half mirrored, so that no leader crosses a label.
  - The existing girder-spacing chain, the out-to-out dimension and the title move up above the elements. Nothing else on the sheet changes.
  - When LLDF and DLs has no result, or its deck width differs from the sizing model drawn, nothing is added and the sheet is as before.
- **3D view (whole bridge):**
  - Concrete prisms along the bridge: barriers, curbs, sidewalks, and the median. They follow the skewed deck ends, as the deck does.
  - Railings and fences: two rails, with posts at about 8 ft.
  - A new layer toggle, "Barriers, curbs, sidewalks", on by default. Not shown in the single-girder view.
  - The wearing surface is in the DXF only.
- **Governing provision:** none (drawing only). No formula, load, or input changed.
- **Check case (xsA test project):**
  - Elements: built-in bridge, sidewalks 6 ft × 8 in and 5 ft × 9 in, fences 0.050 klf at 5.50 ft and 0.030 klf at 4.50 ft, median 4 ft × 9 in with a joint, wearing surface 2.5 in × 0.144 kcf, overlays 5 psf and 1.25 in × 0.145 kcf.
  - Typical section, R12, read with ezdxf 1.4.4 (audit: 0 errors): new entities on DECK-BARR 2, DECK-SDWK 2, DECK-MEDN 2, DECK-RAIL 6 lines, DECK-WSRF 3, plus 10 labels, 10 leaders, and 9 dimensions.
  - Element-width chain: 1'-6", 4'-0", 6", 14'-3", 4'-0", 15'-3", 6", 3'-0", 1'-6". These are the barrier, sidewalk to fence, fence to sidewalk edge, and so on. Total 44'-6" = W<sub>deck</sub>.
  - Labels: LEFT SIDEWALK 6'-0" x 8" (0.580 KLF DC2) = 6 × 8/12 × 0.145; RAISED MEDIAN 4'-0" x 9" (0.435 KLF DC2), LONGIT. JOINT; LATEX OVERLAY 1 1/4" x 145 PCF = 15.1 PSF (0.506 KLF DW).
  - The layouts format (the spec run through the page's own `GD_DXF_PY` with ezdxf 1.4.4) gives an AC1032 file with 31 layouts, 0 audit errors, and the same new entities.
  - The rest of the DXF is unchanged: entity counts differ from `origin/main` only on the new layers, ANNO-TEXT, and DIMS.
- **Other copies:** none.

### XS13. LLDF and DLs report, input echo: deck edges and traffic faces, every superimposed element, options and overrides   [report only] [results bit-identical]
- **Where (anchors):**
  - `gmReportHead`, which is shared by every GM module: after `${tb(e.table2)}` it now renders an optional `e.more` list of `[title, table, note]` as `<h3 class="rpt-h3">` plus a table in the report's existing style. Modules that do not return `more` are unchanged.
  - `GM.df.echo`: `more: dfEchoXs(R)`.
  - New `function dfEchoXs(R)` (before `const DF_VIEW`).
- **Content:** three new blocks in the Input echo of the LLDF and DLs report (the existing rows are unchanged):
  1. **"Deck edges and traffic faces"**, one row per side:
     - type (barrier, or curb and railing);
     - dimensions from the deck edge (barrier width at the deck; curb width × height with "(mountable, < 12 in)"; railing load point and traffic face);
     - weights (marked "(override)" when overridden);
     - the traffic face at the deck edge with its rule (barrier face, railing face for a mountable curb, curb face at 12 in or higher, or "edge to traffic face entered");
     - the live-load traffic face with the governing element (`dfLLTxt`, for example "5.50 ft to the railing or fence on the sidewalk; the 8.00 in sidewalk is mountable (< 12 in) and ignored (it would give 6.00 ft)").
     
     A note follows: whether the edges are entered in this module or sent by Preliminary sizing, the 12 in rule, and the roadway.
  2. **"Superimposed loads on the cross-section"**: every load in `R.dead.per` (barriers, curbs, railings, sidewalks, fences, median, wearing surface, overlays, pedestrian load, utilities and other line loads). For each: class, size (for example "6.00 ft × 8.00 in (mountable)" or "2.50 in × 0.144 kcf = 30.00 psf over 33.50 ft"), x, line load, and distribution ("(method)" for a row that follows the method). An overridden value reads "0.450 (override; auto 0.400)".
  3. **"Cross-section options and overrides"**: appurtenance γ<sub>c</sub>, the wearing-surface basis, the load overrides in use, overrides stored for loads that no longer exist (kept, not used), and beam classes set by hand, with their automatic class.
- **Governing provision:** none (report text). Values are read from `GM.df.compute`.
- **Check case (xsA project with test overrides: left barrier x 0.90 ft and 0.450 klf, right sidewalk "two adjacent", wearing surface pile-cap, a stored override for a missing id `zzz`, G1 and G3 classes):** the report lists:
  - Left barrier "0.90 (override; auto 0.75)" and "0.450 (override; auto 0.400)";
  - Right sidewalk slab "Two adjacent (override; auto MassDOT pile-cap)";
  - "Overrides stored but not used: zzz";
  - G1 "Exterior safety curb beam (auto: Exterior sidewalk beam)";
  - live-load faces 5.50 / 4.50 ft (fences) and roadway 34.50 ft, as on the input tab.
  
  For the curb project: curbs 12 × 10 in and 10 × 8 in, both mountable; faces 1.00 / 1.50 ft entered; roadway 42.00 ft.
- **Other copies:** none.
