Main page and the embedded Preliminary sizing (PlateLine, `PL_B64`, decoded, edited and re-encoded on its one line). No storage key, saved field or `bridgeSuite.v1.*` payload is added, renamed or removed. `lldf.html` is unchanged.

### C1. Design all counts the end (bearing-line) cross-frames in the cross-frame case   [quantities and cost only; no check changes] [resolves CF-D9 open item 2]
- **Where:** `designAllRun0`, the cross-frame branch of step 5 (anchor `else if (cfE) { const R = cfE.R, nF = Math.max(0, (q.frames || 0) - (q.framesSup || 0))`); two new rows after "Cross-frames: bolts" (anchor `// end (bearing-line) cross-frames (C1, 2026-10-13)`). Manual, part "Design all": "cross-frame members and bolts" → "cross-frame members and bolts, intermediate and end (bearing-line) frames".
- **What the module assumes for the end frames:** the Cross-frames module has **no separate end-frame members**; it designs one intermediate frame (top chord, bottom chord, diagonal angles; `cf.mem.top`, `cf.mem.bot`, `cf.mem.diag`; bolts `cf.conn.n` per member end). The DXF end detail (`dxfCF`, title "END CROSS-FRAME AT BEARINGS (ALONG θ DEG. SKEW)", note "MEMBERS PER THE CROSS-FRAME DESIGN") and the 3D view draw every end frame as an **X-frame** along the bearing line (top chord, bottom chord, two diagonals, also when the intermediate frames are K-frames), of length S/cos θ with θ the largest skew. Design all now counts them the same way:
  - n = `qty.framesSup` (the bearing-line frames Preliminary sizing counts, the same n the end diaphragms use);
  - S<sub>e</sub> = S/cos θ<sub>max</sub> (S = `cf.S`, θ<sub>max</sub> = largest |skew| of `P.df.bridge.skews`, 0 if none), work-point lengths as for the intermediate frames: top and bottom chord S<sub>e</sub>, two diagonals √(S<sub>e</sub>² + h²) (h = `cf.h`);
  - steel per frame = [S<sub>e</sub>(A<sub>top</sub> + A<sub>bot</sub>) + 2√(S<sub>e</sub>² + h²)A<sub>diag</sub>] × 0.2836 lb/in³, at `cDet`; bolts per frame = 4 members × 2 ends × `cf.conn.n`, at `cBolt`.
  - Rows: "End cross-frames at the bearing lines (n, X-type, S<sub>e</sub> ft [along θ° skew]): members" and "End cross-frames: bolts". They also appear in the DXF "ESTIMATED QUANTITIES" table, which lists the Design all rows.

- **Decision:** clean-up of the open item left by XS10 ("GirderDetail's S > 16 ft / N<sub>b</sub> = 3 rules for interior girders are not ported"); coordinator, 2026-10-13 (engineer offline: "continue to clean up the app and use judgement"). Copied from GirderDetail `dfMember` (interior branch), not shared (CLAUDE.md §3).
- **Where (anchors), decoded PlateLine:** the comment above `const SG_MPF` (interior rules added); `function sgLever(G, N, j = 0)` (new third argument, the girder; the exterior calls keep j = 0), anchor `R += 0.5 * sgLeverC(pos, Nb, j, s + o)`; `function sgDF(S, L, Kg, ts, de, nb, ext, rdwy)`: the geometry block becomes a local `geo()` (anchor `const geo = () =>`) used by the new interior branch (anchor `// interior girders (C2): GirderDetail dfMember`) and by the exterior branch (`const { w, NL, G } = geo();`, the same arithmetic as before); `renderSuggest`, the "Interior girder, moment" derivation block (anchor `d.rule === 'S16' ? \`S &> 16`) and its reference (anchor `'; S > 16 ft: lever rule'`); Manual, distribution factors paragraph (anchor `for S &gt; 16 ft the lever rule, and for N<sub>b</sub> = 3`). Main page: only the re-encoded `PL_B64` line.
- **Before (interior):**
  ```js
    if (!ext) return { mM: Math.max(m1, m2), mV: Math.max(v1, v2), m1, m2, v1, v2, kr };
  ```
  g<sub>M,int</sub> = max(g<sub>1</sub>, g<sub>2+</sub>) by the equations of Table 4.6.2.2.2b-1, g<sub>V,int</sub> = max(0.36 + S/25, 0.2 + S/12 − (S/35)²) (Table 4.6.2.2.3a-1), for every S and N<sub>b</sub>.
- **After (interior):**
  ```js
    if (!ext) {
      if (!(nb >= 3 && (S > 16.0 || nb === 3))) return { mM: Math.max(m1, m2), mV: Math.max(v1, v2), m1, m2, v1, v2, kr };
      const { G } = geo(), lv = N => { let b = null; for (let j = 1; j < nb - 1; j++) { const l = sgLever(G, N, j); if (l && (b == null || l.df > b)) b = l.df; } return b; }, l1 = lv(1), l2 = lv(2);
      let iM1 = m1, iM2 = m2, iV1 = v1, iV2 = v2, rule;

      else { iM1 = Math.min(m1, l1 != null ? l1 : m1); iM2 = Math.min(m2, l2 != null ? l2 : m2); iV1 = l1 != null ? l1 : v1; iV2 = l2 != null ? l2 : v2; rule = 'N3'; }
      return { mM: Math.max(iM1, iM2), mV: Math.max(iV1, iV2), m1: iM1, m2: iM2, v1: iV1, v2: iV2, kr, rule, eq: { m1, m2, v1, v2 }, l1, l2 };
    }

  - S > 16 ft: one lane g<sub>1</sub> = lever rule (one truck, m = 1.2), two or more lanes g<sub>2+</sub> = lever rule (two trucks with a 4 ft gap, m = 1.0), for moment and shear;
  - N<sub>b</sub> = 3 (S ≤ 16 ft): moment g<sub>1</sub> = min(equation, lever 1 lane), g<sub>2+</sub> = min(equation, lever 2 lanes); shear g<sub>1</sub>, g<sub>2+</sub> = lever rule;
  - the lever rule is taken for each interior girder (trucks 2 ft from the traffic faces, stepped 0.25 ft, as GirderDetail's `dfLever`) and the largest is used, because GirderDetail sends the largest factor over its interior girders (`dfPayload`); N<sub>L</sub> and the lane width as in XS10 (w/2 lanes for 20 ≤ w ≤ 24 ft); a lever case that does not fit the roadway counts as 0 (S > 16 ft) or is not used (N<sub>b</sub> = 3), as in `dfMember`;
  - the fatigue factors follow: `m1`, `v1` now carry the rule's one-lane values (Preliminary sizing's interior fatigue factor is m1/1.2 and v1/1.2, as GirderDetail's fatM, fatV = r.mom1/1.2, r.shr1/1.2);
  - every other case (N<sub>b</sub> ≥ 4 with S ≤ 16 ft, and N<sub>b</sub> = 2) returns the same object as before, so those results are bit-identical; the exterior branch is unchanged (same arithmetic, the geometry moved into `geo()`).

 <p>DC1 (noncomposite): steel self-weight from the current plates increased by the detail allowance, deck slab over the tributary width (S for the interior girder, S/2 + overhang for the exterior girder), haunch, and SIP forms. DC2: two barriers shared equally by all girders. DW: wearing surface over the roadway, shared equally. Deck placement: 1.25 DC1 + 1.50 construction live load over the tributary width.</p>
 <p>Live load is HL-93 (3.6.1.2, 3.6.1.3): the design truck with rear axle spacing 14, 18, 22, 26, and 30 ft, both directions, or the design tandem, plus the 0.64 klf lane on the parts of the influence line that increase the effect. IM = 33% is applied to the truck and tandem. In negative moment regions (between permanent-load contraflexure points around each pier), 90% of two trucks with 14 ft rear spacing, at least 50 ft apart, plus 90% of the lane is also considered.</p>
 <h3>Distribution factors</h3>

The exterior girder uses the lever rule (one lane, multiple presence 1.2) and e × interior (two or more lanes), per Tables 4.6.2.2.2d-1 and 4.6.2.2.3b-1. Negative moment regions use the average length and K<sub>g</sub> of the adjacent spans. The skew correction for shear (Table 4.6.2.2.3c-1) is applied along the whole span; the skew reduction for moment is not taken.</p>

### C3. Preliminary sizing's cross-section drawing shows GirderDetail's deck edges and appurtenances   [display only] [results bit-identical] [optional fields in the `gd-xs` record]
- **Where (anchors), main page:** `dfXsMsg(p)` (anchor `const ll = dfLLFace({}, p.dl, xs, Ed.L.f, Ed.R.f), side = sd => { const q = Ed[sd], fx = xs['fenceX' + sd];`) and its header comment (anchor `Optional drawing fields (C3`).
- **Where (anchors), decoded PlateLine:** `xsSVG(m)` (anchors `const XS = P.bridge && P.bridge.xs && P.bridge.xs.L && P.bridge.xs.R ? P.bridge.xs : null, xa = XS ? xsApp(XS, m.width) : null;`, `if (XS) o += xsAppSVG(xa, X, k, yTop, m.ts);`, and the caption `cap: XS ? \`To scale.`); new `function xsApp(XS, Wd)` and `function xsAppSVG(xa, X, k, yTop, ts)` after `xsSVG`.
- **Before:** the Drawings-tab cross-section drew a 42 in rectangle of width `m.barrier` at each deck edge. Since XS9, with deck edges from GirderDetail, `m.barrier` is the average live-load traffic face. So a project with 6 ft sidewalks drew two 5 to 6 ft wide "barriers", and curbs were drawn as barriers.
- **After (only when `bridge.xs`, GirderDetail's record, is present; the same test `brGeom` uses):** each side is drawn as entered in LLDF and DLs → Cross-section and dead loads:
  - barrier: width `bw` at the deck edge, 34 in high (schematic, as GirderDetail's drawing, DXF and 3D);
  - curb: `cw` × `ch` in; its railing (when `rw` > 0) as a post with a top rail at `rp`, 42 in high (schematic), standing on the curb when `rp` is on it, else on the deck or sidewalk surface;
  - sidewalk (optional fields): `sw` ft × `swT` in at the deck edge, with the barrier or curb on it (as GirderDetail's `dfApp`); its railing or fence at `fx`;
  - raised median (optional field `med`): `w` ft × `t` in, centered, with a dashed line for a longitudinal joint;
  - the live-load traffic faces `r` (each side) as dashed red lines labeled "LL face".
  
  The caption lists each side and the faces, for example: "Deck edges and appurtenances as set in GirderDetail (LLDF and DLs → Cross-section and dead loads): left barrier 1.50 ft, sidewalk 6.00 ft × 8.00 in with railing or fence at 5.50 ft; right barrier 1.50 ft, sidewalk 5.00 ft × 9.00 in with railing or fence at 4.50 ft; median 4.00 ft × 9.00 in with longitudinal joint. Barrier (34 in) and railing or fence (42 in) heights are schematic. Dashed red lines: live-load traffic faces, 5.50 ft (left) and 4.50 ft (right) from the deck edges." The drawing area grows to fit the tallest element. Without `bridge.xs` the SVG and caption are the same string as before (checked).
- **Record (`gd-xs`, stored by Preliminary sizing as `bridge.xs` and echoed in `gd-bridge`):** new **optional** fields, written only when the project has the element, so a record without sidewalks, fences or a median is unchanged (byte for byte) and nothing is re-sent for it:
  - per side `sw` (sidewalk width, ft) and `swT` (thickness, in), when the sidewalk width is > 0; `fx` (sidewalk railing or fence, ft from the deck edge), when one is entered;
  - `med` = `{ w, t, joint }` (ft, in, boolean), when the median width is > 0.
  They are the module's inputs (`P.df.dl.swL`, `swThkL`, `swR`, `swThkR`, the validated `fenceXL`/`fenceXR`, `medW`, `medThk`, `medJoint`), not results, so the record still depends only on GirderDetail's inputs and the exchange ends after one round (checked). Preliminary sizing reads them only in the drawing; `brGeom`, `xsLegacy` and every calculation ignore them, and its own saved fields (`bridge.barrier`, `bridge.edge`, `suggest.bar`) are unchanged.
- **Problem:** the drawing did not show the deck edges GirderDetail sends; with sidewalks it showed wide "barriers" that do not exist. Display only.
- **Governing provision:** none (drawing only). No formula, load or input changed.
- **Check case:** xsA test project (sidewalks 6 ft × 8 in and 5 ft × 9 in with fences at 5.50 and 4.50 ft, 1.50 ft barriers, median 4 ft × 9 in with a joint): record gains `L: { sw: 6, swT: 8, fx: 5.5 }`, `R: { sw: 5, swT: 9, fx: 4.5 }`, `med: { w: 4, t: 9, joint: true }`; the drawing shows both sidewalks with the barriers on them, the fences, the median and joint, and LL faces at 5.50 and 4.50 ft (was: two 5.00 ft wide, 42 in "barriers"). Built-in example: 1.50 ft barriers 34 in high and LL faces at 1.50 ft; record unchanged. Curb project with a left sidewalk: left curb 12 × 10 in on the sidewalk with its railing at 0.50 ft, right curb 10 × 8 in with its railing at 1.25 ft on the deck, LL faces 1.00 / 1.50 ft. Screenshots: `scratchpad/followups/gd-c1/c3_{def,xsA,curbsw}_pl_xs.png` (branch) and `main_{def,xsA}_pl_xs.png` (main).
- **Saved data:** no key renamed or removed; `bridge.xs` (Preliminary sizing) and its echo `P.df.bridge.xs` (GirderDetail) gain the optional fields above in projects that have those elements. An older build ignores them; it re-sends its own record on opening (without them) and Preliminary sizing stores that, with the same results; this build adds them back when the project is opened again.
- **Other copies:** none. (GirderDetail's own drawing, `dfXsSVG`/`dfFoot`, is the reference for what is drawn; unchanged.)

'start' : 'end'}" style="fill:#b42318">LL face</text>`; } });

### C19. Fatigue rows and shop-transition rows from Preliminary sizing carry their girder's deck reinforcement A<sub>r</sub> and its depth d<sub>r</sub>   [§4: section properties of the cracked negative-moment section] [more conservative on the built-in example] [optional fields in the Fatigue and Welds and transitions rows; one field added to an internal request message]
- **Where:**
  - Decoded PlateLine: `detailExport`, new constant before `const types = Object.keys(AN.types)` (anchor `const rbP = AN.rebarPct != null`); the `wt.tr.push` row (anchor `beff: r2(props(sec(t.x), gt).beff), ...reb(sec(t.x), gt) }`); the fatigue `row` helper (anchor `fDL: 0, beff: r2(props(s, gt).beff), ...reb(s, gt) }`); the `pl-export-req` listener, `ANx` (anchor `rebarPct: d.rebar };`). Main page: the re-encoded `PL_B64` line.
  - Main page: new function `rowDk` after `secSet` (anchor `function rowDk(dk, r) {`); `WT_TSPEC` and `FA_SPEC` (two optional fields each, anchor `['Ar', 'Deck rebar A<sub>r</sub> of this girder (blank: the A<sub>r</sub> above)'`); `GM.wt.compute`, transitions (anchor `S = secSet(r.D, s, rowDk(dk, r));`); `GM.fa.compute` (anchor `const S = secSet(r.D, r, rowDk(dk, r)), d = S.s.d`); `GM.fa` calculation card "Detail elevation and sections" and the report tables of both modules (anchor `` `; A_r ${f2(rowDk(R.dk, r).Ar)} in² at ${f2(rowDk(R.dk, r).dr)} in` ``); `faImport`, Welds-and-transitions branch (anchor `Ar: r.Ar != null ? r.Ar : null, dr: r.dr != null ? r.dr : null`); the Structural analysis request to Preliminary sizing (anchor `rebar: nm(R.p.rebar), model:`).
- **What is sent:** for each Fatigue row and each shop-transition row from Preliminary sizing:
  - A<sub>r</sub> = (rebar %)/100 × b<sub>eff</sub> × t<sub>s</sub>, with b<sub>eff</sub> the row's own girder value (the `beff` the row already carries, C5/L6) and t<sub>s</sub> the structural deck thickness of the analysis (`AN.ts`). The rebar % is Preliminary sizing's Analysis input `P.analysis.rebar` (default 1.0 %, read as `num(...) || 1.0`, the same expression its staged analysis uses for the cracked stiffness, `Ar = (num(AM.rebar) || 1.0) / 100 * beffIn * ts`). When the demands come from GirderDetail's Structural analysis (button "from Structural analysis", which sends that module's arrays through Preliminary sizing's export), the % is Structural analysis's own input (`P.sa.rebar`, sent as `sa.rebar` and used as `AN.rebarPct`), the same % its cracked stiffness uses (`Ar = nm(p.rebar) / 100 * beff * ts`).
  - d<sub>r</sub> = t<sub>s</sub>/2: **Preliminary sizing's convention**, the reinforcement at mid-depth of the structural slab (its cracked section places A<sub>r</sub> at `yr = d + hh + ts / 2`, and so does Structural analysis, `saCracked`). The Fatigue and Welds and transitions modules measure d<sub>r</sub> down from the top of the structural slab (`ps.d + dk.hh + dk.ts - dk.dr`), so d<sub>r</sub> = t<sub>s</sub>/2 puts the bar at the same height. For an 8 in slab this equals the modules' own default (4 in).
  - Rows store them as optional numbers `Ar` (in²) and `dr` (in); blank (manual rows, older rows) = the module's A<sub>r</sub> and depth. `rowDk` returns the module's own `dk` object when the row has none of `beff`, `Ar`, `dr`, so manual rows compute exactly as before. The module inputs "Deck rebar A<sub>r</sub>" and "Rebar depth" are unchanged and still apply to manual rows and to rows imported from Girder section.
- **Not sent to Girder section:** its negative section uses two layers (A<sub>rt</sub> at c<sub>rt</sub> below the top, A<sub>rb</sub> at c<sub>rb</sub> above the bottom) for M<sub>p</sub>, the 6.10.1.7 minimum-reinforcement check and the top-layer share; one % at the slab mid-depth cannot be split into the two layers without an assumption the engineer has not made. Left as its own input (open item). Rows the Fatigue module imports from Girder section keep the Fatigue module's A<sub>r</sub>, as before.
- **Problem:** the cracked negative-moment section of every imported Fatigue row and every transition row used the module's own A<sub>r</sub> (9.8 in² Fatigue, 9.3 in² Welds and transitions, both for every girder) instead of the bridge's reinforcement. On the built-in example the bridge's 1 % gives 7.68 in² (exterior, b<sub>eff</sub> 96 in) and 9.12 in² (interior, 114 in): less steel in the cracked section, so higher negative stress ranges. Less conservative before on the built-in example; fixed.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.6.1.2.1 (stress ranges for the negative moment from the section of steel and longitudinal reinforcement unless the deck is effective per the conditions there), 6.10.1.7 (1 % longitudinal reinforcement in the negative-moment regions), 6.6.1.2.2 (γ(Δf) ≤ (ΔF)<sub>n</sub>), Table 6.6.1.2.3-1. Not changed. Not re-checked against the printed 10th Edition here: verify.

### C20. Transverse stiffeners and Fatigue check the same connection plate in each span: the intermediate cross-frame with the largest fatigue moment range   [§4: location of the demand] [Transverse stiffeners rows move; Fatigue rows unchanged on the built-in example] [resolves the C8–C18 open item]
- **Where (decoded PlateLine):** `detailExport`: new helpers `frX0`, `rgF`, `cpAt` before `const shear = (T, x) =>` (anchor `const cpAt = (T, a, b) => {`); the Transverse stiffeners connection-plate row (anchor `const cxF = cpAt(T, x0, x1), cx = cxF != null ? cxF : bx, s = sec(cx);`); the Fatigue span row (anchor `const fx = cpAt(T, a, b); if (fx != null) row(`). Main page: only the re-encoded `PL_B64` line.

- **After:** see the diff below. The **pier region** is the negative permanent-load region around the pier: from the DC + DW contraflexure point in the span on the left to the one in the span on the right, found from this girder's own M<sub>DC1</sub> + M<sub>DC2</sub> + M<sub>DW</sub> at the nodes (walk outward from the pier node while the sum is negative, then interpolate the zero crossing linearly), the same construction as Preliminary sizing's negative-moment regions (`region`, `cf`) in its analysis. Candidates: the intermediate cross-frames of the G1 line (`frX0`, C20) strictly inside the region and more than 0.5 ft from the pier. Selected: the largest max(0, M<sub>f+</sub>) − min(0, M<sub>f−</sub>) at its node (the C4/C20 rule); ties keep the first. When the region has no intermediate cross-frame (or the pier moment is not negative), the old rule (nearest cross-frame) is kept. The row's contents (top flange inner face `tfi`, Category C′, section, moments, n from `nAt`) are built as before at the chosen station.
- **Problem:** the pier connection plate was the cross-frame nearest the pier, but the top-flange weld toe is governed by the stress range, which is largest toward the contraflexure points where both M<sub>f+</sub> and M<sub>f−</sub> are large. On the built-in example (15° skew) the "nearest" frame was also the G1 support frame at 104.91 ft (see the open item on stations below), not a connection plate. Less conservative before; fixed.

### Open items (C19–C23)
- **Cross-frame stations on skewed bridges (raised, not changed; decide):** `detailExport` takes the stations of the cross-frames as their global x on the G1 line (`f.xa` of bay 0) and reads the analysis at those values as if they were girder stations (`node(x)`). On a skewed bridge each girder's bearing is offset (`framingLayout`: `xb(k, i) = m.sup[k] + (ys[i] − yc) tan θ_k`); on the built-in example (15°) G1's bearings are at global −5.09, 104.91, 244.91 and 354.91 ft, so the frame listed at 60.91 ft is 66.0 ft along G1 (0.6L), and the old "nearest" pier row at 104.91 ft was G1's own pier bearing line. Preliminary sizing's own splice-clearance code converts to girder stations (`clearFrames`: `f.xa - FR.girders[f.bay].x0`), and so does its framing conflict check (`x - xb(0, g)`). The same convention is used by the Fatigue and Transverse stiffeners connection-plate rows (C4, C20, C21), the Girder section brace points (L<sub>b</sub>, C<sub>b</sub> in `gsRow`), and the stability-bracing count. Changing it moves demands in several modules (§4), so it is left for the engineer.
- The connection-plate candidates are the G1-line (bay 0) frames for both girder types (as C4). Interior girders also carry the frames of the next bay, and the "exterior" envelope also stands for the last girder, whose frames are in the last bay; with skewed or staggered frames those stations differ. Not changed.
- Girder section's deck reinforcement (two layers, A<sub>rt</sub> and A<sub>rb</sub>) is not sent by Preliminary sizing (C19); its own inputs remain. Fatigue rows imported from Girder section use the Fatigue module's A<sub>r</sub>.
- Carried over: row names from Preliminary sizing still say "cross-frame" in the row editors (C18); auto-designed values outlined as overrides (audit item L8), left as instructed.

- **After:** stations along G1 from its own Abut. 1 bearing, from `framingLayout`'s girder points, the same convention as `clearFrames`, X2 and X4: `s = (f.bay === i ? f.xa : f.xc) − x0(G_i)` with `x0(G_i) = xb(0, i) = m.sup[0] + (y_i − y_c) tan θ_0`. The G1 line is still the only line used here (C25 changes the candidates per girder type).
- **Problem:** the analysis arrays (`AN.xs`, the moments and shears used for every row) are along the girder from its own Abut. 1 bearing, but the frames were looked up at their global x on the G1 line. On a skewed bridge G1's bearing is offset by (y<sub>1</sub> − y<sub>c</sub>) tan θ: on the built-in example (15°, 5 girders at 9.5 ft, y<sub>c</sub> = 19.0 ft) by −19.0 tan 15° = −5.09 ft, so every G1 frame was read 5.09 ft too far toward Abut. 1 (the frame at 0.6L = 66.0 ft was read at 60.91 ft), and the pier region and span limits (`m.sup`, girder stations) were compared with global values. Demands at the plates were from the wrong points (either sign); some failing rows now pass and some passing rows increase. Corrected; it is not conservative or unconservative as a whole.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.6.1.2.2 and Table 6.6.1.2.3-1 detail 4.1 (Category C′ at the connection-plate weld toe), 6.6.1.2.5; 6.10.11.1 (TS1 to TS7, CP1 at the plate); 6.10.9 (panel shear, TS4); 6.10.8.2.3 and Eq. 6.10.8.2.3-7 (L<sub>b</sub>, C<sub>b</sub>), A6 (GS9); 6.7.4.2 (stability bracing, CF8). ### C25. Connection-plate candidates per girder type: the exterior rows consider the frames on G1 and G<sub>n</sub>, the interior rows the frames on both sides of every interior girder, each at that girder's own stations   [§4: location of the demand] [identical on bridges whose frames are at the same station on every girder (parallel frames with equal skews, or normal frames without stagger), including the built-in example] [resolves the C19–C23 open item]
- **Where (decoded PlateLine):** `detailExport`: new `nbG`, `gOf` before `const frX0` (anchor `const nbG = FR.girders.length, gOf = gt =>`); `frX0` and `cpAt` take the girder type (anchor `const cpAt = (T, a, b, gt) =>`); the Transverse stiffeners connection-plate row (anchor `const cxF = cpAt(T, x0, x1, gt)`); `frX` (anchor `const frX = gt => stG(gOf(gt), false);`); the Fatigue span row (anchor `const fx = cpAt(T, a, b, gt);`); the C21 pier rows (anchors `frX0(gt).filter(x => x > xL`, `: frX(gt).filter(x => Math.abs(x - xp) > 0.5)`). Main page: only the re-encoded `PL_B64` line.
- **Before (after C24):** for both girder types, the candidates were the intermediate frames on G1 (`stG([0], true)`), at G1's stations; the pier fallback the frames on G1 (`stG([0], false)`).
- **After:** the candidates for a girder type are the intermediate frames on the girders that type stands for, each at the station along its own girder (`framingLayout`'s `girders[i].pts`, which hold the frames of the bays on both sides of girder i, with `s = (f.bay === i ? f.xa : f.xc) − x0(G_i)`):
  - exterior (`'ext'`): G1 and G<sub>n</sub> (Preliminary sizing's exterior envelope is used for both exterior girders);
  - interior (`'int'`): G2 to G<sub>n−1</sub>;
  - demands from Structural analysis of one girder (`gLabel` "G<i>i</i>", C19 path): that girder alone;
  - any other case: G1 (as before).
  The rule within the candidates is unchanged (C4/C20/C21): inside the span 0.5 ft clear of the supports (span rows) or inside the pier's negative DC + DW region more than 0.5 ft from the pier (pier rows), the largest max(0, M<sub>f+</sub>) − min(0, M<sub>f−</sub>) at the node, ties to the first (lowest station); the pier fallback (nearest frame) uses all frames on the same girders.
- **Problem:** an interior girder also carries the frames of the bay on its other side, and the exterior envelope also stands for G<sub>n</sub>, whose frames are in the last bay. With staggered frames, normal frames on a skew (corner fills) or unequal skews these stations differ from G1's, so the interior rows were checked at stations where the interior girders have no plate, and plates with a larger range were missed. Corrected.
- **Governing provision:** as C24 (6.6.1.2.2, Table 6.6.1.2.3-1 detail 4.1, 6.6.1.2.5, 6.10.11.1, 6.10.9). Not changed. Not re-checked against the printed 10th Edition here: verify.
- **Check case:**

  - **Built-in example with 30° skews and staggered frames (normal to the girders, 6.7.4.2):** stations of the intermediate frames in Span 1: G1 10.97, 29.30, 47.64, 65.97, 84.30, 102.64; G2 (bay 1-2 and bay 2-3) 5.48, 14.65, 23.82, 32.98, 42.15, 51.32, 60.48, 69.65, 78.82, 87.98, 97.15, 106.32; G5 16.53, 34.86, 53.20, 71.53, 89.86. Exterior girder, Span 1: before, among G1's frames, 65.97 ft (M<sub>f+</sub> = 737.6, M<sub>f−</sub> = −380.6, range 1,118.2 k-ft); after, among G1's and G5's, 53.20 ft on G5 (M<sub>f+</sub> = 814.9, M<sub>f−</sub> = −305.6, range **1,120.5** k-ft).

  - The values in the C24 and C25 check cases were read from the running page (rows, sections ȳ and I, f<sub>+</sub>, f<sub>−</sub>, γΔf) and re-worked by hand as shown.
- **Saved data both directions (built-in example; Fatigue, Welds and transitions and Transverse stiffeners loaded from Preliminary sizing, autosave, reopened without importing):** branch → branch identical (Fatigue, Welds and transitions, Transverse stiffeners results); main → branch: the stored rows (main's stations, e.g. 60.91 ft) are kept and give main's results (hashes equal to main's own run); branch → main: the stored rows (66.00 ft) are kept and give the branch's results; no errors. No key or format change.
- **Screenshot:** `scratchpad/followups/gd-c5/c26_manual.png`.
- **Console:** no errors or alerts in any run.
- **Tools containing shared snippets touched:** none (`bridgeSuite.v1.*` bootstrap and handoff code unchanged; no other tool file changed).

### Open items (C24–C26)
- **Girder section brace points per girder type (not changed; decide):** the unbraced segments (L<sub>b</sub>, C<sub>b</sub>, nonprismatic flange) of both girder types are those of G1 (C24 corrected their stations). With staggered or skew-normal frames an interior girder is braced at other stations (frames on both sides), and G<sub>n</sub> at G1's mirror image. A correct envelope takes the most critical segment over the girders of the type (not the union of their brace points, which would shorten L<sub>b</sub>). The stability-bracing count (`cf.sb.n`) likewise counts G1's frames.
- **Plate selection by moment range (C4 rule, not changed; decide):** the connection plate is the frame with the largest max(0, M<sub>f+</sub>) − min(0, M<sub>f−</sub>). The Fatigue module then uses the cracked section for M<sub>f−</sub> (default), so a frame with a slightly smaller moment range can have a larger stress range (C25 check case: 1.10 at the frame with range 1,118.2 against 1.08 at the selected frame with 1,120.5 k-ft). Selecting by Δf would need the section at each candidate (and depends on the Fatigue module's negative-section option).
- **Unequal skews at the supports:** the stations are measured from each girder's own Abut. 1 bearing, but the line-girder analysis has its supports at the centerline span lengths (`m.sup`). With different skews at different supports a girder's span lengths differ from the centerline spans, so its frames and bearings do not fall at the same fractions of the analysed spans. Inherent in the line-girder model; not changed.
- **Transverse stiffeners end panel, unstiffened web:** the "first connection plate" rows use d<sub>o</sub> = the target frame spacing (`FR.sp`), not the station of the first frame on the girder (often shorter: 22.0 ft against 25 ft on the built-in example with stiffeners turned off). Conservative; not changed.
- Carried over: row names from Preliminary sizing say "cross-frame" in the row editors (C18); Girder section's two-layer deck reinforcement is not sent (C19); auto-designed values outlined as overrides (audit item L8).

## 2026-10-13 — PR: claude/girderdetail-fatigue-I-II (one bridge-wide fatigue limit state; PlateLine bearing-stiffener column check; engineer-approved 2026-10-13; PR link added after merge)

Main page (Girder section, Shear connectors, Fatigue module note, Manual) and the embedded Preliminary sizing (PlateLine, `PL_B64`, decoded, edited and re-encoded on its one line). No GirderDetail storage key or saved-data format changes. PlateLine gains one optional saved field, `P.analysis.fat` (F12-1); it is not echoed in the `gd-bridge` payload, which stays byte-identical. No `bridgeSuite.v1.*` payload changes. `lldf.html` is unchanged. Basis: AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) unless stated; the article numbers below were not re-checked against the printed 10th Edition here: verify.

### F12-1. One bridge-wide fatigue limit state: Girder section GS17, Shear connectors SC1 and Preliminary sizing's flange fatigue use Fatigue I or Fatigue II as the Fatigue module decides   [§4: limit state, load factor and resistance of three fatigue checks] [unchanged on every project whose Fatigue module ADTT_SL is at least the infinite-life equivalent, including the built-in example] [less conservative, as the code allows, on low-ADTT bridges]
- **Before:** GS17 (flange stress range), SC1 (stud fatigue pitch) and PlateLine's quick-check / Full design flange fatigue (`checkLayout`) used Fatigue I only: γ = 1.75 (GS17, SC1: the module's own "γ Fatigue I" input; PlateLine: hard-coded 1.75) and (ΔF)<sub>TH</sub> (GS17: Table 6.6.1.2.5-3 by category; PlateLine: 16.0 ksi Category B, 12.0 ksi Category C′) or Z<sub>r</sub> = 7.0A<sub>sc</sub> (= 5.5d²). Only the Fatigue module (FA1) chose Fatigue I or II by ADTT.
- **After:** the Fatigue module's inputs (Fatigue limit state auto / I / II, ADTT, p, design life, γ Fatigue I, γ Fatigue II) are the single source. For each detail category and n:
  - auto: Fatigue I where ADTT<sub>SL</sub> = p × ADTT ≥ A(γ<sub>I</sub>/(γ<sub>II</sub>(ΔF)<sub>TH</sub>))³/(365 × life × n) (the Fatigue module's own rule, `r.ADTTeq` in `GM.fa.compute`; Table 6.6.1.2.3-2 for 75 years and γ<sub>I</sub>/γ<sub>II</sub> = 1.75/0.80), otherwise Fatigue II; I or II: as set.
  - Fatigue I: unchanged (each module's own γ Fatigue I, (ΔF)<sub>TH</sub> or 7.0A<sub>sc</sub>; the arithmetic is the same expression, so results are bit-identical).
  - Fatigue II: γ<sub>II</sub> from the Fatigue module; flanges (ΔF)<sub>n</sub> = (A/N)<sup>1/3</sup>, N = 365 × life × n × ADTT<sub>SL</sub> (6.6.1.2.5, Table 6.6.1.2.5-1 A values as `FA_CAT`); studs Z<sub>r</sub> = αd², α = 34.5 − 4.28 log N (6.10.10.2, 9th Ed. Eq. 6.10.10.2-2 and -3). Stud auto rule: Fatigue I where ADTT<sub>SL</sub> ≥ N<sub>eq</sub>/(365 × life × n), log N<sub>eq</sub> = (34.5 − (7.0A<sub>sc</sub>/d²)(γ<sub>II</sub>/γ<sub>I</sub>))/4.28 (1,087 trucks/day for n = 1, 75 years, 1.75/0.80; the 9th Edition's 1,090).
  - n (Table 6.6.1.2.5-2, longitudinal members): 2.0 in a span of 40 ft or less; 1.5 within 0.1L of an interior support of a continuous girder (L the shorter adjacent span, the rule Preliminary sizing's fatigue inventory `nAt` already uses); 1.0 elsewhere. GS17 uses the row's station (`x`, rows from Preliminary sizing) on Preliminary sizing's bridge (`P.df.bridge`); a row without a station (manual rows): 1.5 at a negative-moment location of a continuous span, else 1.0. SC1 uses the largest n over the zone's stations; without the bridge, 1.5 on a continuous girder (any "pier" region), else 1.0. PlateLine uses its own supports at each analysis node.
  - If the Fatigue module's traffic inputs are incomplete (ADTT, p, life, γ not positive or p > 1), Fatigue I is used, as before.
- **How PlateLine gets the setting (chosen: the existing GD→PL message):** GirderDetail sends `{ type: 'gd-an', analysis: { fat: { limit, ADTT, p, life, gI, gII } } }` (null when incomplete) on every `recompute()` and whenever PlateLine publishes its bridge (`gd-bridge`). PlateLine's existing `gd-an` handler merges it into `P.analysis` (so it is saved with the PlateLine project and the quick check reruns because `sgQKey` includes `P.analysis`) and ignores an unchanged value. Mirroring ADTT inputs in PlateLine was not chosen: it would be a second source that can disagree with the Fatigue module. `bridgeDef` leaves `fat` out of its `analysis` echo, so the `gd-bridge` payload is unchanged and GirderDetail does not schedule a refresh of every module when only the fatigue setting changes. Without the setting (PlateLine on its own, or a PlateLine project not yet opened under GirderDetail) PlateLine uses Fatigue I with γ = 1.75, as before. As before for every analysis setting, a Full design already shown is not re-run when the setting changes (press Full design again).
- **Default behaviour:** the Fatigue module default is auto, ADTT 2000, p 0.85, 75 years, 1.75/0.80: ADTT<sub>SL</sub> = 1,700 ≥ every equivalent PlateLine and the built-in example use (Category B 1,120 for n = 1 and 747 for n = 1.5; C′ 974 / 649; studs 1,087 / 725), so every check stays Fatigue I. Projects with a Fatigue module ADTT<sub>SL</sub> below an equivalent change (that is the intent).
- **Where (main page):** new helpers after `const FA_CATS = Object.keys(FA_CAT);` (anchor `function gdFatSet() {`: `gdFatSet`, `gdFatSup`, `gdFatN`, `gdFatNr`, `gdFatLS`, `gdFatStud`, `gdFatTxt`); `GM.gs.compute` (anchor `// GS17 limit state (F12-1`); the GS17 check (anchor `{ const fs0 = gdFatSet(), anyII =`); `GM.sc.compute` (anchor `z.fat = gdFatStud(`); SC1 (anchor `sym: R.zones.some(z => z.fat.lim === 'II')`), `GM.sc.scope`, `GM.sc.combos`; the Shear connectors Fatigue pane note; the Fatigue module pane note (anchor `These traffic and limit-state inputs apply to the whole bridge`); Manual p14 (Scope and Fatigue); `gdFatPost` and its `gd-bridge` listener after `let PL_FRAME = null;`; one line in `recompute()` (anchor `gdFatPost();   // F12-1`).
- **Where (decoded PlateLine):** `checkLayout` (anchors `const FS = (P.analysis || {}).fat` and `fl = fatAt(x)`); new `plFatTxt` before `function bridgeDef`; `bridgeDef`'s `analysis` (anchor `analysis: (({ fat, ...a }) =>`); the Full design note (anchor `Flange fatigue: ${plFatTxt(P)}`); the Suggest "Flange fatigue (full design)" option labels and the note under them; the GirderDetail demands note (anchor `applies γ for Fatigue I or Fatigue II`).
- **Governing provisions:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.6.1.2.2, 6.6.1.2.3 and Table 6.6.1.2.3-2 (75-year ADTT<sub>SL</sub> equivalent to infinite life), 6.6.1.2.5 (Eq. 6.6.1.2.5-1 and -2, Tables 6.6.1.2.5-1 to -3), Table 3.4.1-1 (Fatigue I γ = 1.75, Fatigue II γ = 0.80), 6.10.10.2 (stud fatigue resistance), 6.10.5.1. **Verify:** the Fatigue II stud expression α = 34.5 − 4.28 log N is the 9th Edition's Eq. 6.10.10.2-3, as the engineer specified; the 10th Edition restates the Fatigue I stud resistance as (ΔF)<sub>TH</sub>A<sub>sc</sub> = 7.0A<sub>sc</sub> with studs in Table 6.6.1.2.3-1, and its Fatigue II stud expression was not checked against the printed 10th Edition here.
- **Check case 1, built-in example (Fatigue module default, ADTT<sub>SL</sub> = 1,700):** main vs this change, headless Chromium: GS17, GS18, SC1, FA1 on the default rows and on the rows imported from Preliminary sizing (157 items) identical apart from the new "Limit state" column (all "Fatigue I"); PlateLine's verify of the current girder (every flange ratio and governing check name at every node, both girder types) hash-identical, max. ratio 1.0586 both; the `gd-bridge` payload identical.
- **Check case 2, built-in example with ADTT = 300 (ADTT<sub>SL</sub> = 0.85 × 300 = 255 trucks/day, auto, 75 years, γ<sub>I</sub> = 1.75, γ<sub>II</sub> = 0.80):**
  - Equivalents: Category B, n = 1: 120 × 10⁸ (1.75/(0.80 × 16))³/(365 × 75 × 1) = 120 × 10⁸ × 0.0025554/27,375 = 1,120 > 255 → Fatigue II.   - N = 365 × 75 × 1 × 255 = 6,980,625 (n = 1); 10,470,938 (n = 1.5).

- **Saved data:** GirderDetail: none. Projects saved before this change: Fatigue I until GirderDetail sends its setting (on first load under GirderDetail, at once).
- **Not changed (open items):** the other fatigue checks still use Fatigue I only: Field splice (flange and splice plate range), Transverse stiffeners CP2, Welds and transitions (FW3 and shop transitions), Cross-frames CF9, GS18 (6.10.5.3 is Fatigue I by definition). ### F12-2. Preliminary sizing: new check A4, bearing stiffener axial resistance as a column (6.10.11.2.4), next to A3 (bearing)   [§4: new check item] [no existing result changes] [the logic of GirderDetail's Bearing stiffeners BS3, copied]
- **Before:** A3 checked the bearing resistance (R<sub>sb</sub>)<sub>r</sub> = φ<sub>b</sub>1.4A<sub>pn</sub>F<sub>ys</sub> only; its note said "The axial resistance of the stiffener as a column (6.10.11.2.4) is not checked here", the Manual limitation said "Bearing stiffeners are checked for proportions and bearing only, not as columns", and the Summary's "Deferred to analysis" list included "Bearing stiffener axial (column) resistance".
- **After:** new check A4 in `analysisChecks`, one item per bearing and girder type (the rows of A3), with BS3's expressions (`bsCompute`, effective column and P<sub>r</sub>):
  - effective column: the stiffener plates plus a web strip of 9t<sub>w</sub> beyond the outer stiffeners on each side, reduced by F<sub>yw</sub>/F<sub>ys</sub> when F<sub>yw</sub> < 0.7F<sub>ys</sub> (6.10.11.2.4b); on the end side of an end bearing the strip is limited to max(0, ed − t<sub>p</sub>/2) with ed = 9 in, the end distance PlateLine's bearing export already sends to GirderDetail (`bearingExport`, `ed: end ? 9 : 0`);

## 2026-10-13 — PR: claude/girderdetail-gs-anywhere (Girder section: check at any location; engineer-approved feature; PR link added after merge)

Main page only; `PL_B64` (embedded Preliminary sizing) is not touched. New UI plus a wrapper around existing code. No formula, factor, check, status, unit or code reference changed. The module's rows, checks, Design all and report are unchanged (hashes below). Saved data: one new optional UI key, `P.ui.gsAny = { g, x, snap }` (girder, station, snap mode), plus the collapse flags `P.ui.col['ga-…']`. No existing key or format changed and no migration is needed: older files do not have the key, and older versions ignore it. No `bridgeSuite.v1.*` payload changes. Tools containing shared snippets touched: none.

### LOC1. Girder section: new output tab "Any location" (check any station of any girder)   [new feature] [existing results bit-identical]
- **What it does:** the tab is shown only in the Girder section module. Controls:
  - girder picker G1…Gn; the default is the exterior girder (G1 or G<sub>n</sub>) with the larger Strength I moment from Structural analysis;
  - station box (ft) and slider;
  - snap to analysis nodes, supports, flange and web changes, the selected girder's cross-frames and diaphragms, or all key points;
  - ◀ ▶ step buttons, and ◀ Peak, Max., Peak ▶.

  At the station, one Girder section row is built and run through the unchanged `GM.gs.compute` and `GM.gs.checks` (GS1–GS19). The tab shows:
  - a checks-at-a-glance table;
  - the row (section, L<sub>b</sub>/L<sub>b,C</sub>/C<sub>b</sub>, d<sub>o</sub>, all demands; `GM.gs.echo`);
  - every check, with every item worked (Checks-tab markup);
  - in a collapsed card, the modular ratio, `GM.gs.combos` and `GM.gs.capacity` for this row.

  A plot shows the largest ratio, overall and per check group, at every analysis node of the girder, with a station marker. Clicking the plot moves the station. The plot is computed when the tab opens and cached until an input changes in this module, Structural analysis, LLDF and DLs, or Preliminary sizing.
- **How the row is built (reuse, no new engineering rules):**
  - **Demands:** `GM.sa.compute({ ...P.sa, girder: g })`. The arrays are assembled exactly as `getDemands('sa:g')` does: `gsaSA` copies the `arr`/`reac` lines of `getDemands`, including the deck-placement sequence `MDCc` from `saSeq`. The analysis object is the one Preliminary sizing makes from them (a copy of the `ANx` line of its `pl-export-req` handler).
  - **Row:** Preliminary sizing's own `detailExport(P, M, ANx, FR, extra)`, called in the embedded page with the station as an `extra` row (the path its "custom station" send uses). It supplies:
    - the section from the plates at x, and b<sub>eff</sub>;
    - L<sub>b</sub> and C<sub>b</sub> from the bracing layout (`feCb`), and the nonprismatic flange;
    - the flexure region, from the larger Strength I moment at the nearest node;
    - d<sub>o</sub>, and f<sub>ℓ</sub> from skew;
    - the shears (the largest of the element and its neighbours) and the fatigue M and V.
  - **Stations:**
    - at a flange or web change, both sides (x ∓ 0.01 ft) are checked and the smaller section is marked;
    - at an interior support, x − 0.01 ft, as the Pier rows;
    - at the girder ends, 0.01 ft inside.
  - **Three new wrapper rules (stated on the tab):**
    1. **Interpolation.** More than 0.01 ft from an analysis node, the moments M<sub>DC1</sub>, M<sub>DC2</sub>, M<sub>DW</sub>, M<sub>LL+</sub>, M<sub>LL−</sub>, M<sub>CL</sub>, M<sub>f</sub>± and M<sub>DCc</sub> are interpolated linearly and rounded to 0.1 k-ft, as the builder rounds. At a node, the node values are used, as in the builder.
    2. **End panel.** A stiffened web within d<sub>o</sub> of an abutment bearing (or of any bearing of a simple span) gets `end = 'yes'`: V<sub>n</sub> = CV<sub>p</sub> (6.10.9.3.3), and GS18 does not apply. This is the rule of the Transverse stiffeners end-panel rows. The existing GS rows never fall in an end panel.
    3. **Abutment bearing.** Both Strength I moments there are round-off (about 1e-10 k-ft), so the builder's sign test gives negative flexure with C<sub>b</sub> = 0, which is an input error. When both moments are below 0.001 k-ft, the row is set to positive flexure with L<sub>b</sub> = L<sub>b,C</sub>, C<sub>b</sub> = 1 and a prismatic section. This is what the builder produces for a positive row.
  - Materials, deck, load factors and the Fatigue I/II limit state are this module's current inputs (`{ ...P.gs, rows: [row] }`), the same as for the module's own rows.
- **Ratio plot:**
  - All nodes (369 rows on the built-in example) go through one builder call and one compute/checks call. Rows with an input error are left out and show as a gap.
  - "Governing" is the largest ratio over all items, leaving out N/A items and "(not the method in use)" items. Each check group has its own line.
  - The Peak and Max. buttons use the largest ratio of the demand checks: every group except Proportions, which depends on the plates only.
- **Where:**
  - CSS: 4 lines after `.pl-plot { width: 100%; …`, including `@media print { #tab-gsany { display: none !important; } }`.
  - Tab button after `data-tab="checks">Checks</button>`.
  - Panel after `<div class="tab-panel" id="tab-checks"></div>`.
  - New block after `GM.gs.capacity` (anchor `const GA = { key: ''`).
  - `gmRecompute` (anchor `RS = m.compute(d);`).
  - End of `applyMod` (anchor `// Girder section: check at any location (LOC1)`).
- **Exact changes:** unified diff against main 9d7fa9b, no context:

### Open items (LOC1)
- **L<sub>b</sub>/C<sub>b</sub> per girder (carried over from C24–C26, not changed):** the builder uses G1's frames for the unbraced segments of every girder. The tab snaps to the selected girder's own frames, but L<sub>b</sub>/C<sub>b</sub> at a station follow the builder (G1). On skewed or staggered layouts, an interior girder's segments differ.
- **Shear between nodes:** shears are the builder's largest of three elements around the station (as for the rows), not interpolated. This is conservative.
- **Abutment rows:** see wrapper rule 3 above. The engineer may prefer the builder itself to treat zero moment as positive flexure.

C<sub>b</sub> = 1.75 − 1.05(f<sub>1</sub>/f<sub>2</sub>) + 0.3(f<sub>1</sub>/f<sub>2</sub>)² remains anywhere in the file.

### CB1. Deck-placement C<sub>b</sub> from Eq. 6.10.8.2.3b-1 with the deck-placement moments (Girder section GS14)   [§4: C<sub>b</sub> of a constructibility check] [less conservative on positive rows; negative rows on the built-in example unchanged (F<sub>nc</sub> at the R<sub>b</sub>R<sub>h</sub>F<sub>yc</sub> cap)]
- **Before:** GS14 (6.10.3.2.1, deck placement, steel section) used the row's C<sub>b</sub>: 1.0 on positive-flexure rows; on negative rows the Strength I value of the final unbraced segment (Strength I minimum envelope). Preliminary sizing's own deck-placement check already used `feCb` with 1.25DC1 + 1.5CL.
- **After:** Preliminary sizing sends `CbC` with every Girder section row: Eq. 6.10.8.2.3b-1, C<sub>b</sub> = 12.5M<sub>max</sub>/(2.5M<sub>max</sub> + 3M<sub>A</sub> + 4M<sub>B</sub> + 3M<sub>C</sub>), from the deck-placement moment M<sub>c</sub> = 1.25DC1 + 1.5CL (the array Preliminary sizing's own check uses) over the unbraced segment(s) containing the row's station, for the flange M<sub>c</sub> compresses at the station (top where M<sub>c</sub> ≥ 0); at a brace point the smaller value of the two segments. GS14 uses C<sub>b,C</sub> (`r.CbCu = r.CbC > 0 ? r.CbC : r.Cb`) in `ltbFnc` and in the 6.10.1.6 amplification; a row without it (saved before, or entered by hand and left blank) keeps C<sub>b</sub>, so old projects are unchanged until re-imported. The 6.10.8.2.3b rule "moment at A, B or C taken as zero where the flange is in compression and continuously braced within an adjacent quarter" is documented in `feCb` but does not arise: no flange checked with C<sub>b</sub> is continuously braced (the bottom flange; the top flange during deck placement, before the deck hardens; the top flange in final positive flexure has no LTB check, 6.10.7).
- **Where (main page):** `GS_SPEC` (anchor `['CbC', 'C<sub>b</sub>, deck placement (blank = C<sub>b</sub>)'`, new optional input next to C<sub>b</sub>); `GM.gs.compute` (anchor `r.CbCu = r.CbC > 0 ? r.CbC : r.Cb;`); GS14 note and worked line (anchor `C_b = ${f2(r.CbCu)}`); report table column `L_b / L_b,C / C_b / C_b,C`; Manual "Moment gradient C<sub>b</sub>" paragraph.
- **Where (decoded PlateLine):** `detailExport` → `gsRow` (anchor `// C_b for deck placement (CB1, 2026-10-13)`); `feCb` comment (term definitions now per 6.10.8.2.3b, was "App. D6.6.2 and D6.6.3").
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 6.10.3.2.1 (F<sub>nc</sub> per 6.10.8.2), 6.10.8.2.3a Eqs. a-2 and a-3, 6.10.8.2.3b Eq. b-1 and the M<sub>max</sub>, M<sub>A</sub>, M<sub>B</sub>, M<sub>C</sub> definitions (text supplied by the engineer).

### CB2. Nonprismatic unbraced lengths per 6.10.8.2.3c (Preliminary sizing checks and the Girder section rows it sends; GS7, GS14)   [§4: LTB resistance of every unbraced length with a section change] [more conservative (much more for pier segments with a flange transition inside L<sub>b</sub>); its interim γ<sub>e</sub> is superseded by App. D6.6.2 Method A in "CB2 (update)" below]
- **Before:** where the compression flange changed within L<sub>b</sub>: LTB with the smallest compression flange (by area) over the full L<sub>b</sub> and C<sub>b</sub> of Eq. b-1 (Preliminary sizing `checkLayout`; Girder section via `lbB`/`lbT`); a row whose own flange was the smallest (rows on the smaller side of a transition) was treated as prismatic, with C<sub>b</sub> and Appendix A6.
- **After:** each unbraced length is classified by the new `feNpr` (decoded PlateLine, after `feCb`) from the section along it (top, bottom flange and web plates; changes located to 1e-4 ft by bisection) and the envelope that compresses the flange considered:
  - **prismatic** (no change): 6.10.8.2.3b, unchanged.
  - **simplification of 6.10.8.2.3c** where all hold: a single section change; at ≤ 0.2L<sub>b</sub> from the brace point with the smaller moment (the end with the smaller compressing envelope value); every plate of the section next to that brace point ≤ the other's (a transition to a smaller section); the largest moment of L<sub>b</sub> within the larger section; I<sub>yt1</sub>/I<sub>yt2</sub> and I<sub>yb1</sub>/I<sub>yb2</sub> ≥ 0.5 (I<sub>y</sub> = tb³/12; 1 = side of the smaller-moment brace point). Constant web depth always holds in GirderDetail. Then F<sub>nc</sub> as prismatic per 6.10.8.2.3b with the compression flange of the larger section (next to the larger-moment brace point) and C<sub>b</sub> of Eq. b-1 over L<sub>b</sub> (no effective length factor).
  - **otherwise:** C<sub>b</sub> = 1.0 in Eq. a-2 (Eq. c-1), F<sub>e</sub> = γ<sub>e</sub>f<sub>bu</sub> (Eq. c-2), r<sub>t</sub> = (L<sub>b</sub>/π)√(F<sub>e</sub>/E) (Eq. c-3), and F<sub>nc</sub> from Eqs. a-1 to a-5 with that r<sub>t</sub> (L<sub>p</sub> = 1.1r<sub>t</sub>√(E/F<sub>yc</sub>), L<sub>r</sub> = πr<sub>t</sub>√(E/F<sub>yr</sub>), a-3 F<sub>nc</sub> = R<sub>b</sub>F<sub>e</sub>). **γ<sub>e</sub> (App. D6.6 not supplied; conservative stand-in, "pending D6.6" on screen):** each section j of L<sub>b</sub> is taken as a prismatic member over the full L<sub>b</sub> under uniform moment (C<sub>b</sub> = 1.0), F<sub>e,j</sub> = π²E/(L<sub>b</sub>/r<sub>t,j</sub>)² (Eq. b-2, r<sub>t,j</sub> by Eq. b-3 with its own D<sub>c</sub>), loaded to the largest Strength I compression-flange stress f<sub>j,max</sub> that section would have anywhere in L<sub>b</sub> (the factored stage moments at each analysis node in L<sub>b</sub> on that section); γ<sub>e</sub> = min<sub>j</sub> F<sub>e,j</sub>/f<sub>j,max</sub> (`feGe`). Justification: a member whose every section is at least as stiff as section j, under moments no larger in magnitude than the largest, buckles at a load ratio no lower than section j's prismatic member under uniform maximum moment; taking the minimum over j covers whichever section is weakest. Girder section gets it as F<sub>e</sub> = γ<sub>e</sub>f<sub>bu</sub> with γ<sub>e</sub> = F<sub>e,s</sub>/(K f<sub>s</sub>): `lbB × lbT` is the governing section's compression flange, f<sub>s</sub> its stress under the row's own moments (Girder section's staged sections and load factors), and `lbK` = K = f<sub>j,max</sub>/f<sub>j</sub>(row) ≥ 1 from Preliminary sizing (blank = 1, which is correct for a row at the largest moment of L<sub>b</sub>, e.g. a pier).
  - **warning:** GS7 adds a warning item where I<sub>y1</sub>/I<sub>y2</sub> < 0.5 at a change in L<sub>b</sub> ("should be at least 0.5", 6.10.8.2.3c); the ratio is listed in the item's "where" table.
  - Appendix A6 is not used for a nonprismatic L<sub>b</sub> (either method), as before for the smallest-flange rows.
  - Deck placement: the same classification with M<sub>c</sub> for the flange it compresses (steel section); Preliminary sizing sends it as `nprC = { kind, fl, b, t, k, Ir, why }` and `CbC` = 1.0 where γ<sub>e</sub> applies; GS14 applies it when `nprC.fl` matches the flange in compression.
  - Segment ranking at a brace point (gsRow) uses the C<sub>b</sub> actually applied (1.0 for γ<sub>e</sub> segments).
- **Girder section row fields (saved data, optional; no key or existing field changed):** spec inputs `npr` (select: blank = "γe method if the flange above is smaller", the previous meaning of `lbB`/`lbT`; `ge`; `simp`) and `lbK` (blank = 1); builder metadata `lbIr`, `nprWhy`, `nprC` (read from the saved row, shown in GS7/GS14). Migration: rows saved before (no `npr`): `lbB × lbT` smaller than the row's flange → γ<sub>e</sub> method with K = 1 (was smallest flange with C<sub>b</sub>); otherwise prismatic, as before. Re-importing from Preliminary sizing fills the new fields.

### CB2 (update, 2026-10-13). γ<sub>e</sub> by App. D6.6.2 Method A in place of the interim bound   [§4: γ<sub>e</sub> of Eq. 6.10.8.2.3c-2 for every nonprismatic L<sub>b</sub> not meeting the simplification] [less conservative than the interim bound of CB2; still more conservative than main at the built-in piers]
- **Before (interim CB2, head 1ac5655):** γ<sub>e</sub> = min over the sections j of L<sub>b</sub> of F<sub>e,j</sub>/f<sub>j,max</sub>, F<sub>e,j</sub> = π²E/(L<sub>b</sub>/r<sub>t,j</sub>)² (C<sub>b</sub> = 1.0, full L<sub>b</sub>), f<sub>j,max</sub> = the largest compression-flange stress section j would have anywhere in L<sub>b</sub> (`feGe`); Girder section γ<sub>e</sub> = F<sub>e,s</sub>/(K f<sub>s</sub>) with `lbB`/`lbT` (that section) and `lbK` ≥ 1; shown "pending D6.6".
- **After:** new `feGeA` (decoded PlateLine, after `feGe`), AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) App. D6.6.2, Method A, text supplied by the engineer 2026-10-13:
  - γ<sub>e</sub> = χC<sub>be</sub>/(M<sub>u</sub>/M<sub>e1</sub>)<sub>max</sub> (Eq. D6.6.2-1); C<sub>be</sub> = 12.5(M<sub>u</sub>/M<sub>e1</sub>)<sub>max</sub>/[2.5(M<sub>u</sub>/M<sub>e1</sub>)<sub>max</sub> + 3M<sub>A</sub>/M<sub>e1A</sub> + 4M<sub>B</sub>/M<sub>e1B</sub> + 3M<sub>C</sub>/M<sub>e1C</sub>] (Eq. D6.6.2-2).
  - Written in stress (CD6.6.2: M<sub>e1</sub> = F<sub>e1</sub>S<sub>xc</sub>, M<sub>u</sub> = f<sub>bu</sub>S<sub>xc</sub>): ratio at x for section s = f(s, x)/F<sub>e1</sub>(s); f = the staged compression-flange stress of section s under the factored moments at x (Strength I: DC1 on the steel section, the rest on steel + deck reinforcement, load factors by sign, Strength I minimum live-load envelope, as the existing checks; deck placement: 1.25DC1 + 1.5CL on the steel section), linear between analysis nodes; F<sub>e1</sub> = π²E/(L<sub>b</sub>/r<sub>t</sub>)² (Eq. 6.10.8.2.3b-2 with C<sub>b</sub> = 1.0, full L<sub>b</sub>, r<sub>t</sub> of Eq. b-3). Using that staged stress makes S<sub>xc</sub> the effective modulus of section s for that moment mix (documented choice).
  - (M<sub>u</sub>/M<sub>e1</sub>)<sub>max</sub>: the largest ratio of each section over its own length (piece ends, i.e. the brace points and both sides of every step, and the nodes inside; f is piecewise linear, so its extremes lie there).
  - A, B, C at 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 L<sub>b</sub>, absolute values. D6.6.2.2: where a step lies in the quarter-lengths adjacent to the point (0–0.5, 0.25–0.75, 0.5–1.0 L<sub>b</sub>, inclusive), M<sub>e1</sub> there = the smallest M<sub>e1</sub> of the sections in that range, taken as the largest |f(s<sub>k</sub>, x<sub>P</sub>)|/F<sub>e1</sub>(s<sub>k</sub>) of those sections (the same moment at the point, so the smallest effective M<sub>e1</sub>). The zero-moment rule for a flange continuously braced next to A, B or C does not arise (discretely braced flanges only, as in `feCb`).
  - χ = 1 − 4d<sub>S,max</sub>/L<sub>b</sub> (Eq. D6.6.2.2-1; D6.6.2.1 gives 1.0 for the constant web depth): shear centre of the steel section from CD6.6.2.2-1, e = h<sub>o</sub>b<sub>ft</sub>³t<sub>ft</sub>/(b<sub>fc</sub>³t<sub>fc</sub> + b<sub>ft</sub>³t<sub>ft</sub>) from the compression-flange centre, converted to a **fixed datum, the bottom of the web** (constant D): y<sub>s</sub> = [I<sub>t</sub>(D + t<sub>t</sub>/2) − I<sub>b</sub>t<sub>b</sub>/2]/(I<sub>t</sub> + I<sub>b</sub>), I = tb³; d<sub>S</sub> = the change of y<sub>s</sub> at a step, or the largest difference of y<sub>s</sub> within a run of steps less than 0.25L<sub>b</sub> apart (consecutive steps chained).
  - Step limit (D6.6.2.2): each flange's lateral moment of inertia (top and bottom, as 6.10.8.2.3c) may change by no more than a factor 2.0 at a step, and by no more than 2.0 in total (largest over smallest of the sections) within a run of steps less than 0.25L<sub>b</sub> apart. Where violated, Method A does not apply: the interim bound `feGe` is kept for that unbraced length, flagged "outside D6.6.2.2 step limit — conservative bound used; engineer to review" (Girder section GS7/GS14 warning items; Full design note lists the segments).
  - Applied to Strength I (`npr`, bottom flange) and deck placement (`nprC`, flange M<sub>c</sub> compresses, noncomposite, deck-placement moments, L<sub>b,C</sub> as before) in Preliminary sizing's own checks (`checkLayout` via `geAt`: F<sub>e</sub> = γ<sub>e</sub>f<sub>bu</sub> at each node) and in the rows it sends (`gsRow`).

With m = 'A', `lbB`/`lbT` = the section at (M<sub>u</sub>/M<sub>e1</sub>)<sub>max</sub> (shown only) and `lbK`/`nprC.k` blank; Girder section takes γ<sub>e</sub> = `geA.ge` and F<sub>e</sub> = γ<sub>e</sub>f<sub>bu</sub> with the row's own f<sub>bu</sub> (Eq. c-2). +    const js = step ? pcs.map((p, j) => j).filter(j => pcs[j].x1 > a && pcs[j].x0 < b) : [Math.max(0, pcs.findIndex(p => x >= p.x0 - 1e-9 && x <= p.x1 + 1e-9))];

+  const A = pt(0.25, 0, 0.5), B = pt(0.5, 0.25, 0.75), C = pt(0.75, 0.5, 1), Cbe = 12.5 * rm / (2.5 * rm + 3 * A.r + 4 * B.r + 3 * C.r);
+  // runs of steps less than 0.25 L_b apart (piece indices k0..k1)
+  const runs = []; tr.forEach((q, k) => { const last = runs[runs.length - 1]; if (last && q - tr[k - 1] < 0.25 * L - 1e-9) last[1] = k + 1; else runs.push([k, k + 1]); });
+  const Iw = (b, t) => t * b ** 3, ys = s => { const It = Iw(s.topB, s.topT), Ib = Iw(s.botB, s.botT); return (It * (D + s.topT / 2) - Ib * s.botT / 2) / (It + Ib); };

-<p><b>Quick suggestion and full design.</b> Suggest has two modes. The <b>quick suggestion</b> updates as you edit. It picks the web depth and web type with the lowest estimated cost from a fast sizing (one constant-stiffness beam model, flange areas from lever-arm estimates, this tool's layout checks), then checks that girder with the same staged analysis and AASHTO checks as Full design (listed below) for the interior and exterior girders, including the Table 2.5.2.6.3-1 minimum depths when span-to-depth applies to Suggest. Where a ratio exceeds 1.0 it increases the flange plates there (required area = current area &times; ratio/0.97 &times; 1.01, at most 1.35 times per round, never less than the plate already there) and thickens the web by one increment if the web ratio exceeds 1.0, then checks again, up to 8 rounds. Plates are only increased, never trimmed, so the quick suggestion passes the strength and service checks (the card says so, or names the ratio that still exceeds 1.0) but is not necessarily the lightest girder. The check runs in the background after the fast result appears (the card shows &ldquo;checking&rdquo; with a progress bar; typically a second or less after the fast result); a new edit restarts it, and Apply pressed during the check applies the checked result, after confirmation, when it is ready. The girder-count study and the Alternatives study use the fast sizing only, without this check, to rank layouts. <b>Run full design</b> optimizes for the least steel: it takes the best fast candidates and, for each, repeats: the staged, cracked analysis of the current layout (the Structural analysis settings); the AASHTO checks at every node for the interior and exterior girders, on both sides of every plate boundary (Strength I positive flexure with the plastic moment, compactness, D<sub>p</sub>/D<sub>t</sub>, and 1.3M<sub>y</sub>;     alert(`The browser blocked the new tab.\n\nOpen ST-Girder (stgirder.html, in the same folder or on the same website as this tool) and click "Pull from GirderDetail".`); return; }
  flash(`${sent} In stgirder.html click "Pull from GirderDetail".`); });
  /* ST-Girder's file for "open now" (OD1): where the bridge suite last saw ST-Girder in this folder (read only, key bridgeSuite.v1.appPaths,
     the same record and rules as BridgeApps.path in stgirder.html / lldf.html / psbeam.html / index.html), else stgirder.html next to this file. */
  function gdStHref() { let f = '';
    try { const o = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('bridgeSuite.v1.appPaths') || '{}') || {}, e = o.stgirder, h = String(location.href || '').split('#')[0].split('?')[0], d = h.slice(0, h.lastIndexOf('/') + 1);
      if (e && e.at && e.at[d] && e.at[d].file) f = e.at[d].file; else if (e && e.file && !e.dir) f = e.file;
      let me = (location.pathname || '').split('/').pop() || ''; try { me = decodeURIComponent(me); } catch (er) { }
      if (f && f.toLowerCase() === me.toLowerCase()) f = ''; } catch (er) { f = ''; }
    return encodeURI(f || 'stgirder.html'); }
  ```
- **Text (`gdStUi`):** button title `…for ST-Girder (stgirder.html): Pull from GirderDetail` → `…for ST-Girder (stgirder.html): Pull from GirderDetail. Then offers to open ST-Girder in a new tab with this girder loaded`; the note gets the sentence `After sending you can open ST-Girder in a new tab with this girder loaded, or click Pull from GirderDetail there later.` before `Opened as files, …`.
- **Problem / request:** the engineer asked to go straight from GirderDetail to ST-Girder with the girder loaded, instead of switching tools and clicking Pull from GirderDetail. Cancel keeps the previous behaviour (message only). The payload, the channel (`bridgeSuite.v1.girderDemands`), its keys and schema are unchanged; `producedAt` (as stamped by `BridgeXfer.publish`) is the flag value ST-Girder matches. `bridgeSuite.v1.appPaths` is only read.
- **Governing provision:** none (hand-off UI; no engineering value changes).
- **Check case:** built-in example, Preliminary sizing built, Structural analysis, G2: Send → dialog "G2 sent to ST-Girder (363 stations). … Open ST-Girder now with this girder loaded? …" → OK → new tab `stgirder.html` (flag removed) with the girder loaded; message "G2 sent to ST-Girder (363 stations). ST-Girder opened in a new tab." Cancel → no tab, message "… In stgirder.html click "Pull from GirderDetail"." `window.open` returning null → the same message and the alert "The browser blocked the new tab. …". `gdStHref()`: no record → `stgirder.html`; record for this folder `ST Girder v2.html` → `ST%20Girder%20v2.html`; record for another folder only → `stgirder.html`; legacy record without a folder → its file; record naming this file → `stgirder.html`; unreadable record → `stgirder.html`.
- **How verified:** `node --check`-equivalent parse of every inline script (`new Function`); headless Chromium (Playwright) with both files in one folder, served over http (`python3 -m http.server`) and opened as `file://`: 28 checks pass in each (the ST-Girder side is in fixlog/stgirder.md OD1: inputs and results identical to a manual Pull, refresh, mismatched / missing / invalid flag, undo); the `gdStHref()` cases run in Node with a stubbed `localStorage`/`location`. No console errors.
- **Other copies:** the receiving side is in `stgirder.html` (fixlog/stgirder.md OD1). The BridgeApps path rules are mirrored (read only) from the bootstrap block in `index.html`, `lldf.html`, `psbeam.html`, `stgirder.html`; that block is unchanged.
- **Open items:** whether a browser allows `window.open` after the confirm dialog is up to its popup blocker (Chrome/Edge normally allow it from a click handler; the blocked case falls back to the message and alert). Not testable headless with a real popup blocker.

## 2026-10-13 — PR: claude/gd-stiffener-per-bay (Preliminary sizing: D/t<sub>w</sub> ≤ 150 for stiffened webs; transverse stiffeners designed per cross-frame bay with optional tension-field action; engineer-approved 2026-10-13; PR link added after merge)

All code in this PR except the GirderDetail drawing and Structural analysis hunks is inside the embedded Preliminary sizing page (`const PL_B64 = '…'`, base64 of a UTF-8 HTML file). To re-apply by hand: decode `PL_B64` (base64 → UTF-8), edit the decoded page as below, re-encode it to base64 on one line, and replace the string. Line numbers "PL ~n" are lines of the decoded page.

### DT1. Suggest sizes a transversely stiffened web from D/t<sub>w</sub> ≤ 150 (was 300)   [§4: code limit] [results: only where D/150 governs t<sub>w</sub>]
- **Where:** decoded PL, new constant after `const SG_PLF = 490 / 144;` (PL ~1868); `sizeForDepth` (anchor `let tw = up(Math.max(L.minTw, D / ((wt || SG.web) === 'stiffened'`, PL ~2050); `webFromShear` → `size` (anchor `let tw = up(Math.max(L.minTw, D / (st ?`, PL ~2210); Suggest input tab note "AASHTO LRFD minimums always apply" (PL ~2860) and Manual Part 2 "Rules." (PL ~2586).
- **Before:**
  ```js
  let tw = up(Math.max(L.minTw, D / ((wt || SG.web) === 'stiffened' ? 300 : 150), 0.3125, twMin || 0), L.incTw);
  let tw = up(Math.max(L.minTw, D / (st ? 300 : 150), 0.3125, twMin || 0), L.incTw), C, Vn, lam;
  ```
  text: `D/t<sub>w</sub> ≤ 150 unstiffened or 300 stiffened (6.10.2.1)` (2 places)
- **After:**
  ```js
  // D/t_w limit Suggest sizes a transversely stiffened web to: 150, AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Eq. 6.10.2.1.1-1 (webs without longitudinal stiffeners; approved 2026-10-13,
  // was 300, the limit of Eq. 6.10.2.1.2-1 for longitudinally stiffened webs, which this tool does not design). Unstiffened webs: 150 (same equation)
  const SG_DTW_ST = 150;
  let tw = up(Math.max(L.minTw, D / ((wt || SG.web) === 'stiffened' ? SG_DTW_ST : 150), 0.3125, twMin || 0), L.incTw);
  let tw = up(Math.max(L.minTw, D / (st ? SG_DTW_ST : 150), 0.3125, twMin || 0), L.incTw), C, Vn, lam;
  ```
  text: `D/t<sub>w</sub> ≤ 150, stiffened or not (Eq. 6.10.2.1.1-1, webs without longitudinal stiffeners)` (2 places)
- **Problem:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.10.2.1.1 (Eq. 6.10.2.1.1-1) limits D/t<sub>w</sub> to 150 for webs without longitudinal stiffeners, transversely stiffened or not; 300 (Eq. 6.10.2.1.2-1) applies only to webs with longitudinal stiffeners, which this tool does not design (its own check W1 already applies 150). Suggest could start a stiffened web thinner than W1 allows. More conservative.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.10.2.1.1, Eq. 6.10.2.1.1-1; Art. 6.10.2.1.2, Eq. 6.10.2.1.2-1.
- **Check case:** built-in example, D = 60 in, G12.1 on (minimum t<sub>w</sub> 1/2 in): start t<sub>w</sub> before = up(max(0.5, 60/300 = 0.20, 0.3125), 1/16) = 0.5 in; after = up(max(0.5, 60/150 = 0.40, 0.3125)) = 0.5 in (unchanged; the owner minimum governs). G12.1 off (minimum 5/16 in): before up(max(0.3125, 0.20)) = 0.3125 in; after up(max(0.3125, 0.40)) = 0.4375 in. In both cases shear (k = 10) governs the final t<sub>w</sub> (7/16 in at D = 55 in, G12.1 off), so the quick suggestion is unchanged; only the D = 79 in candidate (79/150 = 0.527 → 9/16 in, was 1/2 in) moves in the candidate list.
- **How verified:** decoded page parsed (`node --check` on its scripts); headless Chromium quick suggestion, built-in example and xsA, G12.1 on and off, main vs this change.
- **Other copies:** none.
- **Open items:** none.

### TB1. Suggest designs transverse stiffeners per cross-frame bay, with optional tension-field action; per-bay layout on the Framing tab and in every consumer   [§4: shear design method, new option] [§5: new optional fields only] [results: Suggest with "Optimize stiffener spacing" on; projects in per-bay mode]
- **Where (decoded PL):** new block before `function framingChecks(m, FR, P) {` (constants `TS_DMIN, TS_DLOW, TS_TWSTEPS, TS_PHIV`, functions `tsVn`, `tsBaysOf`, `tsBayX`, `tsPanels`, `tsEvalBay`, `tsDesignBay`, `tsVu`, `tsSecFns`, `tsDesign`, `tsBaysOn`, `tsGirderBays`, `tsGirderX`, `tsGLbl`); `suggestLayout` (`PB`, `TFA`, `stiffBays`, `costOf`, `evalCand`, `clearFrames`, `opts.clear/costOnly/verify/only`, `tryPB`/`tryD`, fine search, return; `webFromShear` per-bay branch); `suggestFull` (`refine`, picks, return); `suggestQuickCheck`; `sgQuickStart`; `sgFrStiff` (new) and `applySuggestion`; `wsEval`, `wsApply`, `wsfEval`, `wsfApply`, `evalCase`, `applyAlt`; `framingChecks` D3/D4; `quantities`; `detailExport` (TS rows, `gsDo` for gs rows); `DEFAULT` (`framing.doMode: 'uniform'`, `suggest.tfa: 'on'`); Suggest input tab (web option label, Optimize stiffener spacing options, new Tension-field action select and note); Framing tab (Stiffener spacing select, `#fr-bays`, `f1`, `frBaysHtml`, `renderFrBays`, change/click handlers, CSS `.atbl.tsb`); `recompute` (calls `renderFrBays`); `sgQKey`, `sgcKey`, `sgCurNSt` (new), `sgcIn`; `renderSuggest` (cost card, depth candidates, Full design table, web card via `sgWebPB`, new card `sgBaysCard`); `sgCmpHtml` and new `sgBayCmp`; Alternatives web table label; Manual (Part 1 Framing tab and inputs table, Part 2 Suggest rules and Apply, Part 3 web thickness and D3/D4, Alternatives cost note).
- **Where (GirderDetail page):** `gsaSA` (Structural analysis, anchor `const sup = A(R.sup).map(i => xs[i]), F = G.P.framing`), new `gdStiffX` / `gdStiffBays` before `const dxfPM = () =>`, `dxfPlan` and `dxfElev` stiffener loops, 3D view (`v3bBuild`) stiffener loop.
- **Data model (§5):** `framing.doRatio` and `framing.stiff` keep their meaning. New optional fields: `framing.doMode` (`'uniform'` default for new and old projects, through `deepMerge` with `DEFAULT`; `'bays'` uses the per-bay layout) and `framing.bays = { v: 1, D, tw, tfa, list: [{ g, a, b, n, e0?, e1? }] }` (girder g 1-based, bay a..b in ft at that girder's own stations from its Abut. 1 bearing, n intermediate stiffeners, e0/e1 in: end panel with its own stiffener). `suggest.tfa` (`'on'` default for new and old projects). No key or format removed or renamed. A project without the fields loads and computes exactly as before (uniform; verified, below). A project saved with the fields opens in an older copy without errors and uses the uniform d<sub>o</sub>/D; the fields are kept on save (unknown keys survive `deepMerge`). The ST-Girder hand-off (`gdStPayload`) carries no d<sub>o</sub> or stiffener data, so it is unchanged.
- **Before:** Suggest with a stiffened web and "Optimize stiffener spacing" on tried one uniform d<sub>o</sub>/D from {1, 1.5, 2, 3} per depth (`doList`), sized t<sub>w</sub> for the maximum Strength I shear with k = 5 + 5/(d<sub>o</sub>/D)² and no tension field (end panels with d<sub>o</sub> > 1.5D with k = 5), and priced `ceil(L·12/(d_o·D)) − ceil(L/s_xf)` stiffeners per girder. The quick check and Full design never re-checked shear with the staged demands. Every consumer used `framing.doRatio·D` everywhere.
- **After:** with "Optimize stiffener spacing" on (default), a stiffened web is designed per cross-frame bay (connection plates act as stiffeners):
  1. Floor web (`webFromShear`, per-bay branch): the thinnest t<sub>w</sub> (D/t<sub>w</sub> ≤ 150, owner minimum) for which every analysis element passes with d<sub>o</sub> = 1.0D: V<sub>u</sub> (Strength I, envelope of the girder types) ≤ φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>n</sub>, V<sub>n</sub> = CV<sub>p</sub> (Eq. 6.10.9.3.3-1) within 1.0D of an abutment or simple-span bearing, else interior V<sub>n</sub> by Eq. 6.10.9.3.2-2 (2Dt<sub>w</sub>/(b<sub>fc</sub>t<sub>fc</sub> + b<sub>ft</sub>t<sub>ft</sub>) ≤ 2.5, Eq. 6.10.9.3.2-1) or -8, or CV<sub>p</sub> with tension-field action off.
  2. Web candidates (`tryPB`): the floor web and up to 6 webs one increment thicker each, while stiffeners remain; each is sized (flanges re-sized) and priced with its own per-bay stiffener count; the cheapest candidate is kept (replaces the d<sub>o</sub>/D list).
  3. Bays (`tsDesignBay`, per girder, its own bearings and cross-frame points): n = 0 if every panel passes with the connection plates only (a bay > 3D is then unstiffened, 6.10.9.1/6.10.9.2); else interior bays start at the largest spacing allowed, n = ⌈L/3D⌉ − 1 (6.10.9.1), and add one stiffener at a time; a bay at an end support tries, for each n, the even layout and then an end stiffener at the widest whole inch ≤ 1.5D (down to 0.5D) whose end panel carries its largest V<sub>u</sub> with V<sub>n</sub> = CV<sub>p</sub> (6.10.9.3.3), the rest evenly spaced. Each panel is checked with the largest V<sub>u</sub> in it (6.10.9.3.1) and the largest 2Dt<sub>w</sub>/(b<sub>fc</sub>t<sub>fc</sub> + b<sub>ft</sub>t<sub>ft</sub>) along it (6.10.9.3.2). Down to d<sub>o</sub> = 0.5D; a bay that still fails flags the candidate (`bayFail`): the fast search drops it, the quick check and Full design thicken the web.
  4. The quick suggestion's check and Full design redo the bays with the staged shears (`opts.verify` cost); Apply writes `framing.doMode = 'bays'` and `framing.bays` (`sgFrStiff`), also from the girder-count study, its Full design, and the Alternatives study.
  5. Consumers with `framing.doMode === 'bays'`: D3 (narrowest panel in each field piece), D4 (each bay: interior panels against 3D, own-stiffener end panels against 1.5D, wider even end panels advisory), quantities (sum of the counts), TS rows (first stiffener or connection plate from each support at its actual station with the actual panel widths and end flag; cross-frame row with its adjacent panels), gs rows (`do`/`end` of the panel at x: of two at a boundary, the one with the smaller V<sub>n</sub>), Structural analysis / Any location (no extra end panel: `doFt = 0`, the rows carry it), DXF plan and elevation and 3D stiffener positions (`gdStiffX` → `tsGirderX`), Suggest cost and comparison card (per-bay table). Uniform mode: every consumer as before (same code path).
  With the setting off: the uniform Framing tab ratio as before (only DT1 differs).
- **Problem / request:** engineer's decision 2026-10-13: design the stiffener spacing per cross-frame bay at the largest spacing the code allows, tightened only where φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>n</sub> < V<sub>u</sub>; tension-field action in interior panels as an option; keep the web-thickness cost trade-off; per-bay layout stored and used everywhere. Fewer stiffeners than the uniform d<sub>o</sub> = 1.0D (less conservative only in the sense of fewer stiffeners; every panel is checked against its own largest V<sub>u</sub>, and the staged shear is now checked, which the uniform method did not do).
- **Governing provisions:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.10.9.1 (Eq. 6.10.9.1-1; interior panel without longitudinal stiffeners stiffened when d<sub>o</sub> ≤ 3D; end panel when d<sub>o</sub> ≤ 1.5D; stiffeners required wherever V<sub>u</sub> > φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>n</sub> of the unstiffened web), 6.10.9.2 (Eqs. 6.10.9.2-1, -2, k = 5), 6.10.9.3.1 (spacing from the maximum shear in a panel), 6.10.9.3.2 (Eqs. 6.10.9.3.2-1 to -8), 6.10.9.3.3 (Eq. 6.10.9.3.3-1; end panel ≤ 1.5D), 6.5.4.2 (φ<sub>v</sub> = 1.00); 6.10.11.1.1 (connection plates as stiffeners).
- **Check case (built-in example, quick suggestion, GirderDetail LLDF factors not applied (`P.dfx = null`), tension-field action on):** D = 63 in, t<sub>w</sub> = 1/2 in, F<sub>yw</sub> = 50 ksi, V<sub>p</sub> = 0.58(50)(63)(0.5) = 913.5 kip, D/t<sub>w</sub> = 126.

  - End bay G1–G5, Span 1, 0–22 ft (Abut. 1): n = 0 → 264 in > 1.5D, k = 5, φV<sub>n</sub> = 262.0 < 280.9 kip; n = 1 even → end panel 132 in > 1.5D = 94.5 in, unstiffened, 262.0 < 280.9 kip; n = 1 with an end stiffener at e = 94 in (largest whole inch ≤ 94.5): k = 5 + 5/(94/63)² = 7.246, C = 1.57/126² × 29,000(7.246)/50 = 0.4156, φV<sub>n</sub> = 0.4156(913.5) = 379.7 kip ≥ 280.9 kip (Eq. 6.10.9.3.3-1); remaining panel 170 in = 2.698D: k = 5.687, C = 0.3262, 2Dt<sub>w</sub>/(18×0.75 + 16×1.25) = 1.881 → Eq. -2: 0.87(0.6738)/√(1 + 2.698²) = 0.2037, φV<sub>n</sub> = 913.5(0.5299) = 484.1 kip ≥ 245.8 kip. n = 1, e<sub>0</sub> = 94 in.
  - Before (main, same inputs): D = 69 in, t<sub>w</sub> = 1/2 in, uniform d<sub>o</sub> = 1.0D (k = 10, no tension field), 48 stiffeners per girder (240 for 5 girders) in the Suggest cost. After: D = 63 in, t<sub>w</sub> = 1/2 in, 50 intermediate stiffeners for all 5 girders (10 per girder); cost (Unit costs) $1,714,870 → $1,682,391. Tension-field action off: 80 stiffeners, $1,686,891.
