 <h3>Girder count from the deck width</h3><p>With an <b>Out-to-out deck width</b> W on the Suggest input tab, <b>Suggest girder count, spacing, and overhangs</b> compares girder counts. For each N from 3, every overhang on a 0.25 ft grid within the limits gives S = (W &minus; 2&middot;overhang)/(N &minus; 1); a layout is kept when S, the overhang (also &le; a fraction of S), and d<sub>e</sub> = overhang &minus; barrier (or curb) width are within the limits (defaults: overhang 1.5 to 4.0 ft and &le; 0.5S; d<sub>e</sub> &minus;1.0 to 5.5 ft; S 3.5 to 16 ft, the ranges of the 4.6.2.2 equations; verify / owner). The overhang limits used are the stricter of these settings and the Limits tab overhang limits of check G6 (overhang / S and maximum overhang, 0.40S and 4.0 ft by default), so the study never proposes an overhang that G6 warns about; the results note says which value governs. Of those, the overhang whose exterior and interior girder live load moment distribution factors (this tool's 4.6.2.2 equations, longest span) are closest is used (ties: nearest 0.375S); the girder is then sized with Suggest's fast sizing (without the quick suggestion's strength and service check) and checked like an alternative. The table lists N, S, overhang, d<sub>e</sub>, the factors, the section, the steel per girder and in total (lb/ft<sup>2</sup> of deck), the governing ratio of the layout checks, the bracing type from the girder depth, and pass/fail. The recommendation is the passing row with the least total steel (or the fewest girders, if chosen). Nothing changes until you press Apply. With W blank, Suggest uses the girder count and spacing on the Bridge tab as before. Distribution factors are an estimate for comparing layouts: run LL &amp; DL for the chosen layout.</p>
 <p><b>Fast study, then full design of the best few.</b> The study sizes every girder count with Suggest's <i>fast sizing</i> (without the quick suggestion's strength and service check): one constant-stiffness continuous-beam model, flange areas from lever-arm estimates, and only this tool's layout checks (proportions, transitions, splices, framing), with no strength, service, or fatigue check. That makes it quick enough to try every girder count, but its weights are a ranking aid. The overhang of each row is chosen with the K<sub>g</sub> of a trial girder sized at the overhang nearest 0.375S. When the study finishes, the Suggest tab offers <b>Full design of the best N</b> (N on the Suggest input tab, default 3, at most 5). It takes the best N rows (by the objective: passing rows first, then the others by governing ratio) and runs Full design (see <i>Quick suggestion and full design</i> below) on each with that row's girder count, spacing, and overhangs, on a copy of the project: each iteration re-runs the staged analysis of the current plates (DC1 on the steel section; DC2 and DW on the long-term composite section, 3n; live load on the short-term composite section, n; cracked near interior piers), recomputes the 4.6.2.2 distribution factors from that section's K<sub>g</sub>, checks every node, and resizes; the live load model of the first iteration is reused inside the loop, and the final verification recomputes everything, so the pass/fail of each row comes from fully recomputed demands. The girder count, spacing, and overhangs are kept from the fast study. Full design takes about 20 to 60 s for each girder count, which is why it runs only for the best few and only when you press the button (it can be cancelled). The results table lists the full-design section, cross-frame spacing, steel per girder, total and per deck area (with the fast-study value beside it), the largest ratio of the final verification, the interior and exterior moment distribution factors of the final girder (longest span), the iterations, and pass/fail (every full-design check at or below 1.0 and no failing layout check; failing Analysis tab checks A1 to A3 are named beside it but do not decide it, because they depend on the bearing stiffener and bearings, which Suggest does not size); the recommendation follows the same objective. Apply sets the girder count, spacing, overhangs, plates, splices, stiffener setting, and cross-frame spacing (Revert restores the previous design). The result is still preliminary: run LL &amp; DL (lldf) for the chosen layout and complete the design checks in GirderDetail.</p>
 <h3>Suggest: lowest-cost layout</h3><p>Suggest proposes the web and flange layout and the field splices for the bridge on the Bridge tab, with one layout for all girders (designed for the envelope of the interior and exterior girders). It searches web depths from about L/36 to L/18 and, unless one is chosen, both an unstiffened and a transversely stiffened web, and keeps the layout with the <b>lowest total cost</b>: structural steel (weight × $/lb), flange shop transitions, transverse stiffeners, and field splices, each priced from the <b>Unit costs</b> on the Suggest tab, which are the same single price list used by the Alternatives study (and sent to GirderDetail's Design all). The defaults are placeholders; only their ratios affect the choice, and the tab shows each as an equivalent weight of steel. Within each field piece the flange width is constant and the thicknesses are chosen by an optimization that adds a transition only where it saves more than it costs. Field splices are placed by the program near the dead-load points of contraflexure and within the shipping length and weight, and moved off cross-frame locations where the framing check X4 finds a conflict.</p>
-<p><b>Rules.</b> AASHTO LRFD minimums always apply: D/t<sub>w</sub> ≤ 150, stiffened or not (Eq. 6.10.2.1.1-1, webs without longitudinal stiffeners), b<sub>f</sub>/2t<sub>f</sub> ≤ 12, b<sub>f</sub> ≥ D/6, t<sub>f</sub> ≥ 1.1t<sub>w</sub>, 0.1 ≤ I<sub>yc</sub>/I<sub>yt</sub> ≤ 10 (6.10.2.2), plates at least 5/16 in (6.7.3), and one steel grade (no hybrid girders). With the AASHTO/NSBA G12.1 fabrication guidelines on (the default), the Limits tab minimum sizes, increments, and transition ratios also apply. The Suggest setting can turn them off only when the Limits tab does not treat span-to-depth as mandatory; with "Treat span-to-depth (G1, G2) as mandatory" on, Suggest (fast and full design, the deck-width study, and the web economy comparison) always applies them, so it never proposes a girder that fails G1 or G2. Full design also requires the final plates of each candidate to meet the minimum depths, since resizing can thin the flanges.</p><p><b>Optimizing the framing.</b> Stiffener spacing and cross-frame spacing are design variables. For stiffened webs, the fast search tries d<sub>o</sub>/D = 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, and 3.0 (shear buckling coefficient k = 5 + 5/(d<sub>o</sub>/D)²): wider panels need fewer stiffeners but a thicker web, and the cost decides. Apply sets the Framing tab spacing and d<sub>o</sub>/D. The deck overhang is not modeled in sizing: GirderDetail's Deck overhang auto-design gives the largest spacing the deck placement allows at the exterior girder, so set the maximum spacing no higher than that.</p><p><b>Flange widths.</b> Every flange at a field splice is made wide enough for the number of bolt gage lines each side of the web set on the Suggest tab (default 2) without staggering, using the same geometry as GirderDetail's splice auto-design: the first line clear of the web splice plate by the plate clearance plus the edge distance and by the tightening clearance C₁, the gage between lines, and the edge distance at the flange tip (about 14 in for 7/8 in bolts and two lines). The top flange is kept at one width along the girder unless turned off (it simplifies the haunch and stay-in-place forms), and the width of either flange changes by no more than the set maximum at a field splice (default 4 in; 0 for no limit). Widths are raised, never reduced, to meet these rules, and the thicknesses are then optimized at those widths.</p>

Plates are only increased, never trimmed, so the quick suggestion passes the strength and service checks (the card says so, or names the ratio that still exceeds 1.0) but is not necessarily the lightest girder. The check runs in the background after the fast result appears (the card shows &ldquo;checking&rdquo; with a progress bar; typically a second or less after the fast result); a new edit restarts it, and Apply pressed during the check applies the checked result, after confirmation, when it is ready. The girder-count study and the Alternatives study use the fast sizing only, without this check, to rank layouts. <b>Run full design</b> optimizes for the least steel: it takes the best fast candidates and, for each, repeats: the staged, cracked analysis of the current layout (the Structural analysis settings); the AASHTO checks at every node for the interior and exterior girders, on both sides of every plate boundary (Strength I positive flexure with the plastic moment, compactness, D<sub>p</sub>/D<sub>t</sub>, and 1.3M<sub>y</sub>; Strength I negative flexure by 6.10.8 with flange local buckling, lateral-torsional buckling at the cross-frame spacing with C<sub>b</sub> from the quarter-point moments of each unbraced segment (10th Edition 6.10.8.2.3b: C<sub>b</sub> = 12.5M<sub>max</sub>/(2.5M<sub>max</sub> + 3M<sub>A</sub> + 4M<sub>B</sub> + 3M<sub>C</sub>), with M<sub>max</sub> the largest moment compressing the flange and M<sub>A</sub>, M<sub>B</sub>, M<sub>C</sub> the absolute envelope values at the quarter points (largest compression, or smallest tension where the flange is never in compression), as defined in 6.10.8.2.3b, Eq. 6.10.8.2.3b-1, with F<sub>nc</sub> by Eqs. 6.10.8.2.3a-2 to a-5; brace points at the supports and at the cross-frame spacing), and R<sub>b</sub>; where the section changes within the unbraced length, 6.10.8.2.3c: its simplification where it holds (one change to a smaller section within 0.2L<sub>b</sub> of the brace point with the smaller moment, the larger moment in the larger section, I<sub>y1</sub>/I<sub>y2</sub> ≥ 0.5: prismatic with the larger section), otherwise C<sub>b</sub> = 1.0 and F<sub>e</sub> = γ<sub>e</sub>f<sub>bu</sub> with r<sub>t</sub> = (L<sub>b</sub>/π)√(F<sub>e</sub>/E) (Eqs. c-1 to c-3), γ<sub>e</sub> by Appendix D6.6.2 Method A (γ<sub>e</sub> = χC<sub>be</sub>/(M<sub>u</sub>/M<sub>e1</sub>)<sub>max</sub>, Eqs. D6.6.2-1, D6.6.2-2, D6.6.2.2-1), or, where a flange's lateral moment of inertia changes by more than a factor 2.0 at a step (the D6.6.2.2 limit), the conservative bound (each section of the unbraced length as a prismatic member over L<sub>b</sub> under uniform moment at its largest stress), flagged for review; deck-placement lateral-torsional buckling also uses C<sub>b</sub> from the deck-placement moments, and the same nonprismatic rules; Service II flange stresses and web bend-buckling; deck-placement constructibility; flange fatigue, Fatigue I, Category B at the flange-to-web welds (extreme fiber) and Category C′ at the connection plates welded to the flanges (inner flange face, 6.6.1.3.1; checked at every analysis point along the girder, not only at the cross-frames, which is conservative), unless turned off or limited to Category B; and optionally L/800 deflection); and resizing, with each flange's required area set from the check ratio so plates are thickened where a check exceeds 1.0 and trimmed where there is spare capacity. When the layout stops changing it is verified against its own recomputed demands, and the cheapest passing candidate is selected. The result lists the governing check and ratio for every plate. Applying it replaces the girder layout (and the stiffener setting); Revert restores the previous design.</p>
 <p><b>Current girder compared with the suggestion.</b> Below the quick suggestion (or full design) card, the Suggest tab compares the current girder (the Girder tab plates and splices, with the Framing tab stiffeners and cross-frame spacing) with the suggestion, so you can see what the suggestion changes. The overall rows give the web depth and thickness, transverse stiffeners and d<sub>o</sub>/D, cross-frame spacing, field splices, shop transitions, steel per girder and per deck area, cost (Unit costs), the largest strength and service ratio, and the code proportion check counts, with each changed row highlighted. The top flange, web, and bottom flange are then compared plate by plate: the two plate lists are merged by station, so each row is a station range with the current and the suggested plate and what changes (for example &ldquo;t 1 1/8 &rarr; 1 1/4&rdquo;, &ldquo;b 16 &rarr; 15&rdquo;, &ldquo;new transition at 28 ft&rdquo;). A plot shows the flange thickness and width along the girder for both. The current girder is checked in the background with the same staged analysis and strength and service checks as the quick suggestion, at its own cross-frame spacing (an edit restarts the check); the card says whether a change is needed (the current girder exceeds 1.0, is shallower than the Table 2.5.2.6.3-1 minimum depth where that applies, or fails a code proportion check) or would only save steel and cost, and &ldquo;No change suggested&rdquo; when the suggestion is the same as the current girder. If the current girder has input errors, the card lists them instead. The comparison changes nothing until you press Apply.</p>
 <h3>Analysis model</h3><p>The analysis of the current design uses a variable-stiffness, staged line-girder model: DC1 on the steel section, DC2 and DW on the long-term composite section, and live load on the short-term composite section, with the composite stages cracked near interior supports. Its settings (staged or constant EI, cracked zones, deck reinforcement) are made in GirderDetail's Structural analysis module. Suggest mode searches trial layouts with the faster constant-EI model and then designs the chosen layout with the staged model.</p>

### TB1 (update). Every panel of a stiffened web within the 6.10.9.1 limits   [§4: design rule, engineer's decision 2026-10-13] [results: Suggest per-bay layouts; D4]
- **Where (decoded PL):** `tsDesignBay` (anchor `function tsDesignBay(B0, D, twAt, Fyw, vu, rat, tfa) {`), `framingChecks` D4 per-bay branch (anchor `else if (BM) { const grp2 = {};`), Suggest input note, `sgBaysCard` note, Manual Part 2 (Suggest rules) and Part 3 (D3/D4 not yet, see TB2).
- **Before (TB1 as first built):** a bay got no intermediate stiffener when its panels passed with the connection plates only, even if wider than 3D (an unstiffened panel, k = 5, 6.10.9.1/6.10.9.2); otherwise n started at ⌈L/3D⌉ − 1; an evenly spaced end bay could leave an end panel wider than 1.5D (unstiffened end panel, k = 5). D4 listed only bays with stiffeners; a wide even end panel was advisory.
  ```js
  const L = (B0.b - B0.a) * 12, ok = E => E.r <= 1 + 1e-9, ev = ...;
  let E = ev({ ...B0, n: 0 }); if (ok(E)) return E;
  ...
  const n0 = nE ? 1 : Math.max(1, Math.ceil(L / (3 * D) - 1e-9) - 1);
  for (let n = n0; n <= nHi; n++) { ... }
  ```
- **After:** engineer's rule (2026-10-13): in a stiffened web every panel is a stiffened panel, d<sub>o</sub> ≤ 3D interior and d<sub>o</sub> ≤ 1.5D at an end support. A layout is accepted only when every panel meets those limits and φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>n</sub> ≥ V<sub>u</sub>; n counts up from 0, so the first accepted layout is the fewest stiffeners that meet the limits (the largest spacing allowed), tightened only where shear needs it; end bays try even spacing, then an own end stiffener at the widest whole inch ≤ 1.5D that passes, the rest even. D4 lists every bay; interior panels > 3D and end panels > 1.5D fail (no advisory).
  ```js
  const L = (B0.b - B0.a) * 12, geo = E => E.pans.every(q => q.d <= (q.end ? 1.5 : 3) * D + 1e-9), ok = E => E.r <= 1 + 1e-9 && geo(E), ev = ...;
  let E = ev({ ...B0, n: 0 }); if (ok(E)) return E;
  ...
  for (let n = 1; n <= nHi + nE; n++) { E = ev({ ...B0, n }); if (ok(E)) return E; if (geo(E) || !geo(last)) last = E; /* end-stiffener variant as before */ }
  ```
- **Governing provisions:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.10.9.1 (interior panel stiffened when d<sub>o</sub> ≤ 3D; end panel when d<sub>o</sub> ≤ 1.5D), 6.10.9.3.3 (end panel ≤ 1.5D), 6.10.9.3.2.

The table lists N, S, overhang, d<sub>e</sub>, the factors, the section, the steel per girder and in total (lb/ft<sup>2</sup> of deck), the governing ratio of the layout checks, the bracing type from the girder depth, and pass/fail.  <p><b>Fast study, then full design of the best few.</b> The study sizes every girder count with Suggest's <i>fast sizing</i> (without the quick suggestion's strength and service check): one constant-stiffness continuous-beam model, flange areas from lever-arm estimates, and only this tool's layout checks (proportions, transitions, splices, framing), with no strength, service, or fatigue check. Plates are only increased, never trimmed, so the quick suggestion passes the strength and service checks (the card says so, or names the ratio that still exceeds 1.0) but is not necessarily the lightest girder. The check runs in the background after the fast result appears (the card shows &ldquo;checking&rdquo; with a progress bar; typically a second or less after the fast result); a new edit restarts it, and Apply pressed during the check applies the checked result, after confirmation, when it is ready. When the layout stops changing it is verified against its own recomputed demands, and the cheapest passing candidate is selected. The result lists the governing check and ratio for every plate. ### TB2. Preliminary sizing D3: stiffener moment of inertia with tension-field action (Eqs. 6.10.11.1.3-7 / -8), per-bay stiffeners   [§4: check added] [results: D3 of per-bay projects; uniform mode unchanged]
- **Where (decoded PL):** `framingChecks` signature (new optional `AN0`), D3 block (anchor `const c = { id: 'D3', grp, title: 'Stiffener and connection plate moment of inertia'`), `recompute` (the analysis now runs before `framingChecks`, which gets `AN`; the order of the checks in `C` is unchanged), Manual Part 3 (D3/D4 sentence).
- **Before:** D3 required I<sub>t</sub> ≥ I<sub>t1</sub> = b t<sub>w</sub>³ J (Eq. 6.10.11.1.3-1) only; per-bay mode used the narrowest panel of each field piece; its note said the tension-field requirement is not checked (GirderDetail TS3 checks it).
- **After (per-bay mode only; uniform mode unchanged):** every intermediate stiffener and connection plate (bearing stiffeners excluded: D5/D6) of every girder with its two adjacent panels: d<sub>o</sub> = the smaller panel, b = min(d<sub>o</sub>, D), J = max(2.5/(d<sub>o</sub>/D)² − 2, 0.5), I<sub>t1</sub> = b t<sub>w</sub>³ J; F<sub>crs</sub> = min(0.31E/(b<sub>t</sub>/t<sub>p</sub>)², F<sub>ys</sub>) (Eq. -6), ρ<sub>t</sub> = max(F<sub>yw</sub>/F<sub>crs</sub>, 1.0), I<sub>t2</sub> = D⁴ρ<sub>t</sub><sup>1.3</sup>/40 (F<sub>yw</sub>/E)<sup>1.5</sup> (Eq. -4). A panel relies on tension-field action when it is an interior stiffened panel, Suggest's tension-field setting is on, and V<sub>u</sub> > φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub>, V<sub>cr</sub> = CV<sub>p</sub> (Eq. -9) with k of the panel, V<sub>u</sub> the largest Strength I shear in the panel (Analysis tab, envelope of the girder types); ρ<sub>w</sub> = (V<sub>u</sub> − φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub>)/(φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>n</sub> − φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub>) ≤ 1, the larger of the two panels. ρ<sub>w</sub> > 0: I<sub>req</sub> = I<sub>t1</sub> + (I<sub>t2</sub> − I<sub>t1</sub>)ρ<sub>w</sub> if I<sub>t2</sub> > I<sub>t1</sub> (Eq. -7), else I<sub>t2</sub> (Eq. -8); otherwise I<sub>t1</sub> (Eq. -1, as before). The governing plate of each field piece and plate type is listed. Same equations as GirderDetail TS3.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.10.11.1.3, Eqs. 6.10.11.1.3-1, -3 to -10 (read from the 10th Ed. text: ρ<sub>w</sub> "maximum ratio … within the two web panels" when both rely on the tension field, else the one panel; V<sub>u</sub> = the maximum shear in the web panel under consideration).
- **Check case (built-in per-bay layout after Apply, D = 63 in, t<sub>w</sub> = 1/2 in, F<sub>yw</sub> = F<sub>ys</sub> = 50 ksi, stiffener 6 × 1/2 in):** G1 stiffener at 121.67 ft (field piece 2), panels 110–121.67 and 121.67–133.33 ft, both 140 in: J = max(2.5/2.222² − 2, 0.5) = 0.5, I<sub>t1</sub> = 63(0.5)³(0.5) = 3.94 in⁴; F<sub>crs</sub> = min(0.31·29,000/12², 50) = 50 ksi, ρ<sub>t</sub> = 1.0, I<sub>t2</sub> = 63⁴/40 × (50/29,000)<sup>1.5</sup> = 28.19 in⁴; panel 110–121.67: k = 6.0125, C = 0.3449, φV<sub>cr</sub> = 315.0 kip, φV<sub>n</sub> = 913.5(0.3449 + 0.2339) = 528.7 kip, V<sub>u</sub> = 396.8 kip → ρ<sub>w</sub> = (396.8 − 315.0)/(528.7 − 315.0) = 0.382; I<sub>req</sub> = 3.94 + (28.19 − 3.94)(0.382) = 13.22 in⁴ (Eq. -7) ≤ I<sub>t</sub> = 0.5(6)³/3 = 36.00 in⁴, ratio 0.367. Before: 3.94/36.00 = 0.110. D3 status pass before and after (largest 0.109 → 0.367); tension field off: 0.109 (ρ<sub>w</sub> = 0).
- **Suggest:** stiffener plate sizes come from the Framing tab (Suggest does not size them), so the stiffener cost per plate is unchanged; D3 now reports when the plate is too small for the tension field Suggest relied on (GirderDetail's auto-design sizes plates with TS3).
- **Open item:** for panels not relying on the tension field the 10th Ed. text requires I<sub>t</sub> ≥ the smaller of I<sub>t1</sub> and I<sub>t2</sub> (Eqs. -1, -2); D3 and GirderDetail TS3 both require I<sub>t1</sub> (conservative when I<sub>t2</sub> < I<sub>t1</sub>). Not changed (ENGINEER_CHECKS GD33).
- **How verified:** see TB3.

 <h3>Detailing checks</h3>
 <p>Transverse stiffeners and connection plates (which act as stiffeners) must satisfy 6.10.11.1.2 and 6.10.11.1.3:</p>

Connection plates use d<sub>o</sub> equal to the stiffener spacing if stiffeners are present, otherwise the cross-frame spacing. With per-bay stiffeners, D3 uses the narrowest panel in each field piece and D4 lists every bay with intermediate stiffeners (interior panels against 3D; an end panel with its own stiffener against 1.5D; a wider end panel of an evenly spaced bay is an unstiffened end panel, advisory). Bearing stiffeners satisfy b<sub>t</sub> ≤ 0.48t<sub>p</sub>√(E/F<sub>ys</sub>) (6.10.11.2.2) and must fit within the bottom flange (practice).</p>

### TB3. Web shear and stiffener checks with the largest V<sub>u</sub> in each panel (6.10.9.3.1): Transverse stiffeners TS4/TS3, Girder section GS11, Preliminary sizing rows   [§4: demand definition] [results: TS4, TS3 ρ<sub>w</sub>, GS11 of every project once its rows are re-sent; old rows unchanged until then]
- **Where:** decoded PL `detailExport`: new `shearP`, `uniOf`, `gsPan`, `gsDo` (reworked), TS rows (anchor `[[x0 + doFt, k, 1], [x1 - doFt, k + 1, -1]].forEach`) and cross-frame row, gs rows (`gsRow`, `gP`). GirderDetail page: `TS_ROWSPEC` / `TS_BRG` / new `TS_PN2`, TS `compute` (anchor `r.VuB = `), TS3 and TS4 notes and TS4 work line, Manual "Web shear (6.10.9)"; `GS_SPEC` / new `GS_PAN`, GS `compute` (anchor `r.Vu = G.dc * (r.VDC1 + r.VDC2)`), GS11.
- **Before:** TS4 checked both panels at a stiffener with V<sub>u</sub> at the stiffener, except an end panel (largest V<sub>u</sub> in it, from the optional end-panel shears `VDC1b…VLLb`, sent for end rows only); TS3's ρ<sub>w</sub> used V<sub>u</sub> at the stiffener for both panels; GS11 used V<sub>u</sub> at the location.
  ```js
  r.VuB = r.end === 'yes' && r.VDC1b != null ? g('dc') * (r.VDC1b + r.VDC2b) + g('dw') * r.VDWb + g('ll') * r.VLLb : null;
  r.Vu1 = r.VuB != null ? Math.max(r.VuB, r.Vu) : r.Vu;
  ... q.Vu = i ? r.Vu : r.Vu1; ... q.rho = tfa && r.Vu > PHI.v * q.Vcr ? Math.min(1, (r.Vu - PHI.v * q.Vcr) / ...
  ```
- **After:** every TS row carries the largest shears in panel 1 (`VDC1b…VLLb`, now for every row) and in panel 2 (new optional `VDC1c…VLLc`); TS4 and TS3's ρ<sub>w</sub> use V<sub>u</sub> = max(the panel's largest, the shear at the stiffener) for each panel; a panel with blank shears (rows saved before, or typed) uses the shear at the stiffener and the item says so. Every gs row carries the largest shears in the web panel containing x (new optional `VDC1p…VLLp`): per-bay mode the panel of that girder's layout (at a boundary, the panel with the larger V<sub>u</sub>/V<sub>n</sub>), uniform mode the panel as the drawings place the stiffeners (at a boundary, the larger shear); GS11 uses V<sub>u</sub> = max(at the location, largest in the panel). Panel geometry for TS rows: per bay, the actual panels; uniform, the support or cross-frame and d<sub>o</sub> on each side.
  ```js
  r.VuB = r.VDC1b != null ? g('dc') * (r.VDC1b + r.VDC2b) + g('dw') * r.VDWb + g('ll') * r.VLLb : null;
  r.VuC = r.VDC1c != null ? g('dc') * (r.VDC1c + r.VDC2c) + g('dw') * r.VDWc + g('ll') * r.VLLc : null;
  r.Vu1 = r.VuB != null ? Math.max(r.VuB, r.Vu) : r.Vu; r.Vu2 = r.VuC != null ? Math.max(r.VuC, r.Vu) : r.Vu;
  ... q.Vu = i ? r.Vu2 : r.Vu1; q.pan = (i ? r.VuC : r.VuB) != null; ... q.rho = tfa && q.Vu > PHI.v * q.Vcr ? Math.min(1, (q.Vu - PHI.v * q.Vcr) / ...
  r.VuP = r.VDC1p != null ? Math.max(r.Vu, G.dc * (r.VDC1p + r.VDC2p) + G.dw * r.VDWp + G.ll * r.VLLp) : null;   // GS11
  ```
- **Saved data (§5):** new optional row fields only (`VDC1c…VLLc` on TS rows; `VDC1p…VLLp` on GS rows); the meaning of `VDC1b…VLLb` widens from "end panel 1" to "panel 1" (old rows had them only on end rows, with that meaning). Old rows without the fields compute as before; Preliminary sizing re-sends rows when it recomputes (Design all, Get demands, its automatic hand-off), and those carry the new fields.
- **Governing provisions:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.10.9.3.1 ("The required transverse stiffener spacing shall be calculated using the maximum shear in a panel"); 6.10.11.1.3 (V<sub>u</sub> = maximum shear due to the factored loads in the web panel under consideration, for ρ<sub>w</sub>); 6.10.9.1 (Eq. 6.10.9.1-1).

 <h3>Proportions (6.10.11.1.2)</h3><div class="eq-math">\\[b_t \\ge 2.0 + \\frac{D}{30}, \\qquad 16t_p \\ge b_t \\ge \\frac{b_f}{4}\\]</div><p>b<sub>f</sub> is the full width of the widest compression flange in the field section.</p>
 <h3>Moment of inertia (6.10.11.1.3)</h3><div class="eq-math">\\[I_{t1} = b\\,t_w^3J,\\ J = \\frac{2.5}{(d_o/D)^2} - 2.0 \\ge 0.5; \\qquad I_{t2} = \\frac{D^4\\rho_t^{1.3}}{40}\\left(\\frac{F_{yw}}{E}\\right)^{1.5},\\ \\rho_t = \\max\\left(\\frac{F_{yw}}{F_{crs}}, 1\\right),\\ F_{crs} = \\frac{0.31E}{(b_t/t_p)^2} \\le F_{ys}\\]</div>
 <p>d<sub>o</sub> is the smaller adjacent panel and b the smaller of d<sub>o</sub> and D. Where neither panel needs tension-field action, I<sub>t</sub> ≥ I<sub>t1</sub>. Otherwise I<sub>t</sub> ≥ I<sub>t1</sub> + (I<sub>t2</sub> − I<sub>t1</sub>)ρ<sub>w</sub> when I<sub>t2</sub> > I<sub>t1</sub>, else I<sub>t</sub> ≥ I<sub>t2</sub>, with ρ<sub>w</sub> the larger of (V<sub>u</sub> − φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub>)/(φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>n</sub> − φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub>) in the two panels (confirm the equation numbering against your edition). I<sub>t</sub> is taken about the web face for a single plate and about the web mid-thickness for a pair.</p>
-<h3>Web shear (6.10.9)</h3><p>Each adjacent panel is checked for V<sub>u</sub> ≤ φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>n</sub> with k = 5 + 5/(d<sub>o</sub>/D)². Interior panels include tension-field action (Eq. 6.10.9.3.2-2 or -8 depending on 2Dt<sub>w</sub>/(b<sub>fc</sub>t<sub>fc</sub> + b<sub>ft</sub>t<sub>ft</sub>)); end panels use V<sub>n</sub> = CV<sub>p</sub> (Eq. 6.10.9.3.3-1). An interior panel wider than 3D or an end panel wider than 1.5D is not a stiffened panel (6.10.9.1): it is checked as unstiffened, k = 5 and V<sub>n</sub> = CV<sub>p</sub> (Eq. 6.10.9.2-1). V<sub>u</sub> is the Strength I shear at the stiffener for both panels, except that an end panel is checked with the largest V<sub>u</sub> in it (at the bearing): the location's end-panel shears (V<sub>DC1</sub>, V<sub>DC2</sub>, V<sub>DW</sub>, V<sub>LL+IM</sub>, the largest in panel 1, sent by Preliminary sizing and Structural analysis) give that V<sub>u</sub>, and the larger of it and the shear at the stiffener is used. When they are blank (projects saved before they existed, or entered by hand), the end panel uses the shear at the stiffener and the TS4 item says so. Check TS5 compares each panel with these limits, which decide only whether the panel counts as stiffened: a panel wider than its limit is advisory, because TS4 checks it as unstiffened (k = 5) and decides pass or fail. When the web has no intermediate stiffeners (connection plates only), it is designed as unstiffened and TS5 is not applicable.</p>
+<h3>Web shear (6.10.9)</h3><p>Each adjacent panel is checked for V<sub>u</sub> ≤ φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>n</sub> with k = 5 + 5/(d<sub>o</sub>/D)². Interior panels include tension-field action (Eq. 6.10.9.3.2-2 or -8 depending on 2Dt<sub>w</sub>/(b<sub>fc</sub>t<sub>fc</sub> + b<sub>ft</sub>t<sub>ft</sub>)); end panels use V<sub>n</sub> = CV<sub>p</sub> (Eq. 6.10.9.3.3-1). An interior panel wider than 3D or an end panel wider than 1.5D is not a stiffened panel (6.10.9.1): it is checked as unstiffened, k = 5 and V<sub>n</sub> = CV<sub>p</sub> (Eq. 6.10.9.2-1). V<sub>u</sub> is the largest Strength I shear in each panel (6.10.9.3.1): the location's panel shears (V<sub>DC1</sub>, V<sub>DC2</sub>, V<sub>DW</sub>, V<sub>LL+IM</sub>, the largest in panel 1 and in panel 2, sent by Preliminary sizing and Structural analysis) give it, and the larger of it and the shear at the stiffener is used; ρ<sub>w</sub> of TS3 uses the same V<sub>u</sub>. When a panel's shears are blank (projects saved before they existed, or entered by hand), that panel uses the shear at the stiffener and the TS4 item says so. Check TS5 compares each panel with these limits, which decide only whether the panel counts as stiffened: a panel wider than its limit is advisory, because TS4 checks it as unstiffened (k = 5) and decides pass or fail. When the web has no intermediate stiffeners (connection plates only), it is designed as unstiffened and TS5 is not applicable.</p>
 <h3>Welds and fatigue</h3><p>Intermediate stiffener web welds stop 4t<sub>w</sub> to 6t<sub>w</sub> from the web-to-flange weld at the tension flange (6.10.11.1.1). Connection plates are welded to both flanges and those welds are designed for 20 kip laterally on straight, nonskewed bridges, or the analysis force otherwise (6.6.1.3.1). Base metal at stiffener weld toes is Category C′, (ΔF)<sub>TH</sub> = 12 ksi. Minimum fillet sizes follow Table 6.13.3.4-1.</p>

## 2026-10-13 — PR: claude/gd-stiffener-it-rule (transverse stiffener moment of inertia: the smaller of I<sub>t1</sub> and I<sub>t2</sub> where no panel relies on the tension field; engineer's decision 2026-10-13, ENGINEER_CHECKS GD33; PR link added after merge)

### IT1. Transverse stiffener and connection plate moment of inertia per AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.10.11.1.3 where neither adjacent panel relies on tension-field action: GirderDetail TS3, Preliminary sizing D3 (per-bay and uniform)   [§4: requirement changed, less conservative where I<sub>t2</sub> < I<sub>t1</sub>; code references corrected] [results: TS3/D3 required I<sub>t</sub> and ratio only where I<sub>t2</sub> < I<sub>t1</sub>; Auto-design (Transverse stiffeners) plate sizes there]
- **Where (GirderDetail page):** `GM.ts.compute` (anchor `r.Ireq = r.rhow`), TS3 in `GM.ts.checks` (anchor `{ const c = { id: 'TS3', grp: G1, title: 'Moment of inertia'`: `ref`, `sym`, `note`, work line `I_{req} &=`), Manual "Moment of inertia (6.10.11.1.3)". **Where (decoded PL page, `const PL_B64`):** `framingChecks` D3 (anchor `const c = { id: 'D3', grp, title: 'Stiffener and connection plate moment of inertia'`): `ref`, `sym`, `note` (both modes), new helpers `d3Br` / `d3Pre` just before the D3 block, the per-bay loop (anchor `const rw = Math.max(rho(Lp), rho(Rp))`), the uniform loop (anchor `plates.forEach(([n, b, t, dd0]) => pieceInfo.forEach(({ p, tw }) => { const dd = dd0;`), Manual "Detailing checks".
- **Before:** TS3 required I<sub>t</sub> ≥ I<sub>t1</sub> = b t<sub>w</sub>³J whenever ρ<sub>w</sub> = 0 (neither panel relying on the tension field), Eq. -7/-8 otherwise, but labelled the equations with the former numbering (interpolation "Eq. 6.10.11.1.3-2", I<sub>t2</sub> "Eq. 6.10.11.1.3-3"). D3 per-bay required I<sub>t1</sub> where ρ<sub>w</sub> = 0, Eq. -7/-8 otherwise; D3 uniform required I<sub>t1</sub> always (note: "tension-field requirement (Eq. 6.10.11.1.3-2) is not checked").
- **After:** a panel "supports V<sub>u</sub> > φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub>" with V<sub>cr</sub> = CV<sub>p</sub> (Eq. 6.10.11.1.3-9), C with k of the panel (k = 5 unstiffened, Eq. 6.10.9.3.2-7 stiffened, end panels included), φ<sub>v</sub> = 1.0, V<sub>u</sub> the largest Strength I shear in the panel (as TS4 / TB3).
  - Neither adjacent panel with V<sub>u</sub> > φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub>: I<sub>req</sub> = min(I<sub>t1</sub>, I<sub>t2</sub>) (Eqs. 6.10.11.1.3-1, -2; the work line names -2 when I<sub>t2</sub> < I<sub>t1</sub>, else -1).
  - A panel relying on tension-field action (ρ<sub>w</sub> > 0): unchanged, I<sub>t1</sub> + (I<sub>t2</sub> − I<sub>t1</sub>)ρ<sub>w</sub> if I<sub>t2</sub> > I<sub>t1</sub> (Eq. 6.10.11.1.3-7), else I<sub>t2</sub> (Eq. 6.10.11.1.3-8). TS3 now prints -7 / -8 (were -2 / -3; same expressions).
  - A panel with V<sub>u</sub> > φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub> that cannot use the tension field (end panel, unstiffened panel, Suggest's tension field off): I<sub>t1</sub> as before (that panel fails its shear check, TS4).
  - No analysis shears (D3 without an Analysis tab result; the Alternatives, girder-count and deck-width studies call `framingChecks` without it): I<sub>t1</sub> as before.
  - D3 uniform: per plate type and field piece, the largest V<sub>u</sub> (Analysis envelope of the girder types) within 1.5d<sub>o</sub> of the piece (the last panel of a uniform bay can be up to 1.5d<sub>o</sub>) against φ<sub>v</sub>CV<sub>p</sub> with k of d<sub>o</sub> (the smaller of the interior and end-panel values where an end support lies in that range) and the thinnest web there; the tension-field requirement (Eqs. -7/-8) is still not checked in uniform mode (GD34).
  - The work line of every TS3/D3 item now shows V<sub>u</sub> vs φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub> for the panel(s), the branch (no tension field / tension field / tension field not used) and the governing equation.
  - Exact code: diffs below.
- **Problem:** the 10th Ed. text requires only the smaller of I<sub>t1</sub> and I<sub>t2</sub> for stiffeners adjacent to panels not subject to post-buckling tension-field action; requiring I<sub>t1</sub> was conservative where I<sub>t2</sub> < I<sub>t1</sub> (closely spaced stiffeners, d<sub>o</sub>/D below about 1.12 where J > 0.5, thicker webs). The change is **less conservative** in exactly those cases and identical elsewhere.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.10.11.1.3: Eqs. 6.10.11.1.3-1 and -2 ("the smaller of the following limits" for panels where neither supports V<sub>u</sub> > φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub>), -3 (I<sub>t1</sub>), -4 (I<sub>t2</sub>), -5 (J), -6 (F<sub>crs</sub>), -7/-8 (panels subject to tension-field action, ρ<sub>w</sub>), -9 (V<sub>cr</sub> = CV<sub>p</sub>), -10 (V<sub>p</sub>); 6.5.4.2 (φ<sub>v</sub> = 1.0).
- **Check case 1 (no tension field, changes; GirderDetail Transverse stiffeners, built-in input with d<sub>o</sub> = 30 in on both sides of location 1):** D = 60 in, t<sub>w</sub> = 0.5625 in, F<sub>yw</sub> = F<sub>ys</sub> = 50 ksi, single plate 6 × 1/2 in: I<sub>t</sub> = 0.5(6)³/3 = 36.00 in⁴. J = 2.5/(30/60)² − 2.0 = 8.0, b = min(30, 60) = 30 in, I<sub>t1</sub> = 30(0.5625)³(8.0) = 42.71 in⁴. F<sub>crs</sub> = min(0.31(29,000)/(6/0.5)², 50) = 50 ksi, ρ<sub>t</sub> = 1.0, I<sub>t2</sub> = 60⁴/40 × (50/29,000)<sup>1.5</sup> = 324,000 × 7.159×10⁻⁵ = 23.20 in⁴.  <p>Girders are placed at y = 0, S, 2S, … and each support line passes through the bridge centerline station at its skew angle, so the bearing of girder i at support k is at x = X<sub>k</sub> + (y<sub>i</sub> − y<sub>c</sub>)tan θ<sub>k</sub>. A cross-frame is placed in every bay along every bearing line. Between bearing lines, n = ⌈L/s⌉ − 1 intermediate frames are placed, where s is the target spacing. Parallel frames interpolate between the two bearing lines. Normal frames are placed at even stations (offset by half a spacing in alternate bays if staggered), dropped where they would fall within the clear distance of a skewed bearing line, and supplemented near the acute corners so no girder exceeds the target spacing. If any frame falls within the splice clearance of a field splice or shop transition, up to three additional frames per span are tried and the layout with the fewest conflicts is kept.</p>
 <h3>Detailing checks</h3>
 <p>Transverse stiffeners and connection plates (which act as stiffeners) must satisfy 6.10.11.1.2 and 6.10.11.1.3:</p>
-<div class="eq-math">\\[b_t \\ge 2.0 + \\frac{D}{30}, \\qquad 16t_p \\ge b_t \\ge \\frac{b_f}{4}, \\qquad I_t = \\frac{t_p b_t^3}{3} \\ge b\\,t_w^3 J, \\quad J = \\frac{2.5}{(d_o/D)^2} - 2.0 \\ge 0.5\\]</div>
-<p>b<sub>f</sub> is the widest flange in the field piece (conservatively either flange), t<sub>w</sub> the thickest web in the piece, and b the smaller of d<sub>o</sub> and D. Connection plates use d<sub>o</sub> equal to the stiffener spacing if stiffeners are present, otherwise the cross-frame spacing. With per-bay stiffeners, D3 checks every intermediate stiffener and connection plate with its two adjacent panels, adding Eq. 6.10.11.1.3-7 or -8 where a panel relies on tension-field action (ρ<sub>w</sub> from the largest V<sub>u</sub> in each panel), and D4 lists every bay (interior panels against 3D, end panels against 1.5D). Bearing stiffeners satisfy b<sub>t</sub> ≤ 0.48t<sub>p</sub>√(E/F<sub>ys</sub>) (6.10.11.2.2) and must fit within the bottom flange (practice).</p>
+<div class="eq-math">\\[b_t \\ge 2.0 + \\frac{D}{30}, \\qquad 16t_p \\ge b_t \\ge \\frac{b_f}{4}, \\qquad I_t = \\frac{t_p b_t^3}{3} \\ge \\min(I_{t1}, I_{t2}), \\quad I_{t1} = b\\,t_w^3 J, \\quad J = \\frac{2.5}{(d_o/D)^2} - 2.0 \\ge 0.5, \\quad I_{t2} = \\frac{D^4\\rho_t^{1.3}}{40}\\left(\\frac{F_{yw}}{E}\\right)^{1.5}\\]</div>
+<p>b<sub>f</sub> is the widest flange in the field piece (conservatively either flange), t<sub>w</sub> the thickest web in the piece, and b the smaller of d<sub>o</sub> and D. Connection plates use d<sub>o</sub> equal to the stiffener spacing if stiffeners are present, otherwise the cross-frame spacing. AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.10.11.1.3: where neither adjacent panel carries V<sub>u</sub> > φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub> (V<sub>cr</sub> = CV<sub>p</sub>, Eq. 6.10.11.1.3-9), the web does not rely on tension-field action and I<sub>t</sub> need only satisfy the smaller of I<sub>t1</sub> (Eq. 6.10.11.1.3-1) and I<sub>t2</sub> (Eq. 6.10.11.1.3-2); I<sub>t2</sub> uses ρ<sub>t</sub> = max(F<sub>yw</sub>/F<sub>crs</sub>, 1.0), F<sub>crs</sub> = 0.31E/(b<sub>t</sub>/t<sub>p</sub>)² ≤ F<sub>ys</sub>. D3 takes V<sub>u</sub> from the Analysis tab (uniform spacing: the largest within 1.5d<sub>o</sub> of the field piece); without an analysis result, or where a panel carries more than φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub>, I<sub>t1</sub> is required (uniform spacing does not check the tension-field requirement). The item's work line shows which equation governs. With per-bay stiffeners, D3 checks every intermediate stiffener and connection plate with its two adjacent panels, adding Eq. 6.10.11.1.3-7 or -8 where a panel relies on tension-field action (ρ<sub>w</sub> from the largest V<sub>u</sub> in each panel), and D4 lists every bay (interior panels against 3D, end panels against 1.5D). Bearing stiffeners satisfy b<sub>t</sub> ≤ 0.48t<sub>p</sub>√(E/F<sub>ys</sub>) (6.10.11.2.2) and must fit within the bottom flange (practice).</p>
 <h3>Camber and deflection</h3>
 <p>Moments come from the constant-EI influence lines described in the Suggest methodology. Deflections are then computed by virtual work with the actual stiffness at each point:</p>
 <div class="eq-math">\\[\\Delta(x) = \\int \\frac{M(s)\\,m_x(s)}{E\\,I(s)}\\,ds\\]</div>

### IT2. Preliminary sizing D3, uniform spacing: Eq. 6.10.11.1.3-7 / -8 where an interior stiffened panel relies on tension-field action   [§4: requirement added, more conservative] [results: D3 uniform mode only where the largest V<sub>u</sub> near a field piece exceeds φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub> of an interior stiffened panel]

GirderDetail page: only the `PL_B64` line.
- **Before (IT1):** uniform mode per plate type and field piece, with V<sub>u</sub> the largest Strength I shear (analysis envelope) within 1.5d<sub>o</sub> of the piece: V<sub>u</sub> ≤ φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub> (smaller of the interior and, where an end support is in range, the end-panel value) → min(I<sub>t1</sub>, I<sub>t2</sub>); otherwise I<sub>t1</sub>; Eqs. -7/-8 never checked. `req = nt ? Math.min(It1, It2) : It1`.
- **After:** the interior panel at d<sub>o</sub> (thinnest web in the range, largest 2Dt<sub>w</sub>/(b<sub>fc</sub>t<sub>fc</sub> + b<sub>ft</sub>t<sub>ft</sub>) in the range) with tension-field action: `Vi = tsVn(D, twm, Fyw, dd, false, fns.rat(a, z), true)`, φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub> = φ<sub>v</sub>CV<sub>p</sub>; where it is a stiffened panel (d<sub>o</sub> ≤ 3D, `Vi.tfa`) and V<sub>u</sub> > φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub>: ρ<sub>w</sub> = min(1, (V<sub>u</sub> − φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub>)/(φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>n</sub> − φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub>)), I<sub>req</sub> = I<sub>t1</sub> + (I<sub>t2</sub> − I<sub>t1</sub>)ρ<sub>w</sub> if I<sub>t2</sub> > I<sub>t1</sub> (Eq. -7), else I<sub>t2</sub> (Eq. -8): `req = rw > 0 ? (It2 > It1 ? It1 + (It2 - It1) * rw : It2) : nt ? Math.min(It1, It2) : It1`. Unchanged: no panel over φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub> → min(I<sub>t1</sub>, I<sub>t2</sub>); only an end panel or an unstiffened panel (d<sub>o</sub> > 3D, e.g. connection plates only) over φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub> → I<sub>t1</sub> (GD34 (b), engineer-accepted); no analysis → I<sub>t1</sub> (GD34 (c)). As GirderDetail TS3, the tension field is taken as relied on whenever an interior stiffened panel exceeds φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub> (Suggest's tension-field setting is a per-bay design option and is not applied in uniform mode). More conservative; identical where no interior stiffened panel exceeds φ<sub>v</sub>V<sub>cr</sub>.

## 2026-10-13 — PR: claude/gd-crossframe-dc1 (DC1 includes the cross-frame and diaphragm weight, computed from the Cross-frames module; engineer's decision 2026-10-13; PR link added after merge)

### XF1. Cross-frames and diaphragms as DC1 point loads on the steel section   [results change: DC1 and everything fed by it; §4 callout in the PR]
- **Where (GirderDetail, outer page):**
  - New helpers after `cfDiaEnd` (anchor `const cfDiaEnd = q =>`, about line 2706): `XF_ROW`, `gdXfW`, `gdXfModel`, `gdXfPts`, `gdXfNodal`, `gdXfPost`, `gdXfDesc`, `gdXfDupRows`, `gdXfAlerts`, and a click handler for `[data-xfack]`.

  - `recompute()` (anchor `gdFatPost();   // F12-1`) and the `gd-bridge` listener (anchor `gdFatPost(); gdXfPost();`); `gdXfPost` also sends `pl-bridge-req` when the stored bridge has no frame list (a project saved before XF1, or loaded in the running session), so Preliminary sizing publishes it again.
  - `gmRecompute` (anchor `gdXfAlerts(m.id === 'df'`): the notice in every module, the double-count warning in LLDF and DLs and Structural analysis.
  - The bridge listener's "real change" test `nx` (anchor `const nx = o => {`): before `JSON.stringify({ ...o, ts: 0, xs: 0 })`, after `const { ts, xs, xf, ...r } = o; return JSON.stringify(r);`. The frame list is not a bridge change for the automatic refresh, and the keys are removed rather than zeroed (zeroing appended `xs` after `xf` on a bridge without `xs`, so the key order differed and every module was re-imported on first open).
  - `initP` and `loadData` (`gdXfMark`).
- **Where (embedded Preliminary sizing, `const PL_B64`, decoded):** new `plXfW`, `plXfLoads` before `function framingLayout(P, m)`; `suggestLayout` (anchor `const XFL = plXfLoads(`); `demand()` (anchor `const XT = XFL && XFL.types[gt]`) and its `out.types[gt]` (`wXF`, `xf`, `xfErr`); `analyzeGirder` (anchor `const wSteel = Tg.wXF ?`); `bridgeDef` (`xf` excluded from the analysis echo; `xf: plXfDef(FR)`); new `plXfDef` before `let _bdT = null`; new `plXfRow` before `function renderAnalysis()` and its use in the Suggest loads table; the camber caption; the manual DC1 paragraph.
- **Problem / request:** GirderDetail's DC1 had no cross-frame or diaphragm weight unless the user entered a DC1 row (the Preliminary sizing "Detail allowance" covers only stiffeners, connection plates and splices). Engineer's decision 2026-10-13: add it by default, computed from the frames. More conservative (DC1 larger).
- **What is computed:**
  - Weight of one frame (kip), length S between the girder webs along the frame line (from Preliminary sizing's framing; S = bay/cos θ for frames along the skew), steel 490 pcf = 0.2836 lb/in³, × (1 + gusset/bolt allowance %, default 0):
    - cross-frame of angles (Cross-frames module): X: (S·A_top + S·A_bot + 2·√(S² + h²)·A_diag); Kb and Kt: (S·A_top + S·A_bot + 2·√((S/2)² + h²)·A_diag), work point to work point; end (bearing-line) frames X-type with the same angles (as Design all's quantities, GD22);
    - diaphragm (when it is the bracing used): A · (S − 2 · gap), gap = `cfDiaGap` (bolt line less 1.5 in), end diaphragms `cfDiaEnd` (as Design all);
    - entered weights (option): W_int, W_end kip per frame.
  - Each frame puts W/2 on each of the two girders it connects, at that girder's own station (Preliminary sizing's `framingLayout`: skewed, normal and staggered frames as laid out there), mapped into the analysis span proportionally between that girder's bearings; frames on a bearing line load the bearing only.
  - Node loads: a point load P at x between nodes x_e and x_e+1 (about 1 ft apart) adds P(1 − t)/trib_e and P·t/trib_e+1 klf, t = (x − x_e)/(x_e+1 − x_e).
  - Applied with the steel (steel section, before the deck): Structural analysis `wSX = wSt + wXF` gives `MS`, `VS`, `w1`, the deck-sequence stage 0, the camber "Steel" column and the ST-Girder `M_DC1steel`/`V_DC1steel`; Preliminary sizing adds `wXF` to `w1` (all its DC1 demands, quick suggestion, Full design, Alternatives) and to the steel camber.
  - Preliminary sizing per girder type: the girder of that type with the largest frame total (built-in: G2 interior, G1 exterior); the framing of the current girder layout is used for every candidate.
- **Saved data:** new optional fields only. `df.dl.xf` ('auto' default / 'ovr' / 'off'), `df.dl.xfAllow` (%), `df.dl.xfInt`, `df.dl.xfEnd` (kip); `df.xfNew` (notice flag, set on load for projects saved without `df.dl.xf`, removed by Dismiss); `df.bridge.xf` (frames from Preliminary sizing); Preliminary sizing `analysis.xf` (the weight model, from the gd-an message, not echoed in `bridge.analysis`). Projects saved before this change get 'auto' (on) and a notice. No key renamed or removed; storage keys unchanged.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 3.5.1 (DC: dead load of structural components and nonstructural attachments) and 6.10.1.1.1a (stresses from permanent loads applied before the deck is composite act on the steel section alone). Unit weight of steel 0.490 kcf (Table 3.5.1-1).
- **Check case (hand):** simple span 120 ft, 5 girders at 9.5 ft, skew 0, Kb frames h = 52 in, top chord L5x5x3/8 (A = 3.609 in²), bottom chord and diagonals L3x3x3/8 (A = 2.109 in²), frames at 24, 48, 72 and 96 ft:
  - intermediate W = [114(3.609 + 2.109) + 2√(57² + 52²)(2.109)](0.2836)/1000 = (651.94 + 325.50)(0.2836)/1000 = 0.2772 kip; per girder per frame 0.1386 kip;
  - end frame (X) W = [651.94 + 2√(114² + 52²)(2.109)](0.2836)/1000 = 0.3348 kip; 0.1674 kip per girder;
  - interior G2 (two frames at each station): P = 0.2772 kip at 24, 48, 72, 96 ft; ΔM(60 ft) = 0.2772 × (12 + 24 + 24 + 12) = 19.959 kip-ft; ΔR = 0.2772 × 2.0 + 0.3348 = 0.8892 kip;
  - program G2: M_DC1(60) 2483.696 → 2503.654 (Δ 19.958); R_DC1 82.790 → 83.679 (Δ 0.889); G1: Δ 9.979 kip-ft, ΔR 0.4446 kip; steel camber at midspan Δ 0.03669 in (hand Σ 2P a(3L² − 4a²)/48EI with I = 49,019 in⁴: 0.03668 in).
- **Built-in example and xsA:** see the PR (§4 table). As shipped, the built-in Cross-frames module has no design yet, so the default X-frames are used: L5x5x3/8, h = 48 in, 0.502 kip each; G2 8.54 kip; SA G2 M<sub>DC1</sub> +1008.35 → +1025.67 kip-ft. After its Get demands (auto-designed Kb frames), built-in G2: M_DC1 +1008.35 → +1018.19 kip-ft (321 ft), −2382.58 → −2403.94 (Pier 2); R_DC1 Abut. 51.844 → 52.567, Pier 192.927 → 194.752 kip; camber 1.9024 → 1.9156 in.
- **How verified:** script blocks parse (node --check, outer page and decoded Preliminary sizing). Headless Chromium on the built-in example, xsA, curb and a 30° staggered variant: with the setting forced off (test copy), every check and number of every module (as loaded, and after Get demands from 'pl' and 'sa:2' in 9 modules) is identical to main; the only differences are the new optional fields in stored objects and the new display (LLDF and DLs card and line, Structural analysis text); with it on, only DC1-dependent results change, all in the expected direction (equilibrium: ΣR_DC1 increases by exactly the frame total); Get demands (sa:G) rows equal the Any location rows; save/load both ways; ST-Girder hand-off M_DC1 = steel + wet within 0.001 at all 363 stations, the wet part unchanged and the steel part larger by the frame moments; no console errors.
- **Other copies:** none (the weight function is in both the outer page, `gdXfW`, and the embedded Preliminary sizing, `plXfW`; keep them identical).
- **Note:** the frame weights are those of the Cross-frames module when the demands are computed. Get demands and Design all auto-design the Cross-frames module after importing, so after its member sizes change, get the demands again to carry the new weights (the next import uses them).
- **Open items:** ENGINEER_CHECKS GD35 (gusset/bolt allowance default 0%; work-point member lengths; end frames X-type; representative girder per type in Preliminary sizing; no automatic re-import of stored detail-module demands for old projects).

#### Exact changes, outer page (`git diff -U1`, the `PL_B64` line omitted)
```diff
@@ -2360,3 +2360,3 @@ function showManPart() { const id = P.ui.man || 'p1'; $$('.man-btn').forEach(b =
 
 /* =====================================================================
@@ -2706,2 +2706,71 @@ const cfDiaGap = q => Math.max(0.5, (+q.ecc || 3.5) - 1.5);
 const cfDiaEnd = q => ({ ...q, shape: q.eShape || q.shape, nb: +q.eNb >= 2 ? q.eNb : q.nb });
+/* ---------- cross-frame and diaphragm weight in DC1 (XF1, engineer's decision 2026-10-13) ----------
+   DC1 includes the cross-frames or diaphragms as point loads at every frame, on the steel section (steel erected before the deck): each frame weighs
+   W and puts W/2 on each of the two girders it connects (an exterior girder gets one side, an interior girder both), at that girder's own frame
+   stations from Preliminary sizing's framing (skewed and staggered frames as laid out there; bridge.xf). Setting df.dl.xf (LLDF and DLs module):
+   'auto' (default, also for projects saved before): from the Cross-frames module's member sizes; 'ovr': entered kip per frame; 'off': none.
+   Weight model X:
+     kind 'xf': angles, type X / Kb / Kt, depth h (in), areas At, Ab, Ad (in^2) of the top chord, bottom chord and diagonals; the end (bearing-line)
+       frames are X-type with the same angles (as Design all's quantities); member lengths work point to work point over the frame length S between
+       the girder webs along the frame line: X: 2S + 2 sqrt(S^2 + h^2); K: 2S + 2 sqrt((S/2)^2 + h^2);
+     kind 'dia': channel or W, nominal area A over S less the end gap g at each girder (cfDiaGap: bolt line less 1.5 in); end diaphragms cfDiaEnd;
+     kind 'ovr': Wi, We kip per frame;
+     allow: % added for gusset plates and bolts (df.dl.xfAllow, default 0; the module does not size gussets). Connection plates are not added here:
+       they are in the girder's detail allowance. Steel at 490 pcf = 0.2836 lb/in^3.
+   The same weight function is in Preliminary sizing (plXfW); keep the two identical. */
+const XF_ROW = /cross[\s-]*frame|diaphragm|\bx[\s-]?frame|\bk[\s-]?frame|bracing/i;   // a DC1 line load that looks like cross-frame weight (double-count warning)
+function gdXfW(X, Lft, end) {
+  if (X.kind === 'ovr') return Math.max(0, +(end ? X.We : X.Wi) || 0);
+  const S = Lft * 12, k = 1 + (+X.allow || 0) / 100;
+  if (X.kind === 'dia') return (end ? X.Ae : X.A) * Math.max(0, S - 2 * (end ? X.ge : X.g)) * 0.2836 / 1000 * k;
+  const d = end || X.type === 'X' ? Math.hypot(S, X.h) : Math.hypot(S / 2, X.h);
+  return (S * (X.At + X.Ab) + 2 * d * X.Ad) * 0.2836 / 1000 * k;
+}
+/* the weight model from the current inputs; own = false: the Cross-frames module has not been designed, imported or edited (its default sizes are used) */
+function gdXfModel() {
+  const dl = (P && P.df && P.df.dl) || {}, mode = dl.xf === 'off' || dl.xf === 'ovr' ? dl.xf : 'auto', al = dfOpt(dl.xfAllow), allow = al > 0 ? al : 0;
+  if (mode === 'off') return { on: false, mode };
+  if (mode === 'ovr') { const Wi = dfOpt(dl.xfInt), e = dfOpt(dl.xfEnd), We = e === null ? Wi : e; return Wi >= 0 && We >= 0 ? { on: true, mode, kind: 'ovr', Wi, We } : { on: false, mode, bad: true }; }
+  const d = GM.cf.def, c0 = P.cf || d, dia = cfDiaOn(c0), own = !!c0.source || JSON.stringify(dia ? c0.dia : [c0.type, c0.h, c0.mem]) !== JSON.stringify(dia ? d.dia : [d.type, d.h, d.mem]);
+  if (dia) { let q = c0.dia, X = cfDiaSec(q), eq = cfDiaEnd(q), XE = cfDiaSec(eq), bad = false; if (!(X.A > 0 && XE.A > 0)) { q = d.dia; X = cfDiaSec(q); eq = cfDiaEnd(q); XE = cfDiaSec(eq); bad = true; }
+    return { on: true, mode, kind: 'dia', A: X.A, g: cfDiaGap(q), Ae: XE.A, ge: cfDiaGap(eq), allow, own: own && !bad, bad, nm: X.nm_, nmE: XE.nm_, wpf: X.wpf, wpfE: XE.wpf }; }
+  const ang = c => { const o = {}; for (const [k] of CF_MEM) { const m = (c.mem || {})[k] || {}, dims = m.sec === 'custom' ? [nm(m.b1), nm(m.b2), nm(m.t)] : ANGLES[m.sec];
+    if (!dims || !(dims[0] > 0 && dims[1] > 0 && dims[2] > 0 && dims[2] < Math.min(dims[0], dims[1]))) return null; o[k] = { A: angleProps(...dims).A, nm: m.sec === 'custom' ? `L${f2(dims[0])}x${f2(dims[1])}x${frac(dims[2])}` : m.sec.replace(' (LLV)', '') }; } return o; };
+  let c = c0, A = ang(c), bad = false; if (!A || !(nm(c.h) > 0)) { c = d; A = ang(d); bad = true; }
+  return { on: true, mode, kind: 'xf', type: c.type === 'X' || c.type === 'Kb' ? c.type : 'Kt', h: nm(c.h), At: A.top.A, Ab: A.bot.A, Ad: A.diag.A, allow, own: own && !bad, bad, nmT: A.top.nm, nmB: A.bot.nm, nmD: A.diag.nm };
+}
+/* the point loads of every girder (array per girder of { x (ft, analysis model), P (kip), end, W (kip, the whole frame), Lf (ft) }), or null without
+   the model or Preliminary sizing's framing. A station is mapped into its span proportionally between that girder's bearings (exact when the girder's
+   span equals the analysis span); a frame on a bearing line loads that bearing only */
+function gdXfPts(b, X) {
+  if (!X || !X.on || !b || !b.xf || !Array.isArray(b.xf.f) || !Array.isArray(b.xf.g)) return null;
+  const sp = b.spans, X0 = [0]; sp.forEach(L => X0.push(X0[X0.length - 1] + L)); const G = b.xf.g.map(() => []);
+  b.xf.f.forEach(([sup, k, bay, sa, sc, Lf]) => { const end = !!sup, W = gdXfW(X, Lf, end);
+    [[bay, sa], [bay + 1, sc]].forEach(([g, st]) => { const B = b.xf.g[g]; if (!B || !G[g]) return; let x;
+      if (end) x = X0[k]; else { const a = B[k], c = B[k + 1]; x = Math.max(X0[k], Math.min(X0[k + 1], X0[k] + (c > a ? (st - a) / (c - a) : 0.5) * sp[k])); }
+      G[g].push({ x, P: W / 2, end, W, Lf }); }); });
+  return G;
+}
+/* point loads as node loads: klf on each node's tributary length, a load split linearly between the two nodes of its element */
+function gdXfNodal(pts, xs, trib) { const N = xs.length, w = new Float64Array(N);
+  (pts || []).forEach(p => { let e = 0; while (e < N - 2 && xs[e + 1] < p.x - 1e-9) e++; const t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (p.x - xs[e]) / (xs[e + 1] - xs[e]))); w[e] += p.P * (1 - t) / trib[e]; w[e + 1] += p.P * t / trib[e + 1]; });

+/* cross-frame and diaphragm weight in DC1 (XF1, engineer's decision 2026-10-13). GirderDetail sends the weight model of its Cross-frames module with the
+   gd-an message (P.analysis.xf; absent, null or on = false: no load, exactly as before):
+     kind 'xf': cross-frame of angles, type X / Kb / K, depth h (in), member areas At, Ab, Ad (in^2); end (bearing-line) frames are X-type with the same angles;
+     kind 'dia': diaphragm (channel or W), area A (in^2) over the frame length less the end gap g (in) at each girder; end diaphragms Ae, ge;
+     kind 'ovr': the weights entered in GirderDetail, Wi (intermediate) and We (end), kip per frame;
+     allow: % added for gusset plates and bolts (kinds 'xf' and 'dia').
+   Steel at 490 pcf (0.2836 lb/in^3). Member lengths are work point to work point over the frame length S (between girder webs, along the frame
+   line): X: 2S + 2 sqrt(S^2 + h^2); K: 2S + 2 sqrt((S/2)^2 + h^2). The same function is in GirderDetail (gdXfW); keep the two identical. */
+function plXfW(X, Lft, end) {
+  if (X.kind === 'ovr') return Math.max(0, +(end ? X.We : X.Wi) || 0);
+  const S = Lft * 12, k = 1 + (+X.allow || 0) / 100;
+  if (X.kind === 'dia') return (end ? X.Ae : X.A) * Math.max(0, S - 2 * (end ? X.ge : X.g)) * 0.2836 / 1000 * k;
+  const d = end || X.type === 'X' ? Math.hypot(S, X.h) : Math.hypot(S / 2, X.h);
+  return (S * (X.At + X.Ab) + 2 * d * X.Ad) * 0.2836 / 1000 * k;
+}
+/* the frame point loads of every girder (XF1): each frame of framingLayout weighs plXfW(its length between the girder webs, on a bearing line) and puts
+   half on each of the two girders it connects, at that girder's own station, mapped into the analysis span proportionally between that girder's
+   bearings (exact when the girder's span equals the analysis span); a frame on a bearing line loads that bearing only. Per girder type the girder of
+   that type with the largest total (ties: the lower number) is used; with two girders the interior type uses an exterior girder.
+   Returns null when GirderDetail sends no load; { err } when the framing cannot be built; else { X, types: { int|ext: { g, pts, tot, nI, nE, w } } },
+   w = the equivalent node loads as klf on the tributary length of each node (a point load split linearly between the two nodes of its element). */
+function plXfLoads(P, beam, spans, types) {
+  const X = (P.analysis || {}).xf; if (!X || !X.on) return null;
+  let m = null; try { m = buildModel(P); } catch (e) { m = null; }
+  if (!m || m.errors.length) return { X, err: 'the current girder layout has input errors, so its cross-frames cannot be located', types: {} };
+  const FR = framingLayout(P, m), { xs, N, trib } = beam, X0 = [0]; spans.forEach(Ls => X0.push(X0[X0.length - 1] + Ls));
+  const G = FR.girders.map(() => []);
+  const mapX = (q, s, f) => { if (f.type === 'sup') return X0[f.k]; const B = q.bear, k = f.k, a = B[k], b = B[k + 1];
+    return Math.max(X0[k], Math.min(X0[k + 1], X0[k] + (b > a ? (s - a) / (b - a) : 0.5) * spans[k])); };
+  FR.frames.forEach(f => { const Lf = Math.hypot(f.xc - f.xa, FR.ys[f.bay + 1] - FR.ys[f.bay]), end = f.type === 'sup', W = plXfW(X, Lf, end);
+    [[f.bay, f.xa], [f.bay + 1, f.xc]].forEach(([g, xg]) => { const q = FR.girders[g]; if (q) G[g].push({ x: mapX(q, xg - q.x0, f), P: W / 2, end, W, Lf }); }); });
+  const nodal = pts => { const w = new Float64Array(N); pts.forEach(p => { let e = 0; while (e < N - 2 && xs[e + 1] < p.x - 1e-9) e++; const t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (p.x - xs[e]) / (xs[e + 1] - xs[e])));
+    w[e] += p.P * (1 - t) / trib[e]; w[e + 1] += p.P * t / trib[e + 1]; }); return w; };
+  const nb = G.length, tot = g => G[g].reduce((a, p) => a + p.P, 0), pick = list => list.reduce((a, g) => tot(g) > tot(a) + 1e-9 ? g : a, list[0]);
+  const ints = [...Array(nb).keys()].filter(g => g > 0 && g < nb - 1), exts = [0, nb - 1], out = { X, types: {} };
+  types.forEach(gt => { const g = pick(gt === 'ext' || !ints.length ? exts : ints), pts = G[g];
+    out.types[gt] = { g, pts, tot: tot(g), nI: pts.filter(p => !p.end).length, nE: pts.filter(p => p.end).length, w: nodal(pts) }; });
+  return out;

## 2026-10-13 — PR: claude/gd-xf-followup (cross-frame DC1 follow-ups: gusset and bolt allowance default 10%; DC1 recomputed once after the cross-frame auto-design; engineer's decisions 2026-10-13 on GD35; PR link added after merge)

### XF2a. Gusset plate and bolt allowance on the computed cross-frame weight: default 0% → 10%   [results change: DC1; §4 callout in the PR]
- **Where:** `GM.df.def.dl` (anchor `medJoint: 'no', xf: 'auto', xfAllow:`); the allowance field note (anchor `'Gusset plates and bolts allowance', 'df.dl.xfAllow'`); the XF1 comment (anchor `allow: % added for gusset plates and bolts`); `gdXfMark` (anchor `function gdXfMark(p, raw)`); the old-project notice in `gdXfAlerts` (anchor `as point loads at each frame, half to each girder`).
- **Before:** `xfAllow: 0`; no migration of the allowance. **After:** `xfAllow: 10, …, xfV: 2`. `gdXfMark` sets `df.dl.xfAllow = 10` for a project saved without `df.dl.xfV` whose stored allowance is 0. That is the XF1 default, which the user could not have chosen apart from it. Projects saved before XF1 have no `xfAllow` and take the default of 10. `xfV: 2` comes with the defaults, so a 0 entered from now on is kept. The notice for old projects states the allowance and that 10% is the default and editable.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 3.5.1 (DC includes the nonstructural attachments; the gussets and bolts of the bracing). The 10% is the engineer's allowance (2026-10-13), not a code value.
- **Check case (hand, the XF1 case):** simple span 120 ft, 5 girders at 9.5 ft, Kb frames h = 52 in, L5x5x3/8 top chord, L3x3x3/8 bottom chord and diagonals, frames at 24, 48, 72, 96 ft.
  - Frame weights: intermediate W = 0.2772 × 1.10 = 0.30492 kip; end W = 0.3348 × 1.10 = 0.36828 kip.
  - Interior G2 takes 0.30492 kip at each station.
  - ΔM(60 ft) from the frames = 0.30492 × 72 = 21.954 kip-ft (program 2505.650 − 2483.696 = 21.954; with 0%: 19.958).
  - ΔR = 0.30492 × 2 + 0.36828 = 0.97812 kip (program 0.97813).
  - Steel camber at midspan from the frames: 0.03668 × 1.1 = 0.04035 in (program 0.04036).
- **Built-in example (designed Kb frames), G2:**
  - Frames 5.0945 → 5.6039 kip.
  - M_DC1 +1018.194 → +1019.178 kip-ft and −2403.939 → −2406.075 kip-ft.
  - R_DC1 Abut. 1 / Pier 1: 52.567 / 194.752 → 52.639 / 194.934 kip.
  - Camber 1.9156 → 1.9169 in.
- **As opened (Cross-frames module not designed, default X-frames):** G2 frames 8.5416 → 9.3958 kip; M_DC1 +1025.672 → +1027.404 kip-ft.

### XF2b. DC1 recomputed once after the cross-frame auto-design   [results change only where the auto-design changes the frame weights]
- **Where:** `getDemands` (anchor `function getDemands(src, tgt, xfPass)`). New `GD_XF_REQ`, `GD_XF_PASS`, `GD_XF_T`, `GD_XF_STALE`, `gdXfSig`, `gdXfReq` and `gdXfAfter` after the `gd-inbox-err` listener. The `gd-inbox` listener: anchor `const xs0 =`, the stale-reply check, `gdXfAfter(...)` in each branch, and the new target `'xfall'`. The summary notices in `gdXfAlerts` (anchor `const re = P.ui && P.ui.xfRe`).
- **Problem:**
  - Get demands, Design all and the automatic refresh import first, then auto-design the Cross-frames module.
  - The imported DC1 therefore used the frame weights from before that design.
  - Engineer's decision 2026-10-13: when the auto-design changes the frame weights, recompute the demands once with the new weights and say so; if they change again, ask for Get demands again; no further passes.
- **After:**
  - **Weight signature:** each request records the signature of the frame weight model (`gdXfSig`: kind, type, h, areas, gaps, entered weights, allowance).
  - **Second pass:** after the import (and auto-design), if the signature changed, `gdXfPost` sends the new model to Preliminary sizing and the same request is made again once, after 300 ms, as the second pass. A load into every module without a target becomes `'xfall'`.
  - **Messages:** if the second pass leaves the weights unchanged, the flash, the Design all window and every module summary say "DC1 recomputed with the designed cross-frame sizes" (`P.ui.xfRe = { st: 'ok' }`). If they change again, a warning asks for Get demands again (`st: 'again'`). The note clears on the next Get demands of the user.
  - **Superseded passes:** a new request of the user cancels a pending second pass, and the reply of a running one is dropped (`GD_XF_STALE`).
- **Saved data:** new optional `ui.xfRe` only.
- **Check case:** the built-in example as opened, Cross-frames → Get demands (Preliminary sizing):
  - Calls are `getDemands('pl')`, then `getDemands('pl', 'cf', true)`, ending with `xfRe.st = 'ok'`.
  - The frames go from default X/48 in to Kb/52 in.
  - The Cross-frames checks after the automatic second pass are identical to those after a manual second Get demands.
  - The same holds from Structural analysis G2 and for Design all: two calls, and the Design all window ends with "DC1 recomputed with the designed cross-frame sizes".
- **How verified (both items):**
  - `node --check` passes on all blocks.
  - Headless Chromium against main (f1b6d49) on the built-in example, xsA and curb.
  - A test copy with the allowance default set back to 0 gives check items identical to main after Get demands from 'pl' and 'sa:2' in 9 modules.
  - With 10%, only DC1-dependent results increase, by about 10% of the XF1 increment.
  - Get demands vs Any location rows are identical.
  - Migration: XF1-saved 0 → 10; a user-entered 0 is kept after reload; pre-XF1 projects get 10 plus the notice.
  - Save and load both ways; the ST-Girder payload satisfies steel + wet = total.
  - No console errors.
- **Other copies:** none.
