## 2026-10-14 — PR: claude/gd-ll-fixes (live load fixes found by the comparison with Moving Load Generator; engineer-approved 2026-10-14; PR link added after merge)

The line-girder engine (`sgBeam`, `sgLLRow`, `sgFatRow`, `feIM`, `feVerify`) is the same code in the main page (Structural analysis) and in the embedded Preliminary sizing (`PL_B64`, decoded, edited and re-encoded on one line). Items LL1 to LL3 change both copies identically; after the change the two copies are still identical (checked by extracting both). Item order in the commits: LL1, LL3, LL2, LL4, LL5, LL6, LL7.

### LL1. Fatigue truck: axles that do not contribute to the extreme are neglected   [§4: fatigue moment and shear ranges] [more conservative; fatigue maxima/minima only where an axle sits on an opposite-sign part of the influence line]
- **Where:** `sgFatRow` (anchor `function sgFatRow(beam, row`), both copies.
- **Problem:** the fatigue truck was summed with every axle on the bridge, so an axle on the opposite-sign part of the influence line reduced the extreme. 3.6.1.4.1 defines the fatigue load as one design truck or some of its axles, and 3.6.1.3.1 requires axles that do not add to the extreme force effect to be left off.
- **Before:** `r1 = 32·IL(q) + 32·IL(q+30) + 8·IL(q+44)` (and the reverse direction), max and min taken from the same sums.
- **After:** a maximum sums only the positive axle effects, a minimum only the negative ones: `r1 = pp(32·IL(q)) + pp(32·IL(q+30)) + pp(8·IL(q+44))`, `n1 = nn(…)`, with `pp(v) = max(v, 0)`, `nn(v) = min(v, 0)`.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 3.6.1.4.1 and 3.6.1.3.1. Load factors and IM (15%) unchanged.
- **Check cases:**
  - Two continuous 100-ft spans, constant EI, moment at x = 98 ft (closed-form influence line: IL(98) = 1.0092, IL(68) = −7.5964, IL(84) = −4.3788 ft). Before: every placement with a 32-kip axle at 98 ft also has an axle on the negative part, maximum 0. After: 32(1.0092) = 32.295 kip-ft, × 1.15 = **0.00 → 37.14 kip-ft** per lane (program 37.14).
  - Built-in example (variable EI), x = 124 ft, per lane × 1.15: max **154.4 → 265.7** kip-ft (before 8@110 + 32@124 + 32@154 = 0 + 219.73 − 85.50 = 134.23; after 32@94 neglected, 32@124 + 8@138 = 219.73 + 11.27 = 231.00), min −744.3 unchanged, range **898.7 → 1,010.0** (Moving Load Generator 265.7 / −744.3 / 1,009.9).
- **Other copies:** Preliminary sizing (`PL_B64`), identical.

### LL3. HL-93: non-contributing axles neglected in the truck, tandem and two-truck sums   [§4: HL-93 envelopes] [more conservative where an axle sits on an opposite-sign part of the influence line; no change on the built-in, xsA and curb projects]
- **Where:** `sgLLRow` (anchor `function sgLLRow(beam, row`), both copies; the live load deflection calls (`sgLLRow(bN, row, null, true)` in Structural analysis `lld` and Preliminary sizing `analyzeGirder`).
- **Problem:** the design truck, the tandem and each truck of the 90% two-truck case were summed with every axle, so axles on the opposite-sign part of the influence line reduced the extreme. 3.6.1.3.1 requires axles that do not add to the extreme force effect being sought to be left off.
- **After:** maxima sum `pp(P·IL)`, minima sum `nn(P·IL)` for the truck (both directions, rear spacing 14 to 30 ft), the tandem and each of the two trucks. The lane load is unchanged (already only the parts that increase the effect). The deflection rows (3.6.1.3.2, "design truck alone") keep every axle (`whole = true`), so live load deflections are unchanged; see open items.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 3.6.1.3.1.
- **Check case:** two continuous 100-ft spans, constant EI, M+ at x = 98 ft (IL(98) = 1.0092, IL(94) = −0.8007): truck before 0 (no placement with a positive sum), after 32(1.0092) = 32.295; tandem before 25(1.0092) + 25(−0.8007) = 5.213, after 25.230; lane + 1.332. M+ with IM 33% per lane: 1.33(5.213) + 1.332 = **8.27 → 1.33(32.295) + 1.332 = 44.28 kip-ft** (program 8.3 → 44.3).
- **Results:** none of the HL-93 moments, shears or reactions of the built-in, xsA and curb projects change (checked per node); the fatigue changes come from LL1.

### LL2. Shear influence lines with the exact unit jump at the section   [§4: shear influence lines] [more conservative: HL-93 and fatigue shears +0.6% to +1.2% at supports, more near midspan of small values]
- **Where:** `sgBeam` (anchor `// shear (LL2, 2026-10-14)`; `MF` is now built before `VLL`), new `sgILGrid`, `sgLLRow` and `sgFatRow` (`cut` argument), `feIM` (anchor `if (!e.alt) return r;`), `feVerify` (new case), both copies.
- **Problem:** the element shear influence line was linearly interpolated across the element that contains the section, smearing the unit jump over about 1 ft. An axle could not stand at the section with its full ordinate, and the lane area next to the section was short: 100-ft simple span, end shear 96.24 kip (exact 97.28), 0.5L 36.40 (exact 37.28).
- **After:**
  - Each element's influence line is split into a smooth part S (row − 1 beyond the element) plus a unit step at the section.
  - Every element is evaluated for two sections: just right of its left node and just left of its right node.
  - An axle exactly at the section is taken on the side that gives the extreme (beyond the section for a maximum, before it for a minimum). Where the section is not on the 1-ft load grid, each axle is also placed exactly at it.
  - The lane load is integrated element by element with the jump, with the exact positive and negative parts.
  - The element keeps both results (`VLL[e].alt`; `VF[e]` holds the envelope). `feIM` and the fatigue shear take the envelope of the two ends, so each element's value bounds the shear anywhere in it: V+ is exact just right of each node, V− just left of each node.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 3.6.1.3.1 (axle and lane positions for the extreme force effect), 3.6.1.2.2, 3.6.1.2.4, 3.6.1.4.1. No load factor or IM change.
- **Check cases (100-ft simple span, per lane, no IM):**
  - End shear: truck 32(1) + 32(86/100) + 8(72/100) = 65.28, lane 0.64(100)/2 = 32.00, total **96.24 → 97.28 kip** (with IM 33%: 117.54 → 118.82). Added to the engine verification (SA1) as "HL-93, 100 ft simple span, end shear (axle at the support, closed form)": 118.822 vs 118.822.
  - 0.5L: truck 32(0.50) + 32(0.36) + 8(0.22) = 29.28, lane 0.64(50)(0.5)/2 = 8.00, total **36.40 → 37.28 kip**.
  - Symmetry: V−(x) = −V+(L − x) at every node (e.g. V−(93) = −87.917 = −V+(7)).
- **Other copies:** Preliminary sizing (`PL_B64`), identical.

### LL4. Reactions at interior supports: 90% two-truck case regardless of continuity   [§4: interior support reactions] [more conservative; simple-span bridges only]
- **Where:** Structural analysis `compute`, `reac` (anchor `interior = k > 0 && k < sup.length - 1;   // LL4`).
- **Problem:** the 90% case (two trucks at least 50 ft apart plus lane) was applied to interior support reactions only for continuous girders. 3.6.1.3.1 applies it to the reactions at every interior support of a multi-span bridge, continuous or not.
- **Before:** `interior = cont && k > 0 && k < sup.length - 1`. **After:** `interior = k > 0 && k < sup.length - 1`.
- **Preliminary sizing:** no change. Its continuous units already use the 90% case at interior bearings; on simple spans it designs a separate bearing for each girder end at a pier ("Pier k, back (Span k)" / "ahead (Span k+1)"), each loaded by its own span, and no bearing there combines both spans. When the arrays come from Structural analysis (Get demands, source "sa"), the pier reaction it receives is Structural analysis's combined reaction, which now includes the 90% case.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 3.6.1.3.1.
- **Check case (two 100-ft simple spans, per lane, IM 33%):** pier reaction influence line = triangle, 1.0 at the pier, 0 at both abutments.
  - One truck: 8(0.86) + 32(1.00) + 32(0.86) = 66.40; 1.33(66.40) + 0.64(200)(1)/2 = 88.31 + 64.00 = **152.31 kip** (before).
  - Two trucks, 50 ft clear: 8(0.72) + 32(0.86) + 32(1.00) = 65.28 and 8(0.50) + 32(0.36) + 32(0.22) = 22.56 → 87.84; 0.9[1.33(87.84) + 64.00] = **162.74 kip** (after).
  - Program: G2 of the built-in example changed to two 100-ft simple spans: Pier 1 LL+IM 139.82 → 149.40 kip (g = 0.918), Strength I 481.21 → 497.97 kip.

### LL5. 90% two-truck negative-moment region   [§4: where the 90% case applies] [never less conservative; no change on the built-in, xsA and curb projects]
- **Where:** Structural analysis `compute` (anchor `const Mu = MofB(bN, 1), tw2 =`; uses `tw2[i]` for `LLn` and `VH.two`; `cmp` with `Mu0`); Preliminary sizing `suggestLayout` → `demand` (anchor `const Mu = MofB(bN, uni(1)), tw2 =`; `Mn[i]`).
- **Problem:** the 90% two-truck case was applied in the negative permanent-load (DC + DW) moment region around each pier. 3.6.1.3.1 defines the region by the points of contraflexure under a uniform load on all spans.
- **After:** the region is the union of (a) the nodes where a unit uniform load on all spans gives negative moment, computed on the live load stiffness model (`bN`: staged short-term composite, or constant EI when the model is constant EI), and (b) the former permanent-load region, so it is never smaller than before. The pier distribution factor region (`region`) is unchanged.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 3.6.1.3.1.
- **Check case:** two equal continuous spans, uniform load: contraflexure at 0.75L, so (a) is 75 to 125 ft for L = 100 ft (program: 76 to 124 at the 1-ft nodes; M(75) = +0.09 kip-ft per klf). Built-in example: (a) 80–141 and 219–280 ft (variable EI), 82–138 and 222–278 (constant EI); (b) 79–142 and 218–281; the union equals (b), so no result changes.

### LL6. Tenth-point shear tables at interior piers   [display only]
- **Where:** Structural analysis `combos` (anchor `const vRows = R.tenth.flatMap`), `T10` takes optional rows; cards `sa-vu` and `sa-vf`.
- **Problem:** at "Span k, end" (an interior pier) the table showed the element just right of the pier, i.e. the next span's shear, and the span-k side was not shown.
- **After:** each interior pier has two rows, "Span k, end (left of pier)" (element just left) and "Span k+1, start (right of pier)" (element just right). Other points unchanged. No computed value changes.

### LL7. Method text   [display only]
- **Where:** Derivations "HL-93 live load" and "Fatigue truck" (anchor `(1-ft steps), both directions`), the vehicles card `sa-ll`, SA5 items, Manual sections "Live load: vehicles and what controls (SA5)", "Influence lines and live load", "Verification"; Preliminary sizing "Suggest mode methodology" (Analysis model, Live load) and the Analysis tab note.
- **Change:** "2-ft steps" → 1-ft steps (what the program does); "constant EI" → the actual model (Suggest mode trial layouts with constant EI, the quick suggestion, Full design and the analysis with the staged model of Structural analysis); "14, 18, 22, 26, and 30 ft" → 14 to 30 ft in 1-ft steps; the new rules (axle neglect, shear jump, two-truck region, interior reactions regardless of continuity, fatigue "or axles thereof") are described.

### Speed (LL2/LL3 follow-up commit)
- The sweeps use the positive and negative parts of the influence line precomputed once per row (`P`, `M`), and the section at a node inside a span is computed once and shared by its two elements. Results are unchanged by this (largest difference 1.5e-8 against the first implementation). The exact changes below show the final code.
- The engine takes about 1.9 times as long as before (more rows: two shear sections per support, and separate positive and negative sums). Preliminary sizing's quick suggestion and Full design on the built-in example: 62 s → 80 s in headless Chromium, with an identical result.

### Verification (LL1–LL7)
- `node --check` on every script block of the main page and of the decoded Preliminary sizing, at every commit.
- Engine: the Structural analysis and Preliminary sizing copies of the engine are byte-identical at every commit. Hand checks above reproduced in Node from the extracted engine.
- Moving Load Generator at every 1-ft node (its output points extended to every node in a scratch copy; Moving Load Generator itself not changed): 100-ft simple span, the built-in 110-140-110 girder with constant EI and with the variable EI of G2's short-term composite section; HL-93 without and with IM, and the fatigue truck. Largest differences after the fix: M+ 0.011% (281.33 vs 281.30 kip-ft near a pier), M− 0.0015% (with Moving Load Generator's uniform-load region), section shears 0.0000%, reactions 0.0000%, fatigue moments and shears 0.0000%. Before: shears low by 1.1% at the supports and up to 12% at small values near the far support, fatigue maximum at x = 124 ft low by 42%.
- Headless Chromium, main vs branch, built-in example, xsA and curb (and two 100-ft simple spans for LL4): Structural analysis and Preliminary sizing key values, every module's checks after Get demands from Preliminary sizing and from Structural analysis G2, the ST-Girder hand-off, Get demands vs Any location rows identical, save/load both ways, the ST-Girder auto-open flow, no console errors.

### Open items (LL1–LL7)
- Live load deflection (3.6.1.3.2, design truck alone) still sums every axle; whether 3.6.1.3.1's axle neglect applies to the optional deflection criterion is the engineer's call.
- Moving Load Generator counts an axle standing exactly at a shear section only on the far side of the jump, so its V− (and V+ just left of a section) are slightly low, e.g. 100-ft simple span V−(50) = −37.21 against the exact −37.28 kip. Not changed here (other tool).
- At the few nodes where the permanent-load negative region is wider than the uniform-load region (built-in example: 79, 142, 218 and 281 ft with variable EI; 79–81 and 139–142 ft and their mirror with constant EI), GirderDetail's M− includes the 90% case and Moving Load Generator's does not (up to 5.4% per lane). This is the approved union (as before this PR).
- The element values are the envelope over the element's two end sections (1 ft apart). Where the shear changes sign along the girder this reports, for example, V− = −0.39 kip in the end element of a simple span (exact 0 at the bearing), and the fatigue shear range of an element combines the maximum at one end with the minimum at the other (at most about 0.5% above the exact range at a section on the cases run).

@@ -2149,3 +2149,3 @@
 <h3>Bracing type (Cross-frames module)</h3><p><b>CF10</b> recommends the intermediate bracing type from the girder depth d (out-to-out of the flanges, the "Girder depth d" input, not the web depth): at or above the <b>Minimum girder depth for cross-frames</b> (default 48 in; common practice, e.g. AISC/NSBA G13.1 guidance; owner standards govern; verify) a cross-frame (X or K by S/h, as the auto-design chooses), below it the lightest channel at least 0.75 d deep, or else the lightest rolled W at least 0.75 d deep. A cross-frame on a girder below the minimum gives a warning, not a failure. Auto-design selects the type: below the minimum it switches to the diaphragm and picks the lightest channel, then W, at least 0.75 d deep that passes every CFD item, with the fewest bolts (one row, pitch 3 in or 3d); at or above the minimum it designs the cross-frame and switches a diaphragm back. Double-click the <b>Intermediate bracing used</b> label to lock the choice (and the shape, bolt count, or pitch labels to lock those). Preliminary sizing sends its own minimum (Framing tab) with the cross-frame geometry, and its Suggest tab states the recommendation. Design all counts the diaphragm steel (S less the end gaps, times the weight per foot from the nominal area) and its bolts in place of the angles.</p>
-<h3>Live load: vehicles and what controls (SA5)</h3><p>At every analysis point the HL-93 design truck (rear axle spacing varied from 14 to 30 ft in 1 ft steps, both directions) and design tandem are moved across the influence line, each with IM, and combined with the design lane load; in negative moment regions and for interior reactions, 90% of two design trucks plus 90% of the lane load is also evaluated. The Combinations tab card <b>Live load: vehicles evaluated and what controls</b> shows, at tenth points, each vehicle's moment per lane, the controlling truck spacing, which combination controls, the distribution factor, and the girder LL+IM; its chart shows every vehicle along the girder.  <h3>Scope</h3><p>Line-girder analysis of any girder of the bridge defined in Preliminary sizing, and the analysis Preliminary sizing itself uses for its design demands (and so every module fed from it). The girder is modeled with beam finite elements about 1 ft long, each with the flexural stiffness of its own plates. Loads act on the section of the stage that carries them: DC1 (steel, deck, haunch, SIP forms) on the steel section; DC2 and DW on the long-term composite section (3n); live load on the short-term composite section (n). In continuous girders the composite stages are cracked, taking the steel plus the longitudinal deck reinforcement, over 15% of the adjacent spans on each side of every interior support, or optionally over the region of negative dead-load moment (found by a first, uncracked pass). The reinforcement is a percentage of the deck area at the deck centroid (1.0%, the minimum of 6.10.1.7, by default). The effective flange width is the girder's tributary width. Not included: deck pour sequence, settlement, temperature, permit or legal vehicles, and grid or curved-girder effects.</p>

## 2026-10-14 — PR: claude/gd-ll-followup (live load follow-ups to LL1–LL7: deflection axle neglect, exact section shears; engineer's decisions 2026-10-14; PR link added after merge)

The engine is the same code in the main page (Structural analysis) and the embedded Preliminary sizing (`PL_B64`, decoded, edited and re-encoded on one line); both copies are changed identically and remain byte-identical.

### LL8. Live load deflection: truck axles that do not contribute are neglected   [§4: optional deflection criterion] [more conservative where an axle would sit on an upward part of the deflection influence line; no change on the test projects]
- **Where:** `sgLLRow` (the `whole` argument is removed; anchor `The live load deflection rows (3.6.1.3.2) use the same rule (LL8`), both copies; Structural analysis `lld` (anchor `const e = sgLLRow(bN, row), dT = (1 + im)`), Preliminary sizing `analyzeGirder` (anchor `const e = sgLLRow(bN, row), dT = (1 + (Tg.IMk`); SA3 note.
- **Problem:** LL3 kept every axle for the deflection rows, pending the engineer's decision. Decision 2026-10-14: apply the axle-neglect rule of 3.6.1.3.1 to the deflection of 3.6.1.3.2 as well (the truck alone, and 25% of the truck with the lane).
- **Before:** truck deflection = max over positions of Σ Pᵢ·δ(xᵢ). **After:** Σ max(Pᵢ·δ(xᵢ), 0). The lane already used only the downward parts.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 3.6.1.3.2 with 3.6.1.3.1; 2.5.2.6.2.
- **Check cases (constant EI, EI = 1, per lane, closed-form deflection influence lines):**
  - Two continuous 100-ft spans, governing point x = 46 ft: truck 32@38 + 32@52 + 8@66 = 32(14,375.8) + 32(14,801.4) + 8(11,908.7) = 1,028,940/EI (program 1,029,208, 0.03%). Every axle is on the downward part, so **no change**: Δ = 1.33 × 1,028,940 = 1,368,491/EI before and after.
  - Three spans 100-20-100, center of the 20-ft span (x = 110 ft): before 8@91 + 32@105 + 32@119 = 8(−150.4) + 32(92.9) + 32(19.4) = 2,393/EI; after only 32@110 adds: 32(137.8) = 4,410/EI. Δ = max(1.33·truck, 0.25·1.33·truck + lane 1,087.2) = **3,182.7 → 5,865.6/EI** (program 3,204 → 5,901, +84%).
- **Results:** live load deflections of the built-in example, xsA, curb and the two-span simple case are unchanged (SA3 identical).

### LL9. Shears: exact section values at the nodes in place of the element envelope   [§4: shear demands] [less conservative than LL2 by up to one element's change, e.g. fatigue shear range up to 1.7% lower; exact]
- **Where:** `sgBeam` (anchor `LL9 (2026-10-14): exact section values, no envelope`), `feIM` (the `alt` envelope removed), `feStages` (`llFrom` also carries `VLLr`, `VFr`), both copies. Structural analysis `compute` (anchor `const vSec = (e, r) =>`; `R.vSec`), `gdStPayload` (anchor `row = (i, e, dx, rt)`), the shear table captions.
- **Problem:** LL2 stored, for each element, the envelope of the sections at its two ends (1 ft apart), so element values (and the fatigue range, max at one end minus min at the other) were up to one element's change above the exact section values. Decision 2026-10-14: report the exact section values.
- **After:**
  - Element e carries the exact section just right of its left node e. An element that ends at a support (or the girder end) carries the section just left of that support, so the support faces are in the element arrays used by the checks.
  - Maxima, minima and the fatigue range of an element come from the same section (range exact).
  - `VLLr`/`VFr` (and `R.vSec(e, true)`) keep the section just right of node e for every element. The ST-Girder hand-off uses them at the node next to a support, so every station is the exact section: just right of each node, both sides of interior supports, just left of the girder end.
  - The pedestrian load on shear is patterned on the same exact section influence line (lane area ÷ 0.64 × w<sub>PL</sub>); before, on the element's nodal influence line.

@@ -2349,3 +2349,3 @@
 <h3>Scope</h3><p>Line-girder analysis of any girder of the bridge defined in Preliminary sizing, and the analysis Preliminary sizing itself uses for its design demands (and so every module fed from it). The girder is modeled with beam finite elements about 1 ft long, each with the flexural stiffness of its own plates. Loads act on the section of the stage that carries them: DC1 (steel, deck, haunch, SIP forms) on the steel section; DC2 and DW on the long-term composite section (3n); live load on the short-term composite section (n). In continuous girders the composite stages are cracked, taking the steel plus the longitudinal deck reinforcement, over 15% of the adjacent spans on each side of every interior support, or optionally over the region of negative dead-load moment (found by a first, uncracked pass). The reinforcement is a percentage of the deck area at the deck centroid (1.0%, the minimum of 6.10.1.7, by default). The effective flange width is the girder's tributary width. Not included: deck pour sequence, settlement, temperature, permit or legal vehicles, and grid or curved-girder effects.</p>
-<h3>Influence lines and live load</h3><p>The stiffness matrix of each stage is factored once (banded Cholesky); a unit load at every node gives the moment, shear, and reaction influence lines. HL-93 (3.6.1.3) is moved along each influence line on a 1-ft grid: the design truck in both directions with the rear axle spacing from 14 to 30 ft in 1-ft steps, the design tandem, and the 0.64 klf lane load on the parts of the line that increase the effect, with 33% dynamic allowance on the truck and tandem; axles that do not contribute to the extreme effect are neglected (3.6.1.3.1). Shear influence lines keep the unit jump at the section, evaluated just right and just left of every element, so axle ordinates and lane areas next to a section are exact. For negative moment between the points of contraflexure under a uniform load on all spans (live load stiffness model), and also wherever the permanent-load moment is negative around a pier, and for the reactions at all interior supports regardless of continuity, 90% of two design trucks at least 50 ft apart plus 90% of the lane load is also considered. The fatigue truck or axles thereof (30-ft rear axle spacing, 15% allowance; axles that do not contribute neglected) gives the fatigue ranges. The live load effects are multiplied by the selected girder's distribution factors from the LLDF and DLs module: the span factor for positive moment and shear, the pier factor in the negative dead-load moment region, and the fatigue factors for fatigue; the pedestrian load is patterned on the influence lines like the lane load.</p>
+<h3>Influence lines and live load</h3><p>The stiffness matrix of each stage is factored once (banded Cholesky); a unit load at every node gives the moment, shear, and reaction influence lines. HL-93 (3.6.1.3) is moved along each influence line on a 1-ft grid: the design truck in both directions with the rear axle spacing from 14 to 30 ft in 1-ft steps, the design tandem, and the 0.64 klf lane load on the parts of the line that increase the effect, with 33% dynamic allowance on the truck and tandem; axles that do not contribute to the extreme effect are neglected (3.6.1.3.1). Shear influence lines keep the unit jump at the section, evaluated and the shears reported are the exact values of the section just right of each analysis point (just left of a support at the end of a span), so axle ordinates and lane areas next to a section are exact. For negative moment between the points of contraflexure under a uniform load on all spans (live load stiffness model), and also wherever the permanent-load moment is negative around a pier, and for the reactions at all interior supports regardless of continuity, 90% of two design trucks at least 50 ft apart plus 90% of the lane load is also considered. The fatigue truck or axles thereof (30-ft rear axle spacing, 15% allowance; axles that do not contribute neglected) gives the fatigue ranges. The live load effects are multiplied by the selected girder's distribution factors from the LLDF and DLs module: the span factor for positive moment and shear, the pier factor in the negative dead-load moment region, and the fatigue factors for fatigue; the pedestrian load is patterned on the influence lines like the lane load.</p>
 <h3>Results</h3><p>Moments and shears at every node for DC1, DC2, DW, LL+IM (positive and negative), and fatigue; the Strength I, Service II, and Fatigue I combinations; reactions with each load on its own stage (interior reactions include the two-truck case); dead load deflections (camber) by virtual work with the staged stiffness; the live load deflection with g<sub>Δ</sub> for the optional L/800 criterion; and a comparison with a constant-EI model under the same loads, which shows how much the stiffness modeling moves moment between spans and supports.</p>

## 2026-10-14 — PR: claude/gd-xf-race (Get demands: requests sent in order once Preliminary sizing is ready; request IDs so only the reply to an outstanding request is applied and the second pass is labelled on its own reply; engineer's decision 2026-10-14; PR link added after merge)

No engineering formula, factor, unit or code reference is changed. This changes only the messaging between GirderDetail and the embedded Preliminary sizing (`PL_B64`, decoded, edited and re-encoded on one line). Saved data is unchanged: no new storage key, `girderdetail_inbox_v1` keeps its format (the request ID is a field of the message, not of the stored inbox), and project files are unchanged.

### XR1. Requests made before Preliminary sizing is ready are queued and sent in order   [messaging] [no result change on a settled project]
- **Where:** `getDemands` (anchor `post = msg => gdPlPost(gdXfSend(msg))`); new `GD_PLQ`, `gdPlPost`, `gdPlFlush` and a `pl-status` listener after `plEnsure` (anchor `XR1 (engineer's decision 2026-10-14)`); `plShow` (anchor `PL_FRAME.dataset.ready = '1'; gdPlFlush();`).
- **Problem:** a request made before the embedded Preliminary sizing was ready was sent by `setTimeout(go, 3500)`. The frame shares the page's thread, so that timer can fire long after 3.5 s, and after a later request has already been sent. Example (xsA, main): a Design all requested at 18.96 s was delivered at 35.22 s, after the automatic refresh requested at 22.12 s. Its reply then arrived while the second pass was outstanding and was labelled "DC1 recomputed with the designed cross-frame sizes" (see XR2).
- **After:** a request waits in `GD_PLQ` until Preliminary sizing is ready. Ready means both: its first `pl-status` message has arrived (posted after its first analysis), and the existing 2.5 s after its `load` event has passed (`dataset.ready`). The queue is then sent in the order the requests were made. A request made while others are waiting joins the queue behind them, so an earlier request never arrives after a later one. Once ready, requests are sent at once, as before.

### XR2. Request IDs: only the reply to an outstanding request is applied; the second pass is labelled only on its own reply   [messaging] [no result change on a settled project; fixes a missing second pass when requests overlap]
- **Where:** `gdXfReq`, new `GD_RQ`, `GD_RID`, `GD_XF_PEND`, `GD_LOADALL`, `gdRqCovers`, `gdXfSend` (anchor `XR2 (engineer's decision 2026-10-14)`); `gdXfAfter`, last two lines (anchor `GD_XF_PEND.push`); the `gd-inbox-err` listener; the `gd-inbox` listener (anchor `XR2: the reply to a request that a newer one replaced is ignored`). Preliminary sizing (`PL_B64`): its `pl-export-req` listener echoes the ID.
- **Problem:** GirderDetail tracked one request in flight (`GD_XF_REQ`) and matched replies by target only. With two requests outstanding, a reply was applied with the other request's frame weights and second-pass flag. Results:
  - A reply that was not the second pass was labelled "DC1 recomputed…" (XR1 example).
  - The second pass could be sent for the wrong target, so a module never got its second pass. Built-in example: Get demands in Cross-frames followed at once by Get demands for Girder section. Main sends the second pass for Girder section only, so Cross-frames keeps demands computed with the frame weights from before its auto-design (final module checks `8b416a50f879`). Running the same two requests one after the other gives `4fbed927adbb`.
  - xsA: Get demands for Girder section right after the automatic refresh was requested. Main never sends the refresh's second pass, so 409 stored values differ from the sequential reference. Example: fatigue row "field splice FS4 at 278.00 ft, bottom flange, interior", MD1 −234.1 instead of −232.7 kip-ft.
- **After:**
  - Every request gets an ID (`rid`). Preliminary sizing echoes it in `gd-inbox` and `gd-inbox-err` as an optional message field.
  - `GD_RQ` holds the outstanding requests. A reply is applied only while its request is outstanding, with that request's own frame weights (`sig`) and second-pass flag. "DC1 recomputed…" is therefore shown only on the reply to a second-pass request. A reply to a replaced request is ignored: not stored in `girderdetail_inbox_v1` and not applied.
  - Replacement rules:
    - A new user request replaces any pending or running second pass. This is the XF2 rule, unchanged.
    - A new request replaces an outstanding request with the same target.
    - A request that loads every module (`all`, `refresh`, `xfall`, `pl`) replaces outstanding module and load-all requests. Exception: the automatic refresh does not replace a Design all, which keeps its summary.
    - A girder report is replaced only by a newer girder report.
  - When the replies to several outstanding requests each need a second pass, the passes wait in `GD_XF_PEND` and one timer sends them in order. Before, a second `setTimeout` overwrote `GD_XF_T`, so a new user request could not cancel the first pass.
  - A reply without an ID (Preliminary sizing's own "Send to GirderDetail" button, or an older embedded page) is handled exactly as before (`GD_XF_REQ`, `GD_XF_STALE`).
- **Governing provision:** none (no calculation change). DC1 of the cross-frames: AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 3.5.1, as in XF1/XF2.
- **Check case (built-in example, Cross-frames undesigned):** Get demands in Cross-frames, then at once Get demands for Girder section.
  - **Before:** the Cross-frames reply is applied with the Girder section request's frame weights. Its auto-design changes the frames from X h = 48 in to K (bottom) h = 52 in, and the second pass is sent for Girder section only. Final module checks `8b416a50f879`.
  - **After:** the Cross-frames reply (rid 1) and the Girder section reply (rid 2) each have their own frame weights. Both were computed with the X frames, so a second pass is sent for each (rids 3 and 4), and each pass reply is labelled "DC1 recomputed…". Final module checks `4fbed927adbb`, equal to the two requests made one after the other on main or the branch.

### Verification (XR1–XR2)
- `node --check` on every script block of the main page and of the decoded Preliminary sizing.
- **Headless Chromium, main (3d5d771) vs branch.** Each run waits until no request is outstanding or queued, no second pass is pending, and the project data has been unchanged for 8 s. Hashes cover every module's checks and the project data (without `ui`).
  - Opening the project, 10 runs each:
    - Built-in example: main and branch `85b05dc5fc25` / `fa53d5a7b0f0`.
    - xsA (automatic refresh and second pass on open): main and branch `e2a00c149767` / `01bf721d4145`.
    - curb: main and branch `6f96ebc6527e` / `1c7bbe4539bc`.
  - Saved data both ways (xsA, curb): main's saved storage opened in the branch, and the reverse, give the same hashes. The saved storage differs only in time stamps.
  - xsA, a user request at a given point of the open-time refresh. Points: before Preliminary sizing is ready; right after the refresh request; right after the first reply with the second pass pending; right after the second-pass request. Requests: Design all, Get demands for Girder section, Get demands for Cross-frames.
    - Design all: identical module checks on main and branch at every point (`e2a00c149767`).
    - Girder section or Cross-frames right after the refresh request: the branch equals the reference with the same request made after everything has settled (identical project data). Main differs (409 values, as above).
    - At the other points the branch equals main.
  - xsA, a Design all, Get demands for Girder section or Get demands for Cross-frames at 15 fixed times during the refresh. Pairing each reply with its request:
    - Main: one request delivered out of order and one reply wrongly labelled as the second pass.
    - Branch: 0 out-of-order deliveries and 0 wrong labels, here and in every other branch run.
  - Built-in example, two overlapping requests (Cross-frames + Girder section, Cross-frames + Design all, Cross-frames twice): branch final checks equal the sequential reference in all three cases; main only for the last two. A reply to a replaced request (rid 1 when the same target is requested again) is ignored.
  - No console errors or alerts in any run.

### Open items
- With the XF2 rule kept, a user request made while a second pass is pending or running cancels that pass. Other modules then keep the demands from the first pass. This happens on main and on the branch. If every module should always get its second pass, the rule needs your decision.

## 2026-10-14 — PR: claude/gd-xf-requeue (a user request no longer drops the cross-frame second pass, unless it loads every module; engineer's decision 2026-10-14 on the open item of claude/gd-xf-race; PR link added after merge)

No engineering formula, factor, unit or code reference is changed, and the embedded Preliminary sizing (`PL_B64`) is unchanged. Saved data is unchanged.

### XR3. The second pass is kept when the user makes another request   [messaging] [every module ends with demands computed with the designed frame weights]
- **Where:** `getDemands`, first two lines (the `P.ui.lastSrc` assignment moves after `gdXfReq`; anchor `after gdXfReq (XR3)`); `gdXfReq` (anchor `XR3 (engineer's decision 2026-10-14)`).
- **Problem:** under XF2/XR2, any new user request cancelled a pending second pass (not yet sent) and dropped the reply of a running one. When the user asked for one module while the second pass was pending or running, the other modules kept the demands from the first pass, computed with the frame weights from before the cross-frame auto-design. Examples on main (974509b):
  - xsA, Get demands for Girder section while the open-time refresh's second pass was pending or running: final module checks `44ada5db4fdb`. Making the same request after the refresh has finished gives `e2a00c149767`.
  - xsA, Get demands for Cross-frames in the same situation: `fdafca22eb1a`.
  - Built-in example, Get demands in Cross-frames, then Get demands for Girder section while its second pass was pending or running: `8b416a50f879`; one after the other gives `4fbed927adbb`.
- **After:**
  - If the new user request loads every module (Design all, the automatic refresh, load all; `GD_LOADALL`), the pending and running second passes are still replaced, as before. That request's own reply makes its own second pass when the frame weights change, so the replaced pass would be redundant.
  - Any other request (one module, the girder report): a pending second pass is sent at once, before the new request, and a running one is kept. Both are answered before the new request, so its reply comes last, exactly as when the requests are made one after the other.
  - `P.ui.lastSrc` is set after `gdXfReq`, so a second pass sent there does not change the source of the user's request.
  - The one-extra-pass limit is kept. A second pass never makes a third; if the weights still change, its reply shows the existing "Run Get demands again" notice.
- **Governing provision:** none (no calculation change). DC1 of the cross-frames: AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 3.5.1, as in XF1/XF2.
- **Check case (built-in example, Cross-frames undesigned):** Get demands in Cross-frames. Its auto-design changes the frames from X h = 48 in to K (bottom) h = 52 in, so a second pass for Cross-frames is pending. Get demands for Girder section is then made during the 300 ms before that pass is sent.
  - **Before:** the pass is cancelled, so Cross-frames keeps demands computed with the X frames. Final module checks `8b416a50f879`.
  - **After:** the Cross-frames second pass is sent first (rid 2, labelled "DC1 recomputed…"), then Girder section (rid 3). Final module checks `4fbed927adbb`, equal to the two requests made one after the other.

### Verification (XR3)
- `node --check` on every script block.
- **Headless Chromium, main (974509b) vs branch.** Each run waits until no request is outstanding or queued, no second pass is pending, and the project data has been unchanged for 8 s.
  - **Opening the project, 10 runs each (no interaction):** identical to main.
    - Built-in example: `85b05dc5fc25` / `fa53d5a7b0f0`.
    - xsA: `e2a00c149767` / `01bf721d4145`.
    - curb: `6f96ebc6527e` / `1c7bbe4539bc`.
  - **xsA, a user request at four points of the open-time refresh:** before Preliminary sizing is ready; right after the refresh request; right after the first reply with the second pass pending; right after the second-pass request.
    - Design all: module checks `e2a00c149767` at every point, on main and branch. As decided, Design all still replaces the second pass; its own reply needs none, because it was computed with the designed frames.
    - Get demands for Girder section or Cross-frames, pass pending or running: main `44ada5db4fdb` / `fdafca22eb1a`; branch `e2a00c149767`. The branch project data equals the reference with the same request made after the refresh has finished (`be17cf4ce77f`, `3fa788586899`).
    - Same requests right after the refresh request: equal to that reference on main and branch.
    - Same requests before Preliminary sizing is ready: equal on main and branch. Here the user's request is made before the refresh, so its reference order is the request first.
  - **Built-in example, Get demands in Cross-frames, then Girder section / Design all / Cross-frames:** made at once, with the second pass pending, or with it running. The branch final module checks equal the one-after-the-other reference in all nine cases (`4fbed927adbb`, `78ca681176cd`, `f43598349cfb`). Main differs for Girder section with the pass pending or running (`8b416a50f879`).
  - **Second-pass labels:** each reply paired with its request. 0 replies labelled as the second pass that were not; the "DC1 recomputed" notice appears on the second-pass reply.
  - No console errors or alerts.

### Open items
- A module request made while a refresh's *first* reply is still outstanding: that refresh's second pass is decided after the user's request was sent, so its reply comes after the user's and reloads every module from the refresh's source. In the tests (same source) the final state equals the reference. With a different source for the module request (for example Structural analysis G2), the refresh's pass wins. Not changed.

#### Exact changes (unified diff, 1 line of context)

+  if (tgt !== 'refresh') P.ui.lastSrc = src;   // after gdXfReq (XR3): a second pass it sends first does not change the source of this request
   plEnsure(); P.ui.srcSel = src; const target = tgt || P.mod, post = msg => gdPlPost(gdXfSend(msg));   // XR1/XR2 (2026-10-14): request ID; sent in order once Preliminary sizing is ready

## 2026-10-14 — PR: claude/girderdetail-pna-below-web (composite positive flexure with the PNA below the web is outside the scope of the app: Girder section, check at any location, Preliminary sizing; engineer's decision 2026-10-14; PR link added after merge)

### OOS1. PNA below the web: OUT OF SCOPE, never passing   [BEHAVIOUR CHANGE — results suppressed, layouts rejected] [no formula, factor or unit changed; normal sections unchanged]
- **Decision (engineer, 2026-10-14):** when the composite positive-flexure plastic force balance puts the plastic neutral axis below the web (P_t > P_s + P_c + P_w, plus P_rt + P_rb when the deck rebar is counted), the section is outside AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table D6.1-1 and Art. D6.3.2 and so outside the scope of the app. Same treatment as ST-Girder (stgirder PR #224), including the whole-span rule: a flagged location blocks the positive-flexure results of its span.
- **Before:** Girder section `d61pos` took Case I whenever P_t + P_w ≥ P_c + P_s + P_rb + P_rt and did not limit Ȳ, so with the PNA below the web Ȳ > D, the PNA was drawn at y_p = t_b + D − Ȳ (below the top of the bottom flange, or below the steel), M_p came from the extrapolated Case I expression, D_cp = Ȳ > D, D_p > D_t was possible, and GS5/GS6 reported PASS/FAIL numbers from those values. The only hint was the cross-check against the direct force balance on the Resistances tab ("differs by x %; review"). Preliminary sizing (`sgPlastic`, force balance by bisection) located the PNA in the bottom flange (D_cp = D), had no flag, and its quick suggestion, Full design and current-girder check could accept such a layout.
- **After (Girder section, `Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html`):**
  - `d61pos` returns `below: true` (only when true) for P_t > P_c + P_s + P_w + P_rt + P_rb; the values it returns are unchanged and are not reported.
  - `GM.gs.compute`: positive-flexure rows with `below`, and every positive-flexure row of the same span (span from the row's station `x` on the bridge of Preliminary sizing, `gdFatSup`; the whole girder where a station is unknown), get `r.oos`; `R.pnaOOS` lists the flagged locations (name, x, span, plastic forces) and is present only when not empty. `p.oosExt` (transient, check at any location): flagged stations of the span found from every analysis node.
  - GS5 (ductility) and GS6 (positive-flexure resistance) items of `r.oos` rows: `gsOosItem`, cells "out of scope", status `fail` with `oos: true` (badge and report status "Out of scope" / "OUT OF SCOPE"), so the module verdict is never passing (status bar adds "(out of scope: plastic neutral axis below the web)").
  - Alert (required wording, each location with x, span and the forces with values) on the Summary, Checks, Resistances and Drawings tabs, in the calculation report (1. Objectives and the conclusion) and on the check at any location. Resistances tab: the case test shows P_t > … ⇒ Ȳ > D, then the alert; no Case I Ȳ, M_p, cross-check, D_cp, compactness, ductility or M_n for that location. Drawing: no PNA line (note instead). Key results: "out of scope" in the positive-section list.
  - Check at any location: `gsaOos` (cached like the ratio plot) builds the rows at every analysis node of the girder; the station's run gets the flagged stations of its span. The ratio plot leaves out the out-of-scope items (no ratio).
- **After (Preliminary sizing, embedded `PL_B64`: decoded, edited, re-encoded on its one line):**
  - `sgPlastic` returns `oos: { Ps, Pc, Pw, Pt }` (only when P_t > P_s + P_c + P_w; rebar and haunch concrete ignored, as its M_p).
  - New `sgOosScan` (positive-flexure nodes, M_u+ > 0, both sides of plate boundaries, per girder type and span). `checkLayout`: positive-flexure ratios (6.10.7.1/6.10.7.2 and the ductility note) of a flagged span are not computed; returns `oos` (only when not empty).
  - Rejection: fast candidates (`evalCand`) with `oos` are `ok = false`; every pass test (quick check, Full design candidates and verification, the current-girder check) adds `!check.oos`; the "closest candidate" when none passes prefers one within scope.
  - Display: "OUT OF SCOPE: not accepted" with the reason on the suggestion card, "Rejected: PNA below the web (out of scope)" in the depth-candidate and Full design candidate tables, an alert on the Full design card, the reason in the current-girder comparison card and in the Apply warning.
- **Not changed:** the hand-off to ST-Girder (Structural analysis, Send to ST-Girder) still sends an out-of-scope girder; ST-Girder flags it itself (checked). Design all summary lists GS5/GS6 under "Fails" (saved `P.designAll.stat` format unchanged).
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Appendix D6.1, Table D6.1-1 (Case I, Ȳ ≤ D only if P_t ≤ P_c + P_s + P_w + P_rt + P_rb); Appendix D6.3.2; 6.10.6.2.2; 6.10.7.1.2; 6.10.7.3.
- **Check case (built-in example, Preliminary sizing: structural deck t_s = 5 in, bottom flange of plate 1, 0–82 ft (span 1 positive region), 30 × 3 in; then Get demands; F_y = 50 ksi, f′_c = 4 ksi, web 60 × 9/16, top flange 16 × 3/4, b_eff = 114 in interior, deck rebar excluded):** P_s = 0.85(4)(114)(5) = 1,938.0; P_c = 50(16)(0.75) = 600.0; P_w = 50(60)(0.5625) = 1,687.5; P_t = 50(30)(3) = 4,500.0 kip. P_c + P_s + P_w = 4,225.5 < P_t ⇒ PNA below the web. Case I extrapolated: Ȳ = 30[(4,500 − 600 − 1,938)/1,687.5 + 1] = 64.88 in > D = 60 in; D_p = 72.63 in > D_t = 70.75 in; M_p = 20,817 kip-ft against 18,337 kip-ft by the direct force balance (PNA 2.91 in above the bottom of the steel, in the bottom flange): +13.5 % (unconservative). Exterior girder: P_s = 1,632.0 kip, 3,919.5 < 4,500 kip.
  - Before (main): GS5 Span 1 interior 2.44 FAIL, exterior 2.63 FAIL; **GS6 Span 1 interior/exterior PASS (noncompact, compression flange 0.41, tension flange 0.27/0.26)**; status bar "2 checks fail"; PNA drawn at y_p = 63 − 64.88 = −1.88 in; Preliminary sizing: no flag.
  - After: GS5 and GS6 Span 1 interior and exterior "OUT OF SCOPE" (status fail, ratio —); status bar "3 checks fail (out of scope: plastic neutral axis below the web)"; alert with both locations and forces; no PNA drawn; check at any location at 44 ft (span 1): alert with the station and the 82 flagged stations of span 1 (1.00–81.99 ft), GS5/GS6 out of scope; at 180 ft (span 2): unchanged, every check satisfied. Preliminary sizing: the current-girder check reports OUT OF SCOPE (166 positive-flexure nodes of span 1, interior and exterior girders) and does not pass; the quick suggestion and Full design (their own plates) are within scope and unchanged.
- **How verified:** every script block parses (Babel/`new Function`; the decoded Preliminary sizing too). Headless Chromium, main (b811952) vs branch, each project settled (`settle`): built-in, xsA and curb — the checks, results, calculation report, tab HTML and status bar of all 11 modules, the check at any location (results and ratio plot) and the project data `P` identical (sha256); quick suggestion (layout, check, candidates, card text) and Full design (layout, candidates, card text) identical for all three; no console errors. Test case as above in main and branch; Send to ST-Girder from Structural analysis still sends (G1, 363 stations) and ST-Girder (main, with #224) flags span 1 out of scope (P_t = 4,500 > 1,632 + 600 + 1,688 = 3,920 kip). Rejection: the Preliminary sizing pass tests read `!check.oos` (verify of the test-case girder: `passTest` false); no fast or Full design candidate became out of scope in sweeps down to t_s = 1.5 in (deck and spans varied), so the candidate-table wording ("Rejected: PNA below the web (out of scope)") was checked with an out-of-scope state injected for the display only.
- **Other copies:** ST-Girder has its own (stgirder.md, PR #224).
- **Open items:** none.

## 2026-10-15 — PR: claude/gd-skew-framing (cross-frame layout at skewed supports and the unbraced lengths taken from it: AASHTO-level fixes approved by the engineer 2026-10-15; owner rules such as "staggered above 20°" are not in this PR; PR link added after merge)

All changes are in the embedded Preliminary sizing page (`const PL_B64`, main file line 2361: decoded, edited, re-encoded on its one line). Nothing else in the main file changed. Basis: AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.7.4.2.1 and C6.7.4.2.1 (first intermediate frame offset "by a minimum of the larger of 4b_f or 0.4L_b from the support ... where b_f is the largest girder flange width within the unbraced lengths on either side of the first cross-frame ... and L_b is the unbraced length between the first and the second intermediate cross-frame ... along the girder under consideration"; "maximized at the obtuse corners"; "as large as practicable but not less than 4b_f"; "4b_f is the recommended lower limit for the smallest unbraced lengths, offsets, or stagger distances"), 6.10.8.2.3 (L_b in LTB), 6.10.3.2.1 (deck placement). Diagnosis: problems P2–P7 of the read-only skew study (2026-10-15).

### SKX1. L_b per girder from the actual frame stations   [CALCULATION CHANGE — §4 callout] [unconservative at skewed piers before; positive-region and deck-placement L_b less conservative everywhere]
- **Where:** `detailExport` — new helpers after the anchor `const frX0 = gt => stG(gOf(gt), true), rgF = ...` (`braceG`, `toG`, `toX`, `lbSegs`, `lbMax`); `gsRow` (anchor `// unbraced segment(s) containing x on every girder of the type`); the Cross-frames block (anchor `const cf = { S: r2(m.S * 12)`); stability bracing `nBr`; deck overhang rows (anchor `lbE = Math.max(...lbSegs('ext', bx)`); Suggest `checkLayout` (SKX5).
- **Before:** Girder section rows took brace points from **G1's** frame stations plus the **centerline** bearing stations (`[...m.sup, ...stG([0], false, 3)]`) for every girder type; negative region L_b = that G1 segment; positive region L_b = `FR.sp` (the target spacing); deck placement L_b,C = `FR.sp` for every row (deck-placement segments ranked by C_b only). Cross-frames module `cf.Lb = FR.sp`; stability bracing `n` = G1's frames between the centerline bearing stations; deck overhang rows `Lb = FR.sp`.
- **After:** each row looks at **every girder of its type** (exterior: G1 and Gn; interior: G2 to G(n−1); the chosen girder for Structural analysis, `gOf`), each at **its own** bearings and frame stations (own station s from its Abut. 1 bearing; an analysis station maps to the girder proportionally within the span, exact when the girder's span equals the analysis span). The segment(s) containing x (both at a brace point) are candidates; the governing one is the largest L_b/C_b (L_b = the girder's own length) in both regions; L_b,C the same way with the deck-placement C_b. `cf.Lb` = the largest unbraced length on any girder; `cf.sb.n` = the fewest intermediate frames in that span on any girder (own bearings); overhang rows `Lb` = the exterior girders' segment at the row station.
- **Check case (built-in, all supports 28°, contiguous, Pier 1 interior, negative flexure):** brace points of G3 (bearings 0 / 110 / 250 / 360 ft):
  - Before: L_b = **10.10 ft** (G1's panel 110.00–120.10, applied to the interior type).
  - With the old layout (main's frames) the actual interior L_b is **18.33 ft** (G3 91.67–110.00 = 110/6); G2 13.28, G4 14.95.
  - After (final layout, SKX2–SKX4): L_b = **19.56 ft** (G3 90.44–110.00; the other side 110.00–130.09 = 20.09 ft has the larger C_b; L_b/C_b governs, both C_b = 1.0 for the nonprismatic segment). GS7 Pier 1 interior 0.859 → **0.973** (pass).
  - Hand check of the station: G3 is the centreline girder, so its stations equal the analysis stations; first line of span 1 at e = 9.45 ft past G5's bearing (+10.10) → 19.55; grid s = 23.63 → 19.55 + 3 × 23.63 = 90.44; L_b = 110 − 90.44 = 19.56 ft.
- **0° and 15° (frames identical to main):** negative-region L_b unchanged (22.00 ft at the piers); positive-region L_b and every L_b,C 25.00 → **22.00 / 23.33 / 22.00 ft** (spans 1/2/3), `cf.Lb` 25.00 → 23.33 ft, overhang rows 25.00 → 22.00 / 23.33 / 22.00 ft. Less conservative (the target spacing was used before, not the spacing built).

### SKX2. Field-splice / transition conflicts: shift the grid, add frames only if that clears them   [layout change]
- **Where:** `framingLayout` (anchor `const FL_MEMO = new Map();`), `parSpan` and `normSpan`; X4 note; Framing tab summary (`frSumHtml`, `renderFrSum`, `#fr-sum`).
- **Before:** each span was regenerated with n, n+1, n+2, n+3 frames and the layout with the fewest conflicts kept (extra frames even when they did not clear anything; built-in at 28°: 72 instead of 52 intermediate frames, still 0.05 ft from splices).
- **After:** parallel frames: shifts of the frame fractions (j + d)/(n + 1), |d| ≤ 0.25 panel (end panel of the longest girder ≤ s), then up to 3 extra per bay line; normal frames: the first / last full grid line moved inward up to 4 ft (an unskewed end: ±4 ft, keeping its end panel ≤ s and ≥ the clear distance; a skewed end keeps e ≥ max(clear, 4b_f, 0.4s)), with the same or up to two more grid intervals. A candidate is kept only if it clears every conflict (fewest frames, then smallest shift); otherwise the unshifted grid is kept and the conflicts are reported (X4 note names the spans; Framing tab table, in red). The Framing tab lists per span the frames, the spacing used against the target (parallel: per girder range when it varies), L_b,max per girder (where it varies), first/last line offsets, shifts, extra frames and conflicts.

### SKX3. Normal-frame grid anchored on each girder's own bearings; first-frame offset at skewed supports   [layout change] [new check X5]
- **Before:** grid x = X_k + j·L_s/(n+1) anchored at the **centerline** bearing; points within `supClear` (3 ft) of the farther bearing of a bay dropped; first panels at 28° of 5.05 ft (G2) up to 18.33 ft.
- **After:** per span, at a support skewed **more than 20°** the first full line is e = max(supClear, 4b_f, 0.4s) past the bearing of the **obtuse-corner girder** (the most advanced bearing on that line), so every girder's first intermediate frame is ≥ e from its own bearing (the obtuse girder gets exactly e, the others more); at a support skewed 20° or less the first line is one spacing from the bearing (as before; identical at 0°). s and e: q + cnt = ⌈(B_min − A_max − Σe)/s_target⌉ intervals, iterated (e depends on s). b_f: the widest top or bottom flange plate in the span. Grid stations are kept in a bay where they are ≥ e (skewed support) or ≥ supClear (other) from both bearings of that bay.
- **New check X5** (AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. C6.7.4.2.1): per span end at a support skewed > 20° with normal frames, the governing girder's d₁ against max(4b_f, 0.4L_b), L_b the first-to-second frame panel on that girder; pass if met, **advisory** if only 4b_f is met, **warning** below 4b_f (the commentary's "should"). 0.005 ft tolerance (stations are kept to 0.001 ft).
- **Check case (built-in 28°, span 1):** A (bearings at Abut. 1, centreline 0) = −10.10, −5.05, 0, 5.05, 10.10; B_min = 110 − 10.10 = 99.90; T = 89.80; b_f = 18 in → 4b_f = 6.00 ft; e = 0.4s: e = 10 → s = (89.80 − 20)/3 = 23.27 → e 9.31 → s 23.73 → … → s = 23.63, e = 9.45 ft. First line at 10.10 + 9.45 = 19.55 → G5 own 9.45, G3 19.55, G1 29.65 (G1 panel 29.65 > 25 → corner frame at 14.83 in bay G1–G2, SKX4). X5: d₁ = 9.45 ≥ max(6.00, 0.4 × 23.63 = 9.45) → pass.

### SKX4. Corner (fill) frames and stagger offsets enforced   [layout change] [X3 limit raised to max(min. offset, 4b_f)]
- **Before:** each bay added its own fill frames between its nearest bearing and its first grid frame, independently of the next bay; `stagMin` used only by X3 (warning); offsets down to 2.52 ft (built-in staggered), 1.04 ft in the sweep.
- **After:** while a girder panel in the span exceeds s, a frame is added in an adjacent bay at a position that (a) is ≥ max(supClear, 4b_f) from both bearings of the bay (skewed support) and (b) either coincides with a frame on the other side of either girder it connects (connecting through) or is ≥ d_min = max(stagMin, 4b_f) from every other frame on both girders. Preference: closes the gap, no splice conflict, adjacent panels ≥ 0.4× each other (C6.7.4.2.1), lines up, balanced. Gaps are taken largest first, and smallest first if that leaves a panel over s; staggered by bay uses s/2 only when s/2 ≥ d_min (else contiguous, noted). X3 now checks d = 0 or d ≥ d_min (the span's max(stagMin, 4b_f)).

### SKX5. Suggest / Full design price and check the actual layout   [CALCULATION CHANGE — §4 callout]
- **Where:** `suggestLayout`: new `layoutOf` (memoized per candidate), `stiffBays` uses it, `costOf` (anchor `nFrC = ly ? ly.FR.frames.length : nFr`), `checkLayout(D, top, bot, web, R, spl)` (anchor `// unbraced segments from the candidate's actual cross-frame layout`), both callers pass the splices.
- **Before:** frame cost `nFr = (nb − 1)(Σ(⌈L/s⌉ − 1) + spans + 1)` (idealised); checks with brace points every s from the nearest support and L_b = s everywhere.
- **After:** cost = the candidate's `framingLayout` frame count; each node uses the governing actual segment of the girder type (as SKX1, by L_b/C_b for the check's moment), L_b = its own length; fallback to the old grid when a candidate's model cannot be built.
- **Results (built-in):** 15°: fast $1,686,891 (68 frames) unchanged; Full design D 69 → 66 in, $1,570,591 → $1,596,256 (the iteration path changes with the actual L_b; main's 69 in result still passes the branch checks: max 0.993, $1,570,591). 28° all: fast $1,676,113 (68 frames priced, 88 built) → $1,699,636 (74 = built); Full design D 71 → 69 in, $1,582,491 → $1,581,235. 28° abutments: fast $1,680,012 → $1,691,570 (70 frames); Full D 69 → 69, $1,584,252 → $1,589,552. xsA (15°): Full D 63 → 63, $1,504,022 → $1,496,640.

### SKX6. Parallel frames: n from the longest girder   [layout change]
- **Before:** n = ⌈L_s/s⌉ − 1 from the centerline span (100 ft, skews 20°/0°, S = 12 ft: G1 27.18 ft > 25). **After:** n = ⌈L_max/s⌉ − 1, L_max = max over girders of their span (same example: n 3 → 4, G1 21.75, G5 18.25 ft). Unchanged where all supports have the same skew.

### Saved data
- No new or changed saved fields or keys. `orient[]` and the Framing tab summary are runtime only. Existing projects load unchanged; the frames are re-generated from `P.framing` on every recompute, and GirderDetail's stored `bridge.xf` (DC1 frame loads) is re-published by Preliminary sizing when the project opens (checked: 0 station mismatches in every case below).
- Projects with a skewed support > 20° (normal frames), or with conflicts that main resolved by adding frames, get a different layout; a stored per-bay stiffener table (`framing.bays`, doMode 'bays') then no longer matches those bays: D4 flags them and the uniform d_o/D is used until Suggest Apply or the table is edited (existing behaviour for a changed framing).

### How verified
- Every script block parses (`node --check`, the decoded Preliminary sizing too).
- `framingLayout` run in Node (extracted from the page) on main and branch: built-in at 0°, 15°, 20°, 0° forced normal, 0° at 20 ft spacing: identical stations. Sweep of 270 single-span cases at 28° (L 60–160 ft, S 8/9.5/12, s 15/20/25, contiguous/staggered, 28/28, 28/0, −28/28): X2, X3, X5 pass in all 270 (main: 105 + 107 cases with a first panel < 4b_f, 137 with offsets < stagMin); intermediate frames 6,240 → 6,094.
- Headless Chromium, main (6942b45) vs branch, each project settled (`settle`): built-in at 15°, 0°, 28° all (contiguous and staggered), 28° abutments only; xsA; curb (15° and 0°): all 10 modules after Get demands; DC1 frame list = layout (0 mismatches, every case); no console errors or alerts. Suggest fast + quick + Full design (with the spacing study) on built-in 15°, 28°, 28° abutments, xsA. Screenshots: Framing tab summary and X5 at 28°.
- Performance: `framingLayout` memoizes each span's frames by its inputs (EX 28°: 42 ms first call, 0.3 ms repeated; main 1.5 ms); Full design 15° 75 s → 76 s.

- Owner rules (RIDOT/CTDOT "staggered above 20°") — later owner-profile PR.

 <h3>Cross-frame layout</h3>
-<p>Girders are placed at y = 0, S, 2S, … and each support line passes through the bridge centerline station at its skew angle, so the bearing of girder i at support k is at x = X<sub>k</sub> + (y<sub>i</sub> − y<sub>c</sub>)tan θ<sub>k</sub>. A cross-frame is placed in every bay along every bearing line. Between bearing lines, n = ⌈L/s⌉ − 1 intermediate frames are placed, where s is the target spacing. Parallel frames interpolate between the two bearing lines. Normal frames are placed at even stations (offset by half a spacing in alternate bays if staggered), dropped where they would fall within the clear distance of a skewed bearing line, and supplemented near the acute corners so no girder exceeds the target spacing. If any frame falls within the splice clearance of a field splice or shop transition, up to three additional frames per span are tried and the layout with the fewest conflicts is kept.</p>
+<p>Girders are placed at y = 0, S, 2S, … and each support line passes through the bridge centerline station at its skew angle, so the bearing of girder i at support k is at x = X<sub>k</sub> + (y<sub>i</sub> − y<sub>c</sub>)tan θ<sub>k</sub>. A cross-frame is placed in every bay along every bearing line. Parallel frames (both supports of the span skewed 20° or less, AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.7.4.2.1): n = ⌈L<sub>max</sub>/s⌉ − 1 per bay, where s is the target spacing and L<sub>max</sub> the longest girder span between the two bearing lines, interpolated between the bearing lines, so no girder exceeds s. Normal frames (a support skewed more than 20°): one grid per span at a spacing of at most s (offset by half a spacing in alternate bays if staggered, unless half a spacing is less than d<sub>min</sub>). At a support skewed more than 20° the grid is anchored on the bearing of the obtuse-corner girder: its first line is e = max(clear distance, 4b<sub>f</sub>, 0.4s) from that bearing, so the first intermediate frame on every girder is at least e from that girder's own bearing (C6.7.4.2.1; b<sub>f</sub> is the widest flange plate in the span); at a support skewed 20° or less the first line is one spacing from the bearing. In each bay a grid station is kept where it is at least e (or the clear distance) from both bearings of the bay. Where a girder panel is still longer than s (the acute corners), a frame is added in an adjacent bay: at the station of a frame on the girder's other side (connecting through) or at least d<sub>min</sub> = max(min. offset, 4b<sub>f</sub>) from every other frame on both girders it connects, at least max(clear distance, 4b<sub>f</sub>) from their bearings, preferring positions that close the gap, clear splices and transitions, keep the adjacent panels at least 0.4 times each other, and line up. If any frame falls within the splice clearance of a field splice or shop transition, the grid is shifted within the span (end offsets changed by up to 4 ft, parallel frames by up to a quarter panel, same number of frames), or extra frames are used (up to three per bay line, or two more grid intervals), only when that clears every conflict (the smallest shift with the fewest frames); otherwise the unshifted grid is kept. ## 2026-10-15 — PR: claude/gd-pier-frame-spacing (closer cross-frame spacing near interior supports as a design variable, engineer's decision B of 2026-10-15 on the PR #227 follow-ups; PR link added after merge)

All code changes are in the embedded Preliminary sizing page (`const PL_B64`, main file line 2361: decoded, edited, re-encoded on its one line). Nothing else in the main file changed. Basis: AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.7.4.2.1 and C6.7.4.2.1 (cross-frame spacing; closer frames "may be necessary" near interior supports; first-frame offset; 0.4 panel ratio), 6.10.8.2.3 (lateral-torsional buckling with L_b between brace points), 6.10.3.2.1, 6.10.4.2.2. Engineer's decision A of the same day (keep #227's L_b from the spacing built; Full design at 15° accepted; b_f, X5 levels and the > 20° offset rule confirmed) is recorded in ENGINEER_CHECKS GD36; no code change.

### FSP1. Spacing near interior supports in `framingLayout`   [layout change; only with the new input set]
- **Where:** new helpers before `framingLayout` (anchor `function plPierSp(F, m)`, `function plPierLen(F, Ls)`, `const PL_SPPIER_MIN = 10`); inside `framingLayout`: `pzGrid`, `pzLim` (anchor `const sp2 = plPierSp(F, m), nS = m.sup.length;   // FSP`), the span loop (anchor `// FSP: the pier regions of this span`), new `parSpanP` after `parSpan`, and `normSpan(k, bf, dmin, pz)` (anchors `// FSP pier regions: the end lines at an unskewed support`, `let LIM = null; const limP`, `// FSP: the lines extended past both ends`, `// FSP: end panels within their limits`).
- **New optional inputs (Framing tab, Cross-frames):** `framing.spPier` "Spacing near interior supports" (ft; blank = the target spacing) and `framing.pierLen` "Pier region each side" (ft; blank = 0.25 × the adjacent span).
- **Rule:** active only in a continuous unit with interior supports and 0 < s_p < s (target). Region: R each side of each interior support, measured along each girder from its own bearing (R = `pierLen` or 0.25 × that span — about the dead-load point of contraflexure of continuous spans; chosen over the analysis's DL contraflexure because the layout feeds the analysis' DC1 frame loads, which would make it circular). Per span: from the pier end, panels s_p (normal frames: first line s_p from an unskewed support's bearing, or e = max(clear, 4b_f, 0.4 s_p) from the obtuse bearing of a support skewed > 20°; parallel frames: along the longest girder from the bearings, interpolated on the others, the region taken on the shortest girder) until the region is covered on every girder (to the next grid line beyond it); between the two zones (or to the abutment-end anchor, unchanged rule) evenly at most s, starting on the zone line, so there is no short closing panel; if less than s_p would remain between the zones, the whole span is evenly spaced at most s_p. Corner (fill) frames, conflict shifts, extra intervals (added between the zones), stagger offsets ≥ d_min and the X5 offset are the #227 rules, with the panel limit s_p for every girder panel whose midpoint is in a pier zone (`pzLim`).
- **Before:** `const mk = JSON.stringify([k, o, sp, clr, F.stagMin, F.arrange, fc, m.sup, m.skews, m.bays, feats, bf]);` … `pick = o === 'parallel' ? parSpan(k, Lmax) : normSpan(k, bf, dmin);`
- **After:** `const pz = sp2 ? { sp2, pS: k > 0, pE: k + 1 < nS - 1, rS: plPierLen(F, Ls), rE: plPierLen(F, Ls) } : null;` … `pick = o === 'parallel' ? (pz ? parSpanP(k, Lmax, pz) : parSpan(k, Lmax)) : normSpan(k, bf, dmin, pz);` (full code in the diff below). With `pz` null every expression evaluates as before (`limP` returns s; `ex` = max(0, mx − s) as before).
- **Check case (manual, §4 worked example):** built-in, skews 28° / 0° / 0° / 28° (abutments only), s = 25 ft, s_p = 15 ft, region blank (Span 1/3: 0.25 × 110 = 27.5 ft; Span 2: 0.25 × 140 = 35 ft).
  - Span 1 (normal frames, Abut. 1 skewed, Pier 1 unskewed): pier zone n = ⌈27.5/15⌉ = 2 panels → lines at 95, 80 ft; obtuse bearing at Abut. 1 is G5 (own station 0; global +10.10 ft from the centerline station). Abutment anchor e = max(3, 4·18/12 = 6, 0.4·t_m) with t_m = (80 − 10.10 − e)/3 → e = 8.22 ft, t_m = 20.56 ft. G3 stations: 0, 18.33, 38.88, 59.44, 80, 95, 110.
  - Span 2 (parallel, both piers unskewed, 140 ft): n = ⌈35/15⌉ = 3 each end → 15, 30, 45 and 95, 110, 125 from Pier 1; between 45 and 95: 50/⌈50/25⌉ = 25 ft. G3 stations 110, 125, 140, 155, 180, 205, 220, 235, 250.
  - L_b at Pier 1, interior girder: **22.70 → 15.00 ft** (both sides); exterior: 22.70 → 15.00 ft. Intermediate frames 54 → 70.
  - GS7 (Girder section, Strength I negative flexure, 6.10.8.2.3, nonprismatic L_b → prismatic): Pier 1 interior **1.057 FAIL → 0.915**, Pier 2 interior 1.056 → 0.915, Pier 1 exterior 1.050 FAIL → 0.914, Pier 2 exterior 1.050 → 0.914. GS10 Pier 1 interior bottom flange 0.641 → 0.443.
  - Positive region: Span 1/3 L_b 22.70 → 20.56 ft, Span 2 23.33 → 25.00 ft (two panels of 25 ft between the zones; within the target). Cross-frames module L_b 23.33 → 25.00 ft, stability-bracing n 4 → 5; overhang L_b 22.70 / 23.33 / 22.70 → 20.56 / 25.00 / 20.56 ft.
  - X2: new items "Pier 1 region (27.50 / 35.00 ft)" G4 15.00 ≤ 15.00, "Pier 2 region" G5 15.00 ≤ 15.00 (pass). X3, X5 pass; X4 warns as on main (the built-in transitions at 100/127 ft lie inside the pier zone; 4 girders with a frame within 2 ft, main: 4).

### FSP2. Display: Framing tab, X2, framing plan   [display; X2 items added only with s_p]
- Framing tab: the two inputs and a note; the spacing table shows "t_m; s_p near Pier k" and a pier-region line per span; a note when s_p is entered but not used (not below the target, or not continuous).
- X2 (`framingChecks`, anchor `// FSP (2026-10-15): with a spacing near interior supports s_p`): one item per interior support, the largest panel of any girder whose midpoint is within the region (own bearing ± R), against s_p (pass/warn as X2).
- Framing plan (`framingSVG`, anchor `// FSP: pier regions`): the regions shaded with "s_p = … ft"; caption line.
- Manual: Framing methodology ("Spacing near interior supports"), Suggest Full design paragraph, Framing tab bullet.

### FSP3. Suggest / Full design: s_p as a design variable   [CALCULATION CHANGE — §4 callout: design-variable behaviour]
- **Where:** `checkLayout` (anchors `let ltbLast = false; const ltbB`, `ltbLast = LTB < FLB - 1e-9 && LTB < Rb * Fy - 1e-9;`, `if (ltbLast) ltbB[i]`, `let ltbN = 0;`); new `sgPierCur`, `sgPierList` before `suggestFull`; `suggestFull` (anchor `// FSP (2026-10-15): spacing near interior supports. Where lateral-torsional`); `suggestQuickCheck` (now `runQ(P, f0, f1, tag)` inside, anchor `/* FSP (2026-10-15): spacing near interior supports as a variable`); `sgQuickStart` (`pierSet`), `applySuggestion` and the girder-count study apply (`spPier`), comparison card row, Full design table column, `sgPierQuickTxt` / `sgPierFullTxt`.
- **No formula changed.** `checkLayout` only records, per node, the Strength I negative-flexure bottom-flange ratio where F_nc is set by LTB below R_bF_y (`ltbN`: the largest such ratio that governs the node's bottom flange). L_b in every check still comes from the candidate's own layout (#227).
- **Before:** Full design tried other uniform spacings (cfOpt); the quick suggestion only increased plates.
- **After:** values tried: 22.5, 20, 17.5, 15, 12.5, 10 ft, below the spacing and ≥ max(10 ft, 0.4 × spacing) (0.4 = the C6.7.4.2.1 panel ratio at the region boundary), minus the current s_p (Full design also tries "none" when one is set).
  - Full design (with "Optimize cross-frame spacing" on, continuous units): when `ltbN > 0` for the best passing candidate at the Framing tab spacing, that candidate is re-run (full refine and verification) with each s_p, loosest first, stopping when two closer values in a row each cost more; all are priced with the cross-frames of their own layout; the cheapest passing candidate overall is selected (as before).
  - Quick suggestion: when the fast plates fail and `ltbN > 1.0005`, the check-and-fix is repeated with each s_p (loosest first, until one passes without a plate change); the cheapest passing result is kept (the plates-only result competes).
  - Apply writes `framing.spPier` (only when it differs).
- **Check cases (headless, branch):**
  - Built-in 28° abutments only, default unit costs ($2,500/frame): quick passes as is (0.988; ltbN 0.957 < 1, no variants: same as main). Full design: best at 25 ft D 69 in $1,589,552 (70 frames), ltbN 0.913 → pier study: s_p 22.5 $1,589,552 (70 frames, same layout cost), 20 $1,617,850 (80), 17.5 $1,655,282 (92) → stop. **Kept: plates only, $1,589,552** (the same result as main; closer frames cost $28,298–$65,730 more than the plate steel they save).
  - Same with $500/frame: main and branch both select uniform 17.5 ft, $1,443,764; pier study at 25 ft base: 15 ft $1,474,694, 12.5 ft $1,479,462 → plates/uniform spacing kept.
  - Built-in, target spacing 30 ft, 28° abutments only (quick suggestion): main: fast plates 81.18 (LTB, see open item), plate increases fail after 8 rounds at 16.87, $3,430,161. Branch: plates-only path the same; s_p 22.5 ft passes with the fast plates unchanged (0.989), **$1,686,982, kept**.
  - Two spans 160/160 ft, skews 28/0/28 (quick suggestion): plates only $1,937,683 (pass 0.925); **s_p 22.5 ft $1,915,616 (pass 0.979) kept**. Full design of the same bridge: plates only D 72 $1,765,444 kept; s_p 22.5 … 10: $1,777,500 – $1,819,000.
- **Existing projects:** without s_p the layout is identical, so Full design's plain candidates are identical; Full design can now add pier-study candidates and select one (built-in 15° and 28° abutments only: same selection as main).

 <h3>Cross-frame layout</h3>
 <p>Girders are placed at y = 0, S, 2S, … and each support line passes through the bridge centerline station at its skew angle, so the bearing of girder i at support k is at x = X<sub>k</sub> + (y<sub>i</sub> − y<sub>c</sub>)tan θ<sub>k</sub>. A cross-frame is placed in every bay along every bearing line. Parallel frames (both supports of the span skewed 20° or less, AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.7.4.2.1): n = ⌈L<sub>max</sub>/s⌉ − 1 per bay, where s is the target spacing and L<sub>max</sub> the longest girder span between the two bearing lines, interpolated between the bearing lines, so no girder exceeds s. Normal frames (a support skewed more than 20°): one grid per span at a spacing of at most s (offset by half a spacing in alternate bays if staggered, unless half a spacing is less than d<sub>min</sub>). At a support skewed more than 20° the grid is anchored on the bearing of the obtuse-corner girder: its first line is e = max(clear distance, 4b<sub>f</sub>, 0.4s) from that bearing, so the first intermediate frame on every girder is at least e from that girder's own bearing (C6.7.4.2.1; b<sub>f</sub> is the widest flange plate in the span); at a support skewed 20° or less the first line is one spacing from the bearing. In each bay a grid station is kept where it is at least e (or the clear distance) from both bearings of the bay. Where a girder panel is still longer than s (the acute corners), a frame is added in an adjacent bay: at the station of a frame on the girder's other side (connecting through) or at least d<sub>min</sub> = max(min. offset, 4b<sub>f</sub>) from every other frame on both girders it connects, at least max(clear distance, 4b<sub>f</sub>) from their bearings, preferring positions that close the gap, clear splices and transitions, keep the adjacent panels at least 0.4 times each other, and line up. If any frame falls within the splice clearance of a field splice or shop transition, the grid is shifted within the span (end offsets changed by up to 4 ft, parallel frames by up to a quarter panel, same number of frames), or extra frames are used (up to three per bay line, or two more grid intervals), only when that clears every conflict (the smallest shift with the fewest frames); otherwise the unshifted grid is kept. Conflicts that remain are listed in X4, and the Framing tab lists the spacing used in each span.</p>
+<p><b>Spacing near interior supports</b> (optional; continuous units). With s<sub>p</sub> entered and below the target spacing s, the pier region extends from each interior support a distance R each side (the Pier region input, or, blank, 0.25 times the adjacent span: about the dead-load point of contraflexure of continuous spans; measured along each girder from its own bearing). In each span the frames next to an interior support are spaced s<sub>p</sub>: normal frames from the obtuse-corner bearing (the first line s<sub>p</sub> from an unskewed support, or e = max(clear distance, 4b<sub>f</sub>, 0.4s<sub>p</sub>) at a support skewed more than 20°), parallel frames from the bearings along the longest girder; the pier zone continues to the first grid line beyond the region on every girder. The rest of the span is evenly spaced at most s, starting and ending on the pier-zone lines, so there is no short closing panel (between the zones at least s<sub>p</sub>; where less would remain, the whole span is spaced at most s<sub>p</sub>). Corner frames, splice and transition shifts, extra frames, the stagger offsets d<sub>min</sub> and the first-frame offset at skewed supports follow the rules above, with the limit s<sub>p</sub> for every girder panel whose midpoint is in a pier zone. X2 checks the panels whose midpoint is within the region against s<sub>p</sub>. L<sub>b</sub> everywhere (Girder section rows, Cross-frames module, overhangs, and the checks of the quick suggestion and Full design) is taken from the frames actually laid out. The framing plan shades the regions. Blank, s<sub>p</sub> ≥ s, or simple spans: the layout is the same as without the input.</p>
