## 2026-10-15 — PR: claude/gd-owner-profiles-1 (owner (DOT) profiles, phase 1 of 3: framework and the cross-frame orientation owner rule; engineer's decisions of 2026-10-15; PR link added after merge)

Changes in the main file (GirderDetail outer page) and in the embedded Preliminary sizing page (`const PL_B64`: decoded, edited, re-encoded on its one line). Basis: AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.7.4.2.1 (owner rules applied on top); RIDOT Bridge Design Manual (April 2026) §6.4.3; CTDOT BRSDM Release 1, V2 6.7.4.2 (replaces the 4th and 5th paragraphs of BDS 6.7.4.2); MassDOT LRFD Bridge Manual Part I (Hundredth Anniversary Ed.) 2.3.4.1. Only citations (manual + section) and short paraphrases are in the tool; no manual text is reproduced. Phases 2 (load rules: RIDOT 1.2 multiplier, η, haunch = 0, rating targets) and 3 (owner defaults and checks) are not in this PR; they add rows to the rules table and apply them by rule id.

### OWN1. Owner selector: options, migration, default   [saved data: read-time migration (CLAUDE.md §5)]
- **Where (PL):** `DEFAULT`-adjacent helpers (anchor `const OWN_LIST = ['RIDOT', 'MassDOT', 'CTDOT', 'AASHTO'];`, `function migrateOwner(p)`); autosave load (anchor `P = migrateOwner(migrateCosts(deepMerge(clone(DEFAULT), a.data)))`); `loadData` (same call; used by Open project and Import JSON); Limits tab (anchor `fld('Owner', 'limits.dot'`); owner-limit profiles (anchor `const pfAll = () =>`).
- **Before:** `options: [['MassDOT', 'MassDOT'], ['RIDOT', 'RIDOT'], ['CTDOT', 'CTDOT'], ['Custom', 'Custom']]`; change handler `/* profile switched: nothing else */`; profiles read with `JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY_PF) || '{}')`.
- **After:** `options: [['RIDOT', 'RIDOT'], ['MassDOT', 'MassDOT'], ['CTDOT', 'CTDOT'], ['AASHTO', 'AASHTO (no owner rules)']]`; handler `renderOwnInfo()` (+ the usual recompute).
- **Migration:** `limits.dot` = 'Custom' (or any value not in the list, which no build could write) is read as 'AASHTO'; every limit value is kept (only the `dot` field changes). AASHTO applies no owner rule, which is exactly what 'Custom' (and every owner) did before, so these projects compute identically. Projects without the field get the default `'MassDOT'` (deepMerge), as before. Saved owner-limit profiles (`plateline_profiles_v1`, keyed by owner): a 'Custom' entry is read as the 'AASHTO' entry (copied with `dot: 'AASHTO'`; the stored 'Custom' entry is kept, never deleted); "Load saved limits" keeps the selected owner in `dot`. No key renamed; the stored project is rewritten with 'AASHTO' only when it is next saved.
- **Default for new projects: MassDOT** (unchanged). MassDOT applies AASHTO behaviour plus warnings above 40°/50° (OWN5), so new projects at the built-in skews compute as before.
- **Older builds** opening a project saved as 'AASHTO': the select shows blank, nothing else changes (checked: main `loadData`, no error, no check change).

### OWN2. Bridge-level owner: hand-off, GirderDetail top bar, refresh   [hand-off payload: one new field]
- **PL `bridgeDef`:** new field `owner: plOwner(P)` (also on the `ok: false` object). **New message `gd-owner`** (GirderDetail → PL): sets `limits.dot`, recompute, autosave, publish.
- **GirderDetail:** top bar "Owner [RIDOT ▾] rules" (anchor `<label class="own-pill" for="gd-owner"`), `gdOwner()` (the owner every module reads: `P.df.bridge.owner`, null until Preliminary sizing has published it), `ownSet` (posts `gd-owner` through the ready queue `gdPlPost`, loading Preliminary sizing in the background if needed), `ownBadge` (in `recompute` and on each `gd-bridge`).
- **Refresh (anchor `const ownCh =`):** `nx` now also leaves out `owner` (so the field first appearing on an old project triggers no refresh); an owner change refreshes every module (as a bridge change) only when it also changed the cross-frame list `xf`. An owner change that changes nothing computed (e.g. MassDOT ↔ AASHTO below 40°) does not refresh.
- **Before:** `const nx = o => { const { ts, xs, xf, ...r } = o; ...}; if (ob && ob.ok && nb.ok && nx(ob) !== nx(nb) && ...) gdScheduleRefresh();` **After:** `const nx = o => { const { ts, xs, xf, owner, ...r } = o; ...}; const ownCh = !!(ob && ob.owner && nb.owner && ob.owner !== nb.owner) && JSON.stringify(ob.xf || null) !== JSON.stringify(nb.xf || null); if (ob && ob.ok && nb.ok && (nx(ob) !== nx(nb) || ownCh) && ...) gdScheduleRefresh();`

### OWN3. Owner rules table and infrastructure   [display / infrastructure; no computed change by itself]
- **One table, in GirderDetail:** `OWN_RULES` (anchor `const OWN_RULES = {`): `owners` (manual, short name, AASHTO edition it is written to) and `rules` rows `{ owner, id, kind, sec, value, key?, show?, where, ref?, text }` with kind `default` | `shall-check` | `should-warning` | `pending-reference`. Preliminary sizing receives it when its frame is created: `plShow` places `<script>window.GD_OWN_RULES = …</script>` before the page's own scripts (anchor `// OWN1: the owner rules table, before Preliminary sizing's scripts`); PL reads it as `OWN_TBL` (null when the page runs on its own: no owner rule applied, the Limits tab says so).
- **Rows in phase 1:** RIDOT `xf.orient` (BDM 6.4.3, shall) and CTDOT `xf.orient` (BRSDM V2 6.7.4.2, shall), both `{ thr: 20, scope: 'bridge' }`; MassDOT `xf.skew40` / `xf.skew50` (Part I 2.3.4.1, should); pending references: RIDOT Bridge Standard Details (BDM 6.4.3: spacing, stagger pattern, details), CTDOT standard details (V2 6.7.4.2), MassDOT Part II (2.3.4.1 cross-frame details; 3.6.3.1 plate/weld minimums; 3.6.5.5 stiffener locations; 3.5.2.1 deck tables/overhang; 3.5.1.2 standard haunch; 3.5.6.2 camber Z).
- **Edition note** (table `note`, shown in the top-bar rules panel and the Limits tab): MassDOT and CTDOT BRSDM written to AASHTO 9th Ed. (RIDOT BDM to the 10th); the tool applies the 10th Ed. with owner rules on top.
- **UI:** GirderDetail "rules" opens a panel (`#own-modal`, `ownModal`) listing every owner's rows with section, kind and where applied (pending references: "Not applied: needs …"). PL Limits tab: `renderOwnInfo` (note, the selected owner's rows, link "All owners' rules" → `pl-goto` `to: 'owner'`), and the label of Orientation "Automatic" names the owner rule.
- **Override flags for `default` rows** (`ownFlags`, PL): a row with an input `key` whose value differs is flagged under the input "Overrides <manual> <sec>: <show>" (not blocked). No `default` row exists in phase 1; verified with a test row at run time (RIDOT minTw 7/16: flag at 1/2 in, none at 7/16 in). The cross-frame rule has its own flag (OWN4).

### OWN4. Cross-frame orientation owner rule in `framingLayout`   [LAYOUT / RESULT CHANGE for RIDOT and CTDOT bridges with a support skewed more than 20° — §4 callout]
- **Where (PL):** `framingLayout` span loop (anchors `ox = plOwnXf(P, m), oxA = ox.on && F.orient === 'auto'`, `const arr = oxA && o === 'normal' ? 'staggered' : F.arrange;`), memo key, `normSpan(k, bf, dmin, pz, arr)`, `orient[k].arr`, return `own: ox`; new `plOwnXf(P, m)` after `framingLayout`; Framing tab line `#fr-own` (`frOwnHtml`); spacing table note uses `o.arr`.
- **Before:** `const o = F.orient === 'auto' ? (th <= 20 + 1e-9 ? 'parallel' : 'normal') : F.orient;` (th = larger skew of the span's two supports) and `const stag = F.arrange === 'staggered'`.
- **After:** `const o = F.orient === 'auto' ? (oxA ? ox.o : th <= 20 + 1e-9 ? 'parallel' : 'normal') : F.orient;` and `const stag = arr === 'staggered'`, with `plOwnXf`: θ_max = max |skew| over **every support of the bridge**; owner with `xf.orient` (RIDOT, CTDOT) and Orientation Automatic: θ_max ≤ 20° → every span parallel to the skew (not staggered); θ_max > 20° → every span normal to the girders and **staggered** (the "Normal frames" setting is not used). Orientation set by hand: as entered (flagged, OWN5 fails it if it does not conform). AASHTO, MassDOT, no table: per span exactly as before. All #227/#228 rules still apply unchanged (grid on each girder's obtuse bearing, first offset X5, stagger offsets ≥ max(min. offset, 4b_f) with s/2 < d_min kept contiguous, splice/transition shifts, pier-region spacing) — the owner rule only chooses `o` and the arrangement passed in.
- **Governing provisions:** RIDOT BDM (Apr. 2026) 6.4.3; CTDOT BRSDM R1 V2 6.7.4.2; whole-bridge application per the engineer's decision of 2026-10-15; AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.7.4.2.1 (either arrangement "may" be used, so the owner rule is a permitted choice).
- **Check cases (headless, branch; "main" = the same project on main, MassDOT):**
  1. **Built-in, all supports 28°, RIDOT** (also CTDOT, identical): θ_max = max(28, 28, 28, 28) = 28° > 20° ⇒ normal + staggered in all three spans. Grid s = 23.63 / 24.96 / 23.63 ft (unchanged); stagger s/2 = 23.63/2 = 11.81 ft ≥ d_min = max(4, 4 × 18/12 = 6.00) = 6.00 ft, so the bays are staggered (not flat); X3 G2/G3/G4 11.81 ≥ 6.00 ft pass. Intermediate frames **58 → 52** (all frames 74 → 68). Girder section L_b: interior positive regions **23.63 / 24.96 / 23.63 → 11.82 / 12.48 / 11.81 ft**; **exterior at Pier 1 / Pier 2 12.66 / 13.05 → 22.46 / 21.27 ft** (exterior girders have frames on one side only); interior at the piers 19.56 ft (unchanged). ### OWN5. Check X1 owner items   [CHECK CHANGE — §4 callout]
- **Where (PL):** `framingChecks` X1 (anchor `/* X1 orientation. OWN1 (2026-10-15)`).
- **Before:** items per span: fail only if parallel at θ > 20° (AASHTO 6.7.4.2), ref 'AASHTO LRFD 6.7.4.2', src Code.

MassDOT: θ_max > 40° adds a **warning** item (2.3.4.1: standard details may need modification), > 50° a second warning (diaphragm/connection fatigue; consider an alternate beam layout); X1 is then src DOT.

It is stored with the Preliminary sizing project (its Limits tab has the same selector; a project saved with the former "Custom" owner opens as AASHTO with its limits kept) and every module reads it. (2024); the MassDOT LRFD Bridge Manual and the CTDOT BRSDM are written to the 9th Ed., the RIDOT BDM (April 2026) to the 10th Ed. <b>rules</b> lists every owner rule with the manual section, its kind (shall: pass/fail check; should: warning; default: an editable value, a different entry is flagged "overrides …" but not blocked; pending reference: needs a document not available yet, such as MassDOT Part II, the RIDOT Bridge Standard Details or CTDOT standard details) and where it is applied. In this version (phase 1): the cross-frame orientation rule of RIDOT (BDM 6.4.3) and CTDOT (BRSDM V2 6.7.4.2), applied to the whole bridge in the Preliminary sizing layout (largest support skew 20° or less: parallel to the skew, not staggered; more: normal to the girders and staggered) and checked by X1; and the MassDOT skew warnings above 40° and 50° (Part I 2.3.4.1). Changing the owner refreshes every module like a bridge change when its rules change the cross-frames (otherwise nothing computed changes and no refresh runs). The owners' load rules and owner defaults follow in later versions.</p>
 <h3>Girder report</h3><p><b>Girder report</b> (top bar) builds one calculation package for a selected girder. Choose the girder, the chapters, and whether to re-run auto-design for that girder (otherwise the plates, bolts, and welds as currently entered are checked). Every module is loaded with that girder's demands from the Structural analysis module (its own distribution factors, dead loads, and effective flange width), and each chapter is that module's full worked report: 1, bridge and girder geometry (bridge data, typical cross-section, framing plan, girder elevation, plate schedule); 2, loads and live load distribution factors with derivations; 3, structural analysis (moment and shear envelopes, reactions, deflections, stresses by construction stage); 4, girder section (Strength I, Service II, constructibility, and fatigue at the critical sections); 5, fatigue details; then one chapter per field splice on the girder; bearing stiffeners; transverse stiffeners and connection plates; shear connectors; cross-frames; deck overhang (exterior girders only); and web-to-flange welds and transitions. The package opens with a title page (girder, source of demands, basis of the details, specification, preparer and checker) and a contents list, starts each chapter on a new page, and carries "Girder G# calculation package" in the running header; print it to PDF. The app returns to the module you started from when printing is finished.</p>

## 2026-10-15 — PR: claude/gd-npr-fe-gov (nonprismatic unbraced lengths: F_e = γ_e f_bu with f_bu of the governing section; engineer-approved fix 2026-10-15, strict reading; PR link added after merge)

Changes in the main file (GirderDetail outer page: Girder section) and in the embedded Preliminary sizing page (`const PL_B64`: decoded, edited, re-encoded on its one line). Basis: AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.10.8.2.3c, Eqs. 6.10.8.2.3c-1 to c-3 ("f_bu is calculated at the location where f_bu/R_bR_hF_yc is maximum"; "r_t at the governing cross-section"), Eqs. 6.10.8.2.3a-1 to a-5, 6.10.1.10.2 (R_b), 6.10.3.2.1 (deck placement, R_b = 1.0), C6.10.8.2.3c and Fig. C6.10.8.2.3c-1; App. D6.6.2 (γ_e, unchanged).

**Problem (conservative only, but absurd).** Since CB2 (#198) a nonprismatic unbraced length that does not meet the simplification of 6.10.8.2.3c is checked with C_b = 1.0 and F_e = γ_e f_bu (Eq. c-2), r_t = (L_b/π)√(F_e/E) (Eq. c-3). Every place used **the f_bu of the location being checked**, not the governing f_bu of the unbraced length. Near a point of contraflexure f_bu → 0, so F_e → 0, F_nc → 0 and the ratio → 1/γ_e + f_ℓ/(3γ_e f_bu) blows up (81.18 at 197 ft, built-in, skews 28/0/0/28, 30 ft spacing; Suggest then piled on plate: $3.43M failing at 16.87). Exposed by #227 (per-girder L_b, a 194–222 ft segment straddling the 220 ft flange change).

**Engineer's decision (2026-10-15), STRICT reading:** the governing section is the location within the unbraced length where f_bu/(R_b R_h F_yc) is maximum, each section with its own R_b, R_h and F_yc; F_e = γ_e × f_bu there; the equivalent r_t (Eq. c-3) and the LTB resistance (Eqs. a-4/a-5, a-1 to a-3) are those of that governing section, and that F_nc,LTB is the resistance at every location in the unbraced length. Applied in three places: Preliminary sizing negative flexure (Strength I), Preliminary sizing deck placement, Girder section rows (Method A and the conservative bound / step-limit fallback, F_e = γ_e,bound × f_bu,gov).

Readings to note (ENGINEER_CHECKS GD44): (a) F_nc,FLB (6.10.8.2.2) stays that of each location's own flange (a local check), so F_nc = min(F_nc,FLB of the location, F_nc,LTB of the governing section); (b) Preliminary sizing finds the governing section with R_h = 1.0 and F_yc = F_y of the flanges, as its own checks do (it has no hybrid factor); Girder section then works f_bu,gov, D_c, R_b and R_h of that section itself; (c) candidates: the ends of each constant-section piece in L_b (brace points and section changes) and the analysis nodes within it, with the stress of that piece's section linear between nodes (as App. D6.6.2 in feGeA); (d) in the bound fallback F_e = γ_e,bound f_bu,gov (≤ F_e,s of the governing section, equal to it where the bound's controlling section is the governing one and its largest stress is there); (e) rows saved before this change (no governing-section data) keep their own f_bu (conservative) and say so, until sent again from Preliminary sizing.

### NPG1. Preliminary sizing `checkLayout`: negative flexure and deck placement   [RESULT CHANGE — §4 callout]
- **Where (PL):** new top-level `feGov(pcs, xs, rbOf, fOf)` after `feGeA` (anchor `function feGov(`); in `checkLayout`: `RbOf` and the `'flb'` mode of `Fnc` (anchor `const RbOf = (bf, tf, Dc, tw, Rb1) =>`), `govMemo/govAt` and `fncGov` after `geAt` (anchor `const govMemo = {}, govAt =`), `fncCon` (anchor `const fncCon = (x, T, sgn, fc, f, Dc, tw, beff) =>`), Strength I negative flexure (anchor `if (np.kind === 'ge') { const fF = (s, k) =>`).
- **Before (Strength I):** `Fn = Fnc(b.b, b.t, Dc, tw, false, 1, false, b.b, b.t, G ? Lb / Math.PI * Math.sqrt(G.g * fb / E) : 0);` — `fb` = this node's f_bu.
- **After:** `gv = feGov(np.pcs, xs, s => R_b(s), fF)` (per segment, memoized); `Fn = min(F_nc,FLB(this node's flange), F_nc,LTB(gv.s: its flange, D_c, R_b; r_t = (L_b/π)√(γ_e gv.f/E)))`. `ltbLast` (FSP) = LTB < FLB and LTB < R_b,gov F_y.
- **Before (deck placement):** `Fnc(f.b, f.t, Dc, tw, true, 1, false, f.b, f.t, G ? Lb / Math.PI * Math.sqrt(G.g * fc / E) : 0)` — `fc` = this node's deck-placement stress.
- **After:** the same with gv of the deck-placement stresses (R_b = 1.0, so the largest f_bu in L_b governs) and its flange / D_c.
- `RbOf` is the R_b line that was inside `Fnc`, moved out unchanged (pure refactor: identical results where no 'ge' segment exists; checked, prismatic-only project below).

### NPG2. Preliminary sizing `detailExport`: governing section sent with the Girder section rows   [hand-off payload: two new optional fields]
- **Where (PL):** `rbN`, `govRec` after `fBotN` (anchor `const rbN = (s, gt) =>`); `gsRow` (anchors `nprG = govRec(feGov(np.pcs, xs, q => rbN(q, gt), fS)`, `...(G ? { G: govRec(feGov(cC.n2.pcs, xs, () => 1, fCon)`, `...(nprG ? { nprG } : {})`).
- **New row fields** (only on rows whose unbraced length is 'ge'): `nprG = { x, topB, topT, botB, botT, tw, MDC1, MDC2, MDW, MLL }` (Strength I) and `nprC.G = { x, topB, topT, botB, botT, tw, MDC1, MCL, MDCc? }` (deck placement): the governing location, its plates and the unfactored moments there (linear between nodes, rounded to 0.1 kip-ft as the rows' own). No existing field or key changes. Prismatic rows carry nothing new (identical payload).

### NPG3. Girder section `GM.gs.compute`: F_e and F_nc,LTB of the governing section   [RESULT CHANGE — §4 callout]

- **Before:** `fbu = Math.max(r.cF.f, 0) … Fe = ge != null && fbu > 0 ? ge * fbu : FeS` and `ltbFnc({ … Rb: r.Rb, Rh: r.Rh, … rt: rtE })` (deck: `ge * r.conC.f`, `Rh: r.RhC`).
- **After:** `fbu = Math.max(gv ? gv.f : r.cF.f, 0)` and `ltbFnc({ … Rb: gv ? gv.Rb : r.Rb, Rh: gv ? gv.Rh : r.Rh, … })` (deck: `gv ? gv.f : r.conC.f`, `Rh: gv ? gv.Rh : r.RhC`). `gsGov` works f_bu,gov on the governing section with this module's load factors exactly as a row (Strength I: γ_DC1 M_DC1/S_steel + (γ_DC2 M_DC2 + γ_DW M_DW + γ_LL M_LL)/S_steel+rebar, each permanent load at its max/min factor by its sign; deck placement M_c = γ_DC M_DC(c) + γ_CL M_CL on the steel section) and its D_c, R_b (`rbFactor`) and R_h (`rhFactor`). (2) Preliminary sizing node ratios on the fast plates, 28/0/0/28 at 25 ft: +1e-5 at the two pier nodes (0.95571 → 0.95572): under the strict reading the governing section is chosen by f_bu/R_b, and its F_nc,LTB (with its own R_b) applies to the node; where the node's own R_b is the larger, its LTB resistance can be marginally below the old value. (3) Full design candidates that were not selected show other maxima because they resize to different (cheaper) plates; the "LTB-governed" ratio ltbN (the trigger of the pier-spacing study) moves slightly. Within the same plates every other node ratio decreased or stayed.

### Side note (spec): M_DC1 812.8 vs 807.9 kip-ft "at 197 ft"
Not a bug: the 807.9 value (diagnosis file m_30.json, "standalone check") is the entry at **x = 163 ft** (segment 138–166 ft), the mirror station of 197 ft on the 360 ft bridge, picked up by the diagnosis filter (ratio > 1.0); 812.8 is at 197 ft. Both are from the same fast plates and the same staged analysis; the quick check's first check and a standalone check give identical demands (812.82 at 197 ft before and after a quick check, checked). The two mirror stations differ because the cross-frame point loads in DC1 (XF1) on the interior girder are not mirror-symmetric at skews 28/0/0/28 (frames anchored at the obtuse corner of each skewed abutment, opposite sides at the two ends); on current main 812.82 (197) vs 812.60 (163) kip-ft, and with the cross-frame loads off 800.31 vs 800.66 (plate boundaries at nodes). M_DC2, M_DW and M_LL are equal at the two stations.

 <p><b>Fast study, then full design of the best few.</b> The study sizes every girder count with Suggest's <i>fast sizing</i> (without the quick suggestion's strength and service check): one constant-stiffness continuous-beam model, flange areas from lever-arm estimates, and only this tool's layout checks (proportions, transitions, splices, framing), with no strength, service, or fatigue check. That makes it quick enough to try every girder count, but its weights are a ranking aid. The overhang of each row is chosen with the K<sub>g</sub> of a trial girder sized at the overhang nearest 0.375S. When the study finishes, the Suggest tab offers <b>Full design of the best N</b> (N on the Suggest input tab, default 3, at most 5). It takes the best N rows (by the objective: passing rows first, then the others by governing ratio) and runs Full design (see <i>Quick suggestion and full design</i> below) on each with that row's girder count, spacing, and overhangs, on a copy of the project: each iteration re-runs the staged analysis of the current plates (DC1 on the steel section; DC2 and DW on the long-term composite section, 3n; live load on the short-term composite section, n; cracked near interior piers), recomputes the 4.6.2.2 distribution factors from that section's K<sub>g</sub>, checks every node, and resizes; the live load model of the first iteration is reused inside the loop, and the final verification recomputes everything, so the pass/fail of each row comes from fully recomputed demands. The girder count, spacing, and overhangs are kept from the fast study. Full design takes about 20 to 60 s for each girder count, which is why it runs only for the best few and only when you press the button (it can be cancelled). The results table lists the full-design section, cross-frame spacing, steel per girder, total and per deck area (with the fast-study value beside it), the largest ratio of the final verification, the interior and exterior moment distribution factors of the final girder (longest span), the iterations, and pass/fail (every full-design check at or below 1.0 and no failing layout check; failing Analysis tab checks A1 to A3 are named beside it but do not decide it, because they depend on the bearing stiffener and bearings, which Suggest does not size); the recommendation follows the same objective. Apply sets the girder count, spacing, overhangs, plates, splices, stiffener setting, and cross-frame spacing (Revert restores the previous design). The result is still preliminary: run LL &amp; DL (lldf) for the chosen layout and complete the design checks in GirderDetail.</p>
 <h3>Suggest: lowest-cost layout</h3><p>Suggest proposes the web and flange layout and the field splices for the bridge on the Bridge tab, with one layout for all girders (designed for the envelope of the interior and exterior girders). It searches web depths from about L/36 to L/18 and, unless one is chosen, both an unstiffened and a transversely stiffened web, and keeps the layout with the <b>lowest total cost</b>: structural steel (weight × $/lb), flange shop transitions, transverse stiffeners, and field splices, each priced from the <b>Unit costs</b> on the Suggest tab, which are the same single price list used by the Alternatives study (and sent to GirderDetail's Design all). The defaults are placeholders; only their ratios affect the choice, and the tab shows each as an equivalent weight of steel. Within each field piece the flange width is constant and the thicknesses are chosen by an optimization that adds a transition only where it saves more than it costs. Field splices are placed by the program near the dead-load points of contraflexure and within the shipping length and weight, and moved off cross-frame locations where the framing check X4 finds a conflict.</p>
 <p><b>Rules.</b> AASHTO LRFD minimums always apply: D/t<sub>w</sub> ≤ 150, stiffened or not (Eq. 6.10.2.1.1-1, webs without longitudinal stiffeners), b<sub>f</sub>/2t<sub>f</sub> ≤ 12, b<sub>f</sub> ≥ D/6, t<sub>f</sub> ≥ 1.1t<sub>w</sub>, 0.1 ≤ I<sub>yc</sub>/I<sub>yt</sub> ≤ 10 (6.10.2.2), plates at least 5/16 in (6.7.3), and one steel grade (no hybrid girders). With the AASHTO/NSBA G12.1 fabrication guidelines on (the default), the Limits tab minimum sizes, increments, and transition ratios also apply. The span-to-depth limits of Table 2.5.2.6.3-1 apply by default. The Suggest setting can turn them off only when the Limits tab does not treat span-to-depth as mandatory; with "Treat span-to-depth (G1, G2) as mandatory" on, Suggest (fast and full design, the deck-width study, and the web economy comparison) always applies them, so it never proposes a girder that fails G1 or G2. Full design also requires the final plates of each candidate to meet the minimum depths, since resizing can thin the flanges.</p><p><b>Optimizing the framing.</b> Stiffener spacing and cross-frame spacing are design variables. For stiffened webs with "Optimize stiffener spacing" on (the default), the stiffeners are designed per cross-frame bay: the floor web is the thinnest that works with d<sub>o</sub> = 1.0D in every panel (k = 5 + 5/(d<sub>o</sub>/D)²; interior panels with tension-field action when that setting is on, Eq. 6.10.9.3.2-2 or -8; end panels at an abutment or simple-span bearing with V<sub>n</sub> = CV<sub>p</sub>, 6.10.9.3.3); then each bay between bearings and cross-frames (connection plates act as stiffeners) gets the fewest stiffeners that make every panel a stiffened panel (d<sub>o</sub> ≤ 3D interior, ≤ 1.5D end panels; 6.10.9.1, 6.10.9.3.3) and one more stiffener at a time until every panel passes with its largest Strength I V<sub>u</sub> (6.10.9.3.1; envelope of the interior and exterior girders); an end panel gets its own stiffener at up to 1.5D from the bearing where the even layout does not work, and the rest of the bay is evenly spaced. Webs up to six increments thicker than the floor are priced with their own stiffener counts (a thinner web with more stiffeners against a thicker web with fewer), and the cheapest is kept. The quick suggestion's check and Full design redo the bays with the staged shears and thicken the web if a bay cannot be stiffened enough (d<sub>o</sub> down to 0.5D). With the setting off, the Framing tab ratio d<sub>o</sub>/D is used uniformly, as before. Full design then re-runs its best candidate at cross-frame spacings from 15 ft up to the maximum set on the Suggest tab (default 25 ft) in 2.5 ft steps, with every check (lateral-torsional buckling with the actual spacing and C<sub>b</sub>, deck placement, and the rest), adding the cost of each intermediate cross-frame, and keeps the cheapest. Apply sets the Framing tab cross-frame spacing and the stiffeners (per bay: the Framing tab per-bay table; uniform: d<sub>o</sub>/D). The deck overhang is not modeled in sizing: GirderDetail's Deck overhang auto-design gives the largest spacing the deck placement allows at the exterior girder, so set the maximum spacing no higher than that.</p><p><b>Flange widths.</b> Every flange at a field splice is made wide enough for the number of bolt gage lines each side of the web set on the Suggest tab (default 2) without staggering, using the same geometry as GirderDetail's splice auto-design: the first line clear of the web splice plate by the plate clearance plus the edge distance and by the tightening clearance C₁, the gage between lines, and the edge distance at the flange tip (about 14 in for 7/8 in bolts and two lines). The top flange is kept at one width along the girder unless turned off (it simplifies the haunch and stay-in-place forms), and the width of either flange changes by no more than the set maximum at a field splice (default 4 in; 0 for no limit). Widths are raised, never reduced, to meet these rules, and the thicknesses are then optimized at those widths.</p>

 <p><b>Current girder compared with the suggestion.</b> Below the quick suggestion (or full design) card, the Suggest tab compares the current girder (the Girder tab plates and splices, with the Framing tab stiffeners and cross-frame spacing) with the suggestion, so you can see what the suggestion changes. The overall rows give the web depth and thickness, transverse stiffeners and d<sub>o</sub>/D, cross-frame spacing, field splices, shop transitions, steel per girder and per deck area, cost (Unit costs), the largest strength and service ratio, and the code proportion check counts, with each changed row highlighted. The top flange, web, and bottom flange are then compared plate by plate: the two plate lists are merged by station, so each row is a station range with the current and the suggested plate and what changes (for example &ldquo;t 1 1/8 &rarr; 1 1/4&rdquo;, &ldquo;b 16 &rarr; 15&rdquo;, &ldquo;new transition at 28 ft&rdquo;). A plot shows the flange thickness and width along the girder for both. The current girder is checked in the background with the same staged analysis and strength and service checks as the quick suggestion, at its own cross-frame spacing (an edit restarts the check); the card says whether a change is needed (the current girder exceeds 1.0, is shallower than the Table 2.5.2.6.3-1 minimum depth where that applies, or fails a code proportion check) or would only save steel and cost, and &ldquo;No change suggested&rdquo; when the suggestion is the same as the current girder. If the current girder has input errors, the card lists them instead. The comparison changes nothing until you press Apply.</p>
 <h3>Analysis model</h3><p>The analysis of the current design uses a variable-stiffness, staged line-girder model: DC1 on the steel section, DC2 and DW on the long-term composite section, and live load on the short-term composite section, with the composite stages cracked near interior supports. Its settings (staged or constant EI, cracked zones, deck reinforcement) are made in GirderDetail's Structural analysis module. Suggest mode searches trial layouts with the faster constant-EI model and then designs the chosen layout with the staged model.</p>
 <h3>Variable spacing and deck edges</h3><p>On the Bridge tab, <b>Girder spacing</b> can be <i>Variable</i>: enter the bay spacings from left to right (one fewer than the number of girders). It can also be <i>From exterior girders</i>: enter the center-to-center distance W<sub>cc</sub> between the two exterior girders, and the equal spacing is S = W<sub>cc</sub>/(N<sub>b</sub> − 1), recomputed whenever N<sub>b</sub> or W<sub>cc</sub> changes and shown with the out-to-out deck width W<sub>cc</sub> + left overhang + right overhang; everything else then works exactly as with equal spacing S. The framing plan, cross-section, deck width, and GirderDetail's LLDF and DLs module use each bay; the sizing checks and the built-in approximate distribution factors use the average spacing, and the spacing and overhang checks are made bay by bay. <b>Deck edges</b> can be a barrier (width and the Suggest barrier weight) or a <i>curb and railing</i> on each side: curb width and height, railing load point and weight, and the distance from the deck edge to the traffic face, which sets the roadway. Inside GirderDetail the deck edges are set in the LLDF and DLs module (Cross-section and dead loads) and shown here read-only; the roadway and d<sub>e</sub> then use its live-load traffic faces (mountable curbs and sidewalks under 12 in ignored) and the sizing DC2 per girder is (w<sub>L</sub> + w<sub>R</sub>)/N<sub>b</sub>. When GirderDetail's LLDF and DLs module is in use, its factors and MassDOT dead loads replace the built-in ones (see the Analysis tab).</p>

 <h3>Fatigue detail inventory</h3><p>Demands imported into the Fatigue module now include the full inventory for each girder: web-to-flange welds (B) at the maximum positive range in each span and at each pier; connection plates (C′) at the intermediate cross-frame with the largest fatigue moment range in each span (bottom flange; the same plate the Transverse stiffeners CP2 row checks) and in each pier's negative dead-load region, between the dead-load contraflexure points (top flange), each located at its station along the girder (measured from that girder's own bearing at Abut. 1, so on a skewed bridge it differs from the distance along the bridge centerline) and chosen among the cross-frames on the girders the row stands for (exterior rows: G1 and the last girder; interior rows: every interior girder, with the cross-frames on both sides; demands from Structural analysis: that girder); intermediate stiffener weld toes on the web (C′) for stiffened webs; studs on the top flange at each pier (C, net tension checked); both flanges at each field splice (B, bolted, gross section of the smaller side); and each shop flange transition (B, ground flush, smaller side). Each row carries its girder's effective flange width and deck reinforcement A<sub>r</sub> = (rebar %) × b<sub>eff</sub> × t<sub>s</sub> at mid-depth of the slab, as the analysis uses them; rows entered by hand use the module's b<sub>eff</sub> and A<sub>r</sub>. Cycles per truck passage are 1.5 within 0.1L of an interior support and 1.0 elsewhere. Details you entered by hand are kept.</p>
 <h3>Auto-design (transverse stiffeners, shear connectors, bearing stiffeners, welds, field splices)</h3><p>Each of these modules has an <b>Auto-design</b> button on its Project tab (under Demands from analysis). It searches the module's own inputs and keeps the most economical choice that the module's own AASHTO checks accept, so the result is verified by the same checks shown on screen; a summary lists what was chosen and any check still failing, the module's source note records the date, and <b>Undo auto-design</b> restores the previous inputs. <b>Transverse stiffeners:</b> for each plate type, the smallest plate (width × thickness) passing the projecting-width, b/t, and inertia checks (TS1 to TS3), then the smallest web and flange welds (TS7, CP1) and a weld cutback between 4t<sub>w</sub> and 6t<sub>w</sub> (TS6); connection plates are at least the owner minimum width and thickness so the cross-frame connection fits. Panel shear and spacing (TS4, TS5) depend on the stiffener spacing set by the framing and are reported, not changed; CP2 (Category C′ at the welds) depends on the flange stress range and is reported with the remedy. <b>Shear connectors:</b> the owner stud diameter, the shortest standard stud (3 to 8 in) meeting h/d, penetration, and cover (SC5), transverse spacing 4d, then for each zone the number per row and pitch with the fewest studs per foot passing fatigue, the pitch limits, and edge distance (SC1, SC3, SC4; ties go to fewer studs per row); pitches are then tightened in any strength region short of connectors (SC2). <b>Bearing stiffeners:</b> for each type, the fewest pairs (up to 3) and the smallest plates within the flange width passing BS1, BS2, BS3, and BS6, then the smallest weld (BS4, BS5). <b>Welds:</b> the smallest web-to-flange fillet at each location passing FW1 to FW4. <b>Cross-frames:</b> the type from the bay aspect ratio (K when S/h > 1.5, unless locked), the fewest end bolts for which every member has a passing angle, and for each member the lightest standard angle passing CF1 to CF7 and CF9; the diagonals (and the K-frame horizontal) are then increased until the bracing stiffness CF8 passes. If nothing passes, the summary names the cause: brace forces too large for standard angles (add intermediate cross-frames) or girder in-plane stiffness below the requirement (which stiffer cross-frames cannot fix). <b>Deck overhang:</b> the largest cross-frame spacing at each location that passes OH1 to OH5; a spacing that is too large is reduced, with a note to update the framing. <b>Field splices:</b> see Splices from Preliminary sizing.</p>
 <p><b>Cross-frame stiffness and fatigue.</b> CF8 checks the torsional brace system stiffness of 6.7.4.2.2 (10th Edition): the brace (X frames with tension-only diagonals, or K frames, with single-angle areas reduced by R = 0.65 for end-connection eccentricity), cross-section distortion (infinite when the cross-frame is at least 0.8 of the web depth, otherwise from the connection plate), and the girders' in-plane stiffness β<sub>g</sub> = 24(n<sub>g</sub> − 1)²S²EI<sub>x</sub>/(n<sub>g</sub>L³), in series, against the required stiffness C L M<sub>u</sub>²/(n E I<sub>yeff</sub> C<sub>b</sub>²) with C = 2.4 (twice the ideal stiffness) for deep cross-frames on full-depth connection plates, otherwise 3.6/φ (AISC Appendix 6 form); confirm the coefficient with the edition in use. CF9 checks member fatigue from refined-analysis force ranges with the Fatigue I load factor multiplied by 0.65 for cross-frames (10th Edition, NCHRP 12-113), Category B for bolted slip-critical end connections or E and E′ for welded.</p>

 <p><b>Owner standards</b> (shared by every module): minimum plate thickness (3/8 in), minimum fillet weld (5/16 in), plate thickness and width increments (1/16 and 1/4 in), stud diameter (7/8 in), connection plate minimum width and thickness (5 and 1/2 in), and whether demands imported from an analysis are auto-designed (yes). The defaults are common practice; set your owner's values. <b>Locks:</b> double-click an input's label to lock it (a padlock appears); auto-design keeps locked values and designs everything else around them.</p>
 <h3>Demands from analysis, and overrides</h3><p>Every detail module (Field splice, Bearing stiffeners, Transverse stiffeners, Shear connectors, Cross-frames, Deck overhang, Welds and transitions, Girder section, Fatigue) takes its demands from either analysis. On its Project tab, under <b>Demands from analysis</b>, choose <i>Preliminary sizing</i> (the envelope of the interior and exterior girders that sizing designs) or <i>Structural analysis, G#</i> (the staged, variable-stiffness analysis of any one girder with its own distribution factors and dead loads) and click <b>Get demands</b>. Both use the same conversion to module inputs, so the two sources are directly comparable; the source is recorded in the module's source note and report. A module that needs an exterior girder (Deck overhang) says so if an interior girder is chosen. <b>Send to GirderDetail</b> in Preliminary sizing still loads every module at once.</p><p><b>Overrides.</b> Any imported value can be changed. A changed value is outlined, and hovering it shows the imported value. With <i>Keep my overrides when importing</i> on (the default), overrides are kept when demands are imported again, from either source; rows are matched by location and girder class (exterior or interior), not by position. <b>Reset overrides</b> returns every overridden value to its imported value.</p>
 <h3>Splices from Preliminary sizing</h3><p><b>Sealing, stitching, gage lines, and wrench clearance.</b> DT2 limits the pitch along free edges for sealing, s ≤ 4.0 + 4.0t ≤ 7.0 in (6.13.2.6.2), with t the thinner outside plate: on a flange with inner plates, the thinner of the outer and inner plates. DT3 applies the maximum edge distance 8t ≤ 5.0 in to the splice plates. DT9 applies the stitch-bolt limits of 6.13.2.6.3 to the splice plates, taken to act in compression (the flange splices are designed for P<sub>fy</sub> in tension and compression, and the web plates carry the compressive part of the flange force transferred to the web): pitch s ≤ 12.0t along the force, gage g ≤ 24.0t between lines, including across the web on the outer plate; the end-pitch rule for compression members (6.13.2.6.4) is for built-up members and is not applied. A setting on the Bolts tab makes DT9 advisory instead of required. DT10 is the owner or office minimum number of bolt lines each side of the web (default 2; AASHTO itself requires only two rows along the force, DT6). Staggered holes are not used. DT11 checks the clearance needed to tighten the nuts: flange bolts to the face of the web splice plate, and the web bolts nearest the flanges to the face of the flange splice plates, against C₁ (defaults 1.25, 1.50, 1.625, 1.75 in for 3/4, 7/8, 1, 1-1/8 in bolts; confirm with the AISC Manual Table 7-16 and the fabricator).</p>

## 2026-10-15 — PR: claude/gd-owner-profiles-2 (owner (DOT) profiles, phase 2 of 3: load-level owner rules — RIDOT design load multiplier, load modifiers η, haunch = 0 in composite properties, design rating targets; engineer's decisions of 2026-10-15; PR link added after merge)

Changes in the main file (GirderDetail outer page) and in the embedded Preliminary sizing page (`const PL_B64`: decoded, edited, re-encoded on its one line; round trip byte-identical). Basis: AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 1.3.2.1 (Eqs. 1.3.2.1-1 to -3), 1.3.3–1.3.5, Table 3.4.1-1; AASHTO MBE Eq. 6A.4.2.1-1 (rating form); RIDOT Bridge Design Manual (April 2026) 1.3.1–1.3.3, 3.4.1.2, 4.3.1, 6.5.1, 9.4.6; MassDOT LRFD Bridge Manual Part I (Hundredth Anniversary Ed.) 3.1.2, 3.1.4.3, 3.1.4.4, 3.5.1.2; CTDOT BRSDM Release 1 V2 1.3.3–1.3.5 and V1B "Load Ratings". Only citations and short paraphrases are in the tool. Owner rows are added to the one table `OWN_RULES` (phase 1); Preliminary sizing turns them into one set of factors for the bridge (`plLF`) and publishes it with the bridge (`bridge.lf`); every GirderDetail module reads it (`gdLF`). **AASHTO (and every owner with the factors at 1) computes exactly as before** (all factors multiply by 1, IEEE-exact; proven below).

### OWN6. RIDOT design load multiplier m = 1.2 on HL-93 at Strength and Service   [LOAD FACTOR CHANGE, RIDOT — §4 callout]
- **Reading of BDM 3.4.1.2:** "HL-93 x Multiplier" at the Strength and Service limit states: the multiplier is on the **live load (LL+IM) only** (truck or tandem plus lane), not on DC/DW; not on the live load for deflection (stated), not in the design check load rating (stated), not on fatigue (not a Strength or Service limit state), not on the pedestrian load (not HL-93), not on deck placement (no HL-93). Applied at Strength I, Strength I uplift (A2: the multiplier increases uplift, so it is not "unconservative" there), Service I (bearing reactions), Service II.
- **Where (PL):** `plLF(P)` (new; anchor `function plLF(Pp) {`); `suggestLayout` (anchor `const LF = plLF(P), hh = LF.h0 ? 0 : hhW, gDC = 1.25 * LF.eta`): `demand` (M_u±, V_u, Service II M_s±, required flange areas), `checkLayout` (positive compact/noncompact, Service II, negative compression/tension flange incl. the nonprismatic f_bu), `analyzeGirder` reactions (`strMax`, `strMin`, `serv`), `detailExport` (`fBotN`, `gsPan` ranking), check texts A2/A3, Analysis tab card "Owner load rules", Suggest tab caption, Service II area derivation, manual "Combinations".
- **Where (GD):** `gdOwnM(OWN_K.<module>)` multiplies the module's entered γ: field splice (`llS` × ηm, `llSv` × m), bearing stiffeners (`ll`), transverse stiffeners (`ll`), welds/transitions (`ll`), Girder section (`ll`, `sll`); Structural analysis `saCombosOwn()` (Strength LL × ηm, Service LL × m, pedestrian load `pl` without m; `saComb` uses `C.pl` only when m ≠ 1), `saStress` (Strength/Service stresses with m on LL+IM only), DXF/diagram shear envelopes. Fatigue γ, deck placement γ unchanged.
- **Before:** e.g. PL `Mup[i] = (dc >= 0 ? 1.25 : 0.90) * dc + (dw >= 0 ? 1.50 : 0.65) * dw + 1.75 * Mp[i]; Msp[i] = dc + dw + 1.3 * Mp[i];` GD `const g = k => num(G[k]);` (splice), `r.Vu = g('dc') * (...) + g('ll') * r.VLL` (ts) with g the entered factor.
- **After:** `Mup[i] = (dc >= 0 ? gDC : gDCn) * dc + (dw >= 0 ? gDW : gDWn) * dw + gLL * Mp[i]; Msp[i] = dc + dw + gSV * Mp[i];` with `gLL = 1.75 * LF.eta * LF.m`, `gSV = 1.3 * LF.m`; GD `const gO = gdOwnM(OWN_K.splice), g = k => num(G[k]) * gO(k);` (and the same in each module).
- **Hand check (review case):** M_LL+IM = 1000, M_DC = 800, M_DW = 150 kip-ft. Strength I before: 1.25(800) + 1.50(150) + 1.75(1000) = 1000 + 225 + 1750 = **2975**. RIDOT, m only: 1000 + 225 + 1.75(1.2)(1000) = **3325** kip-ft (the all-loads reading would give 1.2 × 2975 = 3570; the text supports LL only). With RIDOT's default η_I = 1.05 (OWN7): 1.05 × 3325 = **3491.25**. Service II: 800 + 150 + 1.30(1000) = 2250 → 800 + 150 + 1.30(1.2)(1000) = **2510**.
- **Tool check (built-in 15°, RIDOT, Girder section row "Span 1, max. positive at 43.0 ft, interior"):** M_DC1 = 1007.8, M_DC2 = 193.9, M_DW = 160.6, M_LL+IM = 1809.5 kip-ft; γ_DC = 1.25(1.05) = 1.3125, γ_DW = 1.50(1.05) = 1.575, γ_LL = 1.75(1.05)(1.2) = 2.205; M_u = 1.3125(1201.7) + 1.575(160.6) + 2.205(1809.5) = 1577.23 + 252.95 + 3989.95 = **5820.12** kip-ft (tool 5820.12; AASHTO factors on the same row: 4909.65); Service II M_s = 1362.3 + 1.56(1809.5) = **4185.12** (tool 4185.12).

### OWN9. Design rating targets (GS20), owner notice, refresh, documentation   [NEW CHECK (owner); saved data: new optional fields]
- **GS20 "Design load rating, HL-93 inventory"** (Girder section, group "Design load rating", src DOT; only when the owner has a `rate.*` row: RIDOT, CTDOT, MassDOT): per location and limit state, RF = the multiple of the HL-93 inventory live load at which that module's own check reaches 1.00, at the dead load factors entered (no owner η, no multiplier): `RF = (1 − r_0)/(r_1 − r_0)` with r_0 the check ratio with γ_LL = 0 and r_1 with γ_LL = 1.75 (Strength I: GS6, GS7 or GS9 as used, GS8, GS11) or 1.30 (Service II: GS12, GS13) — the MBE form (C − γ_DC DC − γ_DW DW)/(γ_LL(LL+IM)) with φ_c = φ_s = 1.0; where the resistance depends on the load (r at 2 × LL off the straight line: nonprismatic F_e = γ_e f_bu, web bend-buckling through D_c, amplified f_ℓ) RF is the root of the quadratic through 0, 1, 2 × LL; Fatigue: RF = 1/(GS17 ratio) at GS17's limit state. ## 2026-10-15 — PR: claude/gd-mode-toggle (working mode toggle "Preliminary designer" / "Design modules", and one project title block; engineer's decisions of 2026-10-15; PR link added after merge)

No engineering formula, load or resistance factor, unit, unit conversion or code reference is changed. The change is in where the modules take their demands from, when they are reloaded, which inputs are shown, and where the project information is kept. Every module's checks are identical to main for the same demand source (verification below). The embedded Preliminary sizing (`PL_B64`) is decoded, edited and re-encoded on one line.

Saved data: no storage key and no existing field is changed. New optional fields in the GirderDetail project (`girderdetail_autosave_v1`, `girderdetail_projects_v1`, Export JSON): `gdMode` ('pl' or 'mod'), `tb` (the title block), `tbMig` (the migration record, with the earlier values), `plSync` (`{ sig, ts }`: the signature and time of the Preliminary sizing demands last loaded into every module). Preliminary sizing's saved data (`plateline_*`) is unchanged; its project-info fields are hidden in GirderDetail, not changed. `girderdetail_inbox_v1` is unchanged (the demand signature `dsig` is a field of the message, not of the stored inbox). A project saved by this version opens in main without errors and with the same results (main ignores the new fields); a project saved by main opens here through the migrations below.

### GDM1. Working-mode toggle at the top of GirderDetail, saved per project   [UI, saved data: new optional field]
- **Where:** new bar `#gd-top` between the header and the module tabs (anchor `<div class="gd-top" id="gd-top">`); new code block "GirderDetail: working modes (GDM) and the project title block (GDT)" before `/* ---------- print ---------- */` (`gdModeInfer`, `gdModeInit`, `applyGdMode`, `setGdMode`); `initP` and `loadData` call `gdModeInit`; `init` calls `applyGdMode`; CSS anchor `/* working mode and project title block bar (GDM, GDT; 2026-10-15) */`.
- **After:** two large buttons, **Preliminary designer** and **Design modules**. The mode is saved in `P.gdMode`. Switching keeps the module tab, its output tab and scroll position (only the Preliminary sizing tab's own output tab moves to Drawings when its current tab is hidden in Design modules).
- **Projects saved before the toggle** (`gdMode` missing; decision asked of me, stated here): **Design modules** when
  1. a module's demands came from anywhere but Preliminary sizing (`_impSrc` label not "Preliminary sizing…"/"PlateLine…", e.g. "Structural analysis, G2"), or
  2. the last request was from Structural analysis (`ui.lastSrc` = `sa:g`), or
  3. a module that takes demands (field splice, bearing stiffeners, transverse stiffeners, shear connectors, cross-frames, deck overhang, welds, girder section, fatigue) has no import record and its data differ from the built-in example (values entered by hand; not to be overwritten);
  
  otherwise **Preliminary designer**. When an older project opens in Design modules the top bar says why ("Opened in Design modules: Girder section: values entered here…"), until the mode is switched. A new project (built-in example) is Preliminary designer.
- Switching to Preliminary designer with modules on another source asks first ("These modules have other demands: Girder section: Structural analysis, G2 … will be replaced by Preliminary sizing's (your overrides and locked inputs are kept)"); Cancel keeps Design modules.

### GDM2. Preliminary designer: every module takes its demands from Preliminary sizing and stays in sync automatically   [demand source and timing; no formula change]
- **Where:** Preliminary sizing (decoded `PL_B64`): new `plHash`, `plDsigOf`, `plDsig`, `postDsig`, `gdModeSet` and a `gd-mode`/`gd-tb` listener before `function sendSplices(` (anchor `GirderDetail working modes (GDM, engineer's decisions 2026-10-15)`); the `pl-export-req` reply and the embedded "Send to GirderDetail" message carry `dsig`; the recompute wrapper posts `pl-dsig` (anchor `// GDM: the demand signature`); the gd-owner / gd-an / gd-dfx / gd-xs handlers are wrapped in `PL_GDMSG++ … finally PL_GDMSG--`. GirderDetail: `gdScheduleRefresh` (anchor `GDM (2026-10-15): why = 'bridge'`), the `gd-inbox` listener (anchor `gdSyncNote(j, e.data.dsig);`), `gdSyncAdopt`, `gdSyncCheck`, `gdSyncNote`, `gdSyncTxt`, `gdSyncShow`, `srcPanel` (anchor `GDM (2026-10-15): Preliminary designer: no source choice`), `renderInbox`, `getDemands` (anchor `GDM: Preliminary designer keeps Design modules' source`), `designAllStart` and the `da_go` click, the girder report dialog.
- **Before:** each module chose its demand source (Preliminary sizing or Structural analysis Gx) and loaded it with Get demands; the automatic refresh reloaded every module only when the bridge record changed (spans, skews, girders, plates, splices, owner load rules), from the last source.
- **After (Preliminary designer):**
  - All tabs are present. No module offers a source choice, Get demands or the Import-from-PlateLine buttons (the field splice case list stays: it picks which case the module shows). The module's Project tab reads "Demands from Preliminary sizing, updated (time)"; Keep my overrides / Reset overrides and the auto-design panel stay. The top bar says "Demands from Preliminary sizing, in sync, updated (time)", "Updating the modules from Preliminary sizing…", or a warning.
  - After each analysis Preliminary sizing posts `pl-dsig`: a signature (FNV-1a hash and length) of the demands it would send (`inboxPayload` of the envelope analysis, time stamps removed). The reply to a Preliminary sizing request carries the signature of the demands it contains (`dsig`), and GirderDetail stores it in `P.plSync` when the reply loads every module (`all`, `refresh`, `xfall`). When the posted signature differs from `P.plSync.sig`, the existing automatic refresh runs 1.5 s later: `getDemands('pl', 'refresh')`, i.e. every module loaded and auto-designed through the request IDs, ordering and cross-frame second pass of XR1–XR3, unchanged. It is skipped if the signatures match again by then or a request is outstanding (re-checked when it is answered). Any change in Preliminary sizing that changes the demands therefore updates every module, also changes that did not refresh before (for example the cross-frame spacing or the stiffener spacing d<sub>o</sub>/D on the Framing tab, or GirderDetail inputs that Preliminary sizing uses, such as the LLDF and DLs factors) — no button.
  - The bridge-change refresh is unchanged in Design modules mode. In Preliminary designer it always runs (the owner standard "Auto-refresh" is for Design modules) and always from Preliminary sizing; a bridge change and a demand change in the same 1.5 s make one refresh.
  - Preliminary sizing with input errors: no request and no alert; "Preliminary sizing has input errors: the modules keep their last demands."; updated once the errors are fixed.
  - Loop guard: Preliminary sizing counts its own recomputes (`u`, not those caused by GirderDetail's messages). At most 3 automatic updates in a row without a change by the user (in Preliminary sizing, or an input in GirderDetail); then "Automatic updates paused after 3 in a row (the cross-frame auto-design keeps changing the frame weights). Update now".
  - Design all: Preliminary sizing only (no source choice). The girder report still loads one girder's Structural analysis demands into every module for its chapters; afterwards every module is loaded from Preliminary sizing again (the dialog says so). The "Run Get demands again" banner reads "The demands are updated again automatically."
  - The remembered source of Design modules mode (`ui.lastSrc`, `ui.srcSel`) is not changed by requests made in Preliminary designer.
  - A project from before the toggle opening in Preliminary designer whose modules all took their demands from Preliminary sizing is taken as in sync (`plSync.adopted`; nothing is reloaded on opening, as on main, until Preliminary sizing changes). One with modules never loaded (the built-in example) is loaded from Preliminary sizing when it opens.
- **Governing provision:** none (no calculation change).
- **Check case (built-in example saved by main, 5 girders, AASHTO):** Preliminary sizing → Framing → cross-frame spacing 20 ft.
  - **Before (main):** no module changes; Get demands or Design all needed. Module checks `6f4aa5d36108`.
  - **After (Preliminary designer):** 1.5 s later one refresh from Preliminary sizing, no button; module checks `4b91646ea70b`, identical to main with Get demands for every module (`getDemands('pl','refresh')`) after the same edit (`4b91646ea70b`). In Design modules mode nothing is reloaded, as on main (`79446684b1d5` = main).

### GDM3. Design modules: Preliminary sizing becomes "Bridge & girder", the bridge definition only   [UI only]
- **Where:** Preliminary sizing CSS (anchor `GirderDetail working modes (GDM, 2026-10-15): in "Design modules"`), `gdModeSet`, `openReport`/`doPrint` (`RPT_GEO`, `rptOn`); GirderDetail `MODS.pl.title` (getter), `applyGdMode` (tab label), the `pl-status` listener (no sizing-check count on the tab).
- **After:** the tab reads **Bridge & girder**; its Summary and Checks tabs, Suggest and Alternatives (with Full design, candidates and the girder-count study), the status bar of the sizing checks and the Suggest undo bar are hidden (not removed; switching back shows them). Inputs kept: Project, Bridge (spans, supports and skews, girders and spacing, deck and cross-section), Girder (plates, web, field splices, grades), Framing, Limits (owner, η inputs, plate limits). The Suggest input tab reads **Loads** and shows only its Loads section (FWS, SIP forms, barrier, construction live load: part of the bridge record). Output tabs kept: Drawings, Analysis, Schedule, Manual; its print options are those four. It publishes the bridge record exactly as before. Every module keeps its own demand source and Get demands, as on main (Structural analysis Gx, Preliminary sizing, or values entered).

### GDT1. One project title block, read by every report, drawing and hand-off   [UI, saved data: new optional field; printed headers unchanged for the same values]
- **Where:** `#tb-sum` (top bar) and the dialogs `#tb-modal`, `#tb-note`; `gdMeta`, `tbBuild`, `tbRender`, `tbOpen`, `tbNotice`, `gdTbMigrate`, `gdPlState`; the Project tab's "Calculation header" (anchor `Edit the title block</button>`); readers: `bsRenderReportHead`, `gmReportHead`, `renderReportHead`, `buildCalcReport` (cover: bridge No. and description when entered), `crPageCSS`, `crTitleBlock`, girder report cover and footer, `dxfCover`, `dxfSheet` (anchor `const mt = gdMeta(), cells =`), DXF/PNG/CSV file names, Save's default name, `gdStPayload` (`project`), the shared-project-info map (anchor `GDT (2026-10-15): the project title block's fields`); Preliminary sizing `renderReportHead` (anchor `GDT: GirderDetail's project title block`), its Project tab (`#gd-tb-note`, `html.gd-tb`).
- **After:** `P.tb = { name, no, bridge, desc, compBy, compDate, chkBy, chkDate }` (project name, project No., bridge / structure No., description, computed by, date, checked by, checked date), with the owner shown (read only, from the top-bar owner). The top bar shows it; "Title block" edits it. Each module's Project tab keeps only Subject and Task (per calculation), with "Edit the title block"; Preliminary sizing hides its project name, computed/checked and date fields (kept in its data) and its report uses the title block. Imports no longer rewrite `P.meta.name` once the title block exists (the old values stay as they were). "Use shared project info" / "Share project info" (HANDOFF §4.1) moved to the title block dialog, with `bridgeId` now mapped (Bridge / structure No.). The ST-Girder hand-off (`girderDemands`, HANDOFF §4.9) sends the title block's project name as `project` (a string as before; was Preliminary sizing's bridge name, which the title block takes on migration, so the value is the same for migrated projects).

### GDT2. Migration of the project information (§5)   [saved data: new optional fields; nothing removed]
- **Where:** `gdTbMigrate` (runs when Preliminary sizing has loaded: its first status message, or at Open/Import when it is up), `tbNotice`.
- **Rule:** a project without `tb`: each field takes **Preliminary sizing's value** (its own saved `meta`: name, computed by, date, checked by, checked date; it has no project No.); a blank is filled from the **modules' calculation header** (`P.meta`: project No., project name, computed/checked by, dates; one header shared by every GirderDetail module); bridge No. and description start blank. Fields where both are filled and differ are listed **once** in a notice (module, field, earlier value, title block value) and recorded in `P.tbMig.conf`; `P.tbMig` also keeps both sources' values, listed under "Values before the title block" in the title block dialog. `P.meta` and Preliminary sizing's fields are left unchanged.
- **Check case:** modules' header: project No. 2024-117, name "Route 6 over Blackstone River", computed by MLL, date 10/01/2026, checked by JDS; Preliminary sizing: name "Example 3-span continuous", computed by blank, checked by ABC, checked date 10/02/2026.
  - **After:** title block: name "Example 3-span continuous", No. 2024-117, computed by MLL, date 10/01/2026, checked by ABC, checked date 10/02/2026. Notice: "GirderDetail modules (calculation header on the Project tab) | Project name | Route 6 over Blackstone River | Example 3-span continuous" and "… | Checked by | JDS | ABC". `P.meta` unchanged, also after a refresh; no second notice after reopening.

 <p>GirderDetail designs steel I-girder details in modules chosen at the top of the window. <b>Field splice</b> (Parts 2 through 8) designs bolted field splices to AASHTO LRFD Article 6.13.6. <b>Bearing stiffeners</b> (Parts 10 through 12) checks bearing stiffeners to Article 6.10.11.2 at every bearing of a girder line. <b>Transverse stiffeners</b> (Part 13), <b>Shear connectors</b> (Part 14), <b>Cross-frames</b> (Part 15; the tab reads <b>Diaphragms</b> when the diaphragm is the bracing used), <b>Deck overhang</b> (Part 16), and <b>Welds and transitions</b> (Part 17) complete the girder detail package, and <b>Girder section</b> (Part 18) checks the composite girder itself at its critical sections, <b>Fatigue</b> (Part 19) designs and evaluates the fatigue details along the girder, and <b>Distribution factors</b> (Part 20) computes the live and dead load distribution for the whole bridge defined in Preliminary sizing. Every detail module has a <b>Detailing</b> tab (<b>Proportions</b> in the Girder section module) listing its proportion and detailing limits as a checklist (the field splice adds a dimension schedule of plates, fillers, and bolt patterns) and a <b>Report</b> tab with the full calculation document. Choose the module from the list at the top of the window. <b>Preliminary sizing (PlateLine)</b> is the first module: it proportions the girder line, runs the approximate analysis, and has its own manual, projects, and report inside it. Its "Send to GirderDetail" button (Analysis tab) offers to load every detail module at once. The detail modules share one project file and title block; the sizing module keeps its own saved projects. The field splice module covers flange splices with outer and inner splice plates, the web splice with two web plates, slip-critical high-strength bolts, and the detailing rules of Article 6.13.2.6. Every load combination is fully worked, every check shows its governing location with the substituted equation, and drawings and a 3D view are generated to scale. Splice sections and approximate demands can be imported from PlateLine.</p>
+<h3>Working modes and the project title block</h3>
+<p>The toggle at the top of the window chooses how the modules get their demands. It is saved with the project.</p>
+<ul>
+<li><b>Preliminary designer.</b> Preliminary sizing designs the girder, and every tab is present. Every module takes its demands from Preliminary sizing (the envelope of the interior and exterior girders) and is updated automatically, about 1.5 s after any change in Preliminary sizing that changes those demands. The update loads every module and auto-designs the detail modules, exactly as Design all does. There is no demand-source choice and no Get demands button; each module's Project tab reads "Demands from Preliminary sizing, updated (time)", and the bar at the top says when an update is running. Overrides of imported values and locked inputs are kept. When the cross-frame auto-design keeps changing the frame weights, the automatic updates stop after 3 in a row and ask for "Update now". The girder report still loads one girder's Structural analysis demands into every module for its chapters; the modules return to the Preliminary sizing demands afterwards.</li>
+<li><b>Design modules.</b> The Preliminary sizing tab becomes <b>Bridge &amp; girder</b>: the bridge definition only (spans, supports and skews, girders and spacing, deck and cross-section, plates, field splices, framing, materials, limits and owner), which it publishes to the modules as before. Its sizing work (Summary and Checks, Suggest, Full design, candidates, Alternatives and the girder-count study) is hidden, not deleted; the Suggest input tab reads "Loads" and shows only the loads (wearing surface, SIP forms, barrier, construction live load). Each module keeps its own demand source (Structural analysis girder, Preliminary sizing, or values entered on its tabs) with its Get demands button, as before.</li>
+<li><b>Projects saved before the toggle</b> open in Design modules when a module's demands came from Structural analysis (or the last request was from Structural analysis), or when a module that takes demands holds values entered by hand; otherwise in Preliminary designer. A project whose modules all took their demands from Preliminary sizing is taken as in sync when it opens (nothing is reloaded until Preliminary sizing changes); one with modules never loaded is loaded from Preliminary sizing when it opens. The top bar says which rule chose the mode.</li>
+<li><b>Project title block.</b> The button at the top right shows and edits the one title block of the project: project name, project No., bridge or structure No., description, computed by, checked by and dates, with the owner shown. Every module's calculation report, the girder report, Preliminary sizing's report, the DXF title blocks, file names, the ST-Girder hand-off and "Share project info" use it; each module's Project tab keeps only the calculation subject and task. A project saved before the title block takes Preliminary sizing's project info, with blanks filled from the modules' calculation header; fields where the two differed are listed once, and the earlier values stay in the saved project (the title block editor lists them).</li>
+</ul>

### OWN10. GD46 — the owner's η_I question defaults to **no**   [LOAD FACTOR CHANGE (default), MassDOT/RIDOT/CTDOT — §4 callout]
- **Decision (engineer, 2026-10-15):** η = 1.0 unless the user answers yes (RIDOT ADT ≥ 5000, BDM 1.3.3; MassDOT critical/essential, 3.1.4.4; CTDOT NHS/STRAHNET/evacuation route, BRSDM V2 1.3.5). Nonredundant (≤ 3 girders, automatic) and nonductile are unchanged.
- **Where (PL):** `DEFAULT.bridge.eta` (anchor `eta: { I: 'no', R: 'auto'`; was `I: 'yes'`); `plLF` (anchor `if (rI) eI = yn(E.I, false)`; was `yn(E.I, true)`, and `inI: own && rI ? yn(E.I, false)`; new `Imig` flag in the factors); new `migrateEta(p)` called from `migrateOwner` (every load path: autosave, Open, Import, Undo); `onScalar` sets `bridge.eta.Iu = 1` when the user changes the η_I input; `lfInputs` result line says when η_I was changed by the migration.
- **Before:** `if (rI) eI = yn(E.I, true) ? +rI.value.f : 1;` and `eta: { I: 'yes', … }`.
- **After:** `if (rI) eI = yn(E.I, false) ? +rI.value.f : 1;` and `eta: { I: 'no', … }`; `function migrateEta(p) { const E = p && p.bridge && p.bridge.eta; if (E && typeof E === 'object' && E.I === 'yes' && !E.Iu) { E.I = 'no'; E.Imig = 1; } return p; }`.
- **Migration (CLAUDE.md §5):** PR #231 did not record whether the η_I answer was chosen by the user. A saved `'yes'` without the new marker `Iu` is taken as the untouched default and becomes `'no'` (`Imig: 1` records it). From now on a user's answer is marked (`Iu: 1`) and kept. A saved `'no'` is kept. Projects without `bridge.eta` (before #231) get the new default. Limitation: a `'yes'` the user chose deliberately under #231 (before this marker existed) cannot be told apart and also becomes `'no'`; the one-time GirderDetail notice and the Limits tab say so, and setting it back to Yes is kept.
- **Where (GD):** bridge handler (anchor `else if (lfCh && ob.ok && nb.ok && ob.lf && nb.lf.Imig`): when the published factors change because of the migration, `P.ownLd = { o, t: 'Load modifier η_I changed', items }` → the existing one-time notice (`gdOwnLdNote`, title variant `q.t`). Help "Owner load rules (phase 2)": defaults text.
- **Hand check (built-in 15°, RIDOT, Girder section row "Span 1, max. positive at 43.0 ft, interior"; M_DC1+DC2 = 1201.7, M_DW = 160.6, M_LL+IM = 1809.5 kip-ft, m = 1.2):**
  - Before (η_I yes, η = 1.05): M_u = 1.3125(1201.7) + 1.575(160.6) + 2.205(1809.5) = 1577.23 + 252.95 + 3989.95 = **5820.12** kip-ft (tool 5820.12).
  - After (η_I no, η = 1.00): M_u = 1.25(1201.7) + 1.50(160.6) + 2.10(1809.5) = 1502.13 + 240.90 + 3799.95 = **5542.98** kip-ft (tool 5542.98) = 5820.12/1.05. GS6 0.626 → 0.594.
  - CTDOT built-in (η only): Preliminary sizing interior M_u+ 5180 → **4934** kip-ft (the value #231 reported for η_I = "no").
- **Tool check:** every MassDOT/RIDOT/CTDOT project saved by main 9e92c3b (built-in 15°, 28°, xsA, curb) opened in the branch gives **exactly** the results of main with η_I set to "no" (every module check item, Preliminary sizing checks and analysis arrays, Structural analysis G1). Before/after: see the PR description.

### OWN11. GD45 — the RIDOT multiplier is not applied to the pedestrian load in rows from Structural analysis   [LOAD FACTOR CHANGE, RIDOT with a pedestrian load, demands from Structural analysis — §4 callout; less conservative than #231]
- **Problem:** Structural analysis sends LL+IM with the pedestrian load PL added (`Mp = LLp + PLp`, `Vp = LVp + PVp`, `llMax = llMax + Pp`). The detail modules multiply LL+IM by γηm, so under RIDOT the 1.2 also multiplied PL (Structural analysis's own combinations and Preliminary sizing were already exact).
- **Where (GD):** `gsaSA` and `getDemands` (src `sa:g`) also send `PMp, PMn, PVp, PVn` (PL alone, only when nonzero) and `reac.Pp/Pn`. New `gdPLq`, `gdPLe`, `gdGovML`, `gdPLCard` (anchor `/* GD45 (engineer decision 2026-10-15): the design load multiplier m is on HL-93 LL+IM only`). Field splice (`plE`, `M`, `V`; `R.plAdj`), Bearing stiffeners (`gdPLe(r0, r, ['RLL'], …)`), Transverse stiffeners (`VLL, VLLb, VLLc`), Welds (`VLL`), Girder section (`MLLp, MLLn, VLL, VLLp` and `nprG.MLL` in `gsGov`; not in the GS20 rating run, which has no m). Splice: `pl` is skipped by the "must be a number" check, and `spliceApply` keeps only the imported `pl`. Each module's loads tab shows the card "Pedestrian load without the design load multiplier" (received value, PL, value used).
- **Where (PL):** `detailExport` (new `plOn`, `qV`, `qSh`, `qIn`, `qP`, `plTag`; rows get `pl = { key: [PL part, value] }`; `govRec` adds `pl.MLL`; `fBotN` and `gsPan` rank with m off PL), `spliceExport` (`dem.pl`), `bearingExport` (`row.pl.RLL`). Only when m ≠ 1 and the arrays carry PL.
- **Before:** factored LL term = γηm (LL+IM+PL).
- **After:** γηm (LL+IM+PL − PL) + γη PL = γηm × [(LL+IM+PL) − PL + PL/m] (Strength); Service: γm(…) likewise.
- **Saved data:** new optional row field `pl` (and `P.dem.pl`) = `[PL part, the LL+IM value it belongs to]`; used only while the row still holds that value (an edited value drops it). Rows without it compute as before.
- **Hand check (xsA, RIDOT, η = 1.0, Structural analysis G1, Transverse stiffeners row "Span 1, first stiffener from Abut. 1, G1"):** V_LL+IM+PL = 87.3 kip, PL = 11.8 kip, m = 1.2. LL term before 1.75(1.2)(87.3) = 183.33 kip; after 1.75[1.2(87.3 − 11.8) + 11.8] = 1.75(102.40) = **179.20** kip = 2.10 × (87.3 − 11.8 + 11.8/1.2 = 85.33) (tool 85.33). Difference 0.35 × 11.8 = 4.13 kip. Field splice MT1 Strength I positive: 2048.31 → **1985.14** kip-ft (= −0.35 × 180.5).
- **Uplift check A2 (reviewed, no change):** A2 is the Strength I check R_u,min = 0.90/η R_DC + 0.65/η R_DW + 1.75ηm R_LL,min ≥ 0 with the HL-93 LL+IM minimum reaction: an HL-93 LL+IM Strength check, so BDM 3.4.1.2 ("Design Load Multiplier of 1.2 at the Strength and Service Limit States (HL-93 x Multiplier) … Where unconservative to include this multiplier such as substructure overturning, the multiplier shall be removed") applies, and here the multiplier increases the uplift (conservative), so it is kept. In Preliminary sizing's own analysis there is no pedestrian load; with Structural analysis arrays the reactions' `strMin` come from Structural analysis, which already takes PL without m. (The separate BDM requirement to check uplift during deck placement is outside A2.)
