 <h3>DXF export (AutoCAD)</h3><p><b>Format.</b> The default format is an AutoCAD 2018 DXF with the drawings at full size (inches, units stored in the file) in model space and one paper space layout per sheet (tabs 01, 02, …): a true 34 × 22 (or 17 × 11) page with the border and title block and a locked viewport at the sheet scale; plot each layout at 1:1. Linetypes scale with the viewport (PSLTSCALE on). Every layout's page setup is ready to plot: DWG To PDF.pc3, ANSI full-bleed D (or B) paper, 1:1, and the monochrome.ctb plot style, so all sheets plot black and white. To plot the whole set to one PDF, type PUBLISH in AutoCAD, keep the listed layouts (remove the Model entry), set Publish to PDF with Multi-sheet file, and click Publish. With Elevation of every girder selected, each girder also gets its own elevation sheet with its bearing stations, connection plates, moment envelope, and camber. Everything in model space lies on a sheet: each sheet's drawings are sized to fit its viewport with a 1/4 in. margin (text and dimension extents included), no two viewports show the same area, and the export warns if a sheet cannot fit even at 1:1200. This format is written by the ezdxf library running in the browser; the first export downloads it (internet needed, about 15–30 s), later exports are quick. The R12 option works offline and draws each sheet's border around the drawings in model space instead (plot each by window at the scale in its title block).</p><p><b>Also:</b> analysis diagrams for an exterior girder (G1) and an interior girder (G2): moment and shear envelopes (DC1, DC2 + DW, LL+IM, Strength I, values labeled), top and bottom flange stresses by stage with Service II against 0.95F<sub>y</sub>, and dead load deflections, each band at a stated vertical scale; a design summary (every Girder section check with its governing ratio and location, and each detail module's Design all result); and a standard details sheet filled in from the design (bolt holes and edge distances, stiffener clip and weld termination, connection plate at the tension flange, shear studs, flange transitions, splice fillers, camber measurement, bearing stiffeners at skewed supports, weld symbol legend) with typical construction staging notes. A load rating table will follow once rating is added.</p><p><b>Sheets available:</b> cover and sheet index with a revisions table; framing plan (top flanges to scale, connection plates, bearing and intermediate stiffeners, top flange splice plates, bearings, dimension chains, girder length and cross-frame location tables, and callouts to the cross-frame details); erection diagram with piece marks, the shipping piece table (plate weights at 490 pcf, plus 5% for details, heaviest piece flagged), steel by girder, and girder work points relative to CL bearing Abut. 1 at G1; girder elevation and camber with callouts to the connection plate, bearing stiffener, and splice sheets (sheet numbers filled in); typical section with flange-to-web weld symbols, general notes, and quantities; bearing reactions (unfactored DC1, DC2, DW, LL+IM max and min, pedestrian, service max and min, uplift flagged) for every girder and support; fatigue and fracture tables; deck overhang with the temporary bracket; every field splice; bearing stiffener, cross-frame (intermediate, end cross-frame along the skew, typical connection), stiffener and connection plate, shear connector, and flange transition details with weld symbols. In the layout format, bolts are GD_BOLT blocks and callouts are GD_SECT blocks with a TAG attribute. Not generated: sole plate and bearing details (bearings are not designed here), a deck placement sequence (needs a staged deck analysis), survey coordinates (work points are given relative to the girder layout), and office title blocks or layer standards (supply them to have them used).</p><p><b>Export DXF</b> (top bar) writes plot-ready sheets. Each sheet is a border and title block (project, project number, sheet title, scale, designed/checked, sheet n of N) drawn at its plot scale around full-size geometry in inches in model space; the scale is the smallest standard scale at which the sheet's content fits (34 × 22 or 17 × 11 sheets), so plot each sheet window at the scale in its title block. Sheets: 1, framing plan with girder spacing, cross-frame spacing along the exterior girders, field splice and span dimensions, the girder length and splice location table, and the cross-frame location table; 2, girder elevation with flange and web plates, connection plates, transverse stiffeners, bearing stiffeners, stud pitch zones, field splices and bearings, plate and span dimension chains, the plate schedule, the total dead load deflection (camber) table for every girder, the deflection components for a chosen girder, and the camber diagram of all girders; 3, the typical cross-section fully dimensioned, general notes (specification, steel, NSTM status, bolts, studs, deck, welding, camber), and the quantities from Design all; then one sheet per field splice case of the last Design all (plans of both flange splices and the elevation, with plates, fillers, bolts, and dimension chains of pitches, gages, end distances, and plate sizes); bearing stiffener, cross-frame, transverse stiffener and connection plate, and shear connector details; and flange transition details, one per distinct transition with its locations listed (the sheet is omitted when the girder has no shop transitions). Dimensions are AutoCAD DIMENSION entities with a dimension style per scale (GD + scale: ticks, text 0.1 in above the line, feet-inches to 1/8 in); text uses the GD style (romans.shx). Layers are named by content with the prefix you choose (default S-). Set the drawing units to inches in AutoCAD after opening and save as DWG.</p>
 <h3>Automatic refresh</h3><p>When the bridge changes in Preliminary sizing (spans, skews, girders, spacing, plates, splices), every module is updated automatically about 1.5 s after the last edit: demands are re-imported from the last demand source used (Preliminary sizing, or Structural analysis for a chosen girder), overrides and locked values are kept, auto-design runs if it is switched on in Owner standards, every module's checks are recomputed so the status marks on the module tabs are current, and you stay in the module you are working in. The update runs in the background: no module is drawn while it runs (only the module on screen is redrawn once at the end), so the tab and the scroll position do not change. Switch it off with Auto-refresh every module when the bridge changes in Owner standards.</p>
 <h3>Owner (DOT) profile</h3><p><b>Owner</b> (top bar) is the bridge owner: RIDOT, MassDOT, CTDOT, or AASHTO (no owner rules). It is stored with the Preliminary sizing project (its Limits tab has the same selector; a project saved with the former "Custom" owner opens as AASHTO with its limits kept) and every module reads it. The owner's rules are applied on top of AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024); the MassDOT LRFD Bridge Manual and the CTDOT BRSDM are written to the 9th Ed., the RIDOT BDM (April 2026) to the 10th Ed. <b>rules</b> lists every owner rule with the manual section, its kind (shall: pass/fail check; should: warning; default: an editable value, a different entry is flagged "overrides …" but not blocked; pending reference: needs a document not available yet, such as MassDOT Part II, the RIDOT Bridge Standard Details or CTDOT standard details) and where it is applied. In this version (phase 1): the cross-frame orientation rule of RIDOT (BDM 6.4.3) and CTDOT (BRSDM V2 6.7.4.2), applied to the whole bridge in the Preliminary sizing layout (largest support skew 20° or less: parallel to the skew, not staggered; more: normal to the girders and staggered) and checked by X1; and the MassDOT skew warnings above 40° and 50° (Part I 2.3.4.1). Changing the owner refreshes every module like a bridge change when its rules change the cross-frames or the load rules below (otherwise nothing computed changes and no refresh runs). The owners' defaults and detailing checks follow in a later version.</p>
-<h3>Owner load rules (phase 2)</h3><p>Preliminary sizing turns the owner's load rules into factors for the whole bridge and publishes them with it; every module uses them, and each module's loads tab has an <b>Owner load rules</b> card (entered factor, rule, factor used) when any of them is not 1. The rules are worked once on Preliminary sizing's Analysis tab (card "Owner load rules"). <b>Load modifier η</b> (AASHTO LRFD 1.3.2.1; Strength limit states only): η = η<sub>D</sub>η<sub>R</sub>η<sub>I</sub> multiplies the maximum load factors (1.25 DC, 1.50 DW, 1.75 LL) and 1/η the minimum ones (0.90 DC, 0.65 DW); Service, Fatigue and deck placement (constructibility) take η = 1. The owner's yes/no inputs are on Preliminary sizing's Limits tab (Owner profile): RIDOT η<sub>I</sub> = 1.05 for ADT ≥ 5000 (BDM 1.3.3) and η<sub>R</sub> = 1.05 for nonredundant members (1.3.2; η<sub>D</sub> = 1.00, 1.3.1); MassDOT 1.05 each for nonductile, nonredundant, and critical or essential bridges (3.1.4.4); CTDOT 1.05 each (BRSDM V2 1.3.3 to 1.3.5; η<sub>I</sub> for bridges on or over the NHS / STRAHNET or an evacuation route). Defaults: the η<sub>I</sub> question yes (conservative), nonredundant automatic (3 girders or fewer), nonductile no. AASHTO: η<sub>D</sub>, η<sub>R</sub>, η<sub>I</sub> entered (default 1.00, AASHTO 1.3.3 to 1.3.5). <b>Design load multiplier</b> (RIDOT BDM 3.4.1.2): HL-93 (LL+IM) × 1.2 at the Strength and Service limit states (the pedestrian load is not multiplied); not on the live load deflection, fatigue, deck placement, or the design check load rating. <b>Haunch = 0</b> (RIDOT BDM 6.5.1, 9.4.6, 4.3.1; MassDOT 3.5.1.2): the haunch is taken as zero in every composite section property (the stiffness of the analysis and the deflections, K<sub>g</sub> for the distribution factors, section moduli, M<sub>p</sub> lever arms, the reinforcement of the cracked section); its weight stays in DC1, and the stud penetration and cover checks (SC5) use the haunch as entered. Reported only; the girder is not resized for it. The owners' legal, permit and posting vehicles are not in this tool and are listed as pending. A project saved before these rules opens with them applied and a one-time notice listing them.</p>

 <h3>Girder report</h3><p><b>Girder report</b> (top bar) builds one calculation package for a selected girder. Choose the girder, the chapters, and whether to re-run auto-design for that girder (otherwise the plates, bolts, and welds as currently entered are checked). Every module is loaded with that girder's demands from the Structural analysis module (its own distribution factors, dead loads, and effective flange width), and each chapter is that module's full worked report: 1, bridge and girder geometry (bridge data, typical cross-section, framing plan, girder elevation, plate schedule); 2, loads and live load distribution factors with derivations; 3, structural analysis (moment and shear envelopes, reactions, deflections, stresses by construction stage); 4, girder section (Strength I, Service II, constructibility, and fatigue at the critical sections); 5, fatigue details; then one chapter per field splice on the girder; bearing stiffeners; transverse stiffeners and connection plates; shear connectors; cross-frames; deck overhang (exterior girders only); and web-to-flange welds and transitions. The package opens with a title page (girder, source of demands, basis of the details, specification, preparer and checker) and a contents list, starts each chapter on a new page, and carries "Girder G# calculation package" in the running header; print it to PDF. The app returns to the module you started from when printing is finished.</p>
 <h3>Design all</h3><p><b>Design all</b> (top bar) runs the whole detail design for the current bridge from one source of demands (Preliminary sizing, the envelope of the interior and exterior girders, or Structural analysis for one girder, applied to every girder): it auto-designs every field splice case, loads and auto-designs the transverse stiffener, shear connector, bearing stiffener, weld, cross-frame, and deck overhang modules, gives the stud module the splice stations and plate length so no studs are placed over the splice plates (SC6, with the strength count rechecked), loads the full fatigue detail inventory, runs every module's checks including Girder section and Fatigue, and totals the quantities and costs: girder steel and shop transitions (Preliminary sizing unit costs), splice plates and bolts, connection plates, intermediate and bearing stiffeners, studs, and cross-frame members and bolts, intermediate and end (bearing-line) frames, each end frame along its bearing line's skew (owner-standard unit costs, placeholders until replaced). It also lists geometry conflicts: cross-frames within the field splice plates or within 6 in of a shop flange transition, and a stud strength shortfall where studs are omitted over splice plates. Locked inputs are kept.</p>
 <h3>Fatigue detail inventory</h3><p>Demands imported into the Fatigue module now include the full inventory for each girder: web-to-flange welds (B) at the maximum positive range in each span and at each pier; connection plates (C′) at the intermediate cross-frame with the largest fatigue moment range in each span (bottom flange; the same plate the Transverse stiffeners CP2 row checks) and in each pier's negative dead-load region, between the dead-load contraflexure points (top flange), each located at its station along the girder (measured from that girder's own bearing at Abut. 1, so on a skewed bridge it differs from the distance along the bridge centerline) and chosen among the cross-frames on the girders the row stands for (exterior rows: G1 and the last girder; interior rows: every interior girder, with the cross-frames on both sides; demands from Structural analysis: that girder); intermediate stiffener weld toes on the web (C′) for stiffened webs; studs on the top flange at each pier (C, net tension checked); both flanges at each field splice (B, bolted, gross section of the smaller side); and each shop flange transition (B, ground flush, smaller side). Each row carries its girder's effective flange width and deck reinforcement A<sub>r</sub> = (rebar %) × b<sub>eff</sub> × t<sub>s</sub> at mid-depth of the slab, as the analysis uses them; rows entered by hand use the module's b<sub>eff</sub> and A<sub>r</sub>. Cycles per truck passage are 1.5 within 0.1L of an interior support and 1.0 elsewhere. Details you entered by hand are kept.</p>

## 2026-10-15 — PR: claude/gd-st-owner-rules (GD49: owner load rules carried to ST-Girder; cross-tool PR with stgirder.html and HANDOFF.md §4.9, approved exception of 2026-10-04; engineer decision 2026-10-15; PR link added after merge)

### OWN13. Send to ST-Girder carries the owner rules (`ownerRules`)   [HAND-OFF: new optional field; GirderDetail's own results unchanged]
- **Where:** `gdStPayload` (anchor `const ownerRules = (() => { const lf0 = P.df && P.df.bridge && P.df.bridge.lf;`): new optional payload field `ownerRules` = { owner, manual, codeBasis, llMultiplier { m, cite, liveLoad, limitStates, notApplied }, eta { D, R, I, product, max, min, cite, limitStates, rule }, haunchInProperties, haunchCite, ratingTarget { kind, rf, fatigue, cite, basis } | null }, from `gdLF()` (the factors Preliminary sizing publishes) and `OWN_RULES`; present whenever the bridge has published load rules (every owner, including AASHTO). The owner note line now says the rules are sent in `ownerRules` (and that m is not on the pedestrian load); the Send to ST-Girder help text says ST-Girder applies them.
- **Before:** the payload had no owner data; a note asked the receiver to apply the rules.
- **After:** the same stations, section, girderDetail and other fields, plus `ownerRules` (verified: main vs branch payloads differ only in `ownerRules` and that note line).
- **Governing provision / check case:** see `fixlog/stgirder.md` (GD49): ST-Girder's Strength I M_u for the RIDOT built-in G2 at x = 44 ft = 5820.02 kip-ft vs this tool's Structural analysis Strength I 5820.03 kip-ft (0.001 rounding of the payload); xsA G1 with the pedestrian load 6772.18 vs 6772.18.
- **How verified:** payloads from main and branch (built-in RIDOT/AASHTO G2, xsA RIDOT G1) compared field by field; GirderDetail → ST-Girder auto-open test 28/28 over http and as files; `node --check` all blocks.
- **Other copies:** none (`BridgeXfer` helper unchanged).

## 2026-10-15 — PR: claude/gd-owner-profiles-3a (owner profiles phase 3a, part 1 of 2: owner defaults infrastructure, dead loads, utilities, deck, deflection and span-to-depth; engineer decisions GD39, GD40, GD42 of 2026-10-15; PR link added after merge)

Basis: `scratchpad/dotman/owner_spec.md` and the H-priority rows of the RIDOT, MassDOT and CTDOT reviews. Manuals cited, not quoted: RIDOT Bridge Design Manual (April 2026), MassDOT LRFD Bridge Manual Part I, CTDOT BRSDM Release 1 (V2). Code basis AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) with the owner rules on top. **AASHTO profile: identical to main** (every module, every Preliminary sizing check and analysis array, Suggest and Full design; see How verified). Part 2 (plates, weathering steel, studs, integral abutments, CTDOT splice/fatigue/refined analysis, MassDOT A6 and sidewalk beam) follows in a second PR.

The page has two parts: the outer GirderDetail page and the embedded Preliminary sizing page (`const PL_B64`, base64 on one line). Both diffs are at the end (main → branch, decoded for the inner page).

### OWN14. Owner defaults: applied to untouched inputs, user values kept and flagged, one-time notice for older projects   [SAVED DATA: new optional fields; migration, nothing renamed or removed]
- **Where (Preliminary sizing):** new block after `migrateOwner` (anchor `const OWN_DEF_V = 1;`): `ownDefs(o)`, `ownDefOf(o, k)`, `ownBlank`/`ownSame`, `ownApply(p, o0, o1, since)`, `migrateOwnDef(p)` (called from `migrateOwner`, so every load path that already migrates the owner runs it), `ownFmt`, `ownChange(o0)` (owner select on the Limits tab and the owner sent from GirderDetail's top bar). Rule rows of kind `'default'` in `OWN_RULES` carry `key` (a Preliminary sizing input path), `value`, `lbl`, `show`, and `dv` (the defaults version that added the row).
- **Untouched rule (how it is detected):** by value. An input is untouched when it equals the default it had before: the previous owner's default for that key, or Preliminary sizing's generic `DEFAULT` value (AASHTO, and any key the previous owner has no default for). Only untouched inputs move; any other value is the user's and is kept, flagged on the Limits tab ("Overrides <manual> <section>: <owner value>", `ownFlags`), and the owner's checks still apply to it. A user entry that equals the former default cannot be told apart (listed in ENGINEER_CHECKS GD51).
- **Saved data (§5):** new optional field `P.ownDef = { v, o, mig?, kept? }` in the Preliminary sizing project; `v` = `OWN_DEF_V` (1). A project without it (or with an older `v`) is migrated once as if it had had the generic defaults (o0 = 'AASHTO'), applying only rows with `dv > v`. New optional inputs with defaults: `bridge.tsac` (0), `bridge.wcE` ('' = w_c), `limits.sidewalk` ('auto'), `suggest.dlDist` ('equal'). Older builds ignore all of them. Nothing renamed or removed.
- **Notice (GirderDetail):** the bridge definition sent to GirderDetail carries `ownDef` (non-AASHTO owners only). In the bridge handler (anchor `nb.ownDef && ob && ob.ok && nb.ok`), when the owner is the same (or the stored bridge has none) and the stored bridge lacks `ownDef` or has an older `v`, `gdOwnDefItems(nb, gch, v0)` builds the list (inputs moved, values kept, owner checks now applied) and sets the existing one-time notice `P.ownLd` (merged with an OWN6–OWN10 notice if one is pending). `nx()` excludes `ownDef` (a record, not a change of the bridge; the moved values themselves are).
- **GirderDetail-side defaults:** `gdOwnDefApply(o1)` applies rows with `gkey`/`gvalue` (here only `df.dl.method` → 'ridot' under RIDOT) with the same untouched rule (generic value 'massdot'), recorded in `P.ownDefG`; a moved method re-feeds the LLDF and DLs dead loads and refreshes the modules.
- **Rules panel:** the owner rules modal and the Limits tab list each default (kind "Default", value shown, section) next to the checks; Design modules mode gets an "Owner (DOT) checks of the bridge definition" card on the Bridge & girder Drawings tab (the Checks tab is hidden there), linking to the worked checks.
- **Check case:** `def15_ORIDOTu` (main-saved RIDOT project with the wearing surface entered as 30 psf): opens with fws 30 kept and flagged "Overrides RIDOT BDM 3.3.1, 9.4.7: 70 psf …"; barrier distribution moved equal → 60/40; the notice lists both. `def15_OCTDOTu` (fws 40, haunch 0.75 entered): fws 40 kept (flagged), tsac 0 → 0.5, wcE blank → 0.145, cll 20 → 50; haunch 0.75 kept and G11 fails it (0.75 < 1.00 in). Re-opening: no second notice. Owner switch RIDOT → AASHTO → RIDOT on an untouched project returns every input to its value (round trip verified).

### OWN15. Dead loads: RIDOT wearing surface and 60/40 barrier distribution, CTDOT overlay   [LOAD CHANGE (defaults), RIDOT/CTDOT — §4 callout]
- **Where:** `OWN_RULES` rows RIDOT `dl.fws` (suggest.fws 70), RIDOT `dl.dist` (suggest.dlDist '6040'; GirderDetail df.dl.method 'ridot'), CTDOT `dl.fws` (38.75). Preliminary sizing `suggestLayout`/`analyzeGirder` (anchor `const d64 = SG.dlDist === '6040';`); GirderDetail `dfDead` (anchors `const r64 = (L) =>`, `const rAuto = L =>`), `DF_DIST` r64, method select option 'ridot', labels.
- **Before:** fws 25 psf for every owner; barriers equally to all girders (Preliminary sizing) and MassDOT pile-cap (LLDF and DLs, default method).
- **After:**
  - RIDOT DW = 3 in asphalt × 0.140 kcf (AASHTO Table 3.5.1-1, BDM 9.4.7) + 35 psf future wearing surface (BDM 3.3.1; GD39) = 35 + 35 = **70 psf**.
  - CTDOT DW = 3 in × 0.155 kcf (V2 3.5.1, 9.7.7.3CT, Table 3.5.1-1; GD40) = **38.75 psf**.
  - RIDOT barrier/sidewalk DL (BDM 3.3.1): Preliminary sizing exterior w_DC2 = 0.6 w_bar, interior = 0.4(2 w_bar)/(N_b − 2) (N_b ≤ 2: own barrier). LLDF and DLs method "RIDOT BDM 3.3.1": edge loads (barrier, curb, railing, fence) 60% to the fascia beam on their side, 40% evenly to the interior beams; a sidewalk over more than one beam 60% evenly to those, 40% to the remaining interior beams; median and other line loads 60% to the beams under them (else the two either side), 40% to the remaining beams; DW equally; DC1, utility rows and the pedestrian load to the two adjacent beams (lever rule, AASHTO 3.4.1.6 for PL).
- **Governing provision:** RIDOT BDM (April 2026) 3.3.1, 9.4.7; CTDOT BRSDM V2 3.5.1, 9.7.7.3CT; AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 3.5.1-1.
- **Check case (built-in 15°, interior girder, Span 1 max positive at 43 ft; roadway 41.5 ft, 5 girders, barriers 0.40 klf each):**
  - RIDOT: w_DW = 0.070 × 41.5 / 5 = **0.581 klf** (was 0.025 × 41.5 / 5 = 0.2075); w_DC2 exterior 0.6 × 0.40 = **0.240**, interior 0.4 × (2 × 0.40)/3 = **0.1067** (main, MassDOT pile-cap in LLDF and DLs: 0.341 / 0.251 / 0.160). Girder section GS6 M_u = 1.25(M_DC1 + M_DC2) + 1.50 M_DW + 1.75(1.2) M_LL+IM: main 1.25(1007.8 + 193.9) + 1.5(160.6) + 2.1(1809.5) = **5542.98** kip-ft → branch 1.25(1007.8 + 82.5) + 1.5(449.6) + 2.1(1809.5) = 1362.88 + 674.40 + 3799.95 = **5837.23** kip-ft (tool: 5542.98 → 5837.23).
  - CTDOT (with OWN17, OWN18): w_DW = 0.03875 × 41.5 / 5 = **0.3216 klf**; see OWN17 for the full GS6 case.

### OWN16. MassDOT utilities on the noncomposite section and the future utility allowance   [LOAD CHANGE (new load categories), MassDOT — §4 callout; GD42]
- **Where:** GirderDetail LLDF and DLs: added-load categories `UT` "Utility (noncomposite, DW factors)" and `UF` "Future utility allowance (noncomposite, γ 1.25/0)" (`rowSpec`), `dfDead` arrays `ut`/`uf` (only present when used), `dfPayload` `dl.ut/uf`, button `data-dfut` "Add a MassDOT future utility bay (3.5.5.2)", check DF5 (a DW added load under MassDOT: warning "Is it a utility?"). Structural analysis (`GM.sa.compute`): `wUT`/`wUF` on the steel section (`MUT`, `MUF`, `VUT`, `VUF`, reactions `UT`/`UF`, camber `dU`), `saComb` terms `uX`/`uN`. Preliminary sizing `analyzeGirder`: `wUT`/`wUF` from `XF.dl` (sent by LLDF and DLs), in `Mup`/`Mun`/`Msp`/`Msn`, the shear envelope, Service II, the reactions (RUT in DW, RUF with 1.25η) and the camber (existing only). Detail modules: `plUtFold` (Preliminary sizing exports) and `saUtFold` (rows from Structural analysis).
- **Before:** utilities could only be entered as a DW added load on the long-term composite section (main treats a saved UT row as DC2 if opened in main).
- **After:** existing utilities: noncomposite (steel) section, DW load factors (Strength max 1.50η, min 0.65/η; Service 1.0), in the camber. Future allowance: 125 lb/ft per beam on the two beams of a utility bay (one 0.250 klf row, two adjacent), noncomposite, γ 1.25η max and 0 min (Service 1.0 only where it adds), not in the camber. Modules that carry only DC1/DC2/DW/LL+IM get them folded into DC1 as 1.20 × existing + 1.00 × future (1.50/1.25 and 1.25/1.25): exact at Strength I where they add and conservative at Service; **where they relieve, less conservative** (the module's γ_DC,min = 0.90 gives 1.08 × existing and 0.90 × future against the exact 0.65 and 0; ENGINEER_CHECKS GD54); a card "Owner deck and dead load rules" in each module's loads tab says so. Not sent to ST-Girder (a note line in the hand-off lists them).
- **Governing provision:** MassDOT LRFD Bridge Manual Part I 3.5.5.4 (utilities on the noncomposite section), 3.5.5.2 (future utility allowance, 125 lb/ft per beam, γ 1.25/0.0, not in camber); AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 3.4.1-2 (DW factors 1.50/0.65). Engineer decision GD42 (existing utilities DW).
- **Check case (built-in 15° MassDOT, one UT row 0.30 klf and one UF row 0.25 klf at x = 17.5 ft, two adjacent → G2/G3 get 0.150 and 0.125 klf each; G2, x = 317 ft in Span 3):** Structural analysis M_UT = 112.71, M_UF = 93.925 kip-ft (steel section): Strength I M_u adds 1.50(112.71) + 1.25(93.925) = 169.07 + 117.41 = **+286.47** kip-ft (tool +286.47; Preliminary sizing the same); at x = 250 (Pier 2) −672.07 kip-ft. Folded DC1 for the modules at the governing location: M_DC1 1008.4 → **1237.5** kip-ft. Abutment 1 Strength I reaction 288.47 → **303.33** kip.

### OWN17. Deck: CTDOT sacrificial top, w_c for E_c, haunch and thickness checks; MassDOT f′c 5.0 ksi; owner overhang limits; MassDOT 1% deck steel   [MATERIAL/GEOMETRY DEFAULTS and new checks — §4 callout]
- **Where:** Preliminary sizing `buildModel` (anchor `wcE = num(b.wcE) > 0 ? num(b.wcE) : wc, tsac =`), `suggestLayout` (`wDeck = trW * (ts + tsac) / 12 * wc`, `Ec = 120000 * wcE ** 2 * fc ** 0.33`), `sgGeoSig` (wcE appended only when set), `runChecks` G6 (owner `deck.oh`, `deck.oh06`) and new G11 (`deck.min`, `deck.haunch`, `cll.min`), Bridge tab inputs "w_c for E_c" and "Sacrificial deck thickness". GirderDetail `modRatio(b.fc, b.wcE > 0 ? b.wcE : b.wc …)` in LLDF and DLs (K_g), `dfDead` ts + tsac, GS4 owner `deck.rebar1` note.
- **Before:** E_c from w_c; deck weight from t_s; G6 used the Limits-tab placeholder (k = 0.40 S, 4 ft); no G11; MassDOT f′c 4.0 ksi default.
- **After:**
  - CTDOT (V2 9.7.1.1): `bridge.tsac` default 0.5 in, weighed in DC1 (deck weight with t_s + t_sac), not in the section properties; G11 fails t_s + t_sac < 8.5 in or t_sac < 0.5 in. V2 5.4.2.4: `bridge.wcE` default 0.145 kcf for E_c (n, K_g, every composite property; dead load keeps w_c = 0.150). V2 9.7.1.1.1CT: G11 fails a haunch < 1 in.
  - MassDOT (Part I 4.2.2.3): `bridge.fc` default 5.0 ksi (5000 HP).
  - RIDOT (BDM 9.4.1.4): G6 fails w_oh > min(d, S/2, 4 ft; 3 ft if d < 5 ft), d = fascia steel depth (shallowest section); warning w_oh/d > 0.6 (State Bridge Engineer approval and a torsional analysis). CTDOT (V2 9.7.1.5): G6 warning w_oh > min(4 ft, d).
  - MassDOT (Part I 3.5.1.4): GS4 note and reference: 1% deck steel at every negative-flexure location regardless of the deck stress (GS4 already applies 1% at every negative-flexure location; reference and source DOT added, no result change).
- **Governing provision:** CTDOT BRSDM V2 9.7.1.1, 9.7.1.1.1CT, 5.4.2.4, 9.7.1.5; MassDOT Part I 4.2.2.3, 3.5.1.4; RIDOT BDM 9.4.1.4; AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Eq. 5.4.2.4-1 (E_c = 120,000 K_1 w_c² f′c^0.33).
- **Check case:**

GS6 M_u = 1.25(M_DC1 + M_DC2) + 1.50 M_DW + 1.75 M_LL+IM: main 1.25(1007.8 + 194.2) + 1.5(160.8) + 1.75(1822.5) = **4933.08** → branch 1.25(1052.4 + 194.1) + 1.5(249.2) + 1.75(1833.8) = 1558.13 + 373.80 + 3209.15 = **5141.08** kip-ft (tool 4933.07 → 5141.07).
  - MassDOT built-in: E_c = 120,000(0.150)²(5.0)^0.33 = 2,700 × 1.7008 = **4,592 ksi**, n = **6.32** (was 6.80); GS6 M_u 4909.65 → 4888.48 kip-ft.
  - RIDOT built-in G6: w_oh = 3.25 ft, d = 61.88 in = 5.16 ft, S/2 = 4.75 → limit min(5.16, 4.75, 4.0) = 4.00 ft, ratio 0.81 OK; w_oh/d = 3.25/5.16 = **0.630 > 0.6: warning**.

### OWN19. Live load deflection (RIDOT, MassDOT) and span-to-depth (MassDOT, RIDOT)   [CHECK CHANGE — §4 callout]
- **Where:** Preliminary sizing `runChecks` A1 (rule `defl.ll`), G1/G2 (rule `sd.ratio`, helpers `plCfUni`, `plLcf`), `depthOK` in Suggest/Full design (anchor `const sdOwn = ownRule(plOwner(P), 'sd.ratio');`), `plSidewalk`, Limits tab input "Sidewalk or pedestrians" (`limits.sidewalk`, auto from GirderDetail's cross-section); `recompute` computes the analysis before `runChecks` (it needs the contraflexure points). GirderDetail Structural analysis SA3 (anchor `const oR = gdOwner() ? gdOwnRules(gdOwner(), 'defl.ll')[0] : null;`); RIDOT default `limits.sdMandatory` false.
- **Before:** A1/SA3 used the Limits-tab ratio (L/800) and the on/off switch; G1/G2 AASHTO Table 2.5.2.6.3-1 for all owners.
- **After:**
  - RIDOT (BDM 2.4.2.6): deflection mandatory, L/800, L/1000 with pedestrians, HL-93 without the design load multiplier; applied even with the switch off; required ratio = max(owner, Limits-tab entry). Span-to-depth not mandatory: G1/G2 warnings (default `sdMandatory` no).
  - MassDOT (Part I 3.5.6.1): L/1000 with a sidewalk; otherwise L/800 fails and L/1000 is preferred (warning); typical interior beam only (exterior items reported as not applicable). Part I 3.6.1.3: L between the dead load points of contraflexure (interior girder, permanent loads; uniform-load fallback when the analysis is not available), steel depth L/D_st ≤ 30, beam + design slab L/(D_st + t_s) ≤ 25, preferably ≤ 21 (warning) — in place of AASHTO Table 2.5.2.6.3-1 in G1/G2 and in Suggest/Full design's depth rule.
- **Governing provision:** RIDOT BDM 2.4.2.6; MassDOT Part I 3.5.6.1, 3.6.1.3; AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 2.5.2.6.2, Table 2.5.2.6.3-1.
- **Check case:** built-in 15° MassDOT G2 Span 3: L from the abutment to the contraflexure point next to Pier 2 = 78.08 ft, D_st = 61.88 in (shallowest section), t_s = 8 in, D_st + t_s = 69.88 in: L/(D_st + t_s) = 78.08 × 12 / 69.88 = **13.41 ≤ 21** (ratio 0.64; AASHTO G2 before: 0.747). A1 MassDOT built-in: L/800 → interior only, 0.3644 → 0.3454 (f′c 5.0 raises E_c).

### Documentation
- Help, "Owner defaults and checks (phase 3a)": one paragraph per owner, with the utilities paragraph. Preliminary sizing manual: owner defaults, G11 and the new inputs. Rules modal and Limits tab: each default with its value and section. Card "Owner deck and dead load rules" (`gdOwnBrNote`): Girder section, splice, bearing stiffeners and other modules' loads tabs. ST-Girder hand-off: a note line when utilities are present.

### How verified
- **Syntax:** `node --check` on every script block of both pages after each edit. Each block was also scanned for a `//` comment that would hide code on a joined line.
- **Matrix, main vs branch:**
  - Seeds: projects saved by main (built-in 15°, built-in 28°, xsA with sidewalk, curb) × AASHTO/MassDOT/RIDOT/CTDOT, plus RIDOT and CTDOT with user values.
  - Each seed opened in headless Chromium.
  - For every module: Get demands from Preliminary sizing, then all check results compared, together with the Preliminary sizing checks and analysis arrays.
  - **AASHTO: no difference on any of the 4 projects.** Owner results are in the PR (tables).
  - No page errors.
- **Suggest / Full design:** fast suggestion, quick check and Full design (with the cross-frame spacing study) for all 16 project × owner cases, main vs branch.
  - AASHTO is identical.
  - Every Full design passes.
  - No page errors.
- **Hand checks:** the GS6 cases in OWN15 and OWN17 and the utility case in OWN16 were matched to the tool to 0.01 kip-ft. The Preliminary sizing load inputs were read back (w_DW, w_DC2, deck, n, w_CL).
- **Notice and migration:**
  - The user-value seeds show the values kept and flagged.
  - Dismissing the notice and reopening from the saved storage gives no notice and no change.
  - Owner round trip MassDOT → RIDOT → CTDOT → AASHTO → MassDOT on a fresh project returns every input.

The update runs in the background: no module is drawn while it runs (only the module on screen is redrawn once at the end), so the tab and the scroll position do not change.  <h3>Owner load rules (phase 2)</h3><p>Preliminary sizing turns the owner's load rules into factors for the whole bridge and publishes them with it; every module uses them, and each module's loads tab has an <b>Owner load rules</b> card (entered factor, rule, factor used) when any of them is not 1. The rules are worked once on Preliminary sizing's Analysis tab (card "Owner load rules"). <b>Load modifier η</b> (AASHTO LRFD 1.3.2.1; Strength limit states only): η = η<sub>D</sub>η<sub>R</sub>η<sub>I</sub> multiplies the maximum load factors (1.25 DC, 1.50 DW, 1.75 LL) and 1/η the minimum ones (0.90 DC, 0.65 DW); Service, Fatigue and deck placement (constructibility) take η = 1. The owner's yes/no inputs are on Preliminary sizing's Limits tab (Owner profile): RIDOT η<sub>I</sub> = 1.05 for ADT ≥ 5000 (BDM 1.3.3) and η<sub>R</sub> = 1.05 for nonredundant members (1.3.2; η<sub>D</sub> = 1.00, 1.3.1); MassDOT 1.05 each for nonductile, nonredundant, and critical or essential bridges (3.1.4.4); CTDOT 1.05 each (BRSDM V2 1.3.3 to 1.3.5; η<sub>I</sub> for bridges on or over the NHS / STRAHNET or an evacuation route). Defaults: the η<sub>I</sub> question <b>no</b> (engineer decision 2026-10-15: η = 1.0 unless the bridge qualifies and the answer is set to yes), nonredundant automatic (3 girders or fewer), nonductile no. A project saved with the former default yes, which the user had not chosen, opens with no and a one-time notice; an answer the user sets is kept. AASHTO: η<sub>D</sub>, η<sub>R</sub>, η<sub>I</sub> entered (default 1.00, AASHTO 1.3.3 to 1.3.5). <b>Design load multiplier</b> (RIDOT BDM 3.4.1.2): HL-93 (LL+IM) × 1.2 at the Strength and Service limit states (the pedestrian load is not multiplied: demands that Structural analysis sends to a module with the pedestrian load added to LL+IM carry its part, and the module takes (LL+IM+PL) − PL + PL/m so that m is not on it, shown on the module's loads tab, card "Pedestrian load without the design load multiplier"); not on the live load deflection, fatigue, deck placement, or the design check load rating. <b>Haunch = 0</b> (RIDOT BDM 6.5.1, 9.4.6, 4.3.1; MassDOT 3.5.1.2): the haunch is taken as zero in every composite section property (the stiffness of the analysis and the deflections, K<sub>g</sub> for the distribution factors, section moduli, M<sub>p</sub> lever arms, the reinforcement of the cracked section); its weight stays in DC1, and the stud penetration and cover checks (SC5) use the haunch as entered. The package opens with a title page (girder, source of demands, basis of the details, specification, preparer and checker) and a contents list, starts each chapter on a new page, and carries "Girder G# calculation package" in the running header; print it to PDF. +<p>The owner profile (Limits tab) applies owner rules on top of AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024). The MassDOT LRFD Bridge Manual and the CTDOT BRSDM are written to the 9th Ed.; the RIDOT BDM (April 2026) to the 10th Ed. In this version: the cross-frame orientation rule of RIDOT (BDM 6.4.3) and CTDOT (BRSDM V2 6.7.4.2) for the whole bridge (layout and check X1, pass/fail), and the MassDOT skew warnings above 40° and 50° (Part I 2.3.4.1, in X1). The owners' load rules (phase 2) and the high-priority owner defaults and checks (phase 3a) are listed on the Limits tab: RIDOT wearing surface 70 psf, barrier dead load 60/40, span-to-depth not mandatory, deflection L/800 or L/1000 with pedestrians (A1), overhang (G6); MassDOT deck f′<sub>c</sub> 5.0 ksi, deflection L/1000 with sidewalks (else L/800, L/1000 preferred; interior beam only), span-to-depth ratios 30 / 25 / 21 with L between the dead load points of contraflexure (G1, G2 and the Suggest depth rule), utilities on the noncomposite section; CTDOT overlay 38.75 psf, 0.5 in sacrificial deck and 8.5 in total, w<sub>c</sub> = 0.145 kcf for E<sub>c</sub>, haunch ≥ 1 in, construction live load 50 psf (G11), overhang (G6). An owner default sets its input only while the input is untouched (still at the former default); a value you entered is kept and flagged "Overrides …". Items that need the owners' standard details (MassDOT Part II, RIDOT Bridge Standard Details, CTDOT standard details) are listed as pending references. AASHTO has no owner rules.</p>

+<b>CTDOT</b> (BRSDM V2 6.10.2, 6.10.1.3, 6.13.6.1, 6.6.1.2.6CT, App. CT11.1.1.1, 4.4): web at least 3/8 in in 2 in depth increments, flanges at least 3/4 in thick, 12 in and L/85 of the field piece wide, in 2 in width increments, width constant within a shipping piece, thinner plate at least 1/2 of the thicker (W3, W4, F5, F6, S4, T1, T2 fail); hybrid girders a warning (W5); field splices designed as if oversized holes were used (K<sub>h</sub> = 0.85 in the slip resistance), splice plates at least 1/2 in, edge distance at least 2 in, gap at most 1 in (Field splice DT3, DT5, DT7; auto-design and fit); flanges designed for Category C at the connection plates ((ΔF)<sub>TH</sub> = 10 ksi; engineer decision GD41; Fatigue Cp-stiff, Transverse stiffeners CP2, Full design); Owner standards minimum plate 1/2 in; integral abutments: skew less than 30°, length and spans at most 150 ft (G10, fail); refined analysis required above 30° skew, for curved girders or non-uniform spacing (G13 warnings).
+<b>MassDOT</b> (Part I 3.6.1.1, 3.6.3.4, 3.6.3.5, 3.6.5.6, 3.10.11.1, 3.5.1.7, 3.5.3.11): coated Grade 50 is the default grade (flanges and web; F<sub>u</sub> 65 ksi), uncoated 50W only over railroads alone (G12 warning, Limits tab input); L/85 where practical (S4 warning); flange width transitions only at field splices (T1), thinner flange at least 1/2 of the thicker (T2), no more than 3 sizes between bolted splices (T5); integral abutments: simplified method to 140 ft and 30°, beyond a 3D analysis (G10 warnings); Appendix A6 not used: Girder section negative flexure method "Article 6.10.8 only" by default and GS22 warns where A6 is used; the exterior sidewalk beam Case I and Case II are not implemented (DF6 warning when a sidewalk is entered).</p>
 <h3>Girder report</h3><p><b>Girder report</b> (top bar) builds one calculation package for a selected girder. Choose the girder, the chapters, and whether to re-run auto-design for that girder (otherwise the plates, bolts, and welds as currently entered are checked). Every module is loaded with that girder's demands from the Structural analysis module (its own distribution factors, dead loads, and effective flange width), and each chapter is that module's full worked report: 1, bridge and girder geometry (bridge data, typical cross-section, framing plan, girder elevation, plate schedule); 2, loads and live load distribution factors with derivations; 3, structural analysis (moment and shear envelopes, reactions, deflections, stresses by construction stage); 4, girder section (Strength I, Service II, constructibility, and fatigue at the critical sections); 5, fatigue details; then one chapter per field splice on the girder; bearing stiffeners; transverse stiffeners and connection plates; shear connectors; cross-frames; deck overhang (exterior girders only); and web-to-flange welds and transitions. The package opens with a title page (girder, source of demands, basis of the details, specification, preparer and checker) and a contents list, starts each chapter on a new page, and carries "Girder G# calculation package" in the running header; print it to PDF. The app returns to the module you started from when printing is finished.</p>

In this version: the cross-frame orientation rule of RIDOT (BDM 6.4.3) and CTDOT (BRSDM V2 6.7.4.2) for the whole bridge (layout and check X1, pass/fail), and the MassDOT skew warnings above 40° and 50° (Part I 2.3.4.1, in X1). The owners' load rules (phase 2) and the high-priority owner defaults and checks (phase 3a) are listed on the Limits tab: RIDOT wearing surface 70 psf, barrier dead load 60/40, span-to-depth not mandatory, deflection L/800 or L/1000 with pedestrians (A1), overhang (G6); MassDOT deck f′<sub>c</sub> 5.0 ksi, deflection L/1000 with sidewalks (else L/800, L/1000 preferred; interior beam only), span-to-depth ratios 30 / 25 / 21 with L between the dead load points of contraflexure (G1, G2 and the Suggest depth rule), utilities on the noncomposite section; CTDOT overlay 38.75 psf, 0.5 in sacrificial deck and 8.5 in total, w<sub>c</sub> = 0.145 kcf for E<sub>c</sub>, haunch ≥ 1 in, construction live load 50 psf (G11), overhang (G6). An owner default sets its input only while the input is untouched (still at the former default); a value you entered is kept and flagged "Overrides …". ## 2026-10-15 — PR: claude/gd-pl-plaintext (Preliminary sizing page stored as plain text instead of base64; engineer-approved 2026-10-15; PR link added after merge)

### PLSRC. The embedded Preliminary sizing (PlateLine) page is plain HTML text, not the base64 string `PL_B64`   [storage of the embedded page only] [no result change]
- **Why:** the base64 string was one ~1 MB line: every Preliminary sizing edit meant decode → edit → re-encode, every such PR conflicted on that one line, and diffs of it were unreadable. Plain text is diffable, editable in place and about 250 KB smaller.
- **Where:**
  1. The `const PL_B64 = '...';` line (≈ line 2436 before this PR, in the main `<script>`) is **removed**.
  2. A new block just before the main `<script>` (after the `rpt-modal` div, ≈ line 1259): an HTML comment, then `<script type="text/plain" id="pl-src">` + the page + `</script>`. A `text/plain` script is never run by the browser; its text is the page source. Anchor: `<script type="text/plain" id="pl-src">`.
  3. Loader `plShow` (anchor `function plShow(bg) {`) and the new helper `plSrc()` just above it.
- **Escaping rule (so that nothing inside the page can end the block early — HTML spec "script data" states):** in the stored text, every `<` that is followed by zero or more backslashes and then `/script` or `!--` (any letter case) gets **one extra backslash** after the `<`. So the page's four closing script tags are stored as `<\/script>`. `<!--` would be stored as `<\!--` (the page has none today; it matters because `<!--` followed by `<script` switches the parser into the "double-escaped" state, in which the block's own closing tag would not close it). `plSrc()` removes exactly one backslash from each such sequence, so the round trip is exact for any text (including text that already contains `<\/script`). Nothing else is changed: no CR, NUL or BOM is in the page (checked), so the HTML parser hands the text back unchanged. The block starts directly with `<!DOCTYPE html>` and ends directly with the page's final newline; no whitespace is added around it.
- **Before (loader):**
```js
function plShow(bg) {
  const w = $('#pl-wrap'); w.style.top = Math.ceil($('#modbar').getBoundingClientRect().bottom) + 'px';
  if (PL_FRAME) return;
  const bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(PL_B64), c => c.charCodeAt(0));
  ...
  PL_FRAME.srcdoc = new TextDecoder().decode(bytes).replace(/<head>/i, h => h + own); w.appendChild(PL_FRAME);
```
- **After (loader):**
```js
/* PLSRC (2026-10-15): ... (comment explaining the rule) */
function plSrc() { return document.getElementById('pl-src').textContent.replace(/<\\(\\*)(\/script|!--)/gi, '<$1$2'); }
function plShow(bg) {
  const w = $('#pl-wrap'); w.style.top = Math.ceil($('#modbar').getBoundingClientRect().bottom) + 'px';
  if (PL_FRAME) return;
  const src = plSrc();
  ...
  PL_FRAME.srcdoc = src.replace(/<head>/i, h => h + own); w.appendChild(PL_FRAME);
```
  The frame is built exactly as before (`srcdoc`, the owner-rules script inserted after `<head>`, same load/ready handling). One code comment (C_b helper, ≈ line 11798) now says "the pl-src page" instead of "PL_B64".
- **How to edit Preliminary sizing now:** open `Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html`, search `<script type="text/plain" id="pl-src">`, and edit the page text between that tag and the next `</script>` like any HTML. Line numbers of the page inside the block are the decoded-page line number + about 1260 (the page's line 1 is on the line of the opening tag). When adding code: write every closing script tag as `<\/script>` and every HTML comment opener as `<\!--` (one extra backslash; an existing `<\/script` inside the page's own JavaScript would be stored as `<\\/script`). To check your edit, compare `plSrc()` in the browser console with the page you intended, and run `node --check` on the page's inline scripts (copy each inline script of the page to a .js file first). There is no decode/re-encode step any more.
- **Earlier entries in this log** that say "base64-decode `PL_B64`, edit, re-encode" are kept as written (history). To re-apply such an edit to this or a later version, apply the decoded-page diff directly to the text inside the `pl-src` block (escaping closing script tags as above). To re-apply one to a copy from before this PR, follow the entry as written.
- **Governing provision:** none (no calculation, factor, unit or code reference changed).
- **Check case / how verified:**
  - **Byte identity:** SHA-256 of the string handed to the loader — main `new TextDecoder().decode(Uint8Array.from(atob(PL_B64), ...))` and branch `plSrc()` — both `7678d884a13d8a5350c1957e04ad45ea23b6c49b23ad260eab98c8b239838b62` (760,459 characters), measured in headless Chromium from `file://` and from `http://127.0.0.1` for both files; the frame `srcdoc` (with the owner rules inserted) also hashes the same on both (`bd86039b…`). The same identity checked offline in Python (strict UTF-8 decode of the base64 vs un-escaped block text).
  - `node --check` on every inline script of the main page and of the embedded page: all pass.
  - Tier 1 (main 4193ddc vs branch, after settle): built-in project (AASHTO) and xsA (RIDOT): GirderDetail project hash, Preliminary sizing checks hash, analysis hash, every module's check items after Get demands, girder-1 structural analysis, plAdj — identical. Preliminary sizing project data differs only in `dfx.ts` (a time stamp; main vs main differs the same way). No console errors, no alerts; Preliminary sizing renders (screenshot checked).
  - File size: 2,444,330 → 2,191,238 bytes (−253,092 bytes, −10.4 %).
- **Saved data:** no key or format changed.
- **Other copies:** none (no standalone PlateLine file exists).

## 2026-10-15 — PR: claude/gd-testkit (idle signal for headless checks, with the tests/ kit and docs/AGENT_BRIEF.md; engineer-approved 2026-10-15; PR link added after merge)

### IDLE. `window.gdIdle()`: a Promise that resolves when GirderDetail has finished its automatic work   [test hook] [no result change, no behaviour change]
- **Why:** opening a project can start automatic work: the bridge publish from Preliminary sizing, the automatic refresh, the cross-frame auto-design and the XF2 second pass. This takes 20–50 s, so headless checks must not read results at fixed times. Until now the wait (`settle()`) lived in each test script. It now lives in the app, so every script waits the same way.
- **Where:** new code right after `function plEnsure() {` (anchor: `function gdBusy() {`), main script. Nothing calls it; nothing else changed.
- **Code added:**
```js
function gdBusy() { return !!(GD_XF_REQ || GD_XF_T) || GD_RQ.size > 0 || GD_PLQ.length > 0 || !PL_FRAME || !PL_FRAME.dataset.ready; }
window.gdIdle = function ({ quiet = 8000, max = 150000, step = 500 } = {}) {
  const t0 = Date.now(); let last = null, since = t0;
  return new Promise((res, rej) => { const tick = () => {
    let s; try { const q = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(P)); delete q.ui; s = (gdBusy() ? 'busy:' : '') + JSON.stringify(q).replace(/"ts":\d+/g, '"ts":0'); } catch (e) { s = 'busy:' + e.message; }
    const now = Date.now();
    if (s !== last || s.startsWith('busy:')) { last = s; since = now; } else if (now - since >= quiet) return res(now - t0);
    if (now - t0 >= max) return rej(new Error('gdIdle: not idle after ' + max + ' ms'));
    setTimeout(tick, step); }; tick(); });
};
```
  (preceded by a comment block "IDLE (2026-10-15)"). Idle means all of these: no demand request in flight (`GD_XF_REQ`, `GD_RQ`) or waiting for the frame (`GD_PLQ`), no second pass pending (`GD_XF_T`), Preliminary sizing loaded and ready (`PL_FRAME.dataset.ready`), and the project data (`P` without `ui`, time stamps ignored) unchanged for `quiet` ms. It does not load Preliminary sizing itself; call `plEnsure()` first. This is the same logic as the earlier `settle()` helper (the scratchpad's `xfrace/settle.mjs`, 2026-10-14), moved inside the page.
- **Governing provision:** none.
- **How verified (Tier 1):** `node tests/check-syntax.mjs "Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html"` passes (main page and the pl-src page). `node tests/compare.mjs --tool gd` (main 3ef3506 vs branch, built-in project, AASHTO): all 16 sections identical, covering the GirderDetail and Preliminary sizing project data, Preliminary sizing checks and analysis, every module's check items after Get demands, and the girder-1 structural analysis. No console errors. Main was waited on with the external settle logic and the branch with `gdIdle()` (≈23 s each). Also run on xsA × AASHTO/RIDOT and built-in × RIDOT: identical (see PR).
- **Saved data:** none touched.

## 2026-10-15 — PR: claude/gd-owner3a-followups (engineer decisions 2026-10-15 on #237/#238, ENGINEER_CHECKS GD51–GD64: GD54b utilities as their own loads, GD59 weathering steel in the stiffener modules, GD62 CTDOT splice message; PR link added after merge)

### GD54b. MassDOT utilities carried as their own loads in every module's demands, with the exact load factors   [LOAD COMBINATION CHANGE, MassDOT projects with utilities only — §4 callout] [Tier 2]
- **Engineer decision 2026-10-15 (GD54b):** in the detail modules the utilities were folded into DC1 (1.20 × existing + 1.00 × future), so where they relieve the effect the module's γ<sub>DC,min</sub> = 0.90 was applied to them instead of the exact factors. Fix: carry the utilities as their own load components so every module applies the exact maximum and minimum factors.
- **Problem (before):** Preliminary sizing `plUtFold` and GirderDetail `saUtFold` added the utility moments and shears to DC1: M<sub>DC1</sub>′ = M<sub>DC1</sub> + 1.20 M<sub>UT</sub> + 1.00 M<sub>UF</sub> (same for V). Strength I where the utilities add: exact (1.25 × 1.20 = 1.50; 1.25 × 1.00 = 1.25). Where they relieve: 0.90 × 1.20 = 1.08 on the existing utilities (exact 0.65) and 0.90 on the future allowance (exact 0). Service: 1.20 on the existing utilities (exact 1.0). Deck placement (M<sub>DC1</sub> without a deck sequence): the utilities were included (they are installed after the deck, GD54(c)). Fatigue net-tension rule and web check: 1.20 × existing + future in the permanent load.
- **After:** the utility loads are sent as their own components on each row, `ut = { MUT, MUF, VUT, VUF, VUTb, VUFb, VUTc, VUFc, VUTp, VUFp }` (unfactored, on the noncomposite steel section; moments signed, shears magnitudes as the other shears), and M<sub>DC1</sub>, V<sub>DC1</sub> are DC1 alone. Each module applies:
  - existing utilities (UT, GD42 = DW): γ<sub>DW</sub> max (1.50η) where they add to the effect checked, γ<sub>DW</sub> min (0.65/η) where they relieve it; Service 1.0;
  - future utility allowance (UF, MassDOT 3.5.5.2): γ<sub>DC</sub> max (1.25η) where it adds, **0** where it relieves; Service 1.0 where it adds, 0 where it relieves; not in the camber (unchanged);
  - deck placement (constructibility): neither (installed after the deck);
  - modules that take shears and reactions as magnitudes with maximum factors only (Transverse stiffeners, Welds and transitions, Field splice V, Girder section V): the maximum factors (exact where they add; where they relieve, conservative — never below the exact value);
  - Fatigue (net-tension rule 6.6.1.2.1 and web check 6.10.5.3): permanent load at 1.0, the existing utilities always, the future allowance only where it adds tension at the detail; V<sub>u</sub> + V<sub>UT</sub> + V<sub>UF</sub>;
  - Bearing stiffeners: reactions unchanged (existing utilities already in R<sub>DW</sub>, γ 1.50; future allowance in R<sub>DC1</sub>, γ 1.25: the exact factors for the maximum reaction, the only one this module checks).
- **Where (anchors; the full diff is below):**
  - Preliminary sizing (pl-src block): `function plUtFold(AN)` (now only folds the future allowance into the reactions), new `function utRow(T, i, vm, sh)`; `spliceExport` (anchor `GD54b: the utilities as their own loads`); `detailExport`: `fBotN` (anchor `const uT = T.MUT ? T.MUT[k] : 0, uF =`), `gsPan` (`/* GD45; GD54b */`), new `inMx`, `inMxP`, `utAt` after `shearIn`, ts rows, wt rows, gs rows (`utAt(gs.rows[`), `nprG` keys `['MUT', 'MUT'], ['MUF', 'MUF']`, fa rows; the `pl-export-req` handler comment.
  - GirderDetail: `saUtFold` (anchor `function saUtFold(R, arr, reac)`: arrays `arr.MUT/MUF/VUT/VUF` instead of the fold), `gsaRows` (utility moments interpolated); new `gdUt`, `gdUtOn` (anchor `const gdUt = (s, k) =>`); Field splice `gdCompute` (`comp.UT`, `comp.UF`, `fac.UT`, `fac.UF` in every combination, utility shears, `cmpName`), `spliceApply` (`P.dem.ut` of this import only), splice report inputs; Girder section `compute` (anchor `['MUT', 'MUF', 'VUT', 'VUF', 'VUTp', 'VUFp'].forEach`), `gsGov`, `gsGovTex`, GS11, GS18 and GS19 work, stress accumulation table, yield moment M<sub>D1</sub>; Transverse stiffeners `compute` (anchor `GD54b: MassDOT utilities (shear magnitudes)`), `tsUtTex`; Welds and transitions `compute` (`st.push(['Utilities, existing'`); Fatigue `compute` (anchor `const uS = p.rows[r.i]; if (gdUtOn(uS))`), FA web check work, fatigue rows imported from Girder section and Field splice; `gdOwnBrNote` text.

A project saved by this branch and opened in main: main ignores `ut` (its modules then miss the utilities until the next refresh from Preliminary sizing, which folds them again in main).
- **How verified (Tier 2):** see the PR body (main vs branch on the built-in project under AASHTO, MassDOT, RIDOT, CTDOT and xsA under AASHTO: identical; the built-in MassDOT project with the two utility rows: only the modules listed differ, values as above).
- **Other copies:** none. ST-Girder: not changed (the hand-off still lists the utilities in a note line, GD54(d)).

### GD59. RIDOT uncoated weathering steel: the 1/16 in sacrificial thickness also in the stiffener and connection plate modules   [SECTION CHANGE, RIDOT with the switch on only — §4 callout] [Tier 2]
- **Engineer decision 2026-10-15 (GD59):** the "Uncoated weathering steel" switch (Preliminary sizing, Limits tab, `girder.wsU`) **stays default off**. When it is on, extend the sacrificial thickness to the stiffener and connection plate modules (BDM 6.2.1: +1/16 in on stiffener plates; connection plates taken as stiffeners).
- **Before (switch on):** Transverse stiffeners and Bearing stiffeners designed with the full plate thickness entered (only Preliminary sizing's D7 minimum included the 1/16 in; GD59(e)).
- **After (switch on, RIDOT):** the thickness entered in these modules is the plate as ordered; every check uses the design thickness t<sub>p</sub> − 1/16 in (projecting width TS1/TS2 and BS1, moment of inertia TS3, bearing BS2, column BS3, connection plate checks); the fillet weld minimum (TS7, BS weld) keeps the ordered plate (thicker part joined). Auto-design starts at the Owner standards minimum plate + 1/16 in (connection plates: max(minimum plate, connection plate thickness) + 1/16 in). The module summary shows "4 1/2 × 1/2 (net 7/16)", the owner card lists t<sub>p</sub> − 1/16 per type. Switch off, or any other owner: nothing changes (`gdWsSt()` = 0).

### GD62. CTDOT field splices on flanges too narrow for 2 gage lines: a clear reason and fix in the checks, the summary and the auto-design message   [DISPLAY ONLY — no result change] [Tier 1]
- **Engineer decision 2026-10-15 (GD62):** existing CTDOT projects whose splices fail DT3/DT4/DT7 because 16 in flanges cannot take 2 gage lines at 2 in edge distance with 1/2 in plates **keep failing**; make the message clear and actionable.
- **Before:** DT3/DT4/DT7 failed with the generic notes; the auto-design said "The top flange is 16 in wide; 2 gage lines each side of the web without staggering need at least 17 in. Widen the flange … The splice was not changed."
- **After (CTDOT only, flange at the splice narrower than needed):** new `spCtNarrow(R)` gives the width needed for the minimum gage lines each side of the web (no inner plates, no staggering, with the 2 in edge and the 1/2 in plates; the same geometry as `autoDesignSplice`'s `needB`) rounded up to CTDOT's 2 in flange width increment, and the text: "CTDOT BRSDM V2 6.13.6.1: 2 in minimum edge distance and 1/2 in minimum splice plates, so the flange at the splice must be at least 17 in wide for 2 gage lines each side of the web (18 in with CTDOT's 2 in flange width increment, CTDOT BRSDM V2 6.10.2.2); here the top flange is 16 in and the bottom flange is 16 in. To fix it: widen the flange at the splice to 18 in (Preliminary sizing's Suggest sizes flanges at field splices with the 2 in edge; then Get demands here), or use one gage line each side (Bolts tab, minimum bolt lines) if the flange splice still passes with it. Until then the splice cannot meet the owner's edge distance and plate thickness (DT3, DT4, DT7)." It is put first in the notes of DT3, DT4, DT7 (and DT10) when they fail, as an alert at the top of the splice Summary tab, and as the auto-design message ("… The splice was not changed."). Pass/fail, ratios and the splice itself are unchanged.
- **Where:** new `function spCtNarrow(R)` (just above `function gdChecks(R)`); end of `gdChecks` (anchor `GD62: the reason and the fix (display only)`); `renderSummary` (`ctA`); `autoDesignSplice` narrow branch (anchor `GD62: the owner's reason and fix first`).
- **Governing provision:** CTDOT BRSDM Release 1 (V2) 6.13.6.1 (bolted splices: 1/2 in minimum plates, 2 in minimum edge distance), 6.10.2.2 (flange widths in 2 in increments); AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 6.13.2.6.6. No value changed.
- **Check case (built-in, CTDOT, FS1 @ 82.00 ft):** g<sub>0</sub> = ⌈max(t<sub>w</sub>/2 + t<sub>wp</sub> + c<sub>w</sub> + e, t<sub>w</sub>/2 + t<sub>wp</sub> + C<sub>1</sub>)⌉<sub>1/4</sub> = ⌈max(0.281 + 0.5 + 0.5 + 2.0, 0.281 + 0.5 + 1.5)⌉ = ⌈3.28⌉ = 3.50 in; g = 3.00 in; b<sub>needed</sub> = 2(g<sub>0</sub> + g + e) = 2(3.50 + 3.00 + 2.00) = **17.00 in → 18 in** with the 2 in increment; flanges 16 in → message shown; DT3 1.60, DT4 1.1429, DT7 1.1429 FAIL unchanged.
- **Saved data:** none.
- **Other copies:** none.
- **Diff:**

@@ -7801,0 +7826,10 @@ function gdCompute(P) {
+/* GD62 (engineer decision 2026-10-15; CTDOT BRSDM V2 6.13.6.1, 6.10.2.2): under CTDOT the 2 in minimum edge distance and the 1/2 in minimum splice plates need a
+   wider flange at the splice for the minimum gage lines each side of the web (the width autoDesignSplice's needB uses: no inner plates, no staggering), rounded
+   up to the owner's flange width increment. A splice on narrower flanges keeps failing DT3/DT4/DT7 (or DT10); this gives the reason and the fix as text
+   (display only). null when the owner has no such rule or the flanges are wide enough */
+function spCtNarrow(R) { const rOv = gdOwnR('spl.ovs'); if (!rOv || !R || !R.fl || !R.web) return null;
+  const P_ = R.P, bt = BOLT[P_.bolts.d] || BOLT['0.875'], d = bt.d, u4 = v => Math.ceil(v * 4 - 1e-6) / 4, tw = Math.max(R.secL.tw, R.secR.tw), twp = Math.max(R.web.twp, rOv.value.tp), cw = parseDim(P_.clr.cw), em = R.emin;
+  const C1 = parseDim(P_.bolts.c1) > 0 ? parseDim(P_.bolts.c1) : ({ '0.75': 1.25, '0.875': 1.5, '1': 1.625, '1.125': 1.75 }[P_.bolts.d] || 1.5), nMin = Math.max(1, Math.round(parseDim(P_.bolts.minLines) || 1)), g = u4(Math.max(3, 3 * d));
+  const g0 = u4(Math.max(tw / 2 + twp + cw + em, tw / 2 + twp + C1)), need = Math.ceil(2 * (g0 + (nMin - 1) * g + em) * 4 - 1e-6) / 4, rI = gdOwnR('plate.incBf'), inc = rI && +rI.value > 0 ? +rI.value : 0, needI = inc ? Math.ceil(need / inc - 1e-9) * inc : need;
+  const fl = ['top', 'bot'].map(k => ({ k, b: R.fl[k].bmin })).filter(q => q.b < need - 1e-9); if (!fl.length) return null;
+  return { need, needI, fl, nMin, em, tp: rOv.value.tp, msg: `${gdOwnCite(rOv)}: ${frac(em)} in minimum edge distance and ${frac(rOv.value.tp)} in minimum splice plates, so the flange at the splice must be at least ${frac(need)} in wide for ${nMin} gage line${nMin > 1 ? 's' : ''} each side of the web${inc && needI !== need ? ` (${frac(needI)} in with CTDOT's ${frac(inc)} in flange width increment, ${gdOwnCite(rI)})` : ''}; here the ${fl.map(q => `${q.k === 'top' ? 'top' : 'bottom'} flange is ${frac(q.b)} in`).join(' and the ')}. To fix it: widen the flange at the splice to ${frac(needI)} in (Preliminary sizing's Suggest sizes flanges at field splices with the 2 in edge; then Get demands here)${nMin > 1 ? ', or use one gage line each side (Bolts tab, minimum bolt lines) if the flange splice still passes with it' : ''}. Until then the splice cannot meet the owner's edge distance and plate thickness (DT3, DT4, DT7).` }; }

### SGP. Suggest panel: GirderDetail top bar button, full-screen panel, design inputs with Locked / Range / List / Free, runs with progress and Cancel, options side by side with the current design, Apply   [NEW FEATURE — no result change with the settings as saved] [Tier 2/3]
- **Engineer-approved design (2026-10-15):** a prominent **Suggest** button in GirderDetail's top bar, Preliminary designer mode only (the #232 mode toggle), opens a full-screen panel inside the app. Suggest is no longer buried in Preliminary sizing's input tabs (the engine is kept; its settings are moved into the panel). The panel lists the design inputs grouped (Bridge layout, Girder plates, Framing, Materials), each with its current value and a mode (Locked, Range, List, Free) and the code and owner limits shown as its bounds; runs the existing engines (Quick suggestion; Full design, about 80 s) with a progress bar and Cancel; lists the options side by side with the current design, each linked to its derivation and checks; Apply writes the chosen option into Preliminary sizing (Preliminary designer then updates the modules). Part 2 (next PR): objectives (lowest cost, lowest steel weight, shallowest depth), the max structure depth constraint, and the short list of distinct options (best per objective plus close alternatives).
- **Where (GirderDetail page):** top bar button `id="gd-sgp-b"` (anchor `class="btn btn-primary gd-sgp-b"`); CSS after `body.mod-pl #pl-wrap { display: block; }` (anchor `SGP (2026-10-15): the Suggest panel (inside Preliminary sizing's frame)`); `gdSgpOpen` / `gdSgpClose` above `/* the mode and the title block to Preliminary sizing (gd-mode, gd-tb) once it is up */`; `applyGdMode` (anchor `SGP: the panel belongs to Preliminary designer mode (Preliminary sizing closes`). Manual Part 1, Working modes: new item "Suggest".
- **Where (Preliminary sizing page, `pl-src`):** CSS after `html.gd-geo #rpt-opts .ck-row[data-geo="0"] { display: none; }`; the panel block `SGP (2026-10-15, engineer-approved design): the Suggest panel.` just above `/* ---------------- alternatives study ---------------- */` (`sgpVars`, `sgpVarsHtml`, `sgpOptCur`, `sgpOptSG`, `sgpOptWS`, `sgpTable`, `sgpResHtml`, `sgpBusy`, `sgpQuick`, `sgpFull`, `sgpApply`, `sgpTick`, `sgpOpen`, `sgpClose`, `sgpGo`, `sgpInit`, the `gd-sgp` message listener); `init()` (anchor `if (EMBED) sgpInit();`); `gdModeSet` (anchor `SGP: the Suggest settings are in the Suggest panel`); Manual "Using the program": new section "The Suggest panel (GirderDetail, Preliminary designer mode)" and a step "Suggest panel (in GirderDetail)".
- **Engine constraints (only active when a new optional field is set; with the settings as saved nothing changes):**
  - `suggestLayout` web depth search: new `sgDVar(SG, inc)` (just above `function suggestLayout`). `suggest.dMode = 'range'` (dMin, dMax, dStep on the Limits tab depth increment; blank step: about six steps) replaces the L/36–L/18 limits of the search and keeps the finer search within the range; `'list'` (dList) sizes those depths only. Invalid range or list: an input error. `keepD` (Locked) still wins.
  - `wsSetup` (girder-count study): new `sgNbVar(SG)`; `suggest.nbMode = 'range'` (nbMin, nbMax) or `'list'` (nbList) sizes only those counts (the loop's stop condition is unchanged).
  - `suggestFull` cross-frame spacings: `suggest.cfMin` (Range) drops the trial spacings below it (the Framing tab spacing stays a candidate).
  - Spacing near interior supports: `suggest.pierOpt = 'off'` (Locked) skips the FSP alternatives in `suggestQuickCheck` and `suggestFull`.
  - `runFullDesign`: the progress callback also stores `SG_RUN.f` / `SG_RUN.m` (read by the panel's progress bar). Display only.
- **Modes stored in the existing settings (migration):** Number of girders Locked = no `nbMode` (default; `ws.W` alone does not change it, so the quick suggestion runs as before). Web depth Locked = `suggest.keepD`, Free = neither keepD nor dMode. Web stiffening Free = `suggest.web 'auto'`, Locked = 'stiffened' / 'unstiffened'. Stiffener spacing Free/Locked = `suggest.doOpt` on/off. Tension-field action = `suggest.tfa`. Cross-frame spacing Locked = `suggest.cfOpt 'off'`, Free = on with cfMax 25 ft, Range = on with cfMin/cfMax. Girder spacing (girder count varying) Free = `ws.sMin/sMax` at their defaults, Range = otherwise. Overhangs (girder count varying) Locked = `ws.ohMin = ws.ohMax`, Free = defaults, Range = otherwise. Choosing a mode writes only these fields (new optional fields: nbMode, nbMin, nbMax, nbList, dMode, dMin, dMax, dStep, dList, cfMin, pierOpt); a project saved before opens with every mode derived from its settings, unchanged. Choosing a girder count other than Locked fills `ws.W` with the current out-to-out width when it is blank (shown in the panel as the Locked width).
- **Modes the engines cannot honour yet (shown disabled, with the reason):** web thickness, flanges, transitions and field splice locations (Free only: sized by the engines); out-to-out width (Locked only: a project requirement); spacing Locked or List while the girder count varies (S follows from N and the overhang); cross-frame spacing List (use Range); spacing near piers Range/List; stiffener spacing Range/List; tension-field action Free (a design choice); cross-frame type (designed in GirderDetail's Cross-frames module; shown from the gd-sgp message); steel grade Range/List/Free (one grade, no hybrid in Suggest, no grade-dependent prices); deck f′c (bridge definition).
- **Suggest input tab:** in GirderDetail its sections Design basis, Girder count from the deck width, Sizing rules, Design rules, Unit costs, Full design, Alternatives study and Unit costs (TS&L) are moved into the panel (Engine settings; the same inputs, ids and saved keys); the fields shown as modes are hidden there (`SGP_DUP`); the tab keeps Loads and reads "Loads" (as in Design modules mode).
- **Governing provision:** none changed. The bounds shown are the existing ones: AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 4.6.2.2 (spacing and d_e ranges), Table 2.5.2.6.3-1 (minimum depth), Eq. 6.10.2.1.1-1, 6.10.2.2, 6.10.9.1, 6.10.9.3.2/6.10.9.3.3, C6.7.4.2.1, 6.7.4.2; the Limits tab values and the owner rules (OWN_RULES: def.minTw, def.incD/plate.incD, def.minBf, def.minTf, sd.ratio, deck.oh, defl.ll, flange.sizes, xf.details, def.gF, hybrid, deck.fc) as cited.
- **Check case (built-in project, owner AASHTO, panel defaults):** Quick suggestion D = 63 in, stiffened web, cost $1,686,891, largest ratio 0.983, passes; Full design D = 69 in, $1,568,200, passed (9 candidates): identical to main's Suggest tab (`tests/suggest.mjs same`). Web depth Range 54–66 in, step 6: depths tried 54, 60, 66 and the finer 62, 64 → 66 in; List 50, 70 → only 50 and 70; girder count List 4, 6 at W = 44.50 ft → the study sizes N = 4 and 6 only.
- **How verified:** `node tests/check-syntax.mjs`; `node tests/compare.mjs --tool gd --project builtin,xsA --owner AASHTO,RIDOT` (every section identical); `node tests/suggest.mjs same --project builtin,xsA --owner AASHTO,RIDOT` (main's Suggest tab vs the panel's buttons: quick suggestion and Full design identical); `node tests/suggest.mjs locks` (modes honoured, Cancel, Apply and module sync, saved data both ways, Design modules mode); screenshots.
- **Saved data:** new optional fields in `plateline_autosave_v1` / project JSON (`suggest.*` listed above), written only when the user picks a mode. Older projects open unchanged; main opens a project with the new fields (they are kept, and ignored). No key renamed.
- **Other copies:** none.
- **Open items:** (1) Part 2: objectives, max structure depth, short list of options. (2) Full design runs in steps on the page's thread: the page answers between steps, but one step can take several seconds on a slow machine (the same engine as the Suggest tab; a Web Worker would need the engine split out, against the single-file rule's spirit; not done). (3) Many help texts of Preliminary sizing still say "Suggest input tab"; in GirderDetail those settings are now in the panel (Engine settings) — reworded only where the panel is described.

+<h3>The Suggest panel (GirderDetail, Preliminary designer mode)</h3><p>GirderDetail's top bar <b>Suggest</b> button opens a full-screen panel over the app (Close or Esc returns). The left side lists the design inputs, grouped (bridge layout, girder plates, framing, materials), each with its current value, a mode, and the code and owner (DOT) limits that bound it. <b>Locked</b> uses the current value; <b>Range</b> (minimum, maximum, step) and <b>List</b> limit what the engines try; <b>Free</b> lets the app decide within the code and the owner limits shown. A mode an engine cannot honour yet is disabled, and the row says why. What each mode does: <b>Number of girders</b> Locked: the quick suggestion and Full design below, on the Bridge tab layout; Range, List or Free: the girder-count study at the held out-to-out width (the counts in the range or list only), then Full design of its best counts. <b>Girder spacing</b> and <b>overhangs</b> vary only with the girder count (Range: the study's limits; Free: the default limits; overhangs Locked: both at the Bridge tab value); the study never exceeds the Limits tab overhang limits of check G6. <b>Web depth</b> Locked: the Girder tab depth; Range: the depths from the minimum to the maximum in steps (blank step: about six steps), then a finer search near the cheapest within the range; List: those depths only; Free: L/36 to L/18 as described below. <b>Web stiffening</b> Locked (stiffened or unstiffened) or Free (the cheaper). <b>Cross-frame spacing</b> Locked: the Framing tab spacing; Range: Full design tries 15 to 30 ft in 2.5 ft steps within it (the Framing tab spacing is always a candidate); Free: up to 25 ft. <b>Spacing near interior supports</b> Locked: the Framing tab setting is kept (no closer spacing is tried); Free: tried where lateral-torsional buckling in negative flexure governs. <b>Stiffener spacing</b> Locked: uniform at the Framing tab d<sub>o</sub>/D; Free: per cross-frame bay. <b>Tension-field action</b>: use or do not use. Web thickness, flanges, transitions and field splices are sized by the engines (Free only); the cross-frame type, steel grade and deck f′<sub>c</sub> are Locked (they are set on their own tabs or in GirderDetail's Cross-frames module). The modes are stored in the Suggest settings of the project (existing settings, plus new optional fields only when a mode is chosen), so a project saved earlier opens with its settings as they were.</p><p>The right side runs the existing engines: <b>Quick suggestion</b> (about a second; the girder-count study takes a few seconds) and <b>Full design</b> (about 20 to 80 s), with a progress bar and <b>Cancel</b>; the page stays usable. The options are shown side by side with the current design: girders, spacing, overhangs, web, largest flange plates, field splices, cross-frames, stiffeners, steel weight, cost (Unit costs), the governing strength and service ratio, and the result. Each option links to its worked derivation and checks in Preliminary sizing (the Suggest output tab); the current design links to its Checks tab. <b>Apply</b> writes the option into the Preliminary sizing inputs (with the usual confirmation and Revert); in Preliminary designer mode GirderDetail then updates every module.</p>

## 2026-10-15 — PR: claude/gd-suggest-panel-2 (Suggest panel, part 2 of 2: objectives, maximum structure depth, the short list of options; engineer-approved design of 2026-10-15; PR link added after merge)

Note on the previous entry (SGP, part 1): merged as PR #242 (https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/242).

### SGP2. Suggest panel: objectives (lowest cost, lowest steel weight, shallowest depth), maximum structure depth, short list of distinct options   [NEW FEATURE — no result change with the settings as saved] [Tier 2/3]
- **Engineer-approved design (2026-10-15):** objectives lowest cost (default), lowest steel weight, shallowest depth (cost as tie-break); constraints maximum structure depth (clearance) and deflection limit (part 1); results as a SHORT LIST of distinct options — the best per objective plus notable alternatives close on cost (one girder more/fewer, deeper/shallower web) — side by side with the current design, each linked to its checks, Apply.
- **Engine (only when a new optional field is set):**
  - New `sgObjCmp(obj)` (above `sgDVar`): candidate comparator. `suggest.obj` absent or 'cost': `(a, b) => a.cost.total - b.cost.total`, the comparator used before (results unchanged); 'wt': least `cost.wTot` (steel of all girders with the detail allowance), cost as tie-break; 'shallow': least D, cost as tie-break. Used in `suggestLayout` (fine-search start `best0`, the pick `pool.sort(CMP)`), and in `suggestFull` (the candidates refined `picks` when obj is set, the cross-frame and FSP base candidates, the final pick).
  - `suggest.maxH` (in): structure depth h = t_s + haunch (as entered) + D + max over the girder of (t_top + t_bot) (`hOf` in `suggestLayout`). A fast candidate with h > maxH is rejected (`ok = false`, `hOver`), the verify and one-candidate paths report `hOK`, and the quick check and Full design count `hOK === false` as not passing. Blank: no check (as before).
  - `suggestFull`: the return shaping moved unchanged into `sgFullShape(fast, best, out)` (pure refactor), and `full.outs` keeps every refined candidate (for the short list). `wsEval` rows carry `cost` (the fast sizing cost; ranking only).
- **Panel:** Objective and constraints rows (objective select `#sgp-obj` writes `suggest.obj` only when changed from the default; maximum structure depth `suggest.maxH`; the current structure depth shown). A Structure depth row in the options table (red above the maximum). Short list (`SGP_ALT`): girder count Locked — after a quick suggestion: the recommended (= the quick suggestion, unchanged) plus, found with the engines themselves and each checked like the quick suggestion (`suggestQuickCheck`): the best for each other objective (`suggestLayout` with that objective) and the nearest shallower and deeper depths whose fast cost is within 3% of the cheapest (`suggestLayout(P, { D })`); after Full design: chosen among Full design's refined candidates (best per other objective, nearest shallower / deeper within 3% of the lowest passing cost). Girder count varying: the best of each objective among the study (or its Full design) rows, plus one girder fewer and one more than the recommended. Duplicates merge their labels. Each option: Apply (the existing Apply on that result: `sgpAltUse` makes it the Suggest result first) and "Show the work" (the Suggest tab's derivation, checks and comparison of that option).
- **Governing provision:** none changed. Structure depth is a project clearance input (no code value).
- **Check case (built-in, AASHTO, `tests/suggest.mjs options`):** quick short list: D 63 stiffened $1,686,891, 441.6 kip, h = 8 + 2 + 63 + 3.125 = 76.125 in (recommended; lowest cost and lowest weight); D 44 $1,927,398 h 57.625 (shallowest); D 60 $1,764,883 (shallower, fast cost within 3%); D 66 $1,692,840 (deeper). Objective 'wt' → fast pick 441,630 lb = the least of the passing candidates; 'shallow' → D 44 = the least passing D. maxH = 54 in → 52 fast candidates rejected, no option passes (every girder ≥ 54.875 in). Full design list: D 69 $1,571,864 (recommended), D 69 at another cross-frame layout 420.9 kip (lowest weight), D 63 (shallowest), D 66 (shallower within 3%). Girder count Free: 4 girders (recommended), 10 (shallowest), 5 (one more).
- **How verified:** `node tests/check-syntax.mjs`; `node tests/compare.mjs --tool gd --project builtin,xsA --owner AASHTO,RIDOT` (identical); `node tests/suggest.mjs same --project builtin,xsA --owner AASHTO,RIDOT` (main vs panel identical, default settings); `node tests/suggest.mjs locks`; `node tests/suggest.mjs options` (12 checks pass); screenshots.
- **Saved data:** new optional fields `suggest.obj`, `suggest.maxH` (written only when set). Older projects unchanged; main ignores them.
- **Other copies:** none.
- **Open items:** "close on cost" is 3% (`SGP_NEAR`), an assumption to confirm. The girder-count study's Full design still picks its counts by the study's own objective (Engine settings: weight or fewest girders); the panel ranks the results by the panel objective.
