-<h3>The Suggest panel (GirderDetail, Preliminary designer mode)</h3><p>GirderDetail's top bar <b>Suggest</b> button opens a full-screen panel over the app (Close or Esc returns). The left side lists the design inputs, grouped (bridge layout, girder plates, framing, materials), each with its current value, a mode, and the code and owner (DOT) limits that bound it. <b>Locked</b> uses the current value; <b>Range</b> (minimum, maximum, step) and <b>List</b> limit what the engines try; <b>Free</b> lets the app decide within the code and the owner limits shown. A mode an engine cannot honour yet is disabled, and the row says why. What each mode does: <b>Number of girders</b> Locked: the quick suggestion and Full design below, on the Bridge tab layout; Range, List or Free: the girder-count study at the held out-to-out width (the counts in the range or list only), then Full design of its best counts. <b>Girder spacing</b> and <b>overhangs</b> vary only with the girder count (Range: the study's limits; Free: the default limits; overhangs Locked: both at the Bridge tab value); the study never exceeds the Limits tab overhang limits of check G6. <b>Web depth</b> Locked: the Girder tab depth; Range: the depths from the minimum to the maximum in steps (blank step: about six steps), then a finer search near the cheapest within the range; List: those depths only; Free: L/36 to L/18 as described below. <b>Web stiffening</b> Locked (stiffened or unstiffened) or Free (the cheaper). <b>Cross-frame spacing</b> Locked: the Framing tab spacing; Range: Full design tries 15 to 30 ft in 2.5 ft steps within it (the Framing tab spacing is always a candidate); Free: up to 25 ft. <b>Spacing near interior supports</b> Locked: the Framing tab setting is kept (no closer spacing is tried); Free: tried where lateral-torsional buckling in negative flexure governs. <b>Stiffener spacing</b> Locked: uniform at the Framing tab d<sub>o</sub>/D; Free: per cross-frame bay. <b>Tension-field action</b>: use or do not use. Web thickness, flanges, transitions and field splices are sized by the engines (Free only); the cross-frame type, steel grade and deck f′<sub>c</sub> are Locked (they are set on their own tabs or in GirderDetail's Cross-frames module). The modes are stored in the Suggest settings of the project (existing settings, plus new optional fields only when a mode is chosen), so a project saved earlier opens with its settings as they were.</p><p>The right side runs the existing engines: <b>Quick suggestion</b> (about a second; the girder-count study takes a few seconds) and <b>Full design</b> (about 20 to 80 s), with a progress bar and <b>Cancel</b>; the page stays usable. The options are shown side by side with the current design: girders, spacing, overhangs, web, largest flange plates, field splices, cross-frames, stiffeners, steel weight, cost (Unit costs), the governing strength and service ratio, and the result. Each option links to its worked derivation and checks in Preliminary sizing (the Suggest output tab); the current design links to its Checks tab. <b>Apply</b> writes the option into the Preliminary sizing inputs (with the usual confirmation and Revert); in Preliminary designer mode GirderDetail then updates every module.</p>

## 2026-10-15 — PR: claude/gd-suggest-followups (Suggest panel follow-ups from #242/#243: SGF-a objective picks the girder counts for Full design, SGF-b help texts, SGF-c defaults recorded; PR link added after merge)

Note on earlier entries: SGP2 merged as PR #243; GD54c (claude/gd-st-utilities) merged as PR #244.

### SGF-a. Girder count varying: the panel objective chooses which counts the study designs in full   [BEHAVIOUR CHANGE of the Suggest panel with the girder count Range/List/Free only — no result change with the default settings (count Locked)] [Tier 2]
- **Problem:** with the girder count varying, the panel ranked the results by its objective (`suggest.obj`), but Full design of the study's best counts (`wsfPicks`) still took them by the study's own objective (`ws.obj`: least weight or fewest girders, Engine settings). So, for example, "shallowest depth" could design in full only the lightest counts (SGP2 open item).
- **Where (pl-src page):** new `wsfObj()`, `wsObjCmp(obj)` above `function wsfPicks()` (anchor `/* SGF-a (2026-10-15, #243 follow-up)`); `wsfPicks` (`po = wsfObj()`); `wsfRun` (`obj: wsfObj()` in `WSF`); `wsfHtml` (the "What this step does" sentence names the objective used); Engine settings field `ws.obj` (note).
- **Before:** `pass.sort(P.ws.obj === 'nb' ? (a, b) => a.N - b.N || a.psf - b.psf : (a, b) => a.psf - b.psf || a.N - b.N);`
- **After:** `pass.sort(po ? wsObjCmp(po) : P.ws.obj === 'nb' ? … : …)`. `po` = the panel objective (`suggest.obj`, default 'cost') when the panel's girder count is Range, List or Free, else null (Locked, the default: exactly as before). `wsObjCmp`: cost → fast cost, then total steel, then N; wt → total steel of all girders (`tot`), then cost, then N; shallow → web depth D, then cost, then N (the comparators of the panel's short list, `sgpOptWS`, with N as the last tie-break). Failing rows still follow, by governing ratio.
- **Governing provision:** none (selection of which candidates are designed; no check, factor or formula changed).
- **Check case (built-in, AASHTO, count Free, nFull = 3; `node tests/suggest.mjs objpicks`):** fast study rows (cost objective): N4 $1,504,817 407.9 kip D 68; N5 $1,703,344 447.1 kip; N6 $1,914,369 489.9 kip … all passing → picks **4, 5, 6** by cost. Shallowest: every count sized at D = 41 in (N4 fails) → picks **5, 6, 7** (D tie, then the lowest cost). Count Locked with obj 'shallow': `wsfObj()` = null and the picks follow `ws.obj` (least weight) as before.
- **How verified:** `node tests/suggest.mjs same --project builtin,xsA --owner AASHTO` (default settings, girder count Locked: the quick suggestion and Full design identical to main); `node tests/suggest.mjs objpicks` (7 checks pass); `node tests/suggest.mjs locks`; `node tests/compare.mjs --tool gd` (built-in, AASHTO: all sections identical); `node tests/check-syntax.mjs`.
- **Saved data:** none (no new field; `WSF.obj` is in memory only).
- **Other copies:** none.
- **Open items:** the ranking values used for the panel objectives (fast-study cost, total steel, web depth) are a default to confirm (ENGINEER_CHECKS GD66 (f)).

## 2026-10-16 — PR: claude/gd-owner-profiles-3b-1 (owner phase 3b part 1: MEDIUM owner items of the RIDOT/MassDOT/CTDOT reviews for shipping, splices, flange transitions, spacing, refined analysis, construction wind, extra camber; engineer's decisions 2026-10-15; PR link added after merge)

Note on earlier entries: SGF (claude/gd-suggest-followups) merged as PR #245. Branch name: `claude/gd-owner-profiles-3b` already existed (it carried phase 3a part 2, merged as #238), so phase 3b is on `claude/gd-owner-profiles-3b-1` (this PR) and `-3b-2` (the GirderDetail modules).

Items of the three reviews already done before this PR and skipped here: orientation and stagger (OWN4/5), multiplier, η, haunch 0, rating targets (OWN6–OWN9), dead loads and utilities (OWN15/16, GD54b/c), deck (OWN17/18), deflection and span-to-depth (OWN19), plate minimums and increments, L/85, T1/T2 for CTDOT and MassDOT, T5 (OWN20/21), studs (OWN22), MassDOT grade, A6 (OWN23), integral abutments (OWN24), CTDOT splices, Category C, CTDOT refined analysis (OWN25), weathering steel (OWN26), MassDOT skew 40°/50° warnings (OWN5).

### OWN28. Shipping limits: RIDOT 100 ft / 150 kip / 9 ft and mandatory splice above 150 ft; CTDOT 120 ft / 120 kip   [CHECK CHANGE and DEFAULTS — §4 callout]
- **Where:** `OWN_RULES` RIDOT `def.shipLen` (100), `def.shipWt` (150), `ship`, `ship.splice`; CTDOT `def.shipWt` (120), `ship`. Preliminary sizing `runChecks` lookups (anchor `const rSh = ownR('ship'), rShS = ownR('ship.splice')`), S2 (anchor `const mand = rShS && p.len > rShS.value.mand`), S3 ref, new S6 (anchor `if (rSh && rSh.value.h) {`); `OWN_DEF_V` 2 → 3.
- **Before:** Limits-tab placeholders 120 ft / 90 kip for every owner; S2/S3 warnings, src Practice; no height item.
- **After:** RIDOT defaults 100 ft / 150 kip, CTDOT 120 kip (untouched inputs only; a value entered is kept and flagged; older projects get the one-time notice). S2/S3 cite the owner (warnings as before: these are permit limits). RIDOT: a piece longer than 150 ft fails S2 (field splice mandatory, BDM 6.7.2); S6 warns when the deepest steel section of a piece exceeds 9 ft (camber and supports not included, a default to confirm).
- **Governing provision:** RIDOT BDM (April 2026) 6.4, 6.7.2; CTDOT BRSDM V2 2.3.5.1CT, 2.3.5.2CT.
- **Check case (built-in, owner switched on the Limits tab, `ownChange`):** RIDOT S2 piece 1 = 82.00/100 = **0.82** (was 82/120 = 0.68); S3 piece 1 = 18.68/150 = **0.12** (was 18.68/90 = 0.21); S6 piece 2: d = 63.50 in = 5.29 ft ≤ 9 ft, ratio **0.59**. CTDOT S3 piece 1 = 18.68/120 = **0.16**. A simple 160 ft span without splices under RIDOT: S2 160 > 150 → **fail**.

### OWN29. Flange transitions: RIDOT width only at field splices, thickness ratio at any splice; owner minimum saving for a transition (RIDOT 800 lb, MassDOT 1300 lb)   [CHECK CHANGE and SIZING CHANGE — §4 callout]
- **Where:** `OWN_RULES` RIDOT `flange.wconst`, `flange.tratio` (value 2, `pref: 1.5`, `field: true`), `flange.weld` (800); MassDOT `flange.weld` (1300). T1 (existing owner branch), T2 (anchor `// OWN29 (RIDOT BDM 6.4): "at any splice"`), Suggest flange sizing weld equivalent (anchor `const rWd = ownRule(plOwner(P), 'flange.weld')`), flange schedule note.
- **Before:** RIDOT T1, T2 warnings (Guide), T2 on shop transitions only; transition kept where saving > weld equivalent = costs.trans / costs.steel = 1500/3.00 = 500 lb (price list).
- **After:** RIDOT T1 fails a width change away from a field splice; T2 covers shop transitions and field splices with a thickness change, fails above 2.0 (50% reduction) and warns above 1.5 (33%, the preferred limit). Weld equivalent = max(price list, owner minimum): RIDOT max(500, 800) = **800 lb**, MassDOT max(500, 1300) = **1300 lb**; AASHTO and CTDOT 500 lb as before.
- **Governing provision:** RIDOT BDM 6.4; MassDOT Part I 3.6.5.6.
- **Check case:** built-in RIDOT T2, bottom flange at 100 ft: 2/1.25 = **1.60 > 1.5 → warning** (≤ 2.0 passes the hard limit); field splice at 82 ft top flange 1/0.75 = 1.33 → pass. Suggest (quick suggestion and Full design, Suggest-tab engine, main → branch): built-in MassDOT quick D 63 → **71** in, 9 → 5 top plates, cost $1,709,883 → $1,715,870; Full design D 71 → **74**, $1,593,570 → $1,611,295, 423.9 → 436.4 kip; built-in RIDOT quick D 71 → 71, $1,772,855 → $1,792,972, Full design D 71 → **74**, $1,609,882 → $1,662,812; xsA MassDOT quick D 63 → 69, Full design 63 → 69; xsA RIDOT Full design D 61 → 63. AASHTO and CTDOT: identical (suggest.mjs same).

### OWN30. MassDOT simple-span field splices at the quarter points   [CHECK CHANGE and SPLICE PLACEMENT — §4 callout]
- **Where:** `OWN_RULES` MassDOT `spl.simple` ({ at: 0.25, tol: 0.05 }); S1 (anchor `// OWN30 (MassDOT 3.6.5.3)`); `spliceLocations` (anchor `// OWN30 (MassDOT 3.6.5.3): a whole simple span`); Suggest splice card note.
- **Before:** simple spans: S1 advisory "away from midspan"; Suggest splits a long span into an odd number of equal pieces (thirds).
- **After (MassDOT):** S1 warns when a simple-span splice is more than 0.05L from the nearest quarter point (default tolerance, to confirm); Suggest places the splices at 0.25L and 0.75L when the middle half fits the shipping length (else as before).
- **Governing provision:** MassDOT Part I 3.6.5.3.
- **Check case:** one simple 130 ft span, MassDOT: Suggest splices [43, 87] → **[33, 97]** ft (130 × 0.25 = 32.5 → 33; middle piece 64 ≤ 120 ft); S1 = |33/130 − 0.25| = 0.0038 ≤ 0.05 → pass. Suggest D 66 → 68 in, cost $707,442 → $681,143.

### OWN31. CTDOT girder count and spacing   [DEFAULT and CHECK CHANGE (warnings) — §4 callout]
- **Where:** `OWN_RULES` CTDOT `def.sLo` (9), `spacing`; G4 ref/src, G5 (anchor `rSpc && S_ < rSpc.value.s - 1e-9 ? 'warn'`).
- **Before:** G5 advisory 6 to 12 ft (Practice); G4 Practice (warning below 4 girders).
- **After (CTDOT):** Limits default S<sub>min</sub> 9 ft; G5 warns below 9 ft (rest of the range advisory); G4 cites V2 C2.5.4.1 (still a warning below 4 girders: a "should").
- **Governing provision:** CTDOT BRSDM V2 C2.5.4.1.
- **Check case:** built-in S = 9.50 ≥ 9.00 → pass; S = 8.5 ft would warn.

### OWN32. RIDOT refined analysis by skew   [CHECK CHANGE — §4 callout]
- **Where:** `OWN_RULES` RIDOT `refined` ({ sk: 40, skF: 60, skewOnly: true }); G13 (anchor `if (v.skF) { const fl = skM >= v.skF - 1e-9;`).
- **After (RIDOT):** G13 fails at a support skew of 60° or more (refined analysis required) and warns above 40° (recommended); the curvature and spacing items stay CTDOT-only.
- **Governing provision:** RIDOT BDM 4.4.1.
- **Check case:** built-in 15°: pass (0.375); 28° (builtin28): pass; 45°: warning; 60°: fail.

### OWN33. CTDOT construction wind (G14, advisory) and extra camber L/100 on simple spans   [DISPLAY / ADVISORY — no computed result changed]
- **Where:** `OWN_RULES` CTDOT `wind.con`, `camber.extra`; G14 (anchor `const rWn = ownR('wind.con');`); Analysis tab card `an-camx` (anchor `// OWN33 (CTDOT V1B): extra camber L/100 in on simple spans`).
- **After (CTDOT):** G14 lists the construction wind check (L/150 lateral deflection of the noncomposite girders, V2 3.8.1.2.5CT) as a separate check not computed here (advisory). Simple spans: an "Owner: extra camber" card gives L/100 in at midspan and a parabola along the span (default chosen), in addition to the dead load camber table (not added to it).
- **Governing provision:** CTDOT BRSDM V2 3.8.1.2.5CT, 3.4.2.1; V1B Dead Load Deflection and Cambers.
- **Check case:** built-in longest span 140 ft: L/150 = 140 × 12/150 = **11.20 in**; a 130 ft simple span: extra camber 130/100 = **1.30 in** at midspan, 0.4 × 0.6 × 4 × 1.30 = 1.248 in at 0.4L.

### How verified (Tier 2 per owner; AASHTO Tier 3 projects)
- `node tests/compare.mjs --tool gd --project builtin,xsA --owner AASHTO,MassDOT,RIDOT,CTDOT`: **AASHTO: every computed section identical** (only the saved defaults version `ownDef.v` 2 → 3 and the one-time notice text listing the owner checks now applied differ). MassDOT: identical results (continuous bridge; the new rules act on Suggest and simple spans). RIDOT: T2 (field splices added, 1.60 > 1.5 warnings), new G13 and S6 items. CTDOT: new G14 item. (The test sets the owner directly, so the defaults do not move there; the defaults were checked with the Limits-tab owner select: RIDOT 120 → 100 ft, 90 → 150 kip; CTDOT 90 → 120 kip, S<sub>min</sub> 6 → 9 ft.)

+<h3>Owner shipping, splices and layout (phase 3b part 1)</h3><p>Defaults follow the same rule as before (an untouched input moves, a value you entered is kept and flagged); projects saved earlier open once with a notice listing what moved.

### OWN34. RIDOT bracing type: diaphragms at 40 in or less, X or K by S/d, single members, bottom chord   [DEFAULT and CHECK CHANGE — §4 callout]
- **Where:** `OWN_RULES` RIDOT `def.xfMinD` (key `framing.xfMinD` 40, gkey `cf.dMinXF` 40), `xf.type` ({ strict, xLo 1.0, kHi 1.5, members }). `cfTypeRec` (anchor `/* OWN34–OWN36 (phase 3b part 2): the owner's bracing rules`), CF10 (anchor `shall = !!(TR.rT && TR.rT.value.shallXF`), new CF11 (anchor `// OWN34, OWN35, OWN37 (phase 3b part 2): the owner's bracing details`), `AD.cf` frame type (anchor `kx = cfTypeRec(C0).kx`) and the bracing-type messages.
- **Before:** minimum depth for cross-frames 48 in for every owner (d ≥ 48 → cross-frame); frame type K when S/h > 1.5, else X; no owner items.
- **After (RIDOT):** default 40 in (untouched inputs only, both apps; a value entered is kept and flagged; older projects get the one-time notice); "40 in or less" strict: d ≤ 40 → diaphragm recommended (CF10 warns a cross-frame, as before); X required when S/d ≤ 1.0, K when S/d ≥ 1.5 (CF11 fails the other type; auto-design selects it); between 1.0 and 1.5 the S/h rule as before. CF11 also lists single members and a bottom chord (always met here).

+<b>RIDOT</b> (BDM 6.4.3, 6.4, 6.4.2, 6.3.1, 3.2.3.1): minimum girder depth for cross-frames 40 in (Framing tab and Cross-frames default): a girder 40 in deep or less generally takes a diaphragm (CF10 warns when a cross-frame is used there); X-frames when the girder spacing to girder depth S/d is 1.0 or less and K-frames when 1.5 or more, the designer's choice between (CF11 fails a frame of the other type; auto-design selects it); single members and a bottom chord on every cross-frame (CF11: always met by this module); transverse stiffeners and connection plates of the fascia girder on one side, not exposed to view (Transverse stiffeners TS8 fails a pair on an exterior girder location); stiffener and connection plate minimums 7/16 in, 1/2 × 5 in and bearing stiffeners 7/16 in, plus the sacrificial thickness of uncoated weathering steel (TS8, BS7); primary-member fatigue details only Category A, B or C′ (Fatigue FA7 warns on any other, which needs approval and infinite life; studs are included); the jacking reaction is Strength I with the dead and live load, γ<sub>DC</sub> 1.3 and the factors increased by 10%, 1.1η[1.3DC + 1.5DW + 1.75(m(LL+IM) + PL)] (Structural analysis reaction table and the DXF reaction table; enter it as the end diaphragm jacking reaction in Cross-frames). The bearing stiffener module has no jacking check (not in its scope).
+<b>MassDOT</b> (Part I 3.6.3.6, 3.6.3.2): straight plate girders less than 48 in deep take the rolled-beam diaphragm depth, at least 0.5d (Cross-frames CFD, CFE, CF10 and the diaphragm auto-design; 0.75d otherwise); no transverse stiffeners on the outside face of the exterior girders (TS8).
+<b>CTDOT</b> (BRSDM V2 6.7.4.2.1CT, 6.7.4.2.2CT, Table 6.7.4.2-1, 6.13.5.1.1CT, 6.10.11.1.1, 6.10.11.2.1, 4.6.2.2.1): the bracing type follows the <b>web depth</b> D (the Stability bracing D in Cross-frames, else the girder depth d) against 48 in: under 4 ft channel diaphragms (a cross-frame warns, CF10), over 4 ft cross-frames (a diaphragm fails, CF10); the channel of Table 6.7.4.2-1 for the web depth is shown for skews under 30° (CF11, advisory: the module still designs the diaphragm to AASHTO 6.7.4.2, at least 0.75d, which the table channels do not reach; a depth between two rows takes the larger channel); end bearing diaphragms preferably C15x33.9 or MC18x42.7 (CF11 warning), end bearing cross-frames K-type with a channel top chord (CF11 advisory: not designed separately here); at least 4 bolts per connection (CF11 warning; auto-design starts at 4, per cross-frame member end and per diaphragm end); transverse stiffeners on the inside face only on exterior girders (TS8 fails a pair there), pairs on interior girders (TS8 advisory), at least 1/2 in (TS8), bearing stiffeners at least 3/4 in (BS7; auto-design starts at 3/4 in); dead load distribution in LLDF and DLs "Typical AASHTO (all loads equally to all beams)" by default (no CTDOT method for steel girders).</p>

## 2026-10-19 — PR: claude/gd-ridot-mult-explicit (engineer requests 2026-10-19: the RIDOT design load multiplier m made explicit; the live load distribution factors used by Structural analysis stated; display only; PR link added after merge)

Engineer's questions: "where does it say there is an additional 20% added to the live load forces?", then "make sure it's more explicit"; and "Structural analysis, Results tab: state the actual LLDF values used, not only that they come from LLDF and DLs".

No computed value, load factor, formula, check, saved key or saved format changes: every change below is text, a link or a card. With m = 1 (AASHTO, MassDOT, CTDOT: no multiplier) nothing new shows, and every changed expression returns exactly the text it returned before (the helpers fall back to `f2(v)`, or the branch is guarded by `m !== 1`). Basis of m: RIDOT BDM 3.4.1.2 (owner rule `ld.mult`, OWN6; GD45 for the pedestrian load); AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Table 3.4.1-1, Art. 1.3.2.1 (η). [Tier 1, display only; run at Tier 2/3 breadth: builtin and xsA × AASHTO and RIDOT]

### GDM-1. Helpers (main page)   [new code, display only]
- **Where:** after the `[data-mod-go]` click handler (anchor `/* GDM (engineer request 2026-10-19, display only): the design load multiplier m made explicit`).
- **New:** `GD_M_MODS = ['sa', 'gs', 'wt', 'ts', 'splice', 'bstf']` (the modules whose factored results carry m); `gdGLq`, `gdGLt(v, sv, off)` (TeX: `\underbrace{1.75(η)(m)}_{\gamma_{LL}\eta m = v}`; Service: `\underbrace{1.30(m)}_{\gamma_{LL}m = v}`), `gdGLh` (HTML: `1.75ηm = 1.75(1.000)(1.20) = 2.100`), `gdGLb` (the same in brackets, for a sum), `gdMTxt()` (banner text), `gdMBanner(id)` (Summary-tab banner), and a click handler for `data-gdcard="tab:card"` links (opens the tab, expands the card, scrolls to it). The entered factor is recovered as v/(η·m) (Strength) or v/m (Service) for display only; v itself is the value the module uses, unchanged. `off` = the design-check load rating run of Girder section (GS20, `R.base`), which has no m.

### GDM-2. Banner on each module's Summary tab   [display only]
- **Where:** `gmRecompute()` (Structural analysis, Girder section, Welds and transitions, Transverse stiffeners), the field splice recompute (after `renderSummary()`), and the bearing stiffener recompute (after `bsRenderSummary()`).
- **Before:** the multiplier was stated only in the "Owner load rules" card of the loads tab, the top-bar "rules" pop-up and Preliminary sizing.
- **After (RIDOT):** "**RIDOT design load multiplier m = 1.20 (RIDOT BDM 3.4.1.2) applied:** LL+IM × 1.20 at Strength I and Service I / II in this module's factored results; not on the live load deflection, fatigue, deck placement or the design-check load rating, nor on the pedestrian load (GD45). Unfactored LL+IM values are shown without m. Worked in [Owner load rules]." (link: loads tab, card `cb-own`). Nothing when m = 1.

### GDM-3. Calculation report (D11): the banner and "see §"   [display only]
- **Where:** `crCombos()` (each card's `id` now returned), `buildCalcReport()` (`SEE` map; `H2(t, ref, id, cid)`; the banner as the first paragraph of the loads section; at the end, every `data-gdcard` link becomes a link to its report section followed by "(see §n.k)").

Other modules: "… Worked in Owner load rules (see §3.1)". A link whose card is not in the report prints as plain text.

### GDM-4. γ_LL written symbolically in the worked derivations   [display only]
Each bare γ_LL number (e.g. 2.10) became 1.75(η)(m) under a brace with the product, in TeX, or "1.75ηm = 1.75(1.000)(1.20) = 2.100" in HTML. With m = 1 the text is exactly as before.
- **Field splice:** `gdCompute` → `c.Vexpr` (Strength I and Service II shear), `+ ${f2(g('llS'))}(…)` → `+ ${gdGLt(g('llS'))}(…)`, `${f2(g('llSv'))}` → `${gdGLt(g('llSv'), 1)}`; `renderCombos()` stress table, γ column of the LL+IM rows: `f2(t.g)` → `gdGLh(t.g, cb.type === 'sv')`.
- **Transverse stiffeners:** `combos(R)`: the general Strength I equation and the three per-row V_u equations, `${f2(R.g.ll)}` → `${gdGLt(R.g.ll)}`; echo "Load factors DC / DW / LL / Fatigue": `${f2(R.g.ll)}` → `${gdGLh(R.g.ll)}`.
- **Welds and transitions:** checks' "where" rows (`${gdGLb(t.gm)} × V × Q / I` for LL+IM: "[1.75ηm = 1.75(1.000)(1.20) = 2.100] × V × Q / I"), the note "γ_LL = …", the shear-flow table γ column (LL+IM row), the echo.
- **Bearing stiffeners:** `bsRenderCombos()`: the general and per-bearing R_u equations; the echo.
- **Girder section:** `gsGovTex(v, base)` (f_bu,gov of the governing section: γ_LL term), callers pass `R.base`; GS11 V_u (both forms), GS19 M_u,opp, the "Load combinations" card (`gdGLb`), the stress-accumulation γ column (LL+IM row), the echo (raw `R.G.ll` / `R.G.sll` kept when m = 1).
- **Structural analysis:** "Load factors" card: γ LL+IM column `f2(C.ll)` → `gdGLh(C.ll, !/^Str/.test(C.id))` (Strength I 1.75ηm, Service I 1.00m, Service II 1.30m; the pedestrian factor in brackets unchanged); its reference line "η = 1.0" → "η = 1.000, m = 1.20 (owner load rules)" when m is not 1 (left as before when m = 1; see open items).
- **Check case (built-in, RIDOT, η_I = no, η = 1.000; Transverse stiffeners, "Span 1, first stiffener from Abut. 1, interior"):** before `V_u = 1.25(47.60 + 3.80) + 1.50(7.50) + 2.10(108.10) = 302.51 kip`; after `V_u = 1.25(47.60 + 3.80) + 1.50(7.50) + 1.75(1.000)(1.20)(108.10) = 302.51 kip` with the brace "γ_LLηm = 2.100". ## 2026-10-19 — PR: claude/gd-stgirder-load-inputs (GDL: the load inputs of the girder sent to ST-Girder with its demands; engineer request 2026-10-19; cross-tool PR with stgirder.html and HANDOFF.md §4.9; display only; PR link added after merge)

Engineer's request: "When the analysis is sent from GirderDetail to ST-Girder, bring over the load inputs as well so there is no confusion. Update the load section of the Input tab [in ST-Girder] with the correct inputs from the GirderDetail app."

### GDL. `girderDetail.loads` added to the "Send to ST-Girder" payload   [hand-off data, display only, Tier 1]
- **Where:** new `GD_DL_METH` and `gdStLoads(R, addPL)` above `gdStPayload` (anchor `/* GDL (engineer request 2026-10-19; HANDOFF.md 4.9)`); in `gdStPayload`, after the payload object: `const ldIn = gdStLoads(R, pl); if (ldIn) p.girderDetail.loads = ldIn;`. One note line reworded (anchor `'Not sent as forces: construction live load`).
- **Before:** the payload carried the forces and `girderDetail` (DFs, IM, materials, deck, bracing, skew, utilities in klf) but not the load inputs; ST-Girder showed its own load inputs beside GirderDetail's forces. Note: `'Not sent: construction live load, deck placement sequence, wind and flange lateral bending.'`
- **After:** optional `girderDetail.loads` (HANDOFF.md §4.9), read from the same `GM.sa.compute` run `R` as the forces and its LLDF and DLs dead loads (`R.DF.dead`): `components` = girder steel (length-weighted average of `R.wSt` over the node tributary lengths, min, max, detail allowance), cross-frames (`R.xf`: count, total kip), deck (`D.deck[j]`; t_s + sacrificial, w_c, tributary width), haunch (`D.haunch[j]`), SIP forms (`D.sip[j]`), and every row of `D.per` except the pedestrian load (barriers, curbs, railings, sidewalks, fences, median, wearing surface, overlays, added rows, utilities) with `w = L.r[j]` on this girder, `wTotal`, `x`, `dist`/`distLabel`, `byMethod`, `overridden`, basis fields and source; `totals` (`R.wDeck`, `R.wDC2`, `R.wDW`, `R.wUT`, `R.wUF`, `R.wPL`, steel average, cross-frame kip); `distribution` (method, label, beam class); `deck`, `edges`, `wearingSurface`, `construction` (`b.cll` psf × `R.beffFt` = `R.wCL`), `liveLoad` (HL-93, IM, `geo.NL` lanes, lane width, roadway, `gDef`, pedestrian psf, walkable widths, klf and rows, `inLL`). Rounded to 0.0001. The field is omitted if it cannot be built. Note: `'Not sent as forces: construction live load (its input is listed in girderDetail.loads), deck placement sequence, wind and flange lateral bending.'`
- **Problem:** ST-Girder's own load inputs (barrier/SIDL 0.30, wearing surface 0.25 klf, …) could disagree with what GirderDetail used for the forces it sent.
- **Governing provision:** none changed (data only). The values are the existing LLDF and DLs loads (AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 3.5.1, 4.6.2.2.1; MassDOT 3.5.3; RIDOT BDM 3.3.1) and HL-93 (3.6.1.2, 3.6.1.3.1, 3.6.2.1).
- **Check case (built-in 15°, AASHTO, G2; dead load method MassDOT pile-cap, the project setting):** deck 9.50 ft × 8.00/12 × 0.150 = 0.950 klf; haunch 2/12 × 16/12 × 0.150 = 0.0333; SIP 15 psf × 8.167 ft = 0.1225; wet DC1 = 1.1058 = `R.wDeck` (the load behind `M_DC1wet`). DC2: left barrier 0.1705 + right barrier 0.0800 = 0.2505 = `R.wDC2`. DW: 25 psf × 41.50 ft / 5 = 0.2075 = `R.wDW`. Steel 0.2541 klf average (0.2276 to 0.3454), 34 cross-frame loads, 5.604 kip. Construction 20 psf × 9.50 ft = 0.190 klf. 3 lanes; g_Δ = 3 × 0.85 / 5 = 0.510. MassDOT utility project (`tests/projects/gd/util.json`, G2): also UT 0.150 and UF 0.125 klf = `R.wUT`, `R.wUF`. Built-in with a 6 ft × 8 in left sidewalk and 75 psf, RIDOT, G1: barrier 0.240 + sidewalk 0.360 = DC2 0.600; pedestrian 75 psf × 4.50 ft walkable, 0.320 klf on G1 (two adjacent), `inLL: true`.
- **How verified (Tier 1, plus the payload):** `node tests/check-syntax.mjs "Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html"` (all scripts pass); `node tests/compare.mjs --tool gd --project builtin,util --owner AASHTO,MassDOT`: all sections identical to main, no console errors. G2 payloads (built-in AASHTO; util MassDOT) made headless with main and with the branch: identical except `girderDetail.loads` and the one note line (producedAt removed).
- **Saved data:** none (no key or project field added or changed). Channel, key, `_schema` and `schemaVersion` unchanged; the field is additive and optional (HANDOFF.md §3.6).
- **Other copies:** the receiver is `stgirder.html` (fixlog/stgirder.md GDL).
- **Open items:** ENGINEER_CHECKS GD69 (ST-Girder outputs that still use its own load inputs).
- **Diff (main → branch; no context lines):**

## 2026-10-19 — PR: claude/gd-stgirder-import-all (GDX: the detail-module inputs sent to ST-Girder; engineer decision 2026-10-19 "Whatever can be imported from GirderDetail should be"; cross-tool PR with stgirder.html, HANDOFF.md §4.9 and ENGINEER_CHECKS GD69/GD70; PR link added after merge)

### GDX. `girderDetail.details` added to the "Send to ST-Girder" payload   [hand-off data; no GirderDetail result change, Tier 1 for this file]
- **Where:** new `gdStDetails()` above `gdStPayload` (anchor `/* GDX (engineer decision 2026-10-19`); in `gdStPayload` after the GDL line: `const dtIn = gdStDetails(); if (dtIn) p.girderDetail.details = dtIn;`.
- **Before:** the payload carried no stiffener, stud or fatigue inputs; ST-Girder used its own.
- **After:** optional `girderDetail.details` (HANDOFF.md §4.9), read as entered in the modules: `transverseStiffener` (Transverse stiffeners type A: b_t, t_p, sides, grade and F_y, the d_o values of the type A rows), `bearingStiffeners` (Bearing stiffeners types: name, pairs, b_t, t_p; grade and F_y), `studs` (Shear connectors: d, h, F_u, transverse spacing, zones x1, x2, n per row, pitch), `fatigue` (Fatigue: ADTT one direction, p, (ADTT)SL = p × ADTT, design life, limit state; Girder section top and bottom flange fatigue categories; the cycles n of the Fatigue rows). Bridge-wide values (the module rows cover the interior and exterior girders). Omitted if it cannot be built.
- **Governing provision:** none changed (data only).
- **Check case (built-in 15°, AASHTO, G2):** `details.transverseStiffener` = { b_t 4.5, t_p 0.375, sides 1, grade 50W, F_y 50, spacings [60], rows 12 }; `bearingStiffeners` = abutment 1 pair 6.75 × 0.625, pier 1 pair 8.00 × 0.750, grade 50; `studs` = d 0.875, h 4, 30 zones; `fatigue` = ADTT 2000, p 0.85, (ADTT)SL 1700, life 75, limit auto, catTop B, catBot B, cycles [1, 1.5].
- **How verified:** `node tests/check-syntax.mjs "Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html"` (all scripts pass); `node tests/compare.mjs --tool gd --project builtin,util --owner AASHTO,MassDOT`: all sections identical to main (0573760), no console errors. G2 payloads (built-in AASHTO; `tests/projects/gd/util.json` MassDOT) from main and from the branch: identical except `girderDetail.details` (producedAt removed).
- **Saved data:** none. Channel, key, `_schema`, `schemaVersion` unchanged; the field is additive and optional.
- **Other copies:** receiver `stgirder.html` (fixlog/stgirder.md GDX).

## 2026-10-19 — PR: claude/ridot-stepped-xf (RIDOT, largest support skew over 20°: intermediate cross-frames stepped on lines parallel to the bearings, as the RIDOT standard framing plan; engineer decision 2026-10-19; PR link added after merge)

Engineer's decision (2026-10-19), from the RIDOT standard framing plan sheet "Framing plan for skew greater than 20° (simple span), plate girder (G) or rolled sections (S)": end diaphragms D-1 along the skewed bearing line at each abutment; intermediate diaphragms D-2 normal to the girders, one per bay per line, each intermediate diaphragm line parallel to ℄ of bearings (typ.), so across the bridge the D-2s of one line step from bay to bay (offset ≈ S·tan θ, an echelon, not a half-spacing checkerboard); span and diaphragm spacing dimensioned along ℄ roadway; W.P. where ℄ roadway crosses the bearing lines. Governing: RIDOT BDM (Apr. 2026) 6.4.3 and the RIDOT standard framing plan for skew greater than 20°; AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 6.7.4.2 (normal frames at skews over 20°; either arrangement "may") and C6.7.4.2.1 (first-frame offset max(4b_f, 0.4L_b); 4b_f the recommended lower limit for stagger distances).

### RXF1. `framingLayout` / `normSpan`: arrangement 'stepped' for RIDOT   [LAYOUT CHANGE → L_b, DC1 cross-frame point loads and every result fed by them, RIDOT bridges with θ_max > 20° and Orientation Automatic only — §4 callout]
- **Where (Preliminary sizing page, `pl-src`):** `normSpan(k, bf, dmin, pz, arr)` (anchors `const A = gi.map(i => xb(k, i)), B = gi.map(i => xb(k + 1, i)), stp = arr === 'stepped';`, `// RIDOT stepped: n = ⌈L/s⌉ - 1 lines evenly spaced along ℄`, `const put = x => { const y = mp(b, x);`, `const st = stp ? { ln:`, `...(r.g.st ? { stp:`); the span loop (anchor `const arr = oxA && o === 'normal' ? ox.arr : F.arrange;`); `plOwnXf` (anchor `arr: gt ? ((r.value && r.value.arr) || 'staggered') : null`); main page `OWN_RULES` RIDOT `xf.orient` (`value: { thr: 20, scope: 'bridge', arr: 'stepped' }`, text) and RIDOT `xf.details` (text).
- **Before:** RIDOT and CTDOT with Orientation Automatic and θ_max > 20°: `const arr = oxA && o === 'normal' ? 'staggered' : F.arrange;` and `plOwnXf` returned `arr: gt ? 'staggered' : null`: one normal grid per span at spacing s, alternate bays shifted s/2 (checkerboard), anchored e = max(clear, 4b_f, 0.4s) past the obtuse-corner bearing.
- **After:** `plOwnXf` returns the rule's `value.arr` (RIDOT `'stepped'`; CTDOT has none → `'staggered'`, unchanged). For `'stepped'`, `normSpan` works in ℄ stations: a line at ℄ station x (from the W.P. of support k, X_k) is the line parallel to the bearings, interpolated between the two bearing lines like parallel frames (exactly parallel when both skews are equal); in bay b the frame is normal to the girders at the station where that line crosses the bay centerline, `mp(b, x) = (1 − f)·xm(k, b) + f·xm(k + 1, b)`, f = (x − X_k)/L, xm = the bearing at the bay centerline. Default: n = ⌈L/s⌉ − 1 lines, L = the span along ℄ (`m.sup[k + 1] − m.sup[k]`), evenly at s_c = L/(n + 1), the first line s_c from the W.P.; used when every frame is then clear of its bearings (s_c − h ≥ e at a support skewed > 20°, e = max(clear, 4b_f, 0.4s_c); else the clear distance; h = the largest half-step S_b·tan θ/2 at that support). Otherwise (short spans, very large steps) the existing grid logic with the obtuse reference replaced by X_k + h (end lines e clear of the nearest bearing, lines between evenly at ≤ s). After that everything runs as before on the lines: corner frames where a girder panel would exceed s (acute corners), the splice/transition shift search (end lines moved, extra lines), the pier regions (s_p, region ends in ℄ stations). Non-stepped arrangements: `mp(b, x) = x`, the same filter, identical frames (proved below).
- **On every girder** the frames of its two sides are S·tan θ/2 either side of each line, so adjacent bays step by S·tan θ; interior girder panels alternate S·tan θ and s_c − S·tan θ; exterior girders s_c; the acute-corner end panel of each exterior girder is s_c + S·tan θ/2 and gets a corner frame when that exceeds s.
- **End diaphragms (D-1):** already modelled: a frame in every bay on every bearing line (`type: 'sup'`), unchanged (DC1 end-frame loads, plans, DXF, 3D). No new element added.
- **Spacing along ℄ roadway:** ℄ roadway is taken as the centerline of the girder layout (y_c), through which every support line passes (the W.P. is X_k on it). With unequal overhangs or barriers the roadway centerline can differ from y_c; the tool has no separate roadway offset input (open item).

### RXF2. Consumers   [display / check wording; computed values follow RXF1]
- **Check X1** (`framingChecks`, anchor `stR = ox.arr === 'stepped'`): RIDOT required "Normal, stepped: lines parallel to the bearings, spacing along ℄ roadway"; pass when `o.arr === ox.arr` (was `=== 'staggered'`); symbolic line, note (the standard, the step, X3, corner frames) and work line say "stepped". CTDOT note, required text and pass rule unchanged (its `ox.arr` is `'staggered'`).
- **Check X3** unchanged in code; under RIDOT stepped it reports the step S·tan θ against d_min = max(min. offset, 4b_f) and warns where it is smaller (kept: the standard's pattern; engineer instruction).
- **Framing tab:** owner line `frOwnHtml` (required text; conformity `o.arr === ox.arr`), spacing table `frSumHtml` ("s_c along ℄", the lines' ℄ stations from the W.P., the step S·tan θ with a link to X3, corner frames, the nearest frame of the first/last line); Orientation "Automatic" label (`renderOwnInfo`) "else normal and stepped on lines parallel to the bearings" for RIDOT.
- **Framing plan** (`framingSVG`, anchor `// RIDOT stepped (2026-10-19): ℄ roadway`): ℄ roadway, W.P. circles, the lines dashed, the line spacings written along ℄, caption. **DXF framing plan** (`dxfPlan`, main page, anchor `// RIDOT stepped (2026-10-19, RIDOT standard framing plan`): CL ROADWAY line and W.P. text, layer `XFRM-LINE` (CENTER) for the lines, a chain dimension of the lines along CL ROADWAY, note "INTERMEDIATE CROSS-FRAME (DIAPHRAGM) LINES PARALLEL TO CL OF BEARINGS (TYP.), ONE NORMAL TO THE GIRDERS IN EACH BAY. SPACING MEASURED ALONG CL ROADWAY. W.P. = CL ROADWAY ON CL BEARING." Other sheets, 3D view, tables: from `FR.frames`, unchanged code.
- **Help / manual:** Limits tab "Orientation, arrangement" row; Framing method (new paragraph "RIDOT, largest support skew over 20° (stepped frames)"); GirderDetail manual "Owner (DOT) profile"; the `framingLayout` header comment.
- **Hand-offs:** `bridge.xf` (DC1 point loads, GirderDetail `gdXfPts`), the L_b of every module (`detailExport`), ST-Girder's `bracing.Lb` and DC1 split all come from `framingLayout`; no code change, they follow the new layout. HANDOFF.md does not describe the stagger: unchanged.

### §4 callout: layout rule before / after (RIDOT, Orientation Automatic, θ_max > 20°)
- **Before:** normal to the girders, **staggered**: one grid per span at s = (T − Σe)/⌈(T − Σe)/s_target⌉ (T between the obtuse bearings), first line e = max(clear, 4b_f, 0.4s) past the obtuse-corner bearing, alternate bays shifted s/2.
- **After:** normal to the girders, **stepped**: n = ⌈L/s_target⌉ − 1 lines parallel to the bearings, at s_c = L/(n + 1) along ℄ roadway (L = span along ℄); one frame per bay where the line crosses the bay centerline; frames of adjacent bays offset S·tan θ; corner frames at the acute corners where a panel would exceed s_target; first frame ≥ e from its bearing (else end lines set e clear and the rest evenly spaced).
- **Unchanged:** CTDOT (staggered), MassDOT and AASHTO (per span, as before), RIDOT with θ_max ≤ 20° (parallel), any Orientation set by hand (layout as before; under RIDOT > 20° check X1 now requires "stepped", so Normal + Staggered set by hand, which passed X1 before, now fails it: see open items). End frames on the bearing lines unchanged.
- **Governing:** RIDOT BDM (Apr. 2026) 6.4.3 and the RIDOT standard framing plan for skew greater than 20° (engineer's decision 2026-10-19); AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) 6.7.4.2 and C6.7.4.2.1; L_b in 6.10.8.2.3 and 6.10.3.2.1 (unchanged equations; the brace points move).

### Hand check of the step (case 1)
Simple span L = 120 ft along ℄, θ = 30° both ends, 6 girders at S = 9.5 ft (y_c = 23.75 ft), s_target = 25 ft, b_f = 18 in.
- n = ⌈120/25⌉ − 1 = 5 − 1 = 4 lines; s_c = 120/5 = **24.00 ft** (lines at 24, 48, 72, 96 ft along ℄ from the W.P.).
- Half-step h = (S/2)·tan 30° = 4.75 × 0.57735 = **2.742 ft**; step S·tan θ = 9.5 × 0.57735 = **5.485 ft**.
- e = max(3, 4 × 18/12 = 6.00, 0.4 × 24 = 9.60) = 9.60 ft; s_c − h = 24 − 2.742 = 21.258 ≥ 9.60: the even spacing is used.
- G2 (y = 9.5): its bearing lies on the bearing line, so on G2 the line at 24 ft is at own station 24.000; bay G2–G3 (centerline y = 14.25, 4.75 ft beyond G2) frame at 24 + 2.742 = **26.742**; bay G1–G2 (centerline y = 4.75) at 24 − 2.742 = **21.258**; offset 5.485 = S·tan θ (tool: 21.257 / 26.742).
- Acute corner, G1 (Abut. 1): first frame 24 + 2.742 = 26.742 > 25 → corner frame in bay G1–G2 at 26.742/2 = **13.371** on G1 = 13.371 − 5.485 = **7.886** on G2 (tool: same). X5: d₁ = 7.886 ≥ max(6.00, 0.4 × (21.257 − 7.886) = 5.35) → pass.
- X3: d = 5.485 < d_min = max(4.00, 6.00) = 6.00 ft → **warning** on G2–G5 (kept: the standard's pattern).

- **Governing results (main → branch; main already fails GS7 at the exterior piers under RIDOT 28°):** GS7 negative flexure, nonprismatic L_b: Pier 1 exterior 1.067 → **1.181**, Pier 2 exterior 1.108 → **1.181** (F_nc 44.56 / 43.43 → 41.85 ksi), transitions at 100 / 260 ft exterior 1.071 / 1.062 → 1.130 / 1.130 (still fail), interior Piers 1.030 → 1.029 (fail, unchanged in substance), transitions at 127 / 233 ft 0.684 / 0.641 → 0.641 / 0.642; GS20 (reserve summary of GS7) Pier exterior 1.061 / 1.174 → 1.514; GS10 Pier 1 / 2 exterior 0.424 / 0.483 → 0.614; GS14 Pier exterior bottom flange buckling 0.329 / 0.337 → 0.348, positive exterior 0.339 / 0.322 → 0.328 / 0.299; GS11 transitions 0.425 → 0.436 (interior), 0.449 → 0.465; Cross-frames CF1/CF7 0.105 → 0.104, CF2 0.064 → 0.063, CF4 0.070 → 0.068; Deck overhang OH1 0.568 → 0.519, OH2 0.476 → 0.442, OH4 0.392 → 0.373, OH5 0.538 → 0.456. Fatigue (connection-plate rows), transverse stiffeners, shear connectors, welds, bearing stiffeners and splice follow the new frame stations and DC1 (Structural analysis girder 1 forces change through the DC1 point-load positions). **Pass/fail statuses: no check changes status** (the GS7 exterior pier items fail on main and on the branch); the exterior pier margin is worse. Remedy, as before: the spacing near interior supports s_p (Framing tab) or heavier pier plates.

### How the ends, piers and splices are handled
- **Ends (acute corners):** the lines start s_c from the W.P. along ℄, so the exterior girder on the acute side gets an end panel of s_c + S·tan θ/2; where that exceeds the target s, the existing corner-frame rule adds one normal frame in the exterior bay (at least max(clear, 4b_f) from the bay's bearings, at least d_min from other frames on both girders or lined up with one; built-in: midway). The first frame of every girder is checked against e = max(clear, 4b_f, 0.4s_c) when the even spacing is chosen; if a frame would be closer, the end lines are set e clear of the nearest bearing and the lines between evenly spaced (the existing grid rule, in ℄ stations). X5 is unchanged.
- **Splices / transitions:** the existing shift search moves whole lines (end lines inward up to 4 ft, or up to two more intervals) and keeps the first candidate clear of every conflict; individual frames are never moved. Built-in 28°: no conflict remains (X4 warn → pass).
- **Pier regions (s_p):** pzGrid works on ℄ stations (region ends measured from X_k + h); lines at s_p in the region, evenly at ≤ s between. In mixed-skew or very skewed sweeps with s_p = 15 ft a few pier-region panels end up to 7% over s_p (X2 warns, below), because the corner-frame rule needs d_min from the stepped frames, which are themselves only S·tan θ apart.
- **End diaphragms (D-1):** already modelled on every bearing line (type 'sup'); unchanged.

### Saved data
- No key or format change. `framing.arrange` and `framing.orient` keep their values; the OWN_RULES table is code, not saved data. `bridge.xf` (GirderDetail `P.df.bridge`) has the same format; its frame list changes because Preliminary sizing re-publishes the computed layout.
- **Projects saved under RIDOT with θ_max > 20° and Orientation Automatic re-lay out on open** (the layout is computed): frame stations, every L_b, the DC1 cross-frame point loads and every result fed by them change, as in the cases above. A stored per-bay stiffener table (`framing.bays`) then no longer matches the bays: D4 flags it and the uniform d_o/D is used until Suggest Apply or the table is edited (existing behaviour). Projects with Orientation set by hand keep their layout (X1 now fails under RIDOT > 20°).

### How verified
- `node tests/check-syntax.mjs "Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html"`: all scripts pass.
- **`framingLayout` sweep (headless, main vs branch, same page instance per side), 3,520 configurations:** owners AASHTO, MassDOT, CTDOT, RIDOT × skews 15, 0, 20, 28, 28/0/0/28, 0/28/28/0, 21/15/15/15, 45, −30/30/30/−30, 30/25/25/30, 55 × contiguous / staggered × Orientation auto / normal / parallel × s 20 / 25 × 3 / 5 girders × continuous / simple × s_p none / 15. **Frames identical in every configuration except RIDOT + Automatic + θ_max > 20° (256 of 256 changed).** Checks identical except: those 256; and 384 RIDOT configurations with θ_max > 20° and the orientation set by hand, where only X1's "Required" text changes and Normal + Staggered (128) goes pass → fail (the required pattern is now stepped). In the 256 changed: X1 pass 256/256; X5 pass 256/256; X3 warn 6 → 220 (the step below 4b_f, expected); X4 warn 216 → 132; X2 warn 22 → 28 (gained: s_p = 15 ft cases at 0/28/28/0, 30/25/25/30 and 55° with s = 20 ft, at most 1.07 s_p; lost: 55° without s_p).
- **`node tests/compare.mjs --tool gd`** (origin/main 419921a / bcbd913, the same GirderDetail file, vs branch), every section (`gd.project`, `pl.project`, `pl.checks`, `pl.analysis`, all 11 modules after Get demands, `sa.girder1`): builtin, util, builtin28 (all supports 28°), xsA, curb × AASHTO, MassDOT, CTDOT (15 cases): **all sections identical**, no console errors.
- **RIDOT:** builtin (15°), util (15°), xsA (15°), curb (15°): **all sections identical** (RIDOT ≤ 20° unchanged). builtin28 and the 30° simple span: differences limited to the layout and what it feeds (`pl.checks` X1 text, X2/X3/X4/X5; `pl.analysis` DC1; GS, CF, OH, FA, TS, SC, WT, BSTF, splice items; Structural analysis girder 1 forces through the DC1 point-load positions; the stored demands in `gd.project`); no module check changes status; no console errors.
- Screenshots (session scratchpad, viewed): framing plan + Framing tab + X1 for the RIDOT 30° simple span with 6 girders and for builtin28; DXF framing plan sheet (rendered with ezdxf, audit 0 errors; layer XFRM-LINE 4 lines, CL ROADWAY, W.P., 5@24'-0" along CL roadway); 3D view.

### Open items
- **Exterior girders at the piers (case 2):** frames on one side only give pier panels of s_c + S·tan θ/2 (24.53 ft at 28°); GS7 at the exterior piers, already failing on main under RIDOT 28°, goes 1.108 → 1.181. Engineer to decide whether RIDOT expects closer lines near piers (s_p) by default.
- **X3:** at the usual 8–10 ft girder spacing and 20–32° skews the step S·tan θ (2.9–6.3 ft) is below 4b_f for 18 in flanges, so X3 warns on every RIDOT > 20° bridge of that kind. Kept per the engineer's instruction; confirm whether RIDOT's standard detail accepts it (C6.7.4.2.1 4b_f is a recommendation) or X3 should cite the standard instead.
- **Orientation set by hand under RIDOT > 20°:** cannot produce the stepped pattern (the "Normal frames" options are contiguous / staggered), so X1 fails; a "stepped" option was not added (UI and saved-value change: ask).
- **℄ roadway = centerline of the girder layout** (the tool's support-line reference). With unequal overhangs/edges the true roadway centerline is offset; no input for it (ask whether needed).
- **Unequal skews within a span:** the lines are interpolated between the two bearing lines (as parallel frames), so they are parallel to the bearings only when both skews are equal; the sheet shows equal skews.
- **Pier regions with s_p:** some panels slightly over s_p in mixed-skew / 55° cases (sweep above); corner frames cannot be placed d_min from the stepped frames there.

## 2026-10-19 — PR: claude/ridot-xf-followups (follow-ups to #307, RXF: X3 under the RIDOT stepped layout; "Stepped (RIDOT standard)" Normal frames option; engineer decisions 2026-10-19; PR link added after merge)

Engineer's decisions on the RXF open items (2026-10-19): (2) X3 under RIDOT's stepped layout reports the offset and passes, citing the RIDOT standard framing plan (skew > 20°) instead of the 4b_f recommendation; other owners and arrangements unchanged. (1) Pier s_p default: no change. (3) Add a "Stepped (RIDOT standard)" option to the Normal frames arrangement menu: by hand it gives the same stepped layout for any owner, and X1 under RIDOT > 20° passes with it. (4)–(6): left as logged in RXF.

### RXF3. Check X3 under RIDOT stepped spans   [CHECK CHANGE — §4 callout: X3 status warn → pass, RIDOT stepped only]
- **Where (Preliminary sizing page):** `framingChecks`, X3 block (anchor `// RIDOT stepped (engineer's decision 2026-10-19): in a span with the stepped arrangement under owner RIDOT`).
- **Before:** every pair of frames on opposite sides of an interior girder: d = 0 or d ≥ d_min = max(min. offset, 4b_f), else **warn** (AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. C6.7.4.2.1 4b_f; practice). Under RIDOT > 20° (stepped, #307) d = S·tan θ (5.05 ft at 9.5 ft / 28°, 5.48 ft at 30°) < 6.00 ft → warn on every interior girder.
- **After:** `rS(k)` = owner RIDOT and span k normal with arrangement `'stepped'` (Automatic above 20°, or the new option by hand). Pairs whose frame is in such a span are not compared with d_min: per girder the smallest of those offsets is reported (cells: d, station, "RIDOT standard"), status **pass**, work "d = … ft: step of the RIDOT standard framing plan (skew > 20°), accepted". Ref gains "; RIDOT standard framing plan for skew greater than 20° (stepped spans)", src DOT, symbolic line and note say so. A girder with pairs in other spans is checked as before (those pairs only). Other owners (also with the stepped option by hand) and other arrangements: unchanged.
- **Governing:** RIDOT standard framing plan for skew greater than 20° (intermediate diaphragm lines parallel to ℄ of bearings; the step between bays is the standard's geometry), RIDOT BDM 6.4.3; AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. C6.7.4.2.1 (4b_f is a recommendation, "should").
- **Check case:** built-in, all supports 28°, RIDOT: X3 G2 / G3 / G4 d = 9.5 × tan 28° = 9.5 × 0.53171 = **5.05 ft** < d_min = max(4.00, 4 × 18/12) = 6.00 ft → before **warn** (r 1.19); after **pass**, "5.05 | 154.14 | RIDOT standard" (same offsets and stations). Simple span 30°, 6 girders: 5.48 ft, warn → pass (G2–G5). No other check or result changes.

### RXF4. Normal frames option "Stepped (RIDOT standard)"   [NEW OPTION — layout change only where someone picks it; new saved value]
- **Where:** Framing tab field `framing.arrange` (anchor `['stepped', 'Stepped (RIDOT standard)']`). `framingLayout` already passed `F.arrange` to `normSpan`, whose `stp = arr === 'stepped'` (RXF1) produces the stepped layout, so no layout code changed.
- **Before:** options Contiguous lines / Staggered by bay. **After:** plus Stepped (RIDOT standard). Picked by hand, every normal span (Orientation Normal, or Automatic where a span is normal under an owner without the xf.orient rule or by AASHTO's per-span rule) is laid out stepped, for any owner. Under RIDOT with θ_max > 20° it conforms (X1 pass, Framing tab "The orientation set here conforms"), as `o.arr === ox.arr`; the X1 RIDOT note now says so ("set by hand, Orientation Normal with Normal frames "Stepped (RIDOT standard)" conforms, any other setting fails"). Under CTDOT > 20° it does not conform (staggered required), as before for contiguous.
- **Help:** Limits tab row "Orientation, arrangement" and the Framing method paragraph "RIDOT, largest support skew over 20°" mention the option and the X3 treatment.

### Saved data
- New value `framing.arrange = 'stepped'` only when picked; default and existing projects unchanged (`'contiguous'` / `'staggered'`). A project saved with it, opened by main as of #307: same layout (its `normSpan` already reads `'stepped'`), X3 warns (RXF3 absent), the select has no matching option. Opened by a build before #307: laid out contiguous (unknown value is not 'staggered'), no error.

### How verified
- `node tests/check-syntax.mjs "Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html"`: all scripts pass.
- `framingLayout` + framing checks sweep, origin/main (6e641a1, #307) vs branch, 4,928 configurations (owners AASHTO / MassDOT / CTDOT / RIDOT × 11 skew sets × contiguous / staggered / stepped × auto / normal / parallel × s 20 / 25 × 3 / 5 girders × continuous / simple × s_p none / 15): **frames identical in all 4,928**. Checks differ only in X3 of RIDOT configurations with stepped normal spans (560: warn → pass in 472, pass → pass with the new text in 88). On the branch, Orientation Normal + Stepped by hand gives frames identical to Automatic RIDOT > 20° in all 512 matching configurations (every owner); X1 with RIDOT + Normal + Stepped: pass in all 128 configurations with θ_max > 20° (fail at ≤ 20°, parallel required, as before).
- `node tests/compare.mjs --tool gd`: builtin, util, builtin28 × AASHTO, MassDOT, CTDOT (9 cases): **all sections identical**. RIDOT: builtin (15°): all sections identical (a first run showed a `gd.project` key-order difference only, `std` / `ownDefG` insertion order, values identical; the re-run is identical). builtin28 (28°) and the 30° simple span with 6 girders: the **only** differences are X3 in `pl.checks` (status warn → pass, items warn → pass, r 1.19 / 1.09 → 0, d_min cell 6.00 → "RIDOT standard"); every module, the analysis and the projects identical. No console errors. UI (headless): the select lists Contiguous lines / Staggered by bay / Stepped (RIDOT standard); picking Normal + Stepped on the built-in at 28° under RIDOT gives frames identical to Automatic, X1 pass, X3 pass, the Framing tab line "The orientation set here conforms", and the autosave holds `framing.arrange: "stepped"`.
- Manual contiguous / staggered: unchanged (sweep; only RIDOT stepped spans enter RXF3).

## 2026-10-19 — PR: claude/gd-superreactions (SRX: steel girder reactions for Bridge Substructure Loading from GirderDetail; engineer decision 2026-10-19; cross-tool PR with Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html, Bridge Substructure Loading.html, HANDOFF.md §4.4, AUDIT.md, tools.html, ENGINEER_CHECKS GD72; PR link added after merge)

### SRX. "Send reactions to Substructure Loading" (superReactions sender)   [NEW HAND-OFF — no GirderDetail result changes; §4 callout for the receiver's values, below]
- **Engineer decision (2026-10-19):** ST-Girder no longer sends bearing reactions to Bridge Substructure Loading (#309/#310); steel girder reactions come from GirderDetail, which has the full continuous staged analysis.
- **Where:** Structural analysis, "Girder and model" tab, new section "Send reactions to Substructure Loading" after "Send to ST-Girder" (pane anchor `${secHd('sec-sasr', 'Send reactions to Substructure Loading')}`). New code after `gdStHref` (anchor `const GD_SR = { ch: 'superReactions'`): `gdSrUi()`, `gdSrPayload()` and a click handler (`[data-gdsr]`). The owner-rules object of the ST-Girder hand-off moved unchanged from an inline IIFE in `gdStPayload` into `gdOwnerRulesData()` (anchor `function gdOwnerRulesData()`), called by both hand-offs.
- **What it sends (HANDOFF.md §4.4, schema `bridge-super-reactions` v1 unchanged):** on click only, `GM.sa.compute({ ...P.sa, girder: g })` for every girder g = 1…n (the Structural analysis itself, with its model settings: staged variable stiffness or constant EI), and from each run `R.reac` (the Reactions card): per support (`Abut. 1`, `Pier k`, `Abut. 2`, x in ft) and per girder (`G1`…`Gn`, position) the unfactored DC1, DC2, DW in kip. `factored:false`, `imIncluded:false`, `dfIncluded:false`, `perGirder:true`, `liveLoad:null`, `span:{ index:null, length }`, `project` from the project title block. New optional fields (additive, §5): `allGirders:true` and `ownerRules` (the §4.9 object). The notes list what the schema cannot carry: LL+IM per girder (max / min), the pedestrian load, the MassDOT utilities (UT, UF; not in DC1/DC2/DW), the owner load rules in words, manual DFs, simple-span piers. Written with `BridgeXfer.publish` (key + `updatedAt`), then the copy `bridgeSuite.v1.superReactions.by.girderdetail`; "Export hand-off (JSON)" writes the same payload to a file. An alert lists every value sent.
- **Choice of analysis:** Structural analysis runs per girder, so every girder is run (about 0.4 s each on the built-in) rather than Preliminary sizing's approximate whole-bridge analysis: the reactions are then exactly GirderDetail's own Structural analysis values for each girder, including its girder-specific dead load distribution (LLDF and DLs module) and cross-frame point loads. Manual distribution factors (`sa.dfSrc = 'manual'`) belong to the selected girder only, so the other girders run with the module's factors; this affects only the LL+IM listed in the notes.
- **Saved data:** none changed (no new key in GirderDetail's project; the hand-off keys are the existing channel). `P` is unchanged by a send (checked).
- **§4:** no GirderDetail formula, factor or result changes (`tests/compare.mjs --tool gd`: all sections identical). The values are new for the receiver: steel reactions now come from GirderDetail's continuous staged analysis instead of ST-Girder's copy (which, for a GirderDetail import, was the imported station shears at the two ends of one span). Built-in project as opened (owner MassDOT, 5 girders, spans 110 / 140 / 110 ft, kip):

| Support | G1 (exterior) DC1 / DC2 / DW | G2 (interior) DC1 / DC2 / DW | G3 (interior) DC2 | G1 LL+IM max / min | G2 LL+IM max / min |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Abut. 1 (x = 0) | 44.008 / 13.467 / 8.194 | 52.639 / 9.896 / 8.197 | 6.320 | 99.90 / −15.07 | 113.14 / −17.07 |
| Pier 1 (x = 110) | 164.139 / 47.922 / 29.156 | 194.934 / 35.198 / 29.153 | 22.480 | 199.74 / −16.39 | 226.26 / −18.59 |
| Pier 2 (x = 250) | 164.175 / 47.922 / 29.156 | 194.971 / 35.198 / 29.153 | 22.480 | 199.74 / −16.39 | 226.26 / −18.59 |
| Abut. 2 (x = 360) | 44.021 / 13.467 / 8.194 | 52.652 / 9.896 / 8.197 | 6.320 | 99.90 / −15.07 | 113.14 / −17.07 |

  MassDOT utilities case (`tests/projects/gd/util.json`, owner MassDOT): DC1 / DC2 / DW identical to the table; in the notes, existing utilities UT on G2 and G3 (0.150 klf each): 5.85 kip at each abutment, 21.15 kip at each pier (2 × 5.85 + 2 × 21.15 = 54.0 = 0.150 × 360); future allowance UF (0.125 klf): 4.87 / 17.63 kip (sum 45.0 = 0.125 × 360). G1, G4, G5: none.
- **Hand check (built-in, G2 interior, Pier 1, DC2; staged model):** shear just left of the pier V_L = −17.536 kip, just right V_R = +17.412 kip (Structural analysis "Shears, unfactored", both sides of the pier), load on the pier node w·trib = 0.25053 klf × 1.0 ft = 0.251 kip: R = V_R − V_L + w·trib = 17.412 + 17.536 + 0.251 = **35.198 kip** = the sent value. Abut. 1: R = V + w·trib = 9.771 + 0.25053 × 0.5 = **9.896 kip**. Equilibrium: 2 × 9.896 + 2 × 35.198 = 90.19 kip = 0.25053 × 360 = 90.19 kip (check SA2).
- **Hand check (closed form, constant EI):** with the Structural analysis model set to "Constant EI" the same code gives DW (w = 0.2075 klf, every girder) 8.410 kip at the abutments and 28.940 kip at the piers. Three-moment equation, spans 110 / 140 / 110, symmetric: M₁(2(L₁ + L₂) + L₂) = −w(L₁³ + L₂³)/4 → M₁ = −w(1,331,000 + 2,744,000)/4/640 = −1591.8w; R₀ = wL₁/2 + M₁/L₁ = 55w − 14.471w = 40.529w = **8.410 kip**; R₁ = 180w − 40.529w = 139.471w = **28.940 kip**. The staged model (stiffer composite section over the piers) gives 8.194 / 29.156 kip, about 2.6% less at the abutments and 0.7% more at the piers.
- **How verified:** `node tests/check-syntax.mjs "Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html"`: all scripts pass. `node tests/compare.mjs --tool gd` (builtin / AASHTO): **all sections identical**, no console errors; also `--project util --owner MassDOT` and `--project xsA --owner RIDOT` (see the PR). `gdStPayload(1|2, true)` origin/main vs branch under AASHTO, RIDOT (m = 1.2) and MassDOT: identical (the `gdOwnerRulesData` move changes nothing). Headless end to end (built-in and util): Send → the channel key equals the `.by.girderdetail` copy, `updatedAt` = `producedAt`, `P` unchanged; Substructure Loading's Pull lists it, defaults to G1 → G1 … G5 → G5, Apply writes 60 values, every one equal to the payload. Screenshots of the button and of Substructure Loading after adopting (PR).
- **Other copies:** `BridgeXfer` is used as is (not changed). The Substructure Loading side is in `fixlog/Bridge Substructure Loading.md` SRX.
- **Open items:** ENGINEER_CHECKS GD72: (a) utilities are in the notes only (no schema field; SubLoads does not carry them); (b) owner rules sent for information, not applied by SubLoads; (c) the by-number default.

- **Engineer decision GD72a (2026-10-19):** carry the MassDOT utilities into Substructure Loading as loads.

## 2026-10-19 — PR: claude/aashto10-gd (AASHTO10-SC: shear connectors to AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. — Q_n, φ_sc, stud fatigue Z_r, h/d; splice references and bearing stiffener comment relabelled; PR link added after merge)

Engineer decision 2026-10-19 ("follow the owner"; the engineering calculation follows the 10th Ed., owner rules stay on top). Every factor and equation below was checked against the AASHTO LRFD BDS 10th Ed. (2024) text (articles cited only).

### AASHTO10-SC1. Stud nominal shear resistance Q_n and φ_sc   [CALCULATION CHANGE — Q_r lower; more conservative]
- **Where:** `GM.sc.compute` (anchor `QnE = 0.70 * Asc * g('Fu')`), check SC2 `sym` / `note` (anchor `Q_r = \phi_{sc}Q_n`), the Deck and studs input `sc.Qn10` (label and note only; key unchanged), help page p14 (Strength, Verification).
- **Before:** `Qn1 = 0.5·A_sc·√(f′c·E_c)`, `Qn9 = min(Qn1, A_sc·F_u)`, `Qn = Qn10 > 0 ? Qn10 : Qn9`, `Qr = 0.85·Qn` (9th Ed. form; E_c = 120,000·K1·w_c²·f′c^0.33 used only here).
- **After:** `QnE = 0.70·A_sc·F_u` (Eq. 6.10.10.4.3-1), `Qn = Qn10 > 0 ? Qn10 : QnE`, `phiSc = 1.00` (6.5.4.2), `Qr = phiSc·Qn`. E_c, Qn1, Qn9 removed from the module result (nothing else read them; the modular ratio still comes from `modRatio`).
- **Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5):** the key `sc.Qn10` is kept. Its meaning: 0 = the equation (was the 9th Ed. equation, now the 10th); above 0 = Q_n entered by the user, used instead (as before). A saved project with a Q_n entered keeps it; its Q_r is now 1.00·Q_n (was 0.85·Q_n) — that value was meant to be the 10th Ed. Q_n, which goes with φ_sc = 1.00.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.10.10.4.3, Eq. 6.10.10.4.3-1; Art. 6.5.4.2 (φ_sc = 1.00).
- **Check case (7/8 in stud, F_u = 60 ksi, f′c = 4 ksi, module defaults: w_c = 0.150 kcf, K1 = 1.0):** A_sc = π(0.875)²/4 = 0.6013 in².
  - Before: E_c = 120,000(1.0)(0.150)²(4)^0.33 = 4,266 ksi; 0.5(0.6013)√(4 × 4,266) = 39.27 kip; A_scF_u = 36.08 kip → Q_n = 36.08 kip; Q_r = 0.85 × 36.08 = 30.67 kip. Default region P = 3,100.8 kip → n = 3,100.8/30.67 = 101.11 studs.
  - After: Q_n = 0.70(0.6013)(60) = 25.26 kip; Q_r = 1.00 × 25.26 = 25.26 kip; n = 3,100.8/25.26 = 122.78 studs (+21.4 %).
  - Tool (headless, module defaults): before Q_r 30.6673, n 101.11; after Q_n = Q_r = 25.2555, n = 122.78 ✓.
  - Note: for f′c = 4 ksi the old concrete term (39.27) did not govern, so the change is 0.85·A_scF_u → 0.70·A_scF_u, Q_r × 0.824.

### AASHTO10-SC2. Stud fatigue resistance Z_r, Fatigue II and the Fatigue I/II threshold   [CALCULATION CHANGE — larger Fatigue II Z_r; threshold moves from ≈1,087 to 11,322 trucks/day; less conservative where a zone changes from Fatigue I to II]
- **Where:** `gdFatStud` and the new constant `FA_STUD` (anchor `const FA_STUD = { A: 1040e8, m: 5, th: 7.0 };`), its header comment; check SC1 `sym`, `note` and the Z_r row (anchor `Fatigue II, (ΔF)<sub>n</sub>A<sub>sc</sub>`); the Fatigue note on the Deck and studs tab; help page p14 (Fatigue).
- **Before:** `aEq = ZrI/d²·γII/γI; eq = 10^((34.5 − aEq)/4.28)/(365·life·n)`; Fatigue II `Z_r = max(34.5 − 4.28·log10 N, 0)·d²` (9th Ed. α form).
- **After:** Condition 9.2 of Table 6.6.1.2.3-1 (A = 1040 × 10⁸ ksi⁵, m = 5, (ΔF)_TH = 7.0 ksi): `eq = A·(γI/(γII·(ΔF)_TH))^5/(365·life·n)`; Fatigue II `(ΔF)_n = (A/N)^(1/5)` (Eq. 6.6.1.2.5-2), `Z_r = (ΔF)_n·A_sc` (Eq. 6.10.10.2-1). Fatigue I unchanged (`Z_r = 7.0·A_sc`, already 10th Ed.). Same structure as `gdFatLS` for the other categories (m = 3 there).
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.10.10.2, Eq. 6.10.10.2-1; Art. 6.6.1.2.5, Eq. 6.6.1.2.5-1 to -3; Table 6.6.1.2.3-1 Condition 9.2 (its 75-year ADTT_SL equivalent to infinite life, 11,320, is reproduced by the formula: 1040 × 10⁸ × (1.75/(0.80 × 7.0))⁵/(365 × 75) = 11,322).
- **Check case (7/8 in stud, n = 1, ADTT = 2,000, p = 0.85 → ADTT_SL = 1,700, 75 years, γ_I = 1.75, γ_II = 0.80; module default zone 1: 3 studs per row, V_f = 38 kip, Q = 1,627.58 in³, I = 99,485 in⁴):**
  - N = 365 × 75 × 1 × 1,700 = 46,537,500.
  - Threshold: before log N_eq = (34.5 − 5.498 × 0.80/1.75)/4.28 → 1,087 trucks/day → ADTT_SL 1,700 ≥ 1,087: Fatigue I. After: 11,322 trucks/day → 1,700 < 11,322: Fatigue II.
  - Before (Fatigue I governs): Z_r = 7.0 × 0.6013 = 4.21 kip, V_fat = 1.75(38)(1,627.58)/99,485 = 1.088 kip/in, max. pitch = 3(4.21)/1.088 = 11.61 in.
  - After (Fatigue II): (ΔF)_n = (1040 × 10⁸/46,537,500)^(1/5) = 2,234.7^0.2 = 4.676 ksi; Z_r = 4.676 × 0.6013 = 2.81 kip; V_fat = 0.80(38)(1,627.58)/99,485 = 0.497 kip/in; max. pitch = 3(2.81)/0.497 = 16.96 in.
  - Forced Fatigue II, before: α = 34.5 − 4.28 log(46,537,500) = 1.682, Z_r = 1.682(0.875)² = 1.29 kip, max. pitch 7.77 in; after 16.96 in.
  - Tool (headless): after Fatigue II, (ΔF)_n = 4.676, Z_r = 2.8116, max. pitch 16.96 (zone 2: 24.79) ✓; before as listed ✓.

### AASHTO10-SC3. Stud height-to-diameter ratio   [CALCULATION CHANGE — stricter]
- **Where:** check SC5 `sym` and the "Height-to-diameter ratio" item (anchor `cells: [f2(hd), '5.00']`); help page p14 (Detailing).
- **Before:** h/d ≥ 4.0. **After:** h/d ≥ 5.0 (normal weight concrete).
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.10.10.1.1 (5.0 in normal weight concrete, 7.0 in lightweight; the 0.70 factor of Eq. 6.10.10.4.3-1 relies on these ratios, C6.10.10.4.3). The tool has no lightweight concrete option: the 7.0 limit is not checked (open item).
- **Check case:** 7/8 in × 4 in stud: 4/0.875 = 4.57 — before passes (≥ 4.0), after fails (< 5.0); Auto-design then picks h = 5 in (5.71 ≥ 5.0). Default 7/8 × 6 in: 6.86 passes both.

### AASHTO10-SC4. Preliminary sizing stud pitch seed   [NUMERICAL — 0.04 %]
- **Where:** `detailExport` (Preliminary sizing page, anchor `d = 0.875, Zr = 7.0 * Math.PI * d * d / 4;`).
- **Before:** `Zr = 5.5 * d * d` (4.211 kip). **After:** `Zr = 7.0 * Math.PI * d * d / 4` (4.209 kip), Fatigue I Z_r = (ΔF)_TH A_sc of 6.10.10.2 / Condition 9.2 (10th Ed.). This only seeds the pitch zones sent to the Shear connectors module (rounded down to 0.5 in, then re-designed there); `pl.project` / `pl.checks` were identical in the compare.

### AASHTO10-SC5. Auto-design: strength pass respects the owner minimum pitch   [AUTO-DESIGN FIX — no check formula changed]
- **Where:** `AD.sc`, strength loop (anchor `// OWN22: owner minimum pitch, as in the fatigue search above (was 4d always)`).
- **Before:** `D(z.p) > Math.ceil(4 * d)`. **After:** `D(z.p) > Math.ceil((gdOwnR('stud') ? gdOwnR('stud').value.p : 4) * d)` (the floor the fatigue search a few lines above already uses).
- **Problem:** with the lower 10th Ed. Q_r the strength pass tightened two end zones of the built-in project under RIDOT to p = 5 in < 6d = 5.25 in (RIDOT BDM 6.5.3, OWN22), so Design all ended with SC3 failing. Without an owner stud rule (AASHTO, MassDOT, CTDOT) the floor is 4d as before (identical).
- **Check case (built-in, RIDOT):** before this fix SC3 fails at "Span 1, 0.9L to 1L" and "Span 3, 0L to 0.1L" (5.00 < 5.25); after it every SC check passes (SC2 largest ratio 0.98), stud count 5,375 (main 6,125).

### AASHTO10-L1. Labels (no result change)
- Bolted splice help page, References (anchor `<h3>References</h3><ol><li>AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 10th Edition, 2024, with the owner rules on top`): was "9th Edition, 2020 (confirm article and equation numbers against the edition adopted by the owner)"; now the 10th Ed. (2024) with the owner note, as the OWN_RULES statement.
- Bearing stiffener module header comment: "(AASHTO LRFD 9th Ed., 6.10.11.2)" → "(AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024), 6.10.11.2)". Checked against the 10th Ed. for plate stiffeners: b_t ≤ 0.48t_p√(E/F_ys) (Eq. 6.10.11.2.2-1), (R_sb)_r = φ_b·1.4·A_pn·F_ys with φ_b = 1.00 (Eq. 6.10.11.2.3-1/-2), P_r per 6.9.2.1 with F_ys, KL = 0.75D, 9t_w web strip (6.10.11.2.4) — as the module computes them. The 10th Ed. adds half-round bearing stiffeners (Eq. 6.10.11.2.2-2), which the module does not offer. See open item 3.

- **Owner rules:** the only stud rule in `OWN_RULES` is RIDOT `stud` (OWN22, BDM 6.5.3: 7/8 in studs, at least two across, h ≥ 5 in, pitch ≥ 6d, SC3/SC7). It is detailing only, not Q_n, φ_sc or Z_r, and is kept unchanged. No MassDOT or CTDOT rule overrides studs.
- **How verified:** `node tests/check-syntax.mjs "Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html"`: pass. Headless hand check (module defaults, 7/8 in, F_u = 60 ksi, f′c = 4 ksi) on origin/main and on the branch: the values listed above. `node tests/compare.mjs --tool gd` (builtin / AASHTO): only `gd.project` (the `sc` inputs re-sized by Auto-design: h 4 → 5 in, zone pitches and studs per row; `designAll` stud count 6,065 → 5,625, cost; `_adUndo.sc`) and `mod.sc` differ; every other section identical. Built-in project (f′c = 5 ksi): region "Abut. 1 to max. positive, Span 1" P = 3,187.5 kip, required n 103.94 → 126.21 (= 3,187.5/30.667 → 3,187.5/25.255 ✓); every SC1 zone Fatigue I → Fatigue II (ADTT_SL 1,700 < 11,322). `--owner RIDOT,CTDOT` (after SC5): the same two sections differ and nothing else (RIDOT also `plSync.sig`, `_imp.sc` bookkeeping); every SC check passes on both sides under RIDOT and CTDOT; RIDOT SC3 (6d) and SC7 unchanged in form.
- **Hand-off:** `bridgeSuite.v1.girderDemands` unchanged (it sends the stud inputs d, h, F_u, spacing and zones only).
- **Other copies:** ST-Girder (`stgirder.html`) has its own stud Q_n / φ_sc / Z_r code; it is being fixed in a separate PR (not touched here).
- **Open items:**
  1. Lightweight concrete: 6.10.10.1.1 requires h/d ≥ 7.0; the module has no lightweight option (normal weight assumed). Add one?
  2. `sc.Qn10` ("Q_n entered") stays as an override. Keep it, or retire it now that the 10th Ed. equation is built in?
  3. Bearing stiffeners (not changed): the web strip is reduced by F_yw/F_ys only when F_yw < 0.7F_ys (`r.red`, also in Preliminary sizing's bearing stiffener check and help p11); 6.10.11.2.4b (10th Ed.) reduces it whenever F_yw < F_ys, and separately leaves the strip out at interior supports of continuous hybrid members with F_yw < 0.7 F_y of the higher-strength flange (not modelled). Unconservative e.g. for a 50 ksi web with HPS 70W stiffeners.
  4. Cycles per truck passage n (`gdFatN`, Fatigue module, used by SC1): the tool cites "Table 6.6.1.2.5-2" with 2.0 for spans ≤ 40 ft; in the 10th Ed. it is Table 6.6.1.2.5-1 and longitudinal members have no 40 ft row (simple 1.0; continuous 1.5 near interior supports, 1.0 elsewhere; cantilever 5.0). Not changed here (Fatigue module, all categories).
