## 2026-10-19 — PR: claude/aashto10-gd-2 (AASHTO10-GD2: bearing stiffener web strip and cycles per truck passage to AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed.; lightweight h/d note; follow-up to #338; PR link added after merge)

Engineer instruction 2026-10-19 (after #338): keep the "Q_n entered" override (`sc.Qn10`); no lightweight concrete option, a note only; fix the bearing stiffener web strip and the cycles per truck passage to the 10th Ed. Both provisions were checked against the AASHTO LRFD BDS 10th Ed. (2024) text (articles cited only).

### AASHTO10-GD2a. Bearing stiffener web strip reduction F_yw/F_ys   [CALCULATION CHANGE — more conservative; tiny effect]
- **Where:** `bsCompute` (Bearing stiffeners module, anchor `r.red = Fyw < Fys ? Fyw / Fys : 1.0;`), its BS3 note (anchor `because F_yw < F_ys (6.10.11.2.4b)`), the `r.AwS` comment; Preliminary sizing check A4 (anchor `const red = Fyw < Fys ? Fyw / Fys : 1.0, noW = hyb && !end`) and its note; help page p11.
- **Before:** `red = Fyw < 0.7 * Fys ? Fyw / Fys : 1.0` (module and A4). **After:** `red = Fyw < Fys ? Fyw / Fys : 1.0`.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.10.11.2.4b (the strip is reduced by F_yw/F_ys whenever F_yw < F_ys; the 0.7 ratio belongs to the separate hybrid rule below).
- **Effect:** P_o is unchanged (the reduced strip is already counted at F_ys, the "single reduction"; before, the unreduced strip was counted at F_yw: same force). A_g falls and r_s rises, but P_e = π²EA_g/(KL/r_s)² = π²EI/(KL)² changes only through the web-strip term of I. The axial resistance falls by a few thousandths of a kip. Only F_yw between 0.7F_ys and F_ys is affected: with this tool's grades, a Grade 50/50W/HPS 50W web with HPS 70W stiffeners (50 ≥ 0.7 × 70 = 49), or a Grade 36 web with Grade 50 stiffeners (36 ≥ 35).
- **Check case (module defaults, `BS_DEFAULT`, stiffeners HPS 70W, web 50W; Abut. 1: t_w = 0.5625 in, one pair 7 × 0.875 in, D = 60 in):**
  - F_yw/F_ys = 50/70 = 0.714; strip = 9(0.5625)(0.714) = 3.616 in (was 5.063 in); L_w = 7.232 in (was 10.125 in).
  - A_g = 18.438 → 16.810 in²; I = 225.333 → 225.290 in⁴; KL/r_s = 12.87 → 12.29.
  - P_o = 1,176.72 kip (both); P_e = 31,849 → 31,843 kip; P_r = φ_cP_n = 1,100.729 → 1,100.726 kip (R_u = 267.5 kip). Pier 1: P_r 2,735.915 → 2,735.914 kip.
  - Tool (headless): the values above, from `bsCompute` on origin/main and on the branch ✓.

### AASHTO10-GD2b. Hybrid girders: no web strip at interior supports   [CALCULATION CHANGE — Preliminary sizing A4; note in the module]
- **Where:** Preliminary sizing A4 (anchor `hyb = !!m.cont && nS > 2 && Fyw < 0.7 * Fyf`; `noW = hyb && !end, strip9 = noW ? 0 : 9 * tw * red`), A4 note; Bearing stiffeners BS3 note and help p11 (module: note only).
- **Before:** the web strip was always included. **After (A4):** at interior supports of a continuous girder whose web F_yw < 0.7F_yf (F_yf = the flange grade `m.gF`, one grade for both flanges in Preliminary sizing), the effective column is the stiffener elements only (L_w = 0). The module (`bsCompute`) has no flange grade and no continuity flag, so it is not applied there; BS3's note and help p11 say to check that case by hand.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 6.10.11.2.4b.
- **When it applies:** with this tool's grades only a Grade 36 web with HPS 70W flanges (36 < 0.7 × 70 = 49).
- **Check case (built-in project in Preliminary sizing, web Grade 36, flanges HPS 70W, stiffeners Grade 50, one pair 7 × 1 in, t_w = 0.5625 in, D = 60 in; Pier 1, interior girder, R_u = 727.71 kip):**
  - Before: L_w = 10.13 in; A = 14 + 0.5625 + 10.125(0.5625) = 20.26 in²; P_o = 50(14.5625) + 36(5.695) = 933.2 kip; KL/r = 12.62; P_r = 877.04 kip; ratio 0.83.
  - After: L_w = 0; A = 2(7)(1) + 1(0.5625) = 14.5625 in²; I = 1(1)(2 × 7 + 0.5625)³/12 = 257.35 in⁴; r_s = √(257.35/14.5625) = 4.204 in; KL/r = 0.75(60)/4.204 = 10.70; P_o = 50(14.5625) = 728.1 kip; P_e = π²(29,000)(14.5625)/10.70² = 36,400 kip; P_n = 0.658^(0.020)(728.1) = 722.0 kip; P_r = 0.95(722.0) = 685.9 kip; ratio 727.71/685.95 = **1.06 (fails)**.
  - Abutments (same girder): strip reduced by 36/50 = 0.72 (3.65 in, was 5.06 in): P_r 877.04 → 877.03 kip (GD2a).
  - Tool (headless, A4): Pier 1 interior 14.56 in², KL/r 10.70, P_r 685.95, ratio 1.06; Abut. 1 18.66 in², P_r 877.03 ✓.

### AASHTO10-GD2c. Cycles per truck passage n   [CALCULATION CHANGE — less conservative in spans ≤ 40 ft; more conservative next to the longer span at an interior support]
- **Where:** `gdFatN` and new `gdFatNear` (anchor `const gdFatNear = (x, xs, Lb, La) =>`), header comment of the fatigue helpers; Preliminary sizing `fatN` (flange fatigue, anchor `const fatN = x => { if (cont && supX.length > 2)`) and `nAt` (fatigue inventory sent to the Fatigue module, anchor `// Table 6.6.1.2.5-1, C6.6.1.2.5 (10th Ed.)`); `FA_SPEC` n option labels; the Fatigue help page (Details); every "Table 6.6.1.2.5-2" citation → "Table 6.6.1.2.5-1" (SC1 note, GS17 note and n row, Preliminary sizing fatigue note).
- **Before (9th Ed. Table 6.6.1.2.5-2):** n = 2.0 in any span of 40 ft or less (gdFatN, fatN); 1.5 within 0.1L of an interior support of a continuous girder with L = the shorter adjacent span on both sides (gdFatN, fatN, nAt); else 1.0.
- **After (10th Ed. Table 6.6.1.2.5-1, longitudinal members):** simple-span girders 1.0; continuous girders 1.5 near an interior support, 1.0 elsewhere; there is no span-length row. "Near" = within one-tenth of the span on each side of the interior support (C6.6.1.2.5), so the span on that side: x in [x_s − 0.1L_before, x_s + 0.1L_after]. Cantilever girders (5.0), orthotropic deck connections (5.0), trusses (1.0) and transverse members (cross-frames and diaphragms 1.0; floorbeams 1.0, or 2.0 when spaced ≤ 20 ft) are not modelled by these helpers (the tool designs plate girders; cross-frame fatigue is not checked with n).
- **Saved data:** the Fatigue module's n per detail is a selection with values '1', '1.5', '2' (unchanged; a saved 2.0 stays and is relabelled "entered; not a longitudinal-member value in Table 6.6.1.2.5-1"). Rows imported from Preliminary sizing take nAt (1.0 or 1.5 as before).
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Table 6.6.1.2.5-1 and C6.6.1.2.5; n enters N = 365(75)n(ADTT)_SL (Eq. 6.6.1.2.5-3).
- **Effect by category** (γ_I/γ_II = 1.75/0.80, 75 years): n 2.0 → 1.0 doubles the ADTT_SL above which Fatigue I applies, A(γ_I/(γ_II(ΔF)_TH))^m/(365 × 75 × n), and multiplies the Fatigue II resistance (A/N)^(1/m) by 2^(1/3) = 1.260 (m = 3) or 2^(1/5) = 1.149 (studs, m = 5). At ADTT_SL = 1,700:

| Category | Fatigue I where ADTT_SL ≥ (n = 2 → 1) | (ΔF)_n Fatigue II, ksi (n = 2 → 1) |
|---|---|---|
| A | 346 → 692 | 6.45 → 8.13 |
| B | 560 → 1,120 | 5.05 → 6.36 |
| B′ | 675 → 1,350 | 4.03 → 5.08 |
| C | 841 → 1,682 | 3.62 → 4.56 |
| C′ | 487 → 974 | 3.62 → 4.56 |
| D | 1,226 → 2,453 | 2.87 → 3.62 |
| E | 2,308 → 4,616 | 2.28 → 2.87 |
| E′ | 4,242 → 8,485 | 1.61 → 2.03 |
| Studs (Condition 9.2) | 5,661 → 11,322 | 4.07 → 4.68 (Z_r × 0.6013 in² for 7/8 in) |

  Where the near-support region grows (the longer adjacent span), n 1.0 → 1.5 multiplies (A/N)^(1/m) by 1.5^(−1/3) = 0.874 (studs 1.5^(−1/5) = 0.922) and divides the Fatigue I threshold by 1.5.
- **Check cases:**
  - `gdFatN`, spans 30 / 60 / 30 ft, continuous (headless): main n = 2.0 in both 30 ft spans, 1.5 within ±3 ft of each pier, 1.0 elsewhere in the 60 ft span; branch 1.0 in the 30 ft spans away from the piers, 1.5 from 27 to 36 ft and 84 to 93 ft (0.1 × 30 = 3 ft on the short side, 0.1 × 60 = 6 ft on the long side), 1.0 elsewhere ✓.
  - `gdFatN`, spans 100 / 140 / 100 ft: x = 113.9 and 114 ft: main 1.0 (±10 ft), branch 1.5 (0.1 × 140 = 14 ft) ✓.
  - Built-in project (spans 110 / 140 / 110 ft), Shear connectors zone "Span 2, 0.1L to 0.2L" (124 to 138 ft), ADTT_SL = 1,700, Fatigue II: the near region of Pier 1 on the Span 2 side is now 110 to 124 ft (was 110 to 121 ft), and the zone's first station is on its edge, so the zone takes n = 1.5 (largest n over the zone, inclusive edges, as before). N = 365(75)(1.5)(1,700) = 69,806,250; (ΔF)_n = (1040 × 10⁸/69,806,250)^(1/5) = 4.312 ksi; Z_r = 4.312(0.6013) = 2.593 kip (was 2.811 kip with n = 1); with 2 studs per row and V_sr = 0.628 kip/in, max. pitch = 2(2.593)/0.628 = 8.26 in ✓ (tool 8.26).

### AASHTO10-GD2d. Lightweight concrete note (no result change)
- **Where:** check SC5 (anchor `note: 'h/d ≥ 5.0 is the 6.10.10.1.1 limit for normal weight concrete`). One line: h/d ≥ 7.0 applies in lightweight concrete (AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.10.10.1.1); the module assumes normal weight concrete. No lightweight option was added and `sc.Qn10` is kept (engineer, 2026-10-19).

- **How verified:** `node tests/check-syntax.mjs "Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html"`: pass. Headless checks (`bsCompute`, `gdFatN`, Preliminary sizing A4) on origin/main and the branch: the values above. `node tests/compare.mjs --tool gd --project builtin,xsA,curb --owner AASHTO`: only `mod.sc` and the Shear connectors inputs Auto-design re-sizes (`gd.project.sc`, `_adUndo.sc`, `designAll` stud count) differ — zones 11 and 18 (Span 2, 0.1L to 0.2L and 0.8L to 0.9L) go from n = 1.0 to 1.5 because Span 2 (140 ft) is longer than Spans 1 and 3 (110 ft). Stud count: builtin 5,625 → 5,720; xsA 5,810 → 5,820; curb 5,565 → 5,485 (Auto-design picks a different stud arrangement). All other sections identical, including `pl.checks`, `mod.gs`, `mod.fa` and `mod.bstf` (no project here has a span ≤ 40 ft, F_yw < F_ys or a hybrid girder). All SC checks pass.
- **Other copies:** the three n rules in this file (gdFatN, Preliminary sizing fatN and nAt) are changed together; no other tool was changed.
- **Open items:**
  1. Edge inclusion: a stud pitch zone (and `gdFatNr` in general) takes n = 1.5 when only its end station touches the 0.1L limit (tolerance 1e-6, as before). Strict overlap would give 1.0 to such a zone. Keep the inclusive edge?
  2. The Bearing stiffeners module cannot apply the hybrid interior-support rule (no flange grade, no continuity); add those inputs if hybrid girders are used.

## 2026-10-22 — PR: claude/sbd-1-embed (SBD1: merge of GirderDetail and ST-Girder, PR 1: file renamed to Steel Bridge Design.html, ST-Girder embedded as the Design & Rating view; engineer decisions 2026-10-22; cross-tool rename approved, with tools.html, index, lldf, psbeam, Bridge Substructure Loading, Gusset Plate Rating, abutment_calculator, tests and docs; PR link added after merge)

**No engineering result changes.** No formula, load or resistance factor, unit or code reference was changed; no saved key or format was changed.
Verified with `tests/compare.mjs`: `--tool gd` against `tests/baselines/gd.json` (PR 0), `--tool sbd` (the view vs `stgirder.html`), and
`tests/sbd-verify.mjs` (redirect, saved data, view, printing). Results in the PR description.

### SBD1-a. File renamed; title, header and printed footer   [rename] [no result change]
- `git mv "Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html" "Steel Bridge Design.html"`; `git mv "fixlog/Steel Bridge Beam Modules.md" "fixlog/Steel Bridge Design.md"`.
- New `Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html`: a redirect page (no library, no storage access) that runs
  `location.replace('Steel%20Bridge%20Design.html' + location.search + location.hash)` and shows a link "Open Steel Bridge Design" (same target).
- `<title>`: before `<title>GirderDetail: Steel Girder Detail Design</title>`, after `<title>Steel Bridge Design</title>` (also the default print / PDF title).
- Header (anchor `<div class="brand-text"><span class="logo-name">`): before `GirderDetail`, after `Steel Bridge Design`.
- `crPageCSS()`, page footer: before `@bottom-left { content: "${crEsc(mt.name)}, ${crEsc(lbl)} (GirderDetail)";`,
  after `@bottom-left { content: "${crEsc(mt.name)}, ${crEsc(lbl)} (Steel Bridge Design)";`.
- File name strings (hand-off `producerFile`; HANDOFF.md §4.1, §4.4, §4.9):
  - shared project info block: before `var TOOL='Steel Bridge Beam Modules', FILE='Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html';`, after `var TOOL='Steel Bridge Design', FILE='Steel Bridge Design.html';`
  - `GD_ST` and `GD_SR`: `file: 'Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html'` → `file: 'Steel Bridge Design.html'`.
  No receiver checks GirderDetail's file name (they check `producer:"GirderDetail"`); payloads sent before keep the old name and read the same.
- **Check case:** open `Steel Bridge Beam Modules.html#gdtest=1` → the address becomes `Steel%20Bridge%20Design.html#gdtest=1`; tab title "Steel Bridge Design".

### SBD1-b. ST-Girder embedded verbatim (`st-src`)   [new] [no result change]
- **Where:** right after the `pl-src` block (anchor: the line `</script>` that closes `<script type="text/plain" id="pl-src">`, followed by
  `<script>` and `GirderDetail: bolted field splice engine`). Added an HTML comment and `<script type="text/plain" id="st-src">…</script>` holding
  `stgirder.html` exactly as it is in this commit, escaped as `pl-src` (PLSRC): every `<` followed by zero or more backslashes and then `/script` or
  `!--` (any case) gets one more backslash after the `<`. Re-apply (any later change to stgirder.html too) with:
  `src.replace(/<(\\*)(\/script|!--)/gi, '<\\$1$2')` on the file text, then check that `stSrc()` (below) returns the file unchanged.
- `tests/check-syntax.mjs` now also checks `st-src` (transpiled with the offline Babel).

### SBD1-c. Design & Rating (ST-Girder) view   [new] [no result change]
- **CSS** (after the anchor `@media print { body.mod-pl * { visibility: hidden; } }`):
  ```css
  /* SBD1 (2026-10-22): Design & Rating (ST-Girder) view, the embedded ST-Girder frame shown over the modules (stShow) */
  ```

- **HTML:** after `<div id="pl-wrap"></div>`: `<div id="st-wrap"><div id="st-bar"></div><div id="st-frame-box"></div></div>`.
- **Module tabs** (`gmInitDom`): the Girder group gets a third tab: before `${grp('Girder', [['gs', 'Girder section'], ['fa', 'Fatigue']])}`,
  after `${grp('Girder', [['gs', 'Girder section'], ['fa', 'Fatigue'], ['st', 'Design & Rating (ST-Girder)']])}`. In the `#modbar` click and
  keydown handlers `setMod(b.dataset.mod)` / `setMod(n.dataset.mod)` → `gdModGo(b.dataset.mod)` / `gdModGo(n.dataset.mod)`. The view is not a
  module: `P.mod` and the saved project never hold `'st'`.
- **`applyMod()`**: before
  `document.querySelectorAll('.mtab').forEach(b => { const on = b.dataset.mod === P.mod; …`, after
  `const stv = document.body.classList.contains('mod-st'); document.querySelectorAll('.mtab').forEach(b => { const on = stv ? b.dataset.mod === 'st' : b.dataset.mod === P.mod; …`
  (the view's tab stays selected when a recompute runs under it).
- **`openReport()`**: added at its start `if (document.body.classList.contains('mod-st')) { stReport(); return; }` (Print report in the view opens
  ST-Girder's Report tab, whose "Print this report" prints the frame).
- **Host code**, inserted after the anchor
  `window.addEventListener('resize', () => { if (P && P.mod === 'pl') $('#pl-wrap').style.top = …` (end of the Preliminary sizing frame code), exactly:
  ```js
/* ---------- Design & Rating (ST-Girder), embedded (SBD1, 2026-10-22; merge of GirderDetail and ST-Girder, PR 1) ----------
   ST-Girder (stgirder.html) is stored verbatim as plain text in <script type="text/plain" id="st-src"> (same escaping rule as pl-src, plSrc)
   and loaded on first use into a srcdoc frame named "gd-st" (ST_FRAME), shown by the module tab "Design & Rating (ST-Girder)" in the Girder
   group. The view is not a module: P.mod and the saved project do not change when it is shown (body class mod-st only). A srcdoc frame has this
   page's origin, so ST-Girder reads and writes its own saved keys (stgirder.session, stgirder.ui.v1, stgirder.inputTab.v1, ...) exactly as the
   stand-alone file does: a session saved there opens here, and the reverse.
   Host info: window.GD_ST_HOST { embedded, file, href, host } is placed before ST-Girder's scripts (as window.GD_OWN_RULES for Preliminary sizing).
   Shims (ST_SHIMS, applied to the text when the frame is built; each anchor must occur exactly once, else the frame is not loaded):
   - the app-path record (appPaths 'stgirder') and BridgeXfer.stamp use this file's name and folder, not the frame's about:srcdoc;
   - in place of the #gdpull open-now flag, the hand-off arrives by message { type: 'gd-st-pull', id, payload } from this page only (source and
     origin checked) and goes through ST-Girder's own gdAdopt(p, 'opened from GirderDetail', true), the path #gdpull uses, so every input and
     result is the same as "Send to ST-Girder" + "Open ST-Girder now"; the frame answers { type: 'gd-st-applied', id, ok, producedAt } once the

let ST_FRAME = null, ST_READY = false, ST_Q = [], ST_N = 0;
const ST_WAIT = new Map();   // message id -> { res, rej, payload }
const ST_SHIMS = [
  ["var last=(location.pathname||'').split('/').pop()||'';", "var last=(window.GD_ST_HOST&&GD_ST_HOST.file)||(location.pathname||'').split('/').pop()||'';"],
  ["var h=String(location.href||'').split('#')[0].split('?')[0];", "var h=String((window.GD_ST_HOST&&GD_ST_HOST.href)||location.href||'').split('#')[0].split('?')[0];"],
  ["p.producerFile = p.producerFile || producerFile || decodeURIComponent((location.pathname.split('/').pop()||''));", "p.producerFile = p.producerFile || producerFile || (window.GD_ST_HOST&&GD_ST_HOST.file) || decodeURIComponent((location.pathname.split('/').pop()||''));"],
  ["gdAdopt(r.payload,'opened from GirderDetail',true); },[gdPullReq]);", `gdAdopt(r.payload,'opened from GirderDetail',true); },[gdPullReq]);
  /* SBD1 shim (added by Steel Bridge Design when it loads ST-Girder into its frame; not in stgirder.html): the hand-off by message from the host page */
  const gdAdoptRef=useRef(null); gdAdoptRef.current=gdAdopt;
  const gdHostQ=useRef(null);
  useEffect(()=>{ const H=window.GD_ST_HOST; if(!H||!H.embedded||window.parent===window) return;
    const to=self.origin==='null'?'*':self.origin;
    const h=e=>{ if(e.source!==window.parent||e.origin!==self.origin) return; const d=e.data; if(!d||d.type!=='gd-st-pull') return;
      const p=d.payload, done=(ok,why)=>{ try{ window.parent.postMessage({type:'gd-st-applied',id:d.id,ok:ok,why:why||'',producedAt:(p&&p.producedAt)||''},to); }catch(er){} };
      const bad=!window.BridgeXfer?'The hand-off helper is not available in this browser.':BridgeXfer.validate(p,GD_SCHEMA,1)||(!extFromGD(p)?'The hand-off is not from GirderDetail.':'');
      if(bad){ setGdAuto({ok:false,text:'The hand-off from GirderDetail cannot be used: '+bad+' Nothing was changed.'}); done(false,bad); return; }
      gdHostQ.current={pa:p.producedAt,done:done};

    return ()=>window.removeEventListener('message',h); },[]);
  useEffect(()=>{ const q=gdHostQ.current; if(q&&inp.external&&inp.external.producedAt===q.pa){ gdHostQ.current=null; q.done(true); } },[inp,gdAuto]);`]];
function stSrc() { return document.getElementById('st-src').textContent.replace(/<\\(\\*)(\/script|!--)/gi, '<$1$2'); }
const stTo = () => self.origin === 'null' ? '*' : self.origin;
const gdFromST = e => !!ST_FRAME && e.source === ST_FRAME.contentWindow && e.origin === self.origin;   // messages are accepted only from the ST-Girder frame
function stPos() { const w = $('#st-wrap'); if (w) w.style.top = Math.ceil($('#modbar').getBoundingClientRect().bottom) + 'px'; }
function stEnsure() {
  if (ST_FRAME) return true;
  let src = stSrc(); const miss = ST_SHIMS.filter(([a]) => src.split(a).length !== 2);
  if (miss.length) { console.error('Design & Rating (ST-Girder): the embedded page does not match its shims (' + miss.map(m => m[0].slice(0, 40)).join('; ') + ')'); stMsg('The embedded ST-Girder page could not be prepared (see the browser console). Nothing was changed.', 'fail'); return false; }
  ST_SHIMS.forEach(([a, b]) => { src = src.split(a).join(b); });
  let file = ''; try { file = decodeURIComponent((location.pathname || '').split('/').pop() || ''); } catch (e) { file = ''; }
  const host = { embedded: true, host: 'Steel Bridge Design', file: file || 'Steel Bridge Design.html', href: String(location.href || '').split('#')[0].split('?')[0] };
  const inj = `<script>window.GD_ST_HOST = ${JSON.stringify(host).replace(/</g, '\\u003c')};<\/script>`;   // SBD1: host info, before ST-Girder's scripts
  ST_FRAME = document.createElement('iframe'); ST_FRAME.name = 'gd-st'; ST_FRAME.id = 'st-frame'; ST_FRAME.title = 'Design & Rating (ST-Girder)';
  ST_FRAME.srcdoc = src.replace(/<head>/i, h => h + inj); $('#st-frame-box').appendChild(ST_FRAME);
  return true;
}
window.addEventListener('message', e => { if (!gdFromST(e) || !e.data) return; const d = e.data;
  if (d.type === 'gd-st-ready') { ST_READY = true; ST_Q.splice(0).forEach(m => ST_FRAME.contentWindow.postMessage(m, stTo())); return; }
  if (d.type === 'gd-st-applied') { const w = ST_WAIT.get(d.id); if (!w) return; ST_WAIT.delete(d.id);
    if (d.ok) { stMsg(`${w.payload.member.key} loaded into ST-Girder.`); w.res(w.payload); } else { stMsg(`${w.payload.member.key} was not loaded: ${d.why}`, 'fail'); w.rej(new Error(d.why || 'not applied')); } } });
function stPost(m) { if (ST_READY && ST_FRAME && ST_FRAME.contentWindow) ST_FRAME.contentWindow.postMessage(m, stTo()); else ST_Q.push(m); }
// the view: shown over the modules (P.mod unchanged); the module tabs show it as selected
function stShow() {
  stBar(); stPos(); stEnsure();   // when the frame cannot be prepared, stEnsure says so in the bar
  if (!stShow.ro && window.ResizeObserver) { stShow.ro = new ResizeObserver(stPos); stShow.ro.observe($('#gd-top')); }
  document.body.classList.add('mod-st');

}
function stHide() { if (!document.body.classList.contains('mod-st')) return; document.body.classList.remove('mod-st'); applyMod(); }
function gdModGo(m) { if (m === 'st') { stShow(); return; } stHide(); setMod(m); }

function stBar() {
  const el = $('#st-bar'), b = P && P.df && P.df.bridge, nb = b && b.ok ? b.nb : 0; if (!el) return;
  const cur = $('#st-g') ? +$('#st-g').value : Math.round(nm(P && P.sa && P.sa.girder)) || 1, pl = $('#st-pl') ? $('#st-pl').checked : true;
  const msg = $('#st-msg') ? $('#st-msg').textContent : '';
  el.innerHTML = nb ? `<label for="st-g">Girder</label><select id="st-g">${[...Array(nb)].map((_, i) => `<option value="${i + 1}"${i + 1 === Math.min(cur, nb) ? ' selected' : ''}>G${i + 1} (${i === 0 || i === nb - 1 ? 'exterior' : 'interior'})</option>`).join('')}</select>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-primary" id="st-load" title="Send this girder's Structural analysis results (the same hand-off as Send to ST-Girder) to ST-Girder below; it replaces ST-Girder's current girder inputs (Undo there restores them)">Load girder into ST-Girder</button>
    <span class="ck-row"><input type="checkbox" id="st-pl"${pl ? ' checked' : ''}><label for="st-pl">Pedestrian load (if any) in LL+IM</label></span>
    <span id="st-msg" role="status">${esc(msg || 'ST-Girder shows its own saved inputs until a girder is loaded.')}</span>`
    : `<span id="st-msg" role="status">Define the complete bridge in Preliminary sizing first to load a girder. ST-Girder below shows its own saved inputs.</span>`;
}
// send one girder's hand-off (already built and published) to the frame; resolves with the payload once ST-Girder has applied it
function stSend(pay) {
  pay = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(pay));   // exactly what a reader of the shared channel gets (stgirder.html's #gdpull path reads it back from storage)
  stShow(); if (!ST_FRAME) return Promise.reject(new Error('the ST-Girder frame is not available'));
  const sel = $('#st-g'), g = pay.girderDetail && pay.girderDetail.girder; if (sel && g) sel.value = String(g);
  const id = ++ST_N; stMsg(`Loading ${pay.member.key} into ST-Girder…`);
  return new Promise((res, rej) => { ST_WAIT.set(id, { res, rej, payload: pay }); stPost({ type: 'gd-st-pull', id, payload: pay }); });

// build girder g's hand-off (gdStPayload, as Send to ST-Girder), write it to the shared channel as before (stgirder.html's Pull still works), send it
function stLoad(g, addPL) {
  const r = gdStPayload(g, addPL); if (r.error) return Promise.reject(new Error(`Structural analysis: ${r.error}`));
  let pay = r.payload; try { const w = window.BridgeXfer ? BridgeXfer.publish(GD_ST.ch, r.payload, GD_ST.producer, GD_ST.file) : null; if (w && w.payload) pay = w.payload; } catch (e) { }
  return stSend(pay);
}
/* window.gdStOpen(g): for test scripts and headless checks (tests/compare.mjs --tool sbd) and the same path as the view's Load button:
   opens the view, sends gdStPayload(g, true) to the frame named "gd-st", resolves with the payload sent once the frame has applied it. */
window.gdStOpen = g => stLoad(Math.round(+g) || 1, true);
document.addEventListener('click', e => {
  if (e.target.id !== 'st-load') return; const g = Math.round(+$('#st-g').value) || 1;
  if (!confirm(`Load G${g} into ST-Girder? This replaces ST-Girder's current girder inputs (plates, materials, deck, bracing, skew, forces); Undo in ST-Girder restores them.`)) return;
  stLoad(g, $('#st-pl').checked).catch(er => stMsg(er.message, 'fail')); });
window.addEventListener('resize', () => { if (document.body.classList.contains('mod-st')) stPos(); });
// Ctrl+P / Cmd+P while the view is shown prints ST-Girder (its frame), not this page
document.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (!document.body.classList.contains('mod-st') || !(e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) || e.key.toLowerCase() !== 'p' || !ST_FRAME) return;

// the top bar's Print report while the view is shown: ST-Girder's Report tab (its Print button prints the frame)
function stReport() { if (!ST_FRAME || !ST_FRAME.contentWindow) return; try { const W = ST_FRAME.contentWindow; W.dispatchEvent(new W.CustomEvent('stg-goto', { detail: { tab: 'report' } })); } catch (e) { }
  ```

### SBD2-b. Live link: "GirderDetail changed — Update" banner, girder kept per project   [new] [no result change]
- **Host code**, inserted after `stReport()` (anchor: `  stMsg('ST-Girder\'s Report tab: choose the sections, then Print there.'); }`), exactly:
  ```js
/* ---------- Design & Rating (ST-Girder): live link to the modules (SBD2, 2026-10-22; merge of GirderDetail and ST-Girder, PR 2) ----------
   The frame reports its state after every computation ({ type: 'gd-st-state' }: the hand-off it holds, with its signature stSig, the results of
   every check and the load ratings; SBD2 shim). The host compares the hand-off it would send now for the selected girder, gdStPayload(G, pedestrian
   choice), with the one the frame holds (stSig: the payload without producedAt). When they differ, the bar shows "GirderDetail changed — Update";
   one click sends the girder again (stLoad: published to the girderDemands channel and applied in the frame, as Load girder). Nothing is applied
   automatically. The selected girder and the pedestrian choice are kept per project in P.ui.stG and P.ui.stPL (additive, view settings; older copies
   ignore them). The check runs after a saved change (autosave → stOnSave, debounced) while the view is shown, when the view opens, when the frame
   reports a new state, and for the Design all summary; it skips the hand-off build (gdStPayload, 0.3–0.8 s) when the project data, the girder, the
   pedestrian choice and the hand-off held are all as at the last check (ST_FP). Display only: no input or result of either part changes. */
let ST_STATE = null, ST_LINK = { st: 'wait' }, ST_FP = null, ST_LT = null;
// the hand-off's signature: its JSON without producedAt (the send time) and the frame's _selSpan; a 32-bit FNV-1a and a 31-multiplier hash, with the length
function stSig(p) { const s = JSON.stringify(p, (k, v) => k === 'producedAt' || k === '_selSpan' ? undefined : v) || ''; let a = 0x811c9dc5, b = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) { const c = s.charCodeAt(i); a = Math.imul(a ^ c, 16777619); b = (Math.imul(b, 31) + c) | 0; }
  return s.length + ':' + (a >>> 0).toString(16) + ':' + (b >>> 0).toString(16); }
function stNb() { const b = P && P.df && P.df.bridge; return b && b.ok ? b.nb : 0; }
function stSelG() { const nb = stNb(), g = Math.round(nm(P && P.ui && P.ui.stG)) || Math.round(nm(P && P.sa && P.sa.girder)) || 1; return nb ? Math.min(Math.max(1, g), nb) : g; }
function stSelPL() { return !(P && P.ui && P.ui.stPL === false); }
const stViewOn = () => document.body.classList.contains('mod-st');
function stLinkSoon(ms) { clearTimeout(ST_LT); ST_LT = setTimeout(() => { ST_LT = null; stLinkCheck(); }, ms == null ? 800 : ms); }
function stOnSave() { try { if (ST_FRAME && stViewOn()) stLinkSoon(); } catch (e) { } }   // autosave can run before this code has been evaluated
function stLinkCheck() {
  if (!P) return ST_LINK;
  if (!ST_STATE) { ST_LINK = { st: ST_FRAME ? 'wait' : 'closed' }; stLinkShow(); return ST_LINK; }
  const e = ST_STATE.ext, g = stSelG(), pl = stSelPL();
  if (!e) { ST_LINK = { st: 'none', g }; stLinkShow(); return ST_LINK; }
  if (+e.girder !== g) { ST_LINK = { st: 'other', g, held: e.label || ('G' + e.girder) }; stLinkShow(); return ST_LINK; }
  if ((typeof GR_RUN !== 'undefined' && GR_RUN) || GD_RQ.size || GD_XF_T || GD_PLQ.length || GD_RF_T) { stLinkSoon(1500); return ST_LINK; }   // the modules are being updated: check once they are done
  const fp = `${g}|${pl}|${e.sig}|${JSON.stringify(P, (k, v) => k === 'ui' ? undefined : v)}`;
  if (!ST_FP || ST_FP.fp !== fp) { const r = gdStPayload(g, pl); ST_FP = { fp, st: r.error ? 'err' : stSig(r.payload) === e.sig ? 'sync' : 'stale', why: r.error || '' }; }
  ST_LINK = { st: ST_FP.st, g, held: e.label || ('G' + g), why: ST_FP.why, pl }; stLinkShow(); return ST_LINK; }
function stLinkText(L) { L = L || ST_LINK;
  return L.st === 'sync' ? `ST-Girder holds G${L.g} as the modules give it now (in sync).`
    : L.st === 'stale' ? `GirderDetail changed since G${L.g} was loaded into ST-Girder (demands, plates or design inputs).`
    : L.st === 'other' ? `ST-Girder holds ${L.held}; G${L.g} is selected.`
    : L.st === 'none' ? 'ST-Girder holds its own inputs (no girder of this project loaded).'
    : L.st === 'err' ? `G${L.g}: the hand-off cannot be built (${L.why}).` : ''; }
function stLinkShow() { const el = $('#st-link'); if (!el) return; const L = ST_LINK;
  el.className = L.st === 'stale' ? 'st-stale' : L.st === 'sync' ? 'st-sync' : '';
  el.innerHTML = L.st === 'stale' ? `<b>GirderDetail changed</b> — <button type="button" class="btn btn-primary" data-stupd="1" title="Send G${L.g} again (the same hand-off as Load girder); it replaces ST-Girder's girder inputs, Undo there restores them">Update</button> ${esc(stLinkText(L))}`
    : esc(stLinkText(L)); }
window.addEventListener('message', e => { if (!gdFromST(e) || !e.data || e.data.type !== 'gd-st-state') return;
  ST_STATE = e.data; if (stViewOn()) stLinkSoon(200); const d = document.getElementById('da-st'); if (d) d.innerHTML = stDaHtml(); });
document.addEventListener('change', e => { const id = e.target && e.target.id; if (id !== 'st-g' && id !== 'st-pl') return;
  if (id === 'st-g') P.ui.stG = Math.round(+e.target.value) || 1; else P.ui.stPL = !!e.target.checked; autosave(); stLinkSoon(0); });
document.addEventListener('click', e => { const u = e.target.closest && e.target.closest('[data-stupd]'); if (u) { const g = stSelG();
    stLoad(g, stSelPL()).then(() => stLinkSoon(0)).catch(er => stMsg(er.message, 'fail')); return; }
  const go = e.target.closest && e.target.closest('[data-stgo]'); if (!go) return; e.preventDefault();
  const m = document.getElementById('da-modal'); if (m) m.hidden = true; stShow(); stGoTab(go.dataset.stgo); });
// open a tab of the view (ST-Girder's own derivation-link event, stg-goto); a request made before the frame is up waits for it
function stGoTab(tab) { if (!tab || !ST_FRAME) return; const send = () => { try { const W = ST_FRAME.contentWindow; W.dispatchEvent(new W.CustomEvent('stg-goto', { detail: { tab } })); } catch (er) { } };
  if (ST_READY) send(); else { const t0 = Date.now(), iv = setInterval(() => { if (ST_READY || Date.now() - t0 > 60000) { clearInterval(iv); if (ST_READY) setTimeout(send, 300); } }, 250); } }
// the ST-Girder tab where a check is worked, from its AASHTO LRFD article
function stTabOf(ref) { const r = String(ref || '');
  return /^6\.10\.2|^6\.10\.7\.3/.test(r) ? 'section' : /^6\.10\.3/.test(r) ? 'construct' : /^6\.10\.4|^2\.5\.2\.6/.test(r) ? 'stresses' : /^6\.10\.(7|8)|^6\.10\.1\.7/.test(r) ? 'flexure'
    : /^6\.10\.9/.test(r) ? 'shear' : /^6\.6|^6\.10\.5/.test(r) ? 'fatigue' : /^6\.10\.11/.test(r) ? 'stiff' : /^6\.10\.10/.test(r) ? 'conn' : /^9\.|^13\./.test(r) ? 'deck' : 'report'; }
// Design all: the view's results, read-only, each linked to the tab where it is worked
function stDaHtml() {
  const S = ST_STATE, f = v => v == null || !isFinite(v) ? '—' : (+v).toFixed(2), a = (tab, t) => `<a href="#" data-stgo="${tab}">${esc(t)}</a>`;
  if (!S) return `<h4>Design &amp; Rating (ST-Girder)</h4><p>The view has not been opened in this session. ${a('inputs', 'Open Design & Rating (ST-Girder)')}</p>`;
  const L = stLinkCheck(), e = S.ext;
  const head = `<h4>Design &amp; Rating (ST-Girder): ${esc(S.girderId || '')}</h4><p class="note-p">Read-only, from the ${a('report', 'Design & Rating (ST-Girder) view')}: ${e ? `hand-off ${esc(e.key || e.label)}` : 'ST-Girder\'s own inputs (no girder of this project loaded)'}. ${esc(stLinkText(L))}${L.st === 'stale' ? ' <button type="button" data-stupd="1">Update</button>' : ''}</p>`;
  if (!S.ok) return head + `<p><b style="color:var(--fail)">Input error in ST-Girder:</b> ${esc(S.err)}</p>`;
  const ck = S.checks || [], nf = ck.filter(c => !c.pass).length, R = S.rating, row = (l, i, o) => `<tr><td class="lbl">${a('rating', l)}</td><td class="n">${f(i)}</td><td class="n">${f(o)}</td></tr>`;
  return head + `<p>${ck.length} checks: ${ck.length - nf} pass, ${nf} do not pass.</p>
    <table class="tbl st-da-t"><thead><tr><th>Check (governing location)</th><th>AASHTO LRFD</th><th class="right">D/C</th><th>Result</th></tr></thead><tbody>${ck.map(c => `<tr class="${c.pass ? '' : 'ng'}"><td class="lbl">${a(stTabOf(c.ref), c.n)}</td><td>${esc(c.ref)}</td><td class="n">${c.oos ? 'out of scope' : f(c.r)}</td><td>${c.oos ? 'not reported' : c.pass ? 'pass' : 'FAIL'}</td></tr>`).join('')}</tbody></table>
    ${R ? `<table class="tbl st-da-t"><thead><tr><th>Load rating, HL-93 (MBE 6A)</th><th class="right">Inventory RF</th><th class="right">Operating RF</th></tr></thead><tbody>${row('Flexure (+M)', R.flexInv, R.flexOpr)}${R.negInv != null ? row('Flexure (−M)', R.negInv, R.negOpr) : ''}${row('Shear', R.shearInv, R.shearOpr)}${R.servInv != null ? row('Service II', R.servInv, R.servOpr) : ''}<tr class="tot"><td>Governing</td><td class="n"><b>${f(R.govInv)}</b></td><td class="n"><b>${f(R.govOpr)}</b></td></tr></tbody></table>` : ''}`;
}
  ```

## 2026-10-22 — PR: claude/sbd-3-report (SBD3: merge of GirderDetail and ST-Girder, PR 3: one title block, one report; PR link added after merge)

**No engineering result changes.** No formula, load or resistance factor, unit or code reference was changed; no saved key or format was changed
(one optional view field, `P.ui.rpt.st`, below). ST-Girder (`st-src`) is unchanged; its frame gets six more shims (display and report extract
only; no input or result touched). **Display change in the view:** ST-Girder's title-block fields (Project, Job No., By, Date, Checked by, Check
date) show the project title block, so in `tests/compare.mjs --tool sbd` the sections `G<n> st.tab.Report` and `G<n> st.report.all` differ from
stgirder.html in exactly those lines (title block, cover line, 2.1 Project and girder); every other section is identical. Results in the PR.

### SBD3-b. One report: ST-Girder's report in the Girder report and in Print   [new] [display only]
- **Frame shim** `window.gdStReportHtml(opt)` (last entry of `ST_SHIMS`, above): ST-Girder's `CalcDoc` (the Report tab's document, with the

- **Host code**, inserted after `stDaHtml()` (end of SBD2), exactly:
  ```js
/* ---------- Design & Rating (ST-Girder): one title block, one report (SBD3, 2026-10-22; merge of GirderDetail and ST-Girder, PR 3) ----------
   Title block: the project title block P.tb goes to the frame ({ type: 'gd-st-tb', tb }, after every saved change when it differs, and when the
   view opens); ST-Girder shows it read-only in place of its own Project, Job No., By, Date, Checked by and Check date, on the page, on its Report
   tab and in its printed header (stTbInp, SBD3 shim). ST-Girder's saved fields (inp.proj) are not changed; stgirder.html opened on its own shows them.
   Report: ST-Girder's calculation report (its CalcDoc, the sections chosen on its Report tab) is taken from the frame as HTML (gdStReportHtml, SBD3
   shim) and placed (a) in the Girder report as a chapter (Design & Rating (ST-Girder)), numbered inside the chapter as every other chapter, ids
   prefixed per chapter, and (b) in a module's Print report as Appendix A, its sections numbered A.1, A.1.1 … and its "see §n.k" links reading
   "see §A.n.k". ST-Girder's own CSS goes with it, scoped to the appendix (.st-apx, stApxCss), and KaTeX's style sheet (the same pinned URL as in
   st-src) is added to this page when an appendix is printed. MathJax skips it (tex2jax_ignore). The frame's own Print is unchanged. Display only. */
let ST_TBK = null, ST_APXCSS = null;
function stTbInp(inp, t) { if (!t || !inp) return inp; const p = inp.proj || {};
  return Object.assign({}, inp, { proj: Object.assign({}, p, { name: t.name || '', job: t.no || '', by: t.compBy || '', date: t.compDate || '', checkedBy: t.chkBy || '', chkDate: t.chkDate || '' }) }); }
function stTbPost() { if (!ST_FRAME || !P) return; const tb = P.tb ? JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(P.tb)) : null, k = JSON.stringify(tb); if (k === ST_TBK) return; ST_TBK = k; stPost({ type: 'gd-st-tb', tb }); }
// ST-Girder's own style rules (its inline <style>), every selector scoped to pre; :root, html, body and the document class .crdoc become pre itself
// (the appendix sits inside this page's .crdoc report); @page and @import dropped
function stSplitSel(t) { const out = []; let d = 0, cur = ''; for (const ch of t) { if (ch === '(' || ch === '[') d++; else if (ch === ')' || ch === ']') d--; if (ch === ',' && !d) { out.push(cur); cur = ''; } else cur += ch; } out.push(cur); return out.map(x => x.trim()).filter(Boolean); }
function stScopeCss(rules, pre) { let out = '';
  for (const r of rules) {
    if (r.selectorText != null && r.style) out += stSplitSel(r.selectorText).map(x => /^(:root|html|body)$/.test(x) ? pre : /^(html|body)\b/.test(x) ? x.replace(/^(html|body)/, pre) : /^\.crdoc(?![\w-])/.test(x) ? x.replace(/^\.crdoc/, pre) : `${pre} ${x}`).join(', ') + `{${r.style.cssText}}\n`;
    else if (r.media && r.cssRules) out += `@media ${r.media.mediaText}{${stScopeCss(r.cssRules, pre)}}\n`;
    else if (r.conditionText != null && r.cssRules) out += `@supports ${r.conditionText}{${stScopeCss(r.cssRules, pre)}}\n`;
    else if (/^@(font-face|keyframes)/.test(r.cssText)) out += r.cssText + '\n'; }
  return out; }
function stApxCss() { if (ST_APXCSS != null) return ST_APXCSS; let css = '';
  try { [...ST_FRAME.contentDocument.styleSheets].forEach(sh => { if (!sh.ownerNode || sh.ownerNode.tagName !== 'STYLE') return; css += stScopeCss(sh.cssRules, '.st-apx'); }); } catch (e) { css = ''; }
  return (ST_APXCSS = css); }
function stApxStyle() { if (document.getElementById('st-apx-css')) return; const st = document.createElement('style'); st.id = 'st-apx-css'; st.textContent = stApxCss(); document.head.appendChild(st); }
// KaTeX's style sheet for the appendix (the version and URL ST-Girder loads, st-src); resolves when loaded, or after 8 s
function stKatexCss() { let l = document.getElementById('st-katex-css'); if (l && l.dataset.ok) return Promise.resolve();
  if (!l) { l = document.createElement('link'); l.id = 'st-katex-css'; l.rel = 'stylesheet'; l.href = 'https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/KaTeX/0.16.9/katex.min.css'; document.head.appendChild(l); }
  return new Promise(res => { const done = () => { l.dataset.ok = '1'; res(); }; l.addEventListener('load', done, { once: true }); l.addEventListener('error', () => res(), { once: true }); setTimeout(res, 8000); })
    .then(() => document.fonts && document.fonts.ready ? Promise.race([document.fonts.ready, new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 4000))]) : null); }
// equations wider than the line shrunk to fit, as ST-Girder does before it prints (its crFit, run on the appendix in this page)
function stFit(el) { try { if (el && ST_FRAME && ST_FRAME.contentWindow.crFit) ST_FRAME.contentWindow.crFit(el); } catch (e) { } }
// the report HTML from the frame (it must be up)
function stRptHtml(idp) { const W = ST_FRAME && ST_FRAME.contentWindow; if (!ST_READY || !W || typeof W.gdStReportHtml !== 'function') return { error: 'open Design & Rating (ST-Girder) first' };
  try { return W.gdStReportHtml({ idp }); } catch (e) { return { error: e.message }; } }
// numbering n, n.k and "see §n.k" -> pre + n …, in the HTML of ST-Girder's CalcDoc
function stRenum(html, pre) {
  return html.replace(/(<h2 class="cr-h1"[^>]*>)(\d+)\. /g, `$1${pre}$2. `).replace(/(<h3 class="cr-h2">)(\d+)\.(\d+)\. /g, `$1${pre}$2.$3. `)
    .replace(/(<a href="#[^"]*"[^>]*>)(\d+)\.(?:(\d+)\.)? /g, (m, a, n, k) => `${a}${pre}${n}.${k ? k + '.' : ''} `).replace(/§(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)/g, `§${pre}$1`); }
function stRptOpt() { const S = ST_STATE, e = S && S.ext; if (!S) return '';
  const L = stLinkCheck(), bad = !S.ok ? 'ST-Girder has an input error' : '', note = !e ? 'ST-Girder\'s own inputs, no girder of this project loaded' : L.st === 'stale' ? 'GirderDetail changed since it was loaded: Update it in the view first' : L.st === 'other' ? `ST-Girder holds ${e.label}` : 'in sync';
  return `<div class="ck-row" style="margin-top:6px"><input type="checkbox" id="ro-st" ${P.ui.rpt.st === true && !bad ? 'checked' : ''} ${bad ? 'disabled' : ''}><label for="ro-st">Appendix A: Design &amp; Rating (ST-Girder) report of ${esc(S.girderId || 'the girder')} as the view holds it (${esc(bad || note)})</label></div>`; }
// a module's Print report: Appendix A
function stApxModule() { const r = stRptHtml('stA-'); if (r.error) return r; stApxStyle();
  const id = 'cr-sA', h = `<section class="cr-sec cr-break"><h2 class="cr-h1" id="${id}">Appendix A. Design &amp; Rating (ST-Girder): ${esc(r.girderId)}:</h2><p class="cr-p">ST-Girder's calculation (AASHTO LRFD design check and HL-93 load rating) of this girder, as the Design &amp; Rating (ST-Girder) view holds it: ${esc(stLinkText())} Its sections are numbered A.1, A.2 …</p></section>`;
  return { html: h + `<div class="st-apx tex2jax_ignore">${stRenum(r.html, 'A.')}</div>`, toc: `<li><a href="#${id}" data-crjump="${id}">Appendix A. Design &amp; Rating (ST-Girder)</a><ol>${r.toc.map((t, i) => `<li>A.${i + 1}. ${esc(t)}</li>`).join('')}</ol></li>` }; }
// the Girder report's chapter: girder g's hand-off as the modules give it now; loaded into the view first when the frame holds anything else
async function stChapter(g, k) { const wait = (f, ms) => new Promise(res => { const t0 = Date.now(), iv = setInterval(() => { if (f() || Date.now() - t0 > ms) { clearInterval(iv); res(f()); } }, 200); });
  const pl = stSelPL(), r = gdStPayload(g, pl); if (r.error) return { html: `<p class="cr-p">Not available: ${esc(r.error)}</p>`, toc: [] };
  if (!stEnsure() || !(await wait(() => ST_READY && ST_STATE, 90000))) return { html: '<p class="cr-p">Not available: the Design &amp; Rating (ST-Girder) frame did not start.</p>', toc: [] };
  const e = ST_STATE.ext, sig = stSig(r.payload);
  if (!e || +e.girder !== g || e.sig !== sig) { grMsg(`Loading G${g} into Design & Rating (ST-Girder)…`);
    let pay = r.payload; try { const w = window.BridgeXfer ? BridgeXfer.publish(GD_ST.ch, r.payload, GD_ST.producer, GD_ST.file) : null; if (w && w.payload) pay = w.payload; } catch (er) { }
    try { await stSend(pay, pl, true); } catch (er) { return { html: `<p class="cr-p">Not available: G${g} was not loaded into ST-Girder (${esc(er.message)}).</p>`, toc: [] }; }
    await wait(() => ST_STATE && ST_STATE.ext && ST_STATE.ext.sig === sig, 20000); }
  const x = stRptHtml('stx-'); if (x.error) return { html: `<p class="cr-p">Not available: ${esc(x.error)}</p>`, toc: [] }; stApxStyle();
  const P_ = `c${k}-`, html = x.html.replace(/ id="([^"]+)"/g, ` id="${P_}$1"`).replace(/url\(#([^)]+)\)/g, `url(#${P_}$1)`).replace(/href="#([^"]+)"/g, `href="#${P_}$1"`);   // ids unique to the chapter, as grChapter
  return { html: `<div class="st-apx tex2jax_ignore">${html}</div>`, toc: x.toc, katex: true }; }
  ```
- `stSend(pay, addPL)` → `stSend(pay, addPL, quiet)`; its line `stShow(); if (!ST_FRAME) return …` → `if (quiet) stEnsure(); else stShow(); if (!ST_FRAME) return …`.
- **Girder report:** `GR_CHAPS` gets a last entry `['st', 'Design & Rating (ST-Girder): design check and load rating']`; in `girderReportStart()`
  the chapter checkbox is checked by `(k === 'st' ? ch[k] === true : ch[k] !== false)` (was `ch[k] !== false`: the new chapter is off unless chosen)
  and a note follows the chapter list; in `girderReportRun()`, after the module chapters (anchor
  `const c = await grChapter(mod, k + 1, o, `G${g}: ${lbl}`); add(lbl, c.html, c.toc); }`), added
  `if (R.ch.st === true) { grMsg('Building: Design & Rating (ST-Girder)…'); await grTick(); const c = await stChapter(g, k + 1); add('Design & Rating (ST-Girder)', c.html, c.toc); if (c.katex) await stKatexCss(); }   // SBD3`
  and after its MathJax typeset line `host.querySelectorAll('.st-apx').forEach(stFit);   // SBD3: ST-Girder's chapter`. The chapter is the
  report's girder as the modules give it at that moment (`gdStPayload(g, pedestrian choice)`); when the view holds anything else it is loaded first
  (published and applied as Load girder, without switching to the view). Numbering inside the chapter is ST-Girder's own (1., 1.1 …), as every other
  chapter's; ids and links prefixed `c<k>-` as `grChapter` does.
- **Print (module report):** `openReport()`: `${stRptOpt()}` before the note paragraph (an "Appendix A: Design & Rating (ST-Girder) report of …
  as the view holds it (in sync | …)" checkbox, shown when the view has reported, disabled on an ST-Girder input error, off unless chosen; kept in
  `P.ui.rpt.st`). `doPrint()`: after `o.detail = $('#ro-detail').value; P.ui.rpt.detail = o.detail;` the `autosave();` moved to the next line, after
  `const rst = document.getElementById('ro-st'); if (rst) { o.st = rst.checked && !rst.disabled; P.ui.rpt.st = rst.checked; }`.
  `printCalcReport()`: after `host.innerHTML = buildCalcReport(o);` added
  `if (o.st) { const a = stApxModule(); if (a.error) alert(`Design & Rating (ST-Girder) appendix not added: ${a.error}`); else { host.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', a.html); const t = host.querySelector('.cr-front .cr-toc'); if (t) t.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', a.toc); await stKatexCss(); stFit(host.querySelector('.st-apx')); } }   // SBD3`
  The appendix is numbered A.1, A.1.1 …, "see §n.k" reads "see §A.n.k" (`stRenum`), and the report's contents list gets "Appendix A".
- Styles: ST-Girder's own inline style rules, scoped to `.st-apx` (`stApxCss`, in `<style id="st-apx-css">`), and KaTeX's style sheet
  `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/KaTeX/0.16.9/katex.min.css` (`<link id="st-katex-css">`, added on first use): the same library and pinned
  version that ST-Girder (`st-src`) loads; no new library. MathJax does not process the appendix (`tex2jax_ignore`).
- **Check case:** xsA, view holding G3 → Structural analysis, Print report, Appendix A on → the printed report ends with "Appendix A. Design &
  Rating (ST-Girder): G3 (Interior)" and sections "A.1. Objectives", "A.2. Input parameters", "A.2.1. Project and girder" …; 28 links read
  "see §A.n.k", none "see §n.k"; no duplicate id. Girder report G2 with chapters Structural analysis and Design & Rating (ST-Girder) → "Chapter 1.
  Structural analysis and stresses", "Chapter 2. Design & Rating (ST-Girder)" (ST-Girder's cover "G2 (Interior) … Job PN-77"); the view now holds G2.
  ST-Girder's own "Print this report" in the view prints the frame as before.

**Open items:** none.
